title: Sandboxed model code can reach Docker, other system sockets and mounted drives
description:
Model-written Python (the run_python tutor tool) and model-written video code run inside bwrap. Both sandboxes mount the whole disk read-only and then hide only the home folder, the data folder, /tmp and /run/user. Everything else on the machine stays visible.

Measured on the owner's machine with the exact flags: Python inside the sandbox connected to /run/docker.sock (GET /_ping answered 200 OK), to the libvirt socket and to the system D-Bus socket, and could read drives mounted under /media and /mnt. A Unix socket is not network, so --unshare-all does not block it. For a learner in the docker group, Docker access is full control of the machine, network included. A web page or PDF with hidden instructions can make the tutor write such code.

After this ticket both sandboxes see only the system's program and library folders, plus what each one already binds back on purpose (the Python runtime and venv, node_modules, the Node binary, the render script, the tool root, the workspace).
design: Replace '--ro-bind / /' with read-only binds of /usr and /etc, and of /bin, /sbin, /lib and /lib64 as the distro has them (they are often links into /usr). Keep that list in one place and use it from pythonSandbox (server/tools/python.mjs) and SANDBOX (server/media/video-sandbox.mjs). The tool root from Rabbithole-elx.1 must stay visible read-only when it lies outside those folders. If a new bwrap flag is needed, add it to the BWRAP table in video-sandbox.mjs, which turns the list into Windows launcher arguments. test/tools/python.test.mjs asserts the whole-disk bind today and must change.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inside the run_python sandbox and the video sandbox, /run, /media, /mnt and the learner's home and data folder are absent or empty.
- Code in either sandbox cannot connect to a socket under /run; a test with real bwrap shows this where bwrap is installed.
- A run_python call that imports the offline packages, a video render and a Manim clip still work.
- A test fails if the whole-disk mount comes back.
- The Windows launcher arguments built from the same list still work as before.
notes: Defaults: one SYSTEM_DIRS list + systemBinds() in server/media/video-sandbox.mjs, used by SANDBOX and pythonSandbox. Folders: /usr /etc /bin /sbin /lib /lib32 /lib64 (links stay links via bwrap --symlink, new BWRAP entry) plus /var/lib/texmf (Debian TeX Live formats; Manim LaTeX failed without it), /var/cache/fontconfig (font cache) and /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew (Homebrew Node's own ld.so and libs; video render failed with execvp without it). Dropped --tmpfs /run/user (nothing to hide now); kept home/data tmpfs. Tool root needs no whole bind: its pieces (runtime, venv, TinyTeX, browser, node_modules, Node) already bind individually. launcherArgs skips SYSTEM_DIRS binds so Windows args are unchanged. Not done: --remount-ro of the sandbox's own tmpfs root (ephemeral, not host).

title: Read-page saves can follow a link left by sandboxed Python and write outside the workspace
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

A page the tutor saves with the read-page tutor tool always lands in the conversation's Python workspace and nowhere else. Today Python run by the tutor inside the sandbox can leave a symbolic link in that workspace. A later save under the same name then makes the app, which runs outside the sandbox as the learner, write the downloaded page wherever the link points, for example over a shell startup file. A web page carrying injected instructions can chain both steps. After this ticket a save never writes through a link or any other non-regular file. It still replaces an ordinary file of the same name, as today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A save whose name matches a symbolic link in the workspace leaves the link's target unchanged.
- [ ] A save whose name matches an ordinary file replaces that file, as today.
- [ ] A test plants a link in the workspace, saves a page under that name, and shows the target is untouched.
notes: Save writes a fresh .<uuid>.part file (flag wx) in the workspace and renames it over save_as, so a link, hard link or FIFO under that name is replaced, never written through. A directory under that name makes the save fail and the temp file is removed.

title: Full test command fails at the file size check before any test runs
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

The full test command passes again on master. Today it stops at the file size check because one markdown rendering module grew past the line limit, so the type check and the tests never run, and every agent run fails before it can verify its work. Move one whole job of that module, such as link and citation rendering, into its own module. Do not raise the limit or squeeze lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The full test command passes on master.
- [ ] The markdown module is under the line limit because one whole job lives in its own module.
- [ ] Replies render exactly as before.
notes: Moved DOM selection mapping (markerOf, rawOffsets, rawRange) to src/markdown/rawOffsets.ts instead of link/citation rendering: it shares no closure state with renderMarkdown, so it moves verbatim. markdown.ts re-exports both, like plainText, so callers and tests keep their imports.

title: Fix broken LaTeX in saved conversation replies
description: Latest conversation displays raw LaTeX instead of readable mathematics. Reproduce saved spectral theorem reply and fix the shared renderer without modifying message text or passage offsets.
acceptance_criteria: Spectral theorem equations render as math; existing Markdown and source offset tests pass; production build succeeds.
close_reason: Fixed shared Markdown dollar-display tokenizer: content may begin and end on delimiter lines, including multiline equations and blank lines, without consuming following prose. Verified actual saved spectral-theorem reply: 106 math expressions, 22 display equations, all five section headings. 17 targeted tests, build, scoped formatting and size check pass. Full suite: 710 pass, 3 fail, 8 skipped; same three failures reproduced with original parser. Repo formatting reports 21 pre-existing untouched files. Running app serves rebuilt index and JS bundle.

title: Video cut style validator rejects valid cuts
description: cutSource accepted only a few expression shapes for color/font props, so component props, template literals, series[i], interpolateColors, border:0 and logical expressions all failed with 'Video cut breaks the style brief colors or fonts.' Every recent video failed this way (artifact ade263cb, 2026-11-14).
acceptance_criteria: Realistic cut patterns pass; foreign hex/rgb/named colors and non-house fonts still fail; error names the offending property.
close_reason: Validator now checks literal text only; expressions pass. Error names the property. Regression cases in test/media/video-plan.test.mjs.

title: Verify native Claude Code subscription sign-in

User must complete native claude auth login with their own subscription; do not copy credentials or substitute an API key. Then rerun redacted status and resume the bounded synthetic history-transfer experiment.

notes:
Rechecked 2026-11-08: native claude auth status reports loggedIn=false, authMethod=none, apiProvider=firstParty. Requires account owner to complete native claude auth login; no credentials copied or API key substituted.
2026-11-09: Claude is now the default provider and gates the text release (PRD Providers). If sign-in is lost, the user must run 'claude auth login' themselves.
2026-11-09 verified: Claude Code 2.1.319 'claude auth status' loggedIn=true, authMethod=claude.ai, apiProvider=firstParty, subscription login (no API key; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset). Live bounded synthetic inference via unmodified 'claude -p "Reply with exactly: OK" --output-format json --max-turns 1' returned is_error=false, result=OK, model claude-opus-5-5. No tokens or account identifiers recorded. TreeTutor-7t3.4.2 history-transfer experiment can resume.

title: Custom endpoints survive a restart on Windows
description: Saved custom endpoints and their API keys vanish on Windows after every restart. The check that the saved file belongs to the user calls process.getuid(), which does not exist on Windows. The read throws, the provider swallows the error and starts with an empty list. Adding one endpoint afterwards overwrites the file and drops the rest, and conversations tied to an old endpoint id lose their model. CI runs tests on Ubuntu only, so nothing catches it.
design: Skip only the owner-uid comparison when process.getuid is missing; keep the regular-file and single-link checks on every platform.
acceptance_criteria:
- Endpoints saved before a restart load again when process.getuid is unavailable.
- On POSIX, a file owned by another user is still refused.
- A test reloads saved endpoints with process.getuid removed and fails without the fix.
notes: PR #160: readOwned skips the uid comparison when process.getuid is missing; CI green.

title: Map previews fail on a learning tree with about 390 or more conversations
description:
The map asks the server for a short preview of every conversation in the open learning tree. The page puts up to 500 conversation ids in the address of one request.

Node refuses a request whose headers pass 16,384 bytes, and 500 ids make an address of about 20 KB. Measured against a local Node server with browser-like headers: 380 ids answer 200, 400 ids answer 431. The 431 answer is not JSON, so the page's request helper throws, and because all batches are awaited together no preview loads at all. A learning tree with about 390 or more conversations shows no previews on the map.

After this ticket, previews load for a learning tree of any size.
design: Smallest change: lower the batch size in previewRequests (the map previews module) from 500 to 300 ids, about 12 KB per request. The server's own limit of 500 ids per request can stay. The existing test that expects a batch of 500 changes with it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A learning tree with 1,000 conversations loads every preview on the map.
- No preview request passes Node's default header limit of 16,384 bytes, address and headers together.
- A learning tree with fewer conversations than one batch still makes one request.
notes: Batch 300 ids; test budgets 4 KB for browser headers under Node's 16 KB limit. PR #64.

title: Third repo audit fixes: map previews, layout save, release links, memory note, duplicate code
description:
Fixes from the third whole-repo audit of 2026-11-21 (findings 1-9). Load assumed: one learner, one machine, one server process, a library that can grow to thousands of conversations.

Decisions so far:

- Finding 3 is two tickets. Publishing the desktop release is the owner's step (AGENTS.md keeps pushes and release runs with the owner); setting the tag and the hash is the agent's step and waits for it.
- The stream-collect helper waits for the discussion save throttle, because both edit the same lines in the discussion route.
- The memory note limit is 8,000 characters.
- The theme ticket merges only the icon files if `astryx theme build` cannot follow a shared import.
- Too small for a ticket: the site() helper exists twice (tool runner and exhibits); the usage-validity check is repeated in four files; static files are sent with no-store.

Fog:

- Not read by the audit: the video pipeline internals, PDF parts, suggestions, most page components, the Rust sandbox launcher beyond argument parsing, the GitHub workflows. Nothing was run on Windows or macOS.
- The local embedder module carries two `gitleaks:allow` comments on public model file hashes. AGENTS.md forbids these without the owner's permission; the audit could not tell whether the owner approved them.

title: Claude and Codex receive the system prompt and the tool token on the command line
description:
Each turn starts the Claude Code CLI with the whole system prompt after --system-prompt and the tool server's address and bearer token as JSON after --mcp-config. Codex gets the same token through a -c mcp_servers setting. This causes two problems.

Size: the fixed part of the tutor prompt is about 15,000 characters. The branch snapshot, the concept neighbourhood (up to 8,000 characters), every resource of the tree (no limit) and the memory note (no limit) are added to it. Windows allows 32,767 characters for a whole command line and Linux allows 131,072 bytes for one argument. A branch conversation in a tree with a few dozen resources crosses the Windows limit. From then on every reply in that tree fails with a raw spawn error, and the learner has no way to fix it.

Privacy: command lines are readable by every account on the machine (ps). The token lets another account call the turn's tools, such as read_conversation, while the turn runs. The prompt holds the memory note about the learner.

After this ticket the prompt and the tool token reach the CLIs through files or environment variables that only the learner's account can read, and the prompt lists a bounded number of resources.
design: The installed Claude CLI lists --system-prompt-file, and --mcp-config accepts a file path (checked with claude --help on 2026-11-21). Write both files in the turn's existing workspace under the data folder. For Codex, check the installed version's MCP settings for a way to name an environment variable for the token (bearer_token_env_var or env_http_headers) before choosing; the launch arguments are built in server/providers/codex.mjs. The resource list is added in server/http/routes/send.mjs; 50 is a reasonable limit. Not run on Windows: the limit there comes from the platform's documentation.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Claude launch arguments contain neither the prompt text nor the token.
- The Codex launch arguments contain no token.
- Files written for a turn are readable only by the learner (mode 0600 on Linux) and are removed when the turn ends, also after an error or a stop.
- With 500 resources in a tree and a long memory note, the Claude command line stays under 32,767 characters; a unit test on the launch arguments shows it.
- The prompt lists at most a fixed number of resources, newest first.
- Tutor tools still reach the tool server with a valid token on both providers.
notes: Defaults: Claude turn files live in claude-workspace/turn-XXXX (mkdtemp 0700, files 0600), removed in generate's finally. Tools-off turns keep the inline empty '{"mcpServers":{}}' (no token). Codex uses env_http_headers {Authorization: RABBITHOLE_MCP_AUTHORIZATION} (present in codex-cli 0.171.0); the env var holds the full 'Bearer ...' value so server/tools/mcp.mjs is unchanged. Prompt lists the newest 50 resources (highest number first). Pre-existing, unrelated: RABBITHOLE_TEST_PROVIDER=codex native-tools 'tools-off arguments' fails on base too (usage reasoning field).

title: A long attachment makes the server use gigabytes of memory before the reply starts
description:
Before each reply the server matches the message against the learner's known concepts with the local embedding model (the send route calls ctx.neighbourhood, which calls matched in server/neighbourhood.mjs). The text it passes is the question with the full text of every attachment. That text is split into paragraphs and all paragraphs are embedded in one batch.

Measured with the real embedder: 50 paragraphs (34 KB) took 0.3 s and 316 MB of memory; 200 paragraphs (134 KB) took 1.4 s and 780 MB; 600 paragraphs (403 KB) took 4.9 s and 1.8 GB. A 1 MB text file or a long PDF needs several GB. The server can freeze or be killed, which cuts every running reply and job.

After this ticket only what the learner typed and the branch passage are matched against concepts. Attachment text is never embedded for this step, and the number of paragraphs embedded for one reply has a fixed upper limit.
design: Smallest change: pass body.text and tree.branch?.text to ctx.neighbourhood in server/http/routes/send.mjs instead of the prompt built by withAttachments. Add the paragraph limit inside matched, where the chunks are made.
acceptance_criteria:
- A message with a large text or PDF attachment embeds only the typed text and the branch passage; a test with a counting fake embedder shows it.
- The largest message the server accepts (100 KB of typed text) embeds no more than a fixed number of paragraphs.
- Concept matching for a plain question and for a branch passage works as today.
notes: Default: PARAGRAPH_LIMIT = 20 (first 20 paragraphs; ~50 paragraphs measured at ~300 MB). Attachment text is also left out of whole-name matching, since the same text feeds both.

title: Second repo audit fixes: sandbox reach, attachment memory, command-line limits, reply speed
description:
Fixes from the second whole-repo audit of 2026-11-21 (findings 1-13). Every ticket here stays valid after the Electron desktop epic (Rabbithole-elx): each one is about the server, the providers or the page, which Electron leaves unchanged.

Decisions so far:

- Left out on purpose: pinning the release workflow's actions to commit SHAs. Rabbithole-elx.7 rewrites that workflow, so the pin belongs there.
- Left out on purpose: anything in the Tauri shell, its config or its staging step. Rabbithole-elx.5 removes them.
- The sandbox ticket waits for Rabbithole-elx.1, because the narrowed sandbox must keep the tool root visible.
- Finding 3 (command-line length) was not run on Windows. It rests on the documented limits (32,767 characters per command line on Windows, 131,072 bytes per argument on Linux) and the measured prompt size.
- Too small for a ticket: a JSON body of null answers 500 instead of 400; a folder path on the static route answers 500; concept observations stay after their conversation is deleted.

title: One shared check for video sandbox output; cut snapshots work on Windows
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

Video snapshots work on Windows, and every check on a file the video sandbox wrote lives in one place. Three places each check that a sandbox output is an ordinary file inside the output folder and not a link: videos, cut snapshots and set piece stills. The copies have drifted. The cut snapshot copy splits paths on forward slashes only, so on Windows every snapshot is refused as unreadable, which blocks cut audits there. Merge the three into one shared check. Each caller keeps its own error messages and size limits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Videos, cut snapshots and set piece stills all use one shared output check.
- [ ] Each keeps its current error messages, size limits and refusal of links.
- [ ] Cut snapshots pass the check with Windows-style paths.
- [ ] One test covers the shared check: a link is refused, a file outside the output folder is refused, and an ordinary file inside it is accepted.
notes: Shared check is sandboxOutput(workspace, file) in server/media/video-sandbox.mjs, returning the lstat or null; callers keep their messages and size limits. It resolves the output folder as realpath(workspace)/out like videos did, so a linked out folder is now refused for cut snapshots and piece stills too. Windows: file name comes from node:path basename instead of a '/' split; proven with path.win32 rules only, no Windows machine.

title: Windows desktop app shows "Not found." instead of the UI; bad URL escape gives a server error
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

The Windows desktop app shows the learner the app instead of "Not found." The check that keeps static file requests inside the built UI folder assumes forward-slash paths, so on Windows it rejects every file. In the same place, a request whose URL holds a malformed percent escape crashes into a server error and is logged as a fault. It should get a plain not-found answer instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With Windows-style paths, every file inside the built UI folder is served.
- [ ] Requests that resolve outside the UI folder, including backslash and dot-dot forms, still get not found.
- [ ] A URL with a malformed percent escape gets not found, not a server error, and logs nothing.
- [ ] A unit test exercises the Windows path rules without needing a Windows machine.
notes:
Extracted assetPath(assets, pathname, paths = node:path) in server/http/routes/assets.mjs; boundary is startsWith(assets + sep). Tests inject path.win32. Encoded C: or \\server segments resolve inside dist (harmless missing files), so they are not treated as escapes.
CI first run: unrelated flake in test/media/video-runaway.test.mjs ('a video whose calls take over 20 minutes in total still completes', TypeError: Cannot interpolate an input which is not a number). Passes locally; rerun green.

title: Repo audit fixes: test gate, sandbox write escape, Windows paths, store cleanup

title: Finish review and DESIGN.md for Line Diagram
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-ldr

## What to build

Every screen of the shipped app is reviewed against the Line Diagram mockups and direction contract with the Impeccable finish review, and its material fixes are applied. DESIGN.md is rewritten from the shipped build to describe Line Diagram and its six themes.

Mockup: docs/mockups/line-diagram/index.html

## Guards

- The design authority is the epic's direction contract, the Impeccable surface brief for the workspace, and the mockup pages named in the Mockup line. The old Paperback look is not a reference.
- No coloured line or bar sits beside text anywhere (owner rule).
- Use theme tokens only; the token lint test must pass.
- Keep every existing behaviour, including keyboard and Vim access. Where UI moves, update fixture selectors but keep their behavioural assertions.
- Run the Impeccable detector on changed files and fix what it flags or justify it in the ticket notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The finish review verdict and its fixes are recorded in the ticket notes.
- [ ] DESIGN.md describes the shipped Line Diagram world, its tokens and its six themes; no Paperback references remain.
- [ ] Dark and light screenshots of each screen in Main Line are recorded under docs/verification.
notes:
Finish review (impeccable-finish-reviewer, code-led, critique reference = docs/mockups/line-diagram; 56 captures: 14 screens x dark/light x 1440x900/390x844, Main Line, via scripts/capture-finish.mjs now also covering Usage, Videos, Pieces). Round 1 verdict: disposition fix, 8 material fixes. Applied: (1) map handles are stations: 12px source interchange ring / 15px target ring, 3px porcelain on deep field (map.css); (2) gradient fade under the composer dock removed, composer itself solid (states.css); (3) no second focus ring inside fields: inner outline off for Astryx text inputs, composer editor and title-search palette, palette seam turns porcelain on focus (states.css); (4) enlarged diagram fills the sheet, min(960px,92vw) (media.css); (5) Usage scale max rounded up to a multiple of 3 so empty chart reads 3,2,1,0 not 1,1,0,0 (+unit test); (6) Mermaid themeCSS: 8px node corners, 1.5px node strokes, round-capped 2px links; (7) Downloads absent from captures is kept behaviour (renders only with downloads), recorded in the surface brief; (8) DESIGN.md + .impeccable/design.json rewritten by impeccable-documenter (choice: overwrite, default since AC forbids Paperback references; no structured question tool in this unattended run). Verdict pass: 1,2,4,5,6,7 resolved; 3 partial (title search) then fixed and verified by computed style + screenshot (palette input outline none, header seam porcelain); 8 resolved by the rewrite except seed:d269121b131cc617, which stays uncorroborated (no roll output in repo, no CLI here). Detector after fixes: 0 findings on src/styles (15px step added to DESIGN.md ramp). Screenshots: docs/verification/line-diagram/*.webp.
Drift the documenter found, recorded not fixed (outside the reviewer's list): .visual-drawing-ring conic-gradient spinner (states.css) breaks no-gradient/one-motion; .focus-restore slide and sidebar-toggle rotation (shell.css) travel; .citation-chip fully rounded (workspace.css:187) vs 4px chips; several focus rings use --focus-outline-offset 3px or -4px vs the 2px global; PieceLibrary HUES and some comments keep Paperback names (amber/leaf/rust/lichen); question bubble on raised enamel vs contract's neutral tint; Mermaid series order 1,4,3,2. src/media/player.tsx keeps Archivo/Literata for the video player world. Candidates for a follow-up ticket.

title: Narrow layout in the new world
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-ldr

## What to build

At 48rem and below the learner gets a small header with menu, wordmark, Search learning trees and New chat. The drawer holds the sidebar's contents, including the Contents route strip, and Map opens from the drawer. One pane at a time; no screen scrolls sideways.

Mockup: docs/mockups/line-diagram/narrow.html

## Guards

- The design authority is the epic's direction contract, the Impeccable surface brief for the workspace, and the mockup pages named in the Mockup line. The old Paperback look is not a reference.
- No coloured line or bar sits beside text anywhere (owner rule).
- Use theme tokens only; the token lint test must pass.
- Keep every existing behaviour, including keyboard and Vim access. Where UI moves, update fixture selectors but keep their behavioural assertions.
- Run the Impeccable detector on changed files and fix what it flags or justify it in the ticket notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] At 390px wide, reading, Contents and Map each work without sideways scrolling.
- [ ] The drawer opens and closes by pointer and keyboard and returns focus.
- [ ] Search and New chat in the header work as in the sidebar.
notes: Defaults: the drawer renders the desktop sidebar itself (nav.sidebar.sidebar-drawer) inside the Astryx Drawer, 320px wide: wordmark + Close contents, New chat + search, views in sidebar order (Read, Map, Knowledge, Videos, Pieces, Library), Contents (shown from every tab, as the old drawer did), Downloads + Settings at the foot. ContentsDrawer removed. Header keeps the existing Hide top bar toggle (Ctrl+Shift+F) beside search and New chat so focus mode stays reachable by pointer; the mockup draws only menu/wordmark/search/New chat. Header wordmark is a button to Library as on the sidebar. Drawer wordmark has no tooltip: it opens under the pointer and the tooltip would swallow the first Escape. Any button in the drawer closes it except the Downloads popover. Settings from the drawer returns focus to Contents. Impeccable detector (regex, 4.8.1): 0 anti-patterns; advisory 18px header wordmark (mockup .nbar .mark) off the Paperback-era DESIGN.md ramp; other advisories pre-existing. Browser check at 390x844 (local build with overlay node_modules for missing @fontsource): read, drawer and map scrollWidth 390 = clientWidth; Escape closes the drawer in one press and focus returns to Contents after pointer and keyboard open. verify-settings-window.mjs fails at step 2 on desktop (map card Open covered by a card title span) before any narrow step; unrelated to this change (ldr.5 map cards).

title: States and overlays in the new world
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-ldr

## What to build

The learner sees menus, the passage box, dialogs, enlarged media, composer and reply states, first run, media states and focus rings in the new look.

- Overlays sit on raised enamel with a 1.5px porcelain seam. Scarlet only for failures, always with words and a way forward.
- Loading uses sized skeletons. Focus is a porcelain ring on every focusable control.

Mockup: docs/mockups/line-diagram/states.html

## Guards

- The design authority is the epic's direction contract, the Impeccable surface brief for the workspace, and the mockup pages named in the Mockup line. The old Paperback look is not a reference.
- No coloured line or bar sits beside text anywhere (owner rule).
- Use theme tokens only; the token lint test must pass.
- Keep every existing behaviour, including keyboard and Vim access. Where UI moves, update fixture selectors but keep their behavioural assertions.
- Run the Impeccable detector on changed files and fix what it flags or justify it in the ticket notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every overlay keeps its focus trap, Escape and return-focus behaviour.
- [ ] Focus is visible on every control in every theme and side.
- [ ] First run and every composer, reply and media state shown in the mockup exist in the app.
notes:
Defaults: overlays (.astryx-popover covers menus/selects/downloads, dialogs, alert dialogs, branch form/passage box, merge dialog) get raised enamel + 1.5px --color-border-emphasized seam (mockup .pop/.menu/.dialog use seam2), no shadow; Chrome renders 1.5px as 1px at DPR 1. Destructive follows mockup states.html: delete menu items in scarlet text, AlertDialog destructive confirm uses Astryx's scarlet fill (old Paperback outlined override removed). Global :where(:focus-visible) 2px porcelain ring, 2px offset, zero specificity so area rings (sidebar inset -4px etc.) win; focus contrast per theme/side already covered by themes.test. New states: streaming reply with no text shows three sized skeleton lines (aria-hidden, not on the map); no model = scarlet 'No model is connected. Open Settings, then Connections.' inside both composers (no role, keeps the not-an-alert behaviour); first run is a raised card with per-connection 'Not found' (scarlet + triangle) or 'Connected' (tick). Already present and left as is: stop button, file tray, drop note, unreadable-file refusal, reply failed/interrupted with Retry reply, video drawing/failed/retry, 3D piece turntable. Skipped: visual drawing sweep still uses a conic gradient (contract says flat) — media styling left for ldr.8/finish review; mockup 'Reset view'/'Drag to orbit' caption on 3D pieces not added. Impeccable detector (regex) on changed files: 0 anti-patterns; advisories 22px first-run title (mockup .first h2) and pre-existing 16px. Browser check (built app, temp store, 1440x900): first-run card, model menu seam, tree search dialog, porcelain focus on every visible control, Escape returns focus to opener.
Merged master (ldr.6 had moved delete-menu-item out); map menu Delete item now uses Astryx variant destructive for the mockup's scarlet text. PR #24, CI green.

title: Settings and Usage in the new world
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-ldr

## What to build

description:

The learner sees the learning tree map's links as transit lines: the trunk in porcelain and each family in its colour, 7px and round-capped, turning only at 45 or 90 degrees.

title: Line Diagram UI rework
description:
## Problem

The app still wears Paperback Series. The owner chose a replacement world, Line Diagram, on 2026-11-19, and replaced the six old themes with six new ones. Static mockups of every screen exist; the app code has not moved.

## Solution

Rabbithole is drawn as a transit diagram. A learning tree is a network: the trunk is the porcelain line, each first-level branch family is a coloured line, and every conversation is a station. Every screen moves to this look while every existing behaviour keeps working.

Mockup: docs/mockups/line-diagram/index.html (all screens; the bar on each page switches theme and light/dark)

## Direction contract

The full contract (THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM, FINISH, departures, per-screen rules, kept behaviour) is in the Impeccable surface brief for the workspace (`.impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md`). Key rules:

- Lines turn only at 45 or 90 degrees, round-capped, 5px in the sidebar and 7px on the map.
- Routing: a line leaves its ring horizontally, turns 45 degrees, runs vertically through the centre of the gutter (at least 40px clear of any card edge) when the rise exceeds the run, turns 45 degrees again and enters the target ring horizontally. Rings at the same height join with one straight horizontal.
- A conversation is a white-ringed station; the larger ring with a dot is where the learner is.
- Colour belongs to the lines. Text is never tinted to decorate, and no coloured bar sits beside text.
- An address chip filled with the family colour leads each conversation title.
- Scarlet means failure only and always comes with words and a way forward.
- One motion: a new branch draws its line out of its source ring in 350ms with an exponential ease-out, then the station lands. Reduced motion shows it at once.
- Fonts: Barlow (interface), Barlow Semi Condensed (titles, caps labels, wordmark), Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (replies, 17px/1.68, 640px measure). Self-hosted.
- Flat: no shadow, gradient or blur. 8px corners on controls and containers, 4px on chips.

## Themes

Six themes replace Paperback, Forest, Harbor, Dusk, Ember and Graphite: Main Line (default), Enamel, Tunnel, Timetable, Ferry, Terminus. Each has a light and a dark palette with the same roles; Appearance picks the side. Exact values are in docs/mockups/line-diagram/ld.css; docs/mockups/line-diagram/themes.html shows them side by side. All text pairs reach 4.5:1 and lines and seams 3:1.

## Decisions so far

- Defaults recorded at publishing (2026-11-19) for the three open mockup questions; the owner may override any of them before the run reaches the ticket:
  - The Contents route strip and the small line swatches in keys and legends stay. They are the diagram itself, not decoration beside text.
  - A child card placed left of or above its parent mirrors the routing rule: out sideways, through the gutter centre, in sideways.
  - The map keeps cards at every zoom. Collapsing to bare stations would be new behaviour and is out of scope.

## Fog

- The mockups are static; interaction details not drawn there follow existing behaviour.

title: Fast suite: 3 mid-stream save tests fail after 250 ms save throttle
description: On master (before Rabbithole-4jx.3 changes too), npm test fails 3 tests deterministically: test/media/videos-streaming.test.mjs:12 (saved text 'Before.' vs 'Before.\nAfter.'), test/media/visuals-queue.test.mjs:7 ('First paragraph.\n' vs with 'Last paragraph.'), test/store/branch-tree.test.mjs:10 ('Branch B:1 ' vs 'Branch B:1 Branch B:2 '). Cause: commit 77670c3 added a 250 ms throttle on store.update during streaming in server/http/routes/send.mjs:348, and these tests read the saved reply mid-stream right after each delta. Fix: inject a save clock/budget the tests can control (testing guide: no real sleeps), or have the tests await the stream text instead of the saved row; keep the throttle. Acceptance: the three tests pass and npm test is green.
notes: Result: createApp gains saveEvery (default 250 ms, kept in production); send.mjs throttles mid-stream store.update by ctx.saveEvery. The 3 mid-stream save tests (videos-streaming, visuals-queue, branch-tree) pass saveEvery: 0, no sleeps. Decision: inject interval instead of rewriting tests to read stream text, since they assert the saved row; tradeoff is one extra createApp option. Also fixed a load-dependent hang in test/media/video-audit.test.mjs "cancel stops a running snapshot and a running audit": after Cancel a second snapshot call can start with an already-aborted signal and the fake waited only for a future abort event (the real sandboxSnapshot aborts at once); fake now resolves if signal.aborted. Repro: about 1 in 4 runs of test/media at concurrency 8 hung before the fix; 10/10 clean after. Checks: npm test 704/704 pass; npm run test:affected 355/355 pass; check-size ok; prettier clean on touched files. npm run format:check still fails on 14 untouched files from earlier commits (e.g. server/http/jobs/media.mjs, src/media/player.tsx); not changed here.

title: Video consistency and reliability: set pieces, cut audit, joins, cheap Retry
description:
Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. ADR: docs/adr/0002-audited-cuts-and-set-pieces.md. From the 2026-11-14 grilling session. Follows TreeTutor-tq7 (Remotion validator fix).

## Decisions so far

- Manim validator checks only literal colour/font text, like the fixed Remotion validator; Manim cuts are checked when written.
- Instructions explain the validator rules up front. Two tries per cut; the repair sees the real error with paths stripped, and doubles as the cut audit.
- Set pieces: the plan gives each recurring object a look; one call writes shared components every Remotion cut must use.
- One cut audit per cut, all in parallel, before the cut plays; code plus 960x540 frames per sentence end and the last frame; aligns to the plan, not the neighbour; a broken fix falls back.
- Joins: continuing cut = hard cut; scene change = plan-chosen @remotion/transitions effect played one side at a time.
- Pen is for emphasis only; freehand stays; visible pen tip.

title: Attachments: images, PDFs and text files
description:
Spec: docs/attachments-spec.md. Spec D of four, from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Images, PDFs and plain-text files via paperclip, paste and drop; attachment belongs to its question; deleted with its conversation; no app caps, provider context errors shown.
- Chat model reads images natively (Claude, Codex; custom endpoint models via an Accepts images switch, default off). No smart-model description step.
- Non-vision chat model: tesseract.js OCR automatically, language data downloaded on first use; OCR icon explains limits; OCR unavailable means send refused.
- PDFs via pdfjs-dist structure: visible text as text, embedded images >= 10% of the page as images, full-page scan sent as image with its invisible OCR text ignored; vector diagrams keep only labels.
- Custom endpoints send images only on their own turn; later turns use [image: name]. Children get text and image names through inherited context only.
- Only widely used, maintained libraries; normal semver ranges.
- Image input shapes (D1, verified live on codex-cli 0.167.2 and Claude Code 2.1.325): Codex turn/start input item { type: 'localImage', path } (optional detail auto|low|high|original) after the text item; Claude -p adds --input-format stream-json on image turns with one user message whose content holds text plus { type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type, data } }. Resumed Claude sessions keep the image; text-only turns stay plain stdin. Details on TreeTutor-9lj.1.

## Fog
- None open (D1 resolved by TreeTutor-9lj.1).

title: Visual asking and motion: one Ask button, chips, step-through
description:

## Decisions so far

title: Titles and origin: model-written titles and the origin strip
description:
Spec: docs/titles-and-origin-spec.md. Spec B of four, from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Titles written once by the quick thinking model when the first question is sent: root from the question, child from inherited context plus question. Question text shows meanwhile and stays on failure or unset model. Rename always wins. No Retitle.
- Origin strip at the top of every child: parent address chip (jumps to the source), the source (passage, suggested term or visual title, kind not labelled) and the learner's question. Long sources two lines plus Show all.

title: Setup and tutor style: typed effort, empty first run, tutor style
description:
Spec: docs/setup-and-tutor-style-spec.md. Spec A of four (A, B, C, D), from the 2026-11-14 grilling session.

## Decisions so far
- Typed effort only for custom endpoint models; 1-32 letters, digits, - or _; remembered per endpoint and model; endpoint errors surface in the reply and the selection stays.
- Fresh install: no model profile, no default provider; only Send is blocked; Settings shows Not set. Existing installs unchanged.
- Tutor style: learner-editable, stored null until edited, prepended to the fixed safety and media rules; default text drafted in the spec for owner review.
- From /teach: default style teaches only what is needed then checks understanding, with occasional predict-then-reveal. Familiarity-pitched explanations, per-tree mission and citations are later.

- Owner may still edit the default tutor style text.

title: Make npm test fast: no real waits, unit tests where integration is not needed
description:

## What to build

Profile per file (node --test <file>) and fix the slowest first: artifacts (21 s), suggestions (12 s), startup (10 s), videos (5 s), usage, visuals, credential-boundary. Replace real sleeps and polling loops (for example setTimeout(r, 25) waits in the artifact tests) with injected clocks, budgets or awaited events the code already exposes; add an injection option only where none exists. Where a test boots createApp or a Store only to check pure logic, call the logic directly instead.
design: No production behaviour change; new options default to today's values. Same test count unless a test is an exact duplicate (list removed duplicates in a comment). Record a before/after timing table in a ticket comment.

notes:

Replace test sleeps/polling with fixture/Store events and existing detached-job completion promises exposed by createApp.settled (no network endpoint). Reuse provider launch injection with an in-memory peer for suggestion/usage tests; native subprocess tests remain in providers and media. Test build freshness directly after one successful real launcher run, retain real build failure/startup checks, separate migration/launcher/startup test boundaries to keep every file below 2 seconds. title: Test strategy: fast unit tests replace per-task browser verification
description:
Owner request of 2026-11-13. Verification costs too many tokens, too much time and too much CPU per task. Rebuild how the project tests, not only where the files live. This epic runs before the rest of TreeTutor-p1k: the remaining splits (Store, createApp, ChatPage, TreeOverview) need a fast test net first.

Measured at 8b6ea4f:
- npm test: 248 tests, about 20 s wall, 580% CPU, 514 MB peak RSS. Slowest files: artifacts.test 21 s, suggestions.test 12 s, startup.test 10 s, videos.test 5 s.
- scripts/verify: 71 fixture scripts plus 12 live scripts, about 22k lines. Each one builds the app and drives Chromium through agent-browser. 11 fail at HEAD (TreeTutor-cpi), several are flaky under the parallel pool.
- .ralph-tui/prompt.hbs tells agents "Prefer integration checks", and open p1k tickets name 4 to 8 browser scripts each as acceptance.

## Notes

Test tiers, cheapest first. Every ticket uses the cheapest tier that proves its acceptance:
1. Unit (default): plain functions from src/**/*.ts and server modules; no HTTP, no SQLite file, no real timers. Milliseconds per test.
2. Component: React components rendered into jsdom in node --test (harness from this epic). For what is shown, aria, focus and handlers.
3. Integration: createApp or Store in-process with a temp database and fake providers. Only for HTTP, storage and provider-boundary behaviour.
4. Browser (E2E): a smoke set of at most 5 fixture scripts, run by release tickets or by hand. Never acceptance for a routine ticket.
Live-provider scripts stay manual and unchanged.

## Decisions so far

- Unit over integration over E2E (owner, 2026-11-13).
- Smoke set: verify-first-conversation, verify-branch-first, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-settings-window, verify-video-player.
- TreeTutor-cpi (11 failing fixture scripts) is superseded: each script is triaged by its area ticket instead of debugged in the browser.
- Component tests use jsdom (already a dependency) and the esbuild transform vite already ships; no new dependency.

## Fog

- Some browser-only checks (pixel geometry, CSS cascade) will lose coverage. Triage tickets list each one in docs/agents/testing.md so the owner can promote any back into the smoke set.

title: Speed up npm run verify: parallel runs, ignored output, no retries for known failures
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-p1k

## What to build

40 verify scripts write PNG screenshots and result JSON straight into docs/verification/ (411 files, 24 MB, tracked in Git). Every run rewrites them, so each Ralph ticket leaves dozens of changed binaries that get committed or must be restored by hand. Send all verify output to an ignored folder (.verify-output/) by default. Write to docs/verification/ only when VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1 is set, for release or design evidence.

Also make the full suite faster. Today it runs 84 browser scripts one at a time for about 20 minutes. verify-narrated-video-live (180s) and verify-smart-video-live (57s) need real narration or video providers but are not in the live skip set. Scripts that always fail (break-down-ui, compact-chat, different-version, narrated-playback, passage-selection, smart-video-live, video-library, video-recovery in the last run) are each retried once, costing double time.
design:
Add one shared helper under scripts/verify/lib/ that returns the output folder (docs/verification when VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, otherwise .verify-output) and creates it. Replace every hard-coded 'docs/verification' path in scripts/verify/ with it. Add .verify-output/ to .gitignore. Keep the existing tracked files in docs/verification/ as the last recorded evidence; do not delete them. Scripts that compare against a tracked baseline (for example large-map baselines) keep reading the baseline from docs/verification/.

verify-all runs scripts with a worker pool of min(4, cpus/2) by default (VERIFY_JOBS overrides; VERIFY_JOBS=1 restores serial order). Ports are already random (listen(0)). Before enabling the pool, give every script a unique agent-browser session (for example `<name>-${process.pid}`); about 20 scripts have no per-process session name. Print each result line when its script finishes and keep the final table in file order. Add the two *-live video scripts to the live set. For each script that still fails on the commit before this change, fix it if the cause is small, otherwise add it to known with the one-line reason, so it is not retried.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] grep finds no hard-coded docs/verification write path in scripts/verify/ outside the helper
- [ ] Running three verify scripts (for example verify-states, verify-settings-window, verify-video-player) leaves git status clean
- [ ] The same scripts with VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1 update docs/verification/ as before
- [ ] npm test passes
- [ ] npm run verify finishes in under 8 minutes on this machine, with no result change versus VERIFY_JOBS=1 except timing
- [ ] Every agent-browser script uses a per-process session name
- [ ] verify-narrated-video-live and verify-smart-video-live are in the live set
- [ ] Every remaining failure is in known with a reason; npm run verify reports no FAIL rows
notes:
Result (2026-11-13): verified.
- Output: scripts/verify/lib/output.mjs returns docs/verification with VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, else ignored .verify-output/. No hard-coded docs/verification write path left in scripts/verify (only 2 reads of the tracked narrated-video-native-codex.json input).
- verify-states, verify-settings-window and verify-video-player left git status clean. With VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1, states + video-player updated 8 docs/verification files (restored afterwards).
- Pool: min(4, cpus/2) jobs, VERIFY_JOBS overrides. Every agent-browser script uses a pid session. Both *-live video scripts are in the live set.
- known is now a map of script to one-line reason (TreeTutor-cpi). Dropped smart-video-live (now live). verify-visual-sandbox and verify-tree-overview fail intermittently and stay known.
- Decision: verify-all puts an agent-browser wrapper first on PATH. Clicks go to lib/agent-browser-shim.mjs, which retries for up to 5s when agent-browser refuses a click because the control is covered (the map overlay during layout, the main flake under load). Other commands go straight to the real binary, because a Node start on every call made the Tab-loop script custom-endpoint go from 56s to over 300s. Tradeoff: running scripts by hand gets no retry.
- Decision: each script runs in its own process group (detached), and the group is killed on exit. A forked fixture server that outlived a timed-out custom-endpoint run kept stderr open and hung verify-all.
- Fixed load races in verify-inherited-context (it failed even serially), verify-contents-collapse, verify-map-message-jump and verify-visual-themes (the narrow-fit check ran before reflow).
- Timing: parallel full suite 211s and 198s (0 FAIL; 0 and 1 FLAKY). Serial VERIFY_JOBS=1 took 724s with the same pass/known/skip sets, apart from flakes (2 FLAKY plus the visual-themes race, since fixed; passed 3/3 afterwards). npm test: 246 pass, 0 fail. All fixture checks; no live providers.

title: Usage page redesign
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-2li

## What to build

The Usage page shows one range picker driving everything; the total with its input, output and cache read split, which doubles as the chart legend; the chart with a per period / cumulative switch; and one breakdown table that switches between by model and by task, with a share bar per row. Calls without reported counts are shown, never estimated. Same data as today. Matches the Usage mockup.
design: Follow docs/mockups/usage.html within the existing Paperback/Astryx surface. Keep the existing range API, local-calendar buckets, selected-year control and chart keyboard/text alternatives. Place one exact total above a split that doubles as the legend; keep chart and breakdown switches beside their headings. Use one breakdown table with six columns; Calls includes all attempts and labels unreported calls inline. Share bars divide reported row tokens by reported range tokens; unreported-only rows have dashes and zero reported share (no estimates). Pass existing server provider labels from Settings. Hide stale range results while a new selection loads, so total, chart and table always use the same response. Scope: UsageDashboard, Settings caller/copy, usage CSS, browser verification and its related Settings assertion; no storage/API/provider behavior change.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Range, total, chart and breakdown agree for every range
- [x] Breakdown switches between model and task; each row shows its share
- [x] Unreported calls are labelled, never estimated
- [x] Usage dashboard verify script updated and passes in dark and light
notes:
Verified 2026-11-13. Implemented the Usage mockup using the existing range endpoints and accounting helpers. One exact total and measured split now form the chart legend; chart and single model/task breakdown switches sit beside their headings. Six-column table shows reported-token share bars and total calls with unreported attempts labelled inline. Unreported-only counts are dashed with zero reported share; chart announces missing counts without fabricated bars. Selected-year control, calendar ranges, exact hover/focus readouts, arrow/Home/End navigation and expandable values table remain. Existing server provider labels reach Usage through Settings (named endpoint fixture verified). Request selection guards hide stale results during range changes. No API/storage/provider changes or new dependencies.

Decisions/tradeoffs: exact figures rather than compact k values retain precision; shares use only reported tokens, so unreported attempts never imply token usage. Calls include measured plus unreported attempts. Desktop table fits all columns; narrow layout uses the existing Astryx keyboard-scrollable table instead of dropping data. Existing dark/light theme tokens and one-frame design retained.

Validation: npm run build passed (TypeScript plus Vite; existing large-chunk warning). npm test passed. node --test test/usage.test.mjs test/usage-ranges.test.mjs passed. node scripts/verify-usage-dashboard.mjs passed 17 recorded steps, dark/light at 1400x900 and390x844: Today/Week/Month/Year/All time totals and splits agree with per-period/cumulative charts and both breakdown groupings; exact shares, all tasks, named endpoints, previous-year selection/text values, keyboard/hover, desktop fit/narrow overflow containment, delayed response race, unreported-only and empty ranges, zero inference calls. node scripts/verify-settings-window.mjs passed12 steps including page navigation/deep links/focus/Escape and narrow Usage. git diff --check passed.

Evidence: docs/verification/usage-dashboard.json and ten usage-dashboard PNG captures; settings-window.json and updated Settings Usage captures. Production build with real loopback app HTTP/SQLite, seeded usage records and fake providers; no native authentication/inference claimed or required by this issue. - [ ] Role edits save into the active profile

- [ ] Server tests via the HTTP seam cover migration, activate and role routes acting on the active profile

title: Edit, rename and test endpoints
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-2li

## What to build

Each endpoint row offers Test, Edit and Remove. Edit opens inline. Renaming keeps the key, and conversations and profiles follow the endpoint. Changing the base URL requires the key again, so a key never reaches a new host unasked. Each row shows its last test result: the model count and when, or the failure with what to do; a failed test stays until the next test or save. Changing an endpoint aborts its in-flight requests. Matches the Connections page and States in the Settings mockup.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Rename without a key succeeds and keeps the endpoint working
- [ ] A base URL change without a new key is rejected with an actionable message
- [ ] Last test result persists across restarts and shows on the row; failures stay visible
- [ ] Server tests via the HTTP seam cover rename, URL change, test success and failure
- [ ] Custom endpoint verify script covers the edit form and failed-test state
notes:
Result 2026-11-13 (fixture evidence; no live endpoint tested):
- server/openai.mjs: edit({id,name,baseUrl,apiKey?}) keeps the key when omitted but only for the same normalised base URL; otherwise 400 "The base URL changed. Enter the API key again so the saved key is never sent to a new host." Name uniqueness excludes self. test(id) lists models only, stores lastTest {ok,models,at}|{ok:false,error,at} in the owner-only endpoints file (survives restart); a result is dropped if the endpoint changed meanwhile. Adapter replaced (in-flight aborted) only when name/URL/key change, so a test result never aborts chats.

title: Settings redesign, model profiles and custom endpoints
description:
Owner feedback of 2026-11-13, settled in a grilling session. Settings becomes four pages, model profiles swap the three model roles at once, several named custom endpoints replace the single one, question bubbles follow the theme, surfaces follow one frame per object, and the quick thinking model keeps topics broad. Full spec: docs/settings-redesign-spec.md.

## Notes

Visual reference (done, not part of this epic): the mockups in docs/mockups (settings.html with its States section, usage.html, read.html, knowledge.html; the one-frame rule is written at the top of mock.css).

Tests use the existing seams only: the server HTTP seam (createApp with a temporary Store and fake providers, including the fake OpenAI-compatible server) and one browser verify script per UI ticket in the existing scripts/verify-* style, dark and light.

## Decisions so far

- Settings: separate pages Interface, Models, Connections, Usage; Map help and the Vim toggle merge into a Keyboard section.
- Model profile: named model plus effort for chat model default, smart model and quick thinking model. One always active; starts as "Default" from current settings; last one cannot be deleted. Edits save into the active profile. Swapping changes new learning trees, visuals and suggestions; existing conversations keep their model. Missing models fail visibly when used, never fall back. Picker sits at the top of the Models page only. Automatic suggestions on/off stays global.
- Custom endpoints: a list with unique names; inline add/edit; Remove asks for confirmation. Rename keeps the key; a base URL change requires the key again. The existing endpoint becomes "Custom endpoint" and keeps provider id openai; new ones get openai:<stable id>. Names label every model menu.
- Question bubble: always the theme's colour; tint picker removed; saved tints ignored.
- One frame per object: never an outline inside an outline; tone or spacing inside a frame. Learning tree map unchanged.
- Topics: prompt asks the quick thinking model to reuse known topics and keep them broad and few. Existing topics untouched; no merge action.
- Usage: free redesign keeping the same data.

- None known.

title: Knowledge map: topics as translucent regions
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Each topic is drawn as a translucent, labelled region around its concepts, so the learner sees which area is which. The layout pulls concepts toward their topics; a concept in several topics sits between them. No k-means: topics are the clusters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pure test: each concept lies inside the region of every topic it belongs to
- [ ] Region labels sit at region centres and stay readable in light and dark
- [ ] Verify script passes
design: Extend the existing d3-force layout and native concept buttons. Topic memberships define the clusters directly; sorted topic anchors sit on a circle, and each concept is attracted to the mean of its topics' anchors. Fixed anchors reserve centre-label space. Render each region as a padded circle about its anchor, with radius equal to the furthest member distance plus POINT_SPACE. This guarantees every member is inside every assigned topic. Circles may overlap and include nearby nonmembers; avoiding hull/cluster heuristics keeps geometry pure and small. Reuse theme series inks for translucent fills and opaque deep-field labels with primary text for light/dark contrast. Fit includes full regions; membership changes relayout, familiarity corrections preserve the viewport. No dependencies, schema/API changes, k-means or extra features.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure test: each concept lies inside the region of every topic it belongs to
- Region labels sit at region centres and stay readable in light and dark
- Verify script passes
notes:
Verified 2026-11-13. Implemented topic regions in src/knowledgeLayout.ts, src/KnowledgePage.tsx and src/layout.ts. Topic memberships are the clusters: deterministic sorted anchors, attraction to the average of all assigned topic anchors, and collision space reserved at each centre for labels. Each padded circular region encloses every member; shared concepts remain inside every assigned topic. Regions use the existing four theme series inks with translucent fills, behind links/points. Full topic names sit at exact region centres, use primary text on opaque deep-field ground, retain 14px screen size while zooming, and wrap at word boundaries (long tokens can wrap). Fit map includes complete regions; topic-only refresh invalidates layout; familiarity corrections preserve layout and viewport.

Acceptance evidence:
- test/knowledge-layout.test.mjs: all 5 pure tests pass; deterministic with reversed concept/link/topic order, non-overlap with isolated concepts, empty/single, containment including 5-topic membership and a concept with the same name as its topic, topic attraction and shared-concept placement.
- npm test: 253/253 pass, 0 skipped/failures.
- npm run build: TypeScript and Vite pass; existing large-chunk warning only. Final built assets confirmed current.
- node scripts/verify-knowledge.mjs: pass against production Chromium via agent-browser, isolated temporary SQLite Store and seeded graph/provider fixture; no live model calls. Verifies rendered member containment, translucent distinct theme inks, full region fit, centre alignment, no label/point overlap, DOM Range bounds and intact words (not just textContent), fixed screen text size, AA topic-label contrast 15.19 dark / 13.12 light, phone fit at 390px, topic-only membership refresh, and existing keyboard, pan/zoom, correction, merge/failure-retry and persistence flows. Evidence: docs/verification/knowledge-results.json, knowledge-verify-results.txt and updated knowledge*.png captures.
- Impeccable finish review: initial label truncation then split-word issue repaired; final disposition ship scores the sole label finding resolved at desktop and both phone fixtures. Documenter rechecked final styles: ordinary extension, no design-system changes. Detector ran once: existing 16px visual-viewer heading and turn-rail width transition findings only, outside Knowledge changes. Existing stale radius/card-era DESIGN.md/brief/sidecar prose left untouched.

Decision/tradeoff: padded circles intentionally overlap and may include nearby nonmembers; exact membership is authoritative, without k-means or hull heuristics. No dependency/schema/API changes. One browser attempt started before the rebuild completed and hit the stale-build guard; retried successfully only after confirming current assets. Validation is fixture browser + pure/integration tests, not native provider release evidence. Unrelated initial .beads/issues.jsonl changes preserved; no staging, Git commit, push or sync. Commit pending Ralph.

title: Visuals follow the current theme
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Visuals render with the current theme's palette instead of fixed Paperback colours, in both light and dark. Switching theme updates visuals already on screen. Already-rendered videos keep the colours they were made with.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sandbox receives the current theme palette tokens
- [ ] Switching theme recolours a shown visual without regenerating it
- [ ] Server test: the visual prompt palette matches the requested theme
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Sandbox receives the current theme palette tokens
- Switching theme recolours a shown visual without regenerating it
- Server test: the visual prompt palette matches the requested theme
- npm test passes
notes:
Verified result (2026-11-13): visuals follow Paperback, Forest, Harbor, Dusk, Ember and Graphite in light and dark without regeneration; rendered video colours stay baked in.

Decisions / tradeoffs:
- Chat sends the theme name and resolved light/dark Appearance with each turn and reply Retry. Visual worker inputs freeze that metadata with the original request; explicit artifact retries/different versions keep the existing frozen-input contract. Display always uses the current theme independently of this generation snapshot.
- Prompt palette values are read from the existing generated Astryx CSS, using the same light-dark pair format as the theme tests. There is no second hand-maintained palette and no new dependency. Unknown names fall back to Paperback; missing/invalid mode defaults to dark. Only normalized name/mode are stored, and untrusted theme strings never enter the worker instructions or filesystem paths.
- VisualFrame resends its inherited tokens on both theme-name and Appearance changes. The sandbox updates styles in place and dispatches treetutor-theme for canvas/3D redraws. The prompt requires symbolic CSS references and resolving computed colour values for canvas, without resetting controls. Source, iframe and visual state remain intact.
- Video generation/rendering/player code is unchanged. Existing video files are not recoloured or regenerated.

Acceptance / evidence:
- HTTP integration test in test/visuals.test.mjs failed before implementation (no current palette), then passed for all six requested themes and both variants, plus missing/hostile metadata fallback. Expected colours come from built theme CSS, with an explicit Forest series-colour check.
- npm test: 251/251 pass, zero skips/failures; includes the existing real short sandboxed Remotion render smoke test. Focused visual/async worker suite: 17/17 pass. TypeScript check and npm run build pass (existing Vite chunk-size advisory only).
- node scripts/verify-visual-themes.mjs: exit 0. Production build, isolated temporary Store, synthetic provider, real Chromium. All 12 theme/Appearance pairs match host text and series ink in SVG and actual canvas pixels. System Appearance follows emulated OS changes. The same iframe window and script instance, Step 1 control state and saved visual source survive every switch; provider calls remain zero. A real ffmpeg-encoded 0.2-second solid-colour fixture MP4 retains exact HTTP-served bytes and saved metadata across every switch. Narrow 390px layout fits.
- Browser matrix JSON and inspected desktop/light and narrow/dark screenshots: /tmp/tt-visual-themes-Nwts7E/results.json, paperback-light.png, graphite-dark.png, graphite-narrow.png. These are fixture checks, not native model-generation or video-playback evidence.
- node scripts/verify-visual-sandbox.mjs: exit 0 with the original script unchanged. title: Start compaction when the branch form opens
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

Opening the branch form on a passage starts compaction in the background, since compaction never sees the question. Closing the form cancels the run. Submitting reuses the finished or in-flight result, so the child usually goes straight to "Thinking…". If the parent gains a message before submit, the prepared result is discarded and compaction reruns. Every run, including cancelled ones, is recorded in Usage history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: prepare then submit makes exactly one compaction call
- [ ] Prepare then cancel aborts the call; no child is created
- [ ] Prepare, parent changes, submit: compaction reruns
- [ ] Usage history records the quick-thinking compaction calls
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: prepare then submit makes exactly one compaction call
- Prepare then cancel aborts the call; no child is created
- Prepare, parent changes, submit: compaction reruns
- Usage history records the quick-thinking compaction calls
- npm test passes
notes:
Done: compaction starts when the branch form opens.
Server (server/app.mjs): new POST /api/trees/:id/prepare (same anchor body as /branches minus the question; validated by the shared anchorOf helper) starts one quick-thinking compaction per parent, held in the in-memory `prepared` map {key, passage, controller, run}. POST /api/trees/:id/unprepare with the anchor aborts it only if it is for that passage, so a close that races the next form's prepare can't cancel the new run. POST /branches reuses the prepared run (finished or in flight) when key = JSON([compaction prompt, quick selection]) still matches. The prompt includes the parent's messages and the passage, so a new parent message, a different passage or changed quick-thinking settings all discard the run and compaction reruns. Tree delete and shutdown abort prepared runs. The compaction body is split into compact(prompt, quick, controller); startCompaction(child, ..., reuse) adopts the run's controller, so Stop/delete on the child still abort it.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx): an effect keyed on the branch parent and anchor (not the question) posts prepare on open and unprepare on cleanup. Cleanup after submit does nothing because /branches already took the entry.
Defaults: one prepared run per parent (a new form replaces it). A failed prepared run is never reused: reopening or submitting runs again. The tradeoff is one extra quick-thinking call after a failure, in exchange for a fresh attempt instead of a guaranteed failed child. Prepare errors are ignored on the client; submit reports them.
Evidence (fixtures, synthetic provider): test/branch.test.mjs new HTTP test covers: prepare+submit = exactly 1 compaction call and the child gets that snapshot; the compaction text has no question; cancel aborts the call and creates no child; closing another passage does not cancel; a parent message before submit aborts the prepared run and reruns it with the new message; /api/usage records all 4 compaction calls, cancelled ones included. npm test 241/241 pass; tsc clean.
Browser (fixture): new scripts/verify-branch-prepare.mjs PASS (form open starts compaction, Escape aborts it with no child, reopen+submit reuses the run, 2 calls both in Usage). verify-branch-first, verify-branch-streaming, verify-passage-popup, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-first-conversation all PASS. verify-compaction-retry was updated for the extra form-open call (failures 3, compactions 4) and PASSes. verify-visual-branch now counts tutor turns separately from form-open compaction and PASSes. Before this change (HEAD baseline): verify-passage-selection fails (element outside viewport) and verify-suggestion-branching fails (still expects a failed branch to create no child, obsolete since got.6). verify-chat-management and verify-passage-corrections are flaky on HEAD and still flaky here.

description:
## Parent

## What to build

If compaction fails, the child stays open with an inline error explaining what failed and a Retry button. Retry runs compaction again and then answers the learner's question. The child is never silently answered without inherited context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: a failing fake compaction leaves the child saved, no tutor reply, and an error status readable from the child

- Retry endpoint or action reruns compaction then the reply; a second failure shows the error again

- npm test passes
notes:
Done (compaction failure keeps the child with Retry).
Server (server/app.mjs): extracted quickFor/compactionPrompt/startCompaction from POST /branches (same behaviour). A failed compaction stays in the compactions map with its error. GET /api/trees/:child returns compaction {status:'compacting'|'failed', error} while the snapshot is still '' (if no entry exists, e.g. after a restart: failed, 'context was not prepared. Retry to prepare it again.'). The child's first send still streams the compaction error as a failed empty reply, and the tutor is never called. Later plain sends return 409 (use Retry). POST /retry on a child with a failed or lost compaction rebuilds the prompt from the parent as it is now plus the saved passage, picks quick thinking again from the child's provider/model, starts compaction and then streams compacting -> thinking -> reply. A repeat failure shows the error again. A missing parent gets 409.
Defaults/tradeoffs: Retry reads the parent's current messages rather than the original snapshot input (the prompt isn't stored, and this also works after a restart). quickFor's 502 text no longer says 'Focused chat not created' because it is shared with Retry.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx): the failed-reply status line shows tree.compaction.error plus 'The focused chat is kept; no reply was written without its context.' next to the existing Retry reply button.
Evidence (fixture provider, no live inference): new HTTP test in test/branch.test.mjs checks a failed compaction (child saved, compaction.error readable on GET, no tutor call, empty failed reply), a 409 on a plain send, a second failure via retry, a successful retry (compacting<thinking<answer, snapshot received) and deleting a failed child. npm test: 240/240 pass. Browser: new scripts/verify-compaction-retry.mjs on the built UI PASS (inline error x2 with Retry, then answer). scripts/verify-branch-first.mjs still PASS.

title: Branch first: open the child at once, then compact (happy path)
description:
## Parent

## What to build

Submitting a branch question opens the child conversation immediately, showing the passage and the learner's question bubble, with a status line "Compacting parent context…", then "Thinking…", then the streaming reply. The waiting time is the same, but nothing appears frozen. The child row and branch are saved before compaction finishes; its inherited context is filled in once compaction completes and is fixed from then on. The composer stays locked until the reply starts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: POST branches returns the child before a held fake compaction finishes; the child is listed in /api/state
- [ ] The child's first reply starts only after compaction finishes and receives the compacted inherited context
- [ ] Stream or state shows a compacting status before thinking/streaming

- Verify script or manual check: the child opens within one frame of submit and shows the status line sequence

notes:
Done (branch-first, happy path).
Server (server/app.mjs, store.mjs): POST /branches validates as before (anchor, parent model/effort, quick-thinking selection), builds the compaction prompt from the parent at that moment, saves the child + branch row with snapshot '' and returns 201 at once. Compaction runs detached in an in-memory map `compactions` (child -> {controller, done, settled, error}); store.compacted() writes the snapshot only WHERE snapshot='' (fixed once). /api/state lists `compacting` child ids. The child's messages stream sends saved -> status "compacting" -> (awaits compaction) -> status "thinking" -> reply; the reply receives the reloaded branch with the compacted snapshot. Stop/delete/shutdown abort the compaction. Parent is no longer active during compaction.
Defaults chosen: '' as pending-snapshot marker (no schema migration; column is NOT NULL). Failure path minimal until TreeTutor-got.7: child kept, its first reply fails with "Context preparation failed. <reason>..."; a child left with '' and no running compaction (e.g. after restart) gets 409 on send. got.7 adds Retry.
Client (src/ChatPage.tsx, turn.ts): submitBranch opens the child from the POST response (no extra GET), then sends the question and refreshes concurrently; reply bubble shows "Compacting parent context…" / "Thinking…" from status events; composer stays locked (active) until the reply ends.

Existing tests updated via test/branch-first.mjs compacted() helper (branch, chat-defaults, credential-boundary, openai, visual-branch); old 502-on-compaction-failure assertions now assert kept child + failed first reply. npm test: 232/232 pass (twice).
Browser: new scripts/verify-branch-first.mjs (built UI, held fake compaction) PASS x4: child opens 20-25 ms after submit (branch POST 6-9 ms, rest is React mounting the chat, i.e. the first paint after the response), status lines Compacting parent context… -> Thinking… -> Focused answer., composer locked while waiting, snapshot filled after release. Tradeoff: no optimistic client-side placeholder child; strict <16.7 ms would need one. scripts/verify-passage-popup.mjs: removed its old "compaction failure keeps popup, no branch" step (behaviour replaced; got.7 should add failure checks) -> PASS. Also PASS: verify-first-conversation, map-identity, subtree-folding, branch-streaming, inherited-context, keyboard-journey (flaky once), contents (flaky once). verify-passage-selection fails identically on a HEAD baseline build (viewport click), unrelated. title: End the turn when the reply text ends, not when visuals finish
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-got

## What to build

While a visual or diagram is still generating, the learner can already act: Responding clears, suggestions are picked, and branching works. The server sends done and removes the tree from active as soon as the reply text is complete, then lets visual jobs finish on their own. The focused chat shows each pending visual with its own progress in place and swaps in the result (or failure card) when its job ends, without a reload. Suggestions ignore visual and video content.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Server HTTP test: with a visual job held open by a fake provider, the message stream ends with done, the tree is not in active in /api/state, and POST branches does not return 409
- [ ] Suggestions run before the held visual finishes
- [ ] When the held visual is released it becomes ready and the client view shows it without a reload (verify script or state-polling test)
- [ ] A visual that times out after the turn ended shows its failure card; the reply stays completed
- [ ] npm test passes
acceptance_criteria:
- Server HTTP test: with a visual job held open by a fake provider, the message stream ends with done, the tree is not in active in /api/state, and POST branches does not return 409
- Suggestions run before the held visual finishes
- When the held visual is released it becomes ready and the client view shows it without a reload (verify script or state-polling test)
- A visual that times out after the turn ended shows its failure card; the reply stays completed
- npm test passes
notes: Done 2026-11-13. server/app.mjs: per-reply visual queue (still max 3) now starts each visual through startDrawing(artifact, streamSignal), the detached job runner used by Retry. The message stream no longer waits for visual jobs: done is sent and the tree leaves active when the reply text ends. Stop during streaming still cancels pending visuals (cancelVisuals plus the parent-signal abort); after done, only delete or shutdown stop them. Detached jobs show up in /api/state videos, so the existing ChatPage polling (1.5 s tree refetch) swaps in ready or failed cards without a reload. Suggestions already get only the stripped reply text. Tradeoff: no new per-visual progress UI; the existing pending shimmer is reused. Evidence (fixtures, no live provider): new test/visual-detach.test.mjs (held visual: stream ends with done, tree not active, state.videos holds the tree, branches returns 201, suggestion call made before release with no visual content, release becomes ready via polling; timeout after done gives failed + "timed out" while the reply stays completed). It hangs against HEAD app.mjs. Two visuals.test.mjs tests now wait for the visual to settle after done. npm test 236/236 passed; build OK; scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs (fixture) all PASS, including Stop aborting workers.
