title: Smoother tutoring flow, themes and knowledge map
description:
Owner feedback of 2026-11-13, settled in a grilling session. Make the tutoring flow feel smoother (no waiting on branches or visuals), fix requests shown as raw text, fix children that lose track of their passage, and give the app rounder corners, predefined themes and a knowledge map.

## Notes

Tests use the existing seams only: the server HTTP seam (createApp with a fake provider and a temporary Store, as in the branch and visuals tests), pure module tests (layout, theme tokens), and one browser verify script per UI item in the existing scripts/verify-* style.

## Decisions so far

- Visuals and diagrams get 300 s; video composition gets 600 s. Render and narration budgets already scale with length and stay.
- A turn ends when the reply text ends. Visuals generate in place on their own; they never hold Responding, suggestions or branching.
- Compaction sees each visual or video only as "[Visual: title — description]" so the learner can ask about it in a child; never its code.
- The child's system prompt says its first learner message asks about the passage ("this"/"it" mean the passage) and to explain it even if the parent skipped it. Compaction keeps the sentences around the passage in detail and compresses the rest.
- The request parser accepts the fenced form and the tag-style form (<treetutor-visual>{json}</treetutor-visual>, same for diagram and video), tolerating stray quotes or spaces in the opening tag. Unreadable JSON shows the existing "request could not be read" card with Retry, never raw text. The prompt still asks for the fence.
- Branch first: the child opens at once with passage and question; a status line goes "Compacting parent context…", "Thinking…", then streaming. Compaction failure keeps the child with an inline error and Retry.
- Compaction starts when the branch form opens (it never sees the question); closing the form cancels it; submit reuses it.
- New chat saves nothing until the first send. Existing empty learning trees are removed once at startup.
- Contents collapses with a left chevron at its top-left into a thin rail with a right chevron; saved per browser.
- Clicking any question or reply bubble in a conversation node opens that message at the top of the focused chat. The focused chat gets a right-edge turn rail with one tick per learner question.
- Radii: inner 6 px, element 8 px, container 12 px, page 16 px, chat bubbles 16 px, pills stay full.
- Themes (glossary: Theme, separate from Appearance): Paperback (default), Forest, Harbor, Dusk, Ember, Graphite, each light and dark; picked from swatch cards in Settings → Interface; saved per browser; bubble tint uses the theme's inks; visuals receive the theme palette; rendered videos keep their colours.
- Knowledge view becomes a pannable, zoomable force-layout map: concept points with familiarity rings, concept link lines, topics as translucent labelled regions (no k-means), concept labels hidden when zoomed out, existing detail panel on click.

- TreeTutor-got.16: Ember (terracotta/gold) and Graphite (gray/cobalt), both light/dark, are implemented and verified: full tests/build, token parity/AA and production browser swatch/application/reload/tint/Appearance/narrow checks pass; six new theme captures retained.

## Fog

- The owner's 9router/opencode proxy appears to inject its own coding-agent system prompt; TreeTutor cannot control it and was not inspected.

comments.text: Decisions so far — TreeTutor-got.15: Harbor (slate/teal) and Dusk (plum/violet) reuse the existing theme picker with both variants, Paperback default, existing tint slots and house geometry. All 246 tests, build, theme freshness, picker/Appearance browser checks pass; production UI evidence uses isolated fixtures. Implementation commit remains pending with Ralph.

title: Conversation addresses and branch family inks
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-y36 (spec: the redesign mockup and its surface contract)

## What to build

Every conversation in a learning tree has an address: the trunk is 1, its children 1.1, 1.2, and so on down (1.1.2). Each first-level branch family takes one series ink in order (amber, leaf, rust, lichen, then repeats) and every descendant keeps its family's ink; the trunk wears paper. On the current screens, the passage underline and its address chip, the branch line on the map and the conversation node band all show the family ink. Address and ink come from one shared pure function with a test, so every later screen reads the same answer. Mockup screens: Read and Map.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A test covers addresses and inks for a trunk, more than four families (ink repeats) and deep descendants.
- [ ] Addresses stay stable when a sibling is added after them, and the order rule for siblings is written down in the GLOSSARY.
- [ ] Passage underline, address chip, branch line and node band of one family share one ink.
- [ ] Matches the named mockup screen in both the dark default and the light appearance.
- [ ] Text and controls meet WCAG AA contrast in both appearances; every control is keyboard reachable with a visible paper-coloured focus ring.
- [ ] No current label, action or failure state is lost.
- [ ] npm test and npm run build pass; existing verification scripts that touch this surface are updated and pass; dark and light screenshots saved under docs/verification.
notes:
Result (2026-11-12): conversationAddresses(trees) in src/treeList.ts is the one pure source of address + family ink (0 = trunk/paper, 1-4 = series ink cycling amber, leaf, rust, lichen); inkStyle(ink) sets --ink/--ink-on. Siblings are ordered by created then id, so a later sibling never renumbers earlier ones (GLOSSARY: Address, Branch family; deleting a branch renumbers its later siblings).
- Read: explored passage underline wears --ink; an aria-hidden address chip (sup.passage-address) follows the underline as a sibling with zero-width atomic data-o/data-e, so selection offsets, highlights and u.textContent are unchanged. The explored aria-label now ends ", <address>".
- Map: the conversation node header is a full-width ink band (node-band) with the address; branch lines and the focused branch take the family ink (focused branch is still wider). Trunk band = paper.
- Decisions/tradeoffs: inside a node band the focus ring uses --ink-on (paper-ink on the trunk band), because a paper ring would vanish on the paper trunk band, the same rule the mockup uses for the shell band. The address text is full opacity because amber light at 0.8 opacity measured 4.31:1 (<AA). Band ink-on vs ink measured AA 5.71-16.1 in both appearances.
Evidence (fixtures, built app, agent-browser): npm test 217/217 pass (new: tree-list addresses/inks incl. 5 families, deep descendants, later siblings; markdown chip/ink/offsets). npm run build passes. verify-map-identity updated (ink/address assertions, Read check) and passes; screenshots docs/verification/map-reference-{dark,light}.png and read-inks-{dark,light}.png. verify-canvas-positions updated (ignores chip text in prefix counts) and passes. title: Paperback Series redesign (Seasonal Inks)
description:
Bring the shipped app to the Paperback Series redesign, Seasonal Inks colourway, chosen by the owner on 2026-11-12. The static mockup of every screen and component lives in docs/mockups/ (open index.html; tick Component labels to see each part's name). The direction contract is .impeccable/surfaces/docs-mockups-index-html.md.

## Notes

A learning tree is a volume. The trunk wears paper; each first-level branch family takes one series ink (amber, leaf, rust, lichen, repeating), shared by its passage underline, address chip, branch line and conversation node band. Conversations carry addresses (1, 1.1, 1.1.2). Leaf green is the only action colour, paper is focus, rose red is failure only. The reply owns the centre. No behaviour is removed.

## Decisions so far

- Phase label reuses phase:ui-refresh.
- The shared foundation (theme tokens, fonts, addresses and inks, the shell band) lands before any screen.

## Fog

- No model context-window size exists today; the contents context meter needs one (see its ticket).
notes:
Contents context-window source (TreeTutor-y36.5): use native per-model runtime metadata, not a guessed static alias table. Claude: a single entry in result.modelUsage supplies contextWindow (server/claude.mjs); Codex: thread/tokenUsage/updated.tokenUsage.modelContextWindow (server/codex.mjs). The server accepts only positive safe integers and records the limit on the completed reply with its provider and resolved model (messages.usage JSON, no schema migration). Numerator is the last completed tutor call input + cacheRead + output, not cumulative cost or suggestion/media usage. Display is explicitly Last completed reply. Missing count is unavailable; missing/ambiguous limit or a different current provider/model means measured tokens only, no percentage or bar. Tradeoff: historical replies and custom endpoints without reported window metadata remain tokens-only until a matching measured reply; native session compaction, unsent text and future prompt overhead are not predicted. Protocol-shaped fixture coverage exercises both CLI adapters and SQLite/HTTP persistence; this is not a fresh native-provider evidence claim.
Finish review verdict (TreeTutor-y36.12, 2026-11-13): SHIP after two fix rounds. Fixed: the docked map refits untouched maps with a 75% floor, and the Knowledge/Videos column alignment and outlined secondary buttons. Skipped findings (reasons accepted by the reviewer): top-down orthogonal map, Contents on Map and Read-address return (PRD map behaviour, y36.7); Settings small-caps, segmented Appearance and swatch row (y36.9 review); root heading (not a defect); 'Saved' label (y36.3 decision) and composer hint (removed pre-redesign). DESIGN.md rewritten from the build; shipped contract .impeccable/surfaces/index-html.md now Paperback; 0 shipping rasters. Record: docs/verification/finish-review.md.

title: Visual identity redesign
description:
## Problem Statement

The learner finds TreeTutor unattractive to spend time in. The workspace is grey on grey: no accent color and no identity, so nothing tells the eye where to look. The focused chat is a tall white column with messages pushed to the bottom and a large empty area above them. Conversation nodes are plain white boxes joined by thin grey branch lines that barely read. The learning tree sidebar is mostly empty, with a lone settings gear at its foot and a visible "React Flow" watermark on the map. Reply metadata such as provider, model and token counts is visually noisy. Dark mode is the stock neutral grey. The result reads like a generic admin panel rather than a place to think, even though the product is used for long sessions of reading and asking.

## Solution

Give TreeTutor a complete new visual world, chosen through Impeccable's direction round and applied to every screen at once, while every existing behavior keeps working.

- The learner opens TreeTutor and lands in a dark workspace that feels made for thinking: long tutor replies are comfortable to read, and the learning tree map is recognisable at a glance as TreeTutor.
- The learner can switch Appearance between Dark, Light and System in Settings; both modes are designed, not inverted.
- Layout and structure may change where the chosen direction calls for it, but every flow the learner relies on today (branching from a passage, map navigation, folding, keyboard and Vim access, model switching, saving and restoring, media, suggestions, the knowledge graph) still works the same way.
- Copy buttons, search across learning trees, a map overview (minimap) and Markdown export of a learning tree are included only when the chosen direction calls for them; the direction contract states which.

## Direction contract

Pending. The first step of this epic is the Impeccable direction round, run with the owner present: seven candidate worlds from the learner's cultural world, the `concept-seed` roll, and the decision page where the owner picks. The chosen direction is recorded here (and in the Impeccable surface brief) as THESIS, OWN-WORLD, STORY, FIRST VIEWPORT, FORM and FINISH blocks, followed by a per-screen rule list and the list of optional features the direction adopts. No screen ticket starts before this section is filled.

Pinned inputs the roll must respect:

- Success: "a place to think" first; a recognisable learning tree map second.
- Feels wrong: childish or gamified; generic SaaS dashboard; neon hacker-dark; decoration that competes with reply text; cramped or tool-dense.
- Dark is the default appearance; light is designed with equal care.
- Astryx stays the component library; the world ships as a custom Astryx theme.
- Bubble tint presets stay as a feature, with presets re-derived from the new palette.
- Figtree and the current neutral palette are not pinned.

## User Stories

1. As a learner, I want TreeTutor to open in a dark appearance by default, so that long evening sessions are comfortable without configuration.
2. As a learner, I want an Appearance setting with Dark, Light and System, so that I can choose how TreeTutor looks.
3. As a learner, I want my Appearance choice to persist in this browser, so that I do not have to pick it again after a reload.
4. As a learner choosing System, I want TreeTutor to follow my operating system's light or dark preference, so that it matches my other apps.
5. As a learner, I want light mode to feel as deliberately designed as dark mode, so that neither choice looks like an afterthought.
6. As a learner, I want long tutor replies set in comfortable reading type with a sensible line length, so that I can read for a long time without strain.
7. As a learner, I want my questions and the tutor's replies to be clearly distinct, so that I can tell at a glance who said what.
8. As a learner, I want reply metadata (provider, model, token usage, status) to be present but quiet, so that it does not compete with the reply text.
9. As a learner, I want failed, interrupted and in-progress replies to stay clearly visible, so that I never miss a reply that did not finish.
10. As a learner, I want the focused chat to use its space well when a conversation is short, so that it does not feel like an empty column.
11. As a learner, I want the composer to stay reachable and obvious, so that asking the next question is always one step away.
12. As a learner, I want the inherited context of a child conversation to be presented in the same world as the rest of the chat, so that it feels part of the conversation rather than a debug panel.
13. As a learner, I want diagrams and video cards to sit naturally in the reply, so that media feels like part of the explanation.
14. As a learner, I want Mermaid diagrams to follow TreeTutor's Appearance rather than my operating system, so that a diagram never clashes with the workspace.
15. As a learner, I want the learning tree map to have a recognisable identity, so that I know I am in TreeTutor from a single glance.
16. As a learner, I want branches on the map to read clearly against the canvas, so that I can follow how conversations connect.
17. As a learner, I want each branch to visibly leave its parent beside the message it came from, so that I can see which passage started it.
18. As a learner, I want the focused conversation node to stand out on the map, so that I know where I am in the learning tree.
19. As a learner, I want folded conversation nodes and hidden-branch indicators to remain clear in the new look, so that I know when branches are hidden.
20. As a learner, I want the activity indicator on a replying conversation node to be noticeable but calm, so that I can see work in progress without distraction.
21. As a learner, I want the map controls to fit the new world, so that zoom, fit and the map menu feel part of the product.
22. As a learner, I want no third-party watermark on the map, so that the workspace looks finished.
23. As a learner, I want the learning tree sidebar to feel like navigation through my saved study, not an empty list, so that returning to earlier work is inviting.
24. As a learner, I want the current learning tree to be clearly marked in the sidebar, so that I know which one is open.
25. As a learner, I want rename and delete actions to stay easy to find but unobtrusive, so that managing learning trees does not clutter the list.
26. As a learner, I want the Settings window to share the same world as the workspace, so that it does not feel bolted on.
27. As a learner, I want the Appearance setting to sit alongside the other personal display settings such as question bubble tint, so that related choices are together.
28. As a learner, I want bubble tint presets that suit the new palette in both appearances, so that every preset looks intentional.
29. As a learner, I want the Knowledge page (concepts, topics, concept links and familiarity) in the same world, so that it feels like part of TreeTutor.
30. As a learner, I want dialogs such as delete confirmation to stay clear about what is removed and that it cannot be undone, so that the redesign never makes destructive actions ambiguous.
31. As a learner, I want the model menu and passage prompt box to match the new world, so that every floating surface feels consistent.
32. As a learner, I want suggestion underlines to stay visible but quiet in both appearances, so that they hint without shouting.
33. As a learner, I want text selection and focus outlines to stay clearly visible in both appearances, so that I never lose my place.
34. As a keyboard learner, I want every action that works by keyboard today to keep working after the redesign, so that I can still use TreeTutor without a mouse.
35. As a Vim-bindings learner, I want the optional Vim canvas bindings to keep working, so that the redesign does not break my navigation.
36. As a learner who prefers reduced motion, I want any new motion to respect that preference, so that the app stays comfortable.
37. As a learner on a narrow window, I want the redesigned screens to keep working when chat fills the workspace, so that the redesign does not regress small screens.
38. As a learner, I want my saved learning trees, layouts and preferences to survive the redesign untouched, so that I lose nothing.
39. As a learner, I want copy, search, a map overview or Markdown export only where the chosen direction includes them, so that new features arrive as part of a coherent design rather than bolted on.
40. As the owner, I want one written direction contract and per-screen rules, so that every implementation ticket builds the same world.
41. As the owner, I want every color, type, radius, shadow and spacing value to come from the theme, so that screens cannot drift apart.
42. As the owner, I want reference screenshots of the map and focused chat in both appearances, so that later screens can be checked against them.
43. As the owner, I want a single command that runs every fixture browser check, so that regressions from a redesign this wide are caught immediately.
44. As the owner, I want a final Impeccable finish review across all screens and a rewritten DESIGN.md, so that the shipped world is reviewed and documented.
45. As the owner, I want PRD.md to say that this spec owns look and layout while the PRD owns behavior, so that agents do not treat old layout details as binding.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Scope.** All seven screens: learning tree map (conversation nodes, branches, map controls); focused chat (replies, question bubbles, composer, header, inherited context, diagram and video cards); learning tree sidebar; Settings window; Knowledge page; dialogs and menus (delete confirmation, model menu, passage prompt box); Mermaid diagram theming.
- **Behavior is fixed, look and layout are open.** The direction may change layout and structure, including the shapes delivered by the UI refresh epic (chat-style conversation nodes, hidden-branch stubs, draggable divider, inherited context section, organized message layout), provided every current behavior and every PRD acceptance flow still works.
- **Theme.** The world ships as a project-owned custom Astryx theme authored with the Astryx theme tooling and registered in place of the neutral theme. It carries both appearances. Application CSS uses only Astryx semantic roles and theme tokens; no raw color literals or font family names outside the theme. Fonts are self-hosted, as Figtree is today; no remote font imports.
- **Appearance.** A new browser-stored preference, following the existing per-preference browser storage convention, with values Dark, Light and System; absent value means Dark. It sets the Astryx color scheme for the whole document. Mermaid rendering and the diagram card read the app's resolved appearance instead of the operating system preference. Bubble tint presets resolve per appearance from theme tokens.
- **Map watermark.** Hidden through React Flow's attribution option, which its MIT license permits.
- **Single source of truth.** This spec's Direction contract and per-screen rules are the only design authority during the epic. A ticket that needs a rule not written here edits this spec first, in the same commit. Impeccable's surface brief carries the same direction contract for Impeccable tooling.
- **PRD relationship.** PRD.md gains a short section stating that this spec supersedes its look and layout details (for example the collapsed-by-default sidebar, the control strip composition and node dimensions), while PRD behavior and acceptance criteria stay binding. PRD lines that the chosen direction contradicts are updated in the ticket that changes them.
- **PRODUCT.md** is refreshed before the direction round: it currently describes an early increment and a "quiet light surface", both stale.
- **Optional features.** Copy buttons, search across learning trees, a map overview and Markdown export are not committed. The Direction contract lists which ones the chosen direction adopts; each adopted feature becomes its own ticket with its own acceptance checks.
- **Ticket order.**
  0. Verify runner: one command runs every fixture browser script that needs no live provider and prints a pass/fail summary. Known failures tracked in TreeTutor-wpc are reported, not hidden.
  1. Direction round with the owner (interactive), PRODUCT.md refresh, Direction contract and per-screen rules recorded here, PRD note.
  2. Theme, Appearance setting and dark default.
  3. Learning tree map. Produces map reference screenshots in both appearances.
  4. Focused chat. Produces chat reference screenshots in both appearances.
  5. Learning tree sidebar.
  6. Settings window.
  7. Knowledge page.
  8. Dialogs and menus.
  9. Mermaid theming and bubble tint presets.
  10. One ticket per optional feature the Direction contract adopts.
  11. Impeccable finish review across all screens, fixes, and DESIGN.md rewritten by the Impeccable documenter.
- **Sync guards on every screen ticket.** Links this spec; uses theme tokens only; matches the reference screenshots' type, color, spacing and corner language; attaches its own dark and light screenshots; runs the Impeccable detector on changed files and fixes what it flags; leaves the verify runner green apart from failures already recorded.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test drives the built app the way a learner does and asserts what the learner sees or can do, never component internals or class names chosen for styling.
- **Fixture browser scripts are the main seam.** The existing scripts build the app, use an isolated SQLite store and synthetic providers, and drive Chromium through agent-browser. The new verify runner runs all of them that need no live provider. Every redesign ticket leaves the runner green; where a redesign moves or renames UI, the ticket updates that script's selectors and visual assertions while keeping its behavioral assertions.
- **Appearance gets one new fixture script:** fresh browser storage opens Dark; choosing Light persists across reload; System follows an emulated color scheme preference; Mermaid diagrams and bubble tints follow the app's appearance rather than the operating system.
- **Token lint is one new `node --test` test:** it fails when application source outside the theme contains a raw color literal or a font family name. Today the application source contains no raw hex colors, so the test starts green.
- **Screenshots** use the existing screenshot helper pattern in the fixture scripts and are saved under docs/verification for each screen in both appearances.
- Prior art: the settings window, focused chat layout, chat divider, chat-style nodes and hidden-branch stub scripts from the UI refresh epic; the integration tests under the test directory for server behavior.
- Live-provider scripts are not part of the runner; the redesign does not change provider behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Retrying failed or interrupted replies, and editing or regenerating questions (declined by the owner).
- Any change to provider, storage, branching, inherited context, suggestion or knowledge graph behavior.
- Optional features the Direction contract does not adopt.
- A hosted or desktop delivery; TreeTutor stays a local web app.
- Replacing Astryx or React Flow.
- Fixing TreeTutor-wpc itself; the runner reports it until that bug is closed.

## Further Notes

- Impeccable method: a replacement visual world goes through the direction round (`concept-seed --scope direction --mode operate`) and is code-led because TreeTutor is an Operate surface. Canned aesthetic lanes are avoided; the earlier "study desk, forest green, serif replies" picks were dropped because they match the known AI-default rut of warm paper plus serif.
- The redesign epic follows the UI refresh epic (TreeTutor-u7v) in release order; u7v.11 and TreeTutor-wpc may still be open when it starts.
- Child tickets for steps 2 onward are filed after the Direction contract is recorded, so they can name concrete rules.
notes:
2026-11-10: Direction contract filled in docs/visual-identity-spec.md (Lecture-hall Slate, owner's pick); the 'Pending' wording above is superseded by the spec.

2026-11-11: Visual identity epic complete. All 14 children closed, including adopted copy/search features and finish review TreeTutor-nwx.12. Fresh Impeccable reviewer disposition ship; documenter replaced DESIGN.md + sidecar. Evidence and limits: docs/verification/visual-finish/README.md. Full runner 0 new failures; existing TreeTutor-wpc remains outside scope; no native-provider release claim. Commit pending Ralph; no staging or remote operations.
close_reason: All redesign children verified; finish review ship and design system documented

title: Diagrams fit the panel and open enlarged; videos open large
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-u7v (spec: docs/ui-refresh-spec.md)

## What to build

Inline diagrams scale down to the focused chat width, keep their aspect ratio and are never upscaled past natural size; the fixed-height scroll box goes away. The diagram image is a button: clicking it, or Enter or Space, opens a near full-screen modal with zoom and pan. Videos get an Open large button using the same modal pattern. Mermaid source stays a collapsed section under the diagram, open by default only when rendering fails. Rendering stays in the browser as a sanitized SVG image.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Diagrams fit a slim panel without horizontal scroll and small diagrams are not upscaled
- [ ] Diagram enlarge opens by click and keyboard, with zoom and pan; Esc closes and focus returns
- [ ] Videos open large and play
- [ ] Existing artifact tests still pass
- [ ] npm test, npm run build and astryx doctor --built pass; screenshot evidence recorded
notes: TreeTutor-u7v.11 verified 2026-11-10. Implementation: DiagramCard drawing is a <button class=diagram-open> (img max-width:100%, height:auto, so it scales down to the panel, keeps aspect, never upscales); scroll box removed. Click/Enter/Space opens Astryx Lightbox (hasZoom: zoom and pan). VideoCard adds an "Open large" Button opening a Lightbox video (hasAutoPlay); CSS fills the viewer (92vw x 100dvh-8rem, contain), since Lightbox caps media at natural size. Mermaid source Collapsible unchanged (open only on failure). Fix: focused-chat Escape handler now ignores keys from inside a dialog; before, Esc in the Lightbox also closed the focused chat. Decision: reused the Astryx Lightbox, not a custom zoom modal (less code, focus return built in). Evidence (local fixture server + real Chrome via agent-browser, fixture provider): scripts/verify-diagram-rendering.mjs checks 1-4 PASS: Enter, Space and click open the viewer, Enter zooms (aria-pressed=true), ArrowRight pans, Esc closes and focus returns to the diagram button; desktop and 390px: no card scrolls sideways, every img width <= naturalWidth, wide diagram 332x11 from 1956x65 keeps aspect. Its later selection-drag step ("Ask about selection" never appears) fails the same way on an untouched HEAD copy, so it is pre-existing and outside this issue; the later failure-state and sanitizer checks in that script did not run. scripts/verify-video-player.mjs: all 10 PASS, including that Open large plays the same media at >80% viewport width with controls and Esc returns focus to the button. npm test 162/162 pass; npm run build ok; astryx doctor --built dist: 0 fail, 3 warn. Screenshots: .impeccable/review/diagram-enlarged.png, diagram-narrow.png, video-large.png.

title: Draggable divider between map and focused chat
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-u7v (spec: docs/ui-refresh-spec.md)

## What to build

The fixed focused chat width becomes a draggable divider. It starts at 26rem, is clamped from 22rem to 70% of the workspace, is remembered in this browser and resets to the default on double-click. The divider is a focusable separator adjustable with arrow keys and exposes its value to assistive technology. Map-only and expanded chat modes remain. Hidden on mobile, where the chat stays full width.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pure-seam test: clamp, reset and arrow-key step math
- [ ] Drag, double-click reset, keyboard resize and reload persistence work
- [ ] Map-only and expanded modes still work; mobile unchanged
- [ ] npm test, npm run build and astryx doctor --built pass; screenshot evidence recorded
notes: Verified result (2026-11-10): Draggable divider between map and focused chat. Decisions: custom separator instead of Astryx ResizeHandle because its double-click toggles collapse (spec needs reset) and it works in px with percent bounds resolved once; width kept in rem in src/chatWidth.ts (pure clamp/reset/key math), stored as localStorage treetutor.chat-width, clamped to 22rem..70% of .tree-workspace (ResizeObserver) on render so a narrower window shrinks it without losing the stored preference. Keys: ArrowLeft widens chat 1rem, ArrowRight narrows, Shift x4, Home/End bounds. Divider rendered only when map and chat are side by side (not map-only, expanded or mobile). Checks: npm test 162 pass (new test/chat-width.test.mjs); npm run build ok; astryx doctor --built dist 0 failures (3 pre-existing warns); scripts/verify-chat-divider.mjs PASS (drag, clamp, double-click reset, keyboard, reload persistence, expanded, map-only, mobile); verify-chat-expand, verify-keyboard-journey, verify-focused-chat-layout PASS. Evidence docs/verification/chat-divider.{md,png} and chat-divider-mobile.png. Fixture provider only.

title: Inherited context section in child conversations
description:
## Parent

## What to build

A child conversation's focused chat shows a collapsed, read-only section at the top labelled Inherited from <parent title>. Expanded, it shows the passage, the learner's branching question and the condensed inherited context snapshot as plain text. Root conversations show no section.

- [ ] Section is collapsed by default, read-only, and absent on roots

title: Organized focused chat message layout
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-u7v (spec: docs/ui-refresh-spec.md)

## What to build

In the focused chat, the learner's messages are right-aligned tinted bubbles with no sender label. Tutor replies are left-aligned with no bubble, under a small Tutor · model header, with a capped reading width. Each reply shows text with suggestion underlines, then diagrams and videos, then its status line. The usage line moves to a quiet footer visible on hover and focus-within, always visible without hover. A question and its reply are grouped as one turn, with a larger gap between turns. Passage selection, Ask about selection, underlines, child-branch links and passage corrections keep working.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Layout matches the description on a reply with artifacts, suggestions and usage
- [ ] Streaming, failed and canceled states remain visible on their reply
- [ ] Selection, Ask about selection, underlines, child links and corrections still work
- [ ] Existing chat and branch tests still pass
- [ ] npm test, npm run build and astryx doctor --built pass; screenshot evidence recorded
notes: Done. Decisions: used Astryx ChatMessage name prop for the 'Tutor · model' header (labels the article) and metadata prop for the usage footer; model is the conversation's current modelLabel (messages store no per-reply model; tradeoff: after a model switch older replies show the new model). Removed the ghost bubble around replies so text aligns with header. Turn grouping via ChatMessageList gap=2 plus margin on each later question (CSS only, no wrapper). Reading cap 72ch. title: Hidden-branch stubs on folded conversation nodes

title: Bubble tint presets in Settings
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-u7v (spec: docs/ui-refresh-spec.md)

## What to build

The Interface tab offers about six bubble tint presets mapped to design-system color tokens (accent, blue, green, purple, amber, neutral), readable in light and dark themes. The choice is stored in this browser and exposed as one CSS custom property for the learner's question bubbles. No raw colors and no free color picker.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Picking a preset updates the tint variable immediately and survives reload
- [x] Each preset keeps readable text in light and dark themes
- [x] No raw hex or px values added
- [x] npm run build and astryx doctor --built pass; screenshot evidence recorded
notes:
Plan: add six token-only tint presets to Interface with an immediate preview; store the preset ID in browser storage and expose --question-bubble-tint on the app shell. Default accent, amber uses Astryx yellow background, neutral uses neutral fill. Keep primary text over muted theme fills; verify actual light/dark contrast, selection/reload, keyboard and narrow layout in one screenshot pass. Browser storage failures retain the current-session choice, matching Vim. Full map/focused-chat bubble layouts remain in dependent issues per the UI refresh delivery order. Verify production build, Astryx doctor and relevant integration suite; record evidence, close and export. Preserve initial .beads/issues.jsonl change; stay on master. Ralph owns staging and commit. Ponytail and Matt Pocock workflow skills are not available through installed CLI/tools/skills; use existing spec and Astryx component guidance.

Verified result (2026-11-10): Interface now offers Accent, Blue, Green, Purple, Amber and Neutral as accessible Astryx radio choices with token swatches and an immediate sample question. The browser stores only the preset ID at treetutor.bubble-tint. App-shell --question-bubble-tint exposes the selected theme fill to all descendants; primary text is used on the muted fill. Accent is the default; Amber maps to Astryx --color-background-yellow. Invalid IDs fall back to Accent, and unavailable storage writes keep the new preference for this session, matching Vim. No free picker, new dependencies, raw source colors/px, API/schema changes or bubble layout redesign. Conversation-node/focused-chat adoption remains in their dependent issues per docs/ui-refresh-spec.md.

Evidence: npm run build exit 0 (type check, production bundle and build fingerprint); npm test 149/149 passed, zero skipped; npx astryx doctor --built dist and --built . exit 0, zero failures. Doctor retains font-proof and source-style/component advisories; Figtree is self-hosted through the existing Vite alias. Existing large-bundle advisory only. git diff --check passed; one Impeccable detector pass returned no findings. One-off real Chromium check against production assets and isolated loopback app/SQLite verified all six presets in light and dark, immediate shared-property/preview updates, IDs persisted, native ArrowDown selection and reload restore, unknown-value fallback, blocked-write session retention through Settings close/reopen, and no horizontal overflow at 390x844. Minimum measured question-text contrast was 9.29:1 across 12 combinations (required 4.5:1). Synthetic conversation/provider listings only; no native inference/authentication claim or requirement for this UI issue.

title: Phrase-matched suggestions with the comparison run
description:
## Parent

TreeTutor-u7v (spec: docs/ui-refresh-spec.md)

## What to build

The suggestion model receives each tutor reply once (no word-offset table) and returns only exact terms or short phrases in reading order, plus the unchanged concepts and links: {"suggestions":[{"text":"<exact phrase>","concept":"<optional>"}],"concepts":[...],"links":[...]}. The server anchors each phrase: first occurrence after the previous match; else first non-overlapping occurrence anywhere; else a whitespace-insensitive match; else drop. Matched spans still pass the exact-slice and surrogate-boundary check, and stored suggestions keep exact start/end/text so underlines, branches and corrections are unchanged. Prompt rules: terms or short phrases of one to six words, used but not explained in the reply, relevant to the learner's question; skip terms defined in place, everyday words, the question's own topic and concepts at familiarity 0.8 or higher; prefer low familiarity, then centrality; no count cap; no section headings or sentences. Then run old and new prompts once on about five saved tutor replies from local data and record picks, input/output tokens and dropped-pick counts as verification evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] HTTP-seam test: the suggestion request carries the reply once and no word-offset table
- [x] HTTP-seam tests: in-order anchoring, repeated phrases, whitespace differences, overlaps and unmatched phrases dropped
- [x] Concepts, concept links and usage are still saved; unparseable output still fails the call with usage recorded
- [x] Comparison evidence recorded under docs/verification with picks, tokens and dropped counts for old vs new
- [x] npm test passes
notes:
Plan: (1) HTTP-seam regression coverage for phrase-only requests and anchoring on Claude/Codex; (2) replace offset prompt/table and anchor server-side, preserving exact passage storage/graph/usage; (3) run old and new prompts once per five saved local replies with a native provider, record picks/token usage/drops; (4) npm test, evidence, progress, close/export. Defaults: phrase matching is case-sensitive; whitespace fallback treats runs of whitespace as equivalent and scans for the first non-overlapping match anywhere, per spec. Returned offsets are ignored; stored text always comes from the raw answer slice. No server-side semantic word-count classifier: one-to-six-word/quality rules belong to the prompt. Comparison uses the same model and snapshot inputs for both contracts, without modifying live data. Current source worktree clean except pre-existing .beads/issues.jsonl. Ponytail/Matt Pocock unavailable (empty local plugin caches); Caveman/Beads/RTK/codebase-memory applied. No UI work planned; Ralph stages/commits after response.

All kept spans use raw source text and pass the existing exact-slice/surrogate check; supplied offsets are ignored. Graph, branch, correction, usage and storage contracts are preserved. No server semantic classifier or count cap added.

Acceptance evidence: new HTTP-seam checks were red against the original implementation and pass on both Claude/Codex fake launcher protocols. They cover request carries reply once/no table, occurrence ordering, repeats, earlier fallback, whitespace, overlapping/unmatched/invalid picks, literal regex punctuation, split-surrogate rejection, ten kept picks without cap. title: UI refresh and cheaper suggestions
description:
# UI refresh and cheaper suggestions

## Problem Statement

The learner finds the current workspace confusing and more expensive than it needs to be.

- The learning tree list is hidden. The only way to reach it is a map menu item, and it shares one sidebar with settings, connections and map help, so the list reads like a long chat settings drawer instead of navigation.
- A Learning/Knowledge tab row takes a full row of the screen for a switch the learner rarely uses.
- Settings are scattered in the same sidebar as the tree list, ungrouped.
- Conversation nodes on the map show questions and replies in the same style, so it is hard to tell who said what.
- Folding a conversation node removes its branches and leaves only a small "N hidden branches" line, so the learner cannot see where hidden branches came from.
- The focused chat is not organized: question, reply, artifacts, usage and status are stacked with little hierarchy, and the panel width is fixed.
- Diagrams render at natural size inside a small scroll box, so they do not scale with the slim chat panel and cannot be enlarged.
- Child conversations do receive inherited context, but the learner cannot see what it contains.
- New conversations silently use whatever model the learner's own Claude Code configuration defaults to (for this learner, the most expensive one), and Codex likewise uses the account default.
- The suggestion model is sent every tutor reply twice (once as text, once as a word-offset table) and must return character offsets. Picks with a wrong offset are silently dropped, and the remaining picks often feel random or too long.

## Solution

- A collapsible learning tree sidebar, open by default on desktop, containing only "New chat", the tree list grouped by date, a "Knowledge" entry and a settings gear. The tab row goes away.
- Settings open in a modal floating window with grouped side tabs: Models, Connections, Interface and Usage, redesigned rather than only moved.
- Conversation nodes and the focused chat both read like a chat: the learner's questions right-aligned in a tinted bubble whose tint the learner picks in Settings, tutor replies left-aligned.
- Folded conversation nodes keep a short branch stub per hidden child, leaving from its passage and ending in an eye-slash button that expands the fold.
- The focused chat gets a clear turn structure and a draggable divider that starts slim.
- Diagrams fit the panel width and open enlarged on click; videos get an "Open large" view.
- Child conversations show their inherited context in a collapsed, read-only section.
- Claude defaults to Sonnet and Codex to GPT-6.1 Terra, always sent explicitly and saved on the conversation.
- The suggestion model receives the reply once and returns only exact terms or short phrases; the server finds them in the reply.

## User Stories

### Learning tree sidebar

1. As a learner, I want the learning tree sidebar open by default on desktop, so that I can see and switch between my learning trees without hunting for a menu item.
2. As a learner, I want a collapse button in the sidebar header, so that I can give the map and focused chat the full width.
3. As a learner, I want an expand button pinned at the top-left of the workspace when the sidebar is collapsed, so that I can bring it back in one click.
4. As a learner, I want the sidebar's open or collapsed state remembered across reloads, so that the workspace opens the way I left it.
5. As a learner on a phone, I want the sidebar to open as a drawer from the same button, so that the map keeps the small screen.
6. As a learner, I want the sidebar to hold only "New chat", my learning trees, a "Knowledge" entry and a settings gear, so that it reads as navigation, not a settings page.
7. As a learner, I want my learning trees grouped under Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days and Older by creation time, so that a long list stays scannable.
8. As a learner, I want each learning tree row to show how many branches it has, so that I can see which topics I explored deeply.
9. As a learner, I want the rename and delete actions on a row to appear on hover and on keyboard focus, so that the list is quiet until I need them.
10. As a keyboard user, I want the row actions reachable by Tab, so that hover is never the only way in.
11. As a learner, I want the current learning tree row highlighted, so that I know which tree the map shows.

### Knowledge entry

12. As a learner, I want a "Knowledge" entry in the sidebar instead of a top tab row, so that the workspace gains that row back.
13. As a learner, I want the Knowledge entry to open the knowledge graph as a full view and return me to the learning tree I left, so that visiting it does not lose my place.

### Settings window

14. As a learner, I want the settings gear to open a modal floating window, so that settings never crowd the tree list.
15. As a learner, I want settings grouped into Models, Connections, Interface and Usage side tabs, so that I find a setting by what it is about.
16. As a learner, I want the Models tab to hold the suggestion model choice and the concept-matching cost warning, so that every model decision is in one place.
17. As a learner, I want the Connections tab to hold Claude sign-in status and check, Codex/ChatGPT connect, and the custom endpoint form, so that every provider connection is in one place.
18. As a learner, I want the Interface tab to hold the bubble tint, the Vim canvas bindings toggle and the map help text, so that every look-and-control preference is in one place.
19. As a learner, I want the Usage tab to show today's usage, so that I can watch my spend.
20. As a learner, I want the settings content redesigned with clear section headings and descriptions, so that each tab reads as a designed page and not a moved list.
21. As a learner, I want Esc, a close button and a backdrop click to close the settings window, so that leaving it is obvious.
22. As a keyboard user, I want focus trapped inside the settings window while it is open and returned to the gear when it closes, so that I never lose my place.
23. As a learner on a phone, I want the settings window full-screen, with the side tabs as a list I tap into, so that it fits the screen.
24. As a learner, I want "Help" in the map menu to open Settings on the Interface tab, so that map help is still one click away.
25. As a learner, I want links that used to jump to custom endpoint settings to open the Connections tab with the endpoint form focused, so that those shortcuts still work.

### Bubble tint

26. As a learner, I want to pick my question bubble tint from about six theme presets, so that my questions stand out in a color I like.
27. As a learner, I want the presets to stay readable in light and dark themes, so that a tint never hides my text.
28. As a learner, I want the tint remembered on this browser, so that I pick it once.
29. As a learner, I want one tint applied to both conversation nodes and the focused chat, so that my questions look the same everywhere.

### Conversation nodes on the map

30. As a learner, I want my questions right-aligned in my tinted bubble inside a conversation node, so that I can tell my questions from tutor replies at a glance.
31. As a learner, I want tutor replies left-aligned as plain text inside a conversation node, so that the node reads like a chat.
32. As a learner, I want branch lines to keep leaving from the tutor reply rows they came from, so that the map still shows which passage each branch explores.
33. As a screen reader user, I want each preview row still announced as a question or an answer, so that the new alignment is not the only cue.

### Hidden branches

34. As a learner, I want a folded conversation node to keep one short branch stub per hidden direct child, leaving from the passage that child came from, so that I can see where hidden branches start.
35. As a learner, I want each stub to end in an eye-slash icon button, so that hidden branches are obvious and not a small line of text.
36. As a learner, I want a stub's tooltip and accessible name to give the hidden child's title and how many more conversations are hidden beneath it, so that I know what expanding reveals.
37. As a learner, I want clicking any stub to expand the fold, so that I can reveal hidden branches straight from the map.
38. As a learner, I want "Collapse all", "Expand all" and "Keep current branch" to keep working with stubs, so that existing map controls behave the same.

### Focused chat layout

39. As a learner, I want my messages right-aligned in my tinted bubble with no "You" label, so that the focused chat matches the map.
40. As a learner, I want tutor replies left-aligned with no bubble, under a small "Tutor · model" header, so that I know which model answered.
41. As a learner, I want tutor reply text capped at a comfortable reading width, so that long replies stay readable when I widen the panel.
42. As a learner, I want each reply to show its text with suggestion underlines first, then its diagrams and videos, then its status line, so that every reply has the same order.
43. As a learner, I want the usage line moved into a quiet footer that shows on hover and on keyboard focus, and always on touch screens, so that metadata does not compete with the answer.
44. As a learner, I want each question and its answer grouped as one turn with a larger gap between turns, so that the conversation scans as question-answer pairs.
45. As a learner, I want streaming, failed and canceled states to stay visible on the reply they belong to, so that failures are never hidden.
46. As a learner, I want passage selection, "Ask about selection", suggestion underlines, child-branch links and passage corrections to keep working in the new layout, so that branching is not broken.

### Inherited context

47. As a learner in a child conversation, I want a collapsed "Inherited from *parent title*" section at the top of the focused chat, so that I can check what the tutor was told about the parent.
48. As a learner, I want that section to show the passage, my branching question and the condensed summary, so that I see the full inherited context.
49. As a learner, I want that section to be read-only, so that it matches the fixed snapshot the tutor actually received.
50. As a learner, I want root conversations to show no such section, so that it appears only where inherited context exists.

### Adjustable panel

51. As a learner, I want a draggable divider between the map and the focused chat, so that I can widen the chat for diagrams or videos and slim it for reading.
52. As a learner, I want the focused chat to start slim, so that the map gets most of the screen by default.
53. As a learner, I want the divider clamped between a minimum readable width and 70% of the workspace, so that neither side can disappear.
54. As a learner, I want the divider width remembered on this browser, so that my preferred split stays.
55. As a learner, I want double-clicking the divider to reset it to the default width, so that I can undo a drag quickly.
56. As a keyboard user, I want to focus the divider and move it with arrow keys, so that resizing does not need a mouse.
57. As a learner, I want the existing map-only and expanded chat modes to keep working alongside the divider, so that nothing I rely on goes away.

### Diagrams and videos

58. As a learner, I want diagrams to scale down to the chat panel width, so that a whole diagram is visible in the slim panel.
59. As a learner, I want diagrams never enlarged past their natural size inline, so that small diagrams stay crisp.
60. As a learner, I want clicking a diagram to open it near full-screen with zoom and pan, so that I can read detailed diagrams.
61. As a keyboard user, I want a diagram to be a button I can open with Enter or Space, so that enlarging does not need a mouse.
62. As a learner, I want the Mermaid source to stay collapsed under the diagram and open only when rendering fails, so that source is there when I need it.
63. As a learner, I want videos to have an "Open large" button that plays them in a near full-screen view, so that I can watch generated videos properly.

### Default models

64. As a learner, I want new Claude conversations to use Sonnet unless I pick another model, so that I never pay for the most expensive model by accident.
65. As a learner, I want TreeTutor to ignore my own Claude Code default model, so that my coding setup does not change my tutoring cost.
66. As a learner, I want new Codex conversations to use GPT-6.1 Terra when my account lists it, so that Codex starts on a sensible model.
67. As a learner whose Codex account does not list GPT-6.1 Terra, I want the account default used and a note under the model picker, so that I know why the default differs.
68. As a learner, I want the model picker to show the model a conversation will actually use from the start, so that what I see is what I am billed for.

### Suggestions

69. As a learner, I want the suggestion model sent each tutor reply only once, so that suggestions cost fewer input tokens.
70. As a learner, I want the suggestion model to return only the exact terms or short phrases it picked, so that it outputs less.
71. As a learner, I want TreeTutor to find each picked phrase in the reply itself, so that a correct pick is never lost to a miscounted offset.
72. As a learner, I want a phrase that appears several times anchored to the occurrence the model listed in reading order, so that the right mention is underlined.
73. As a learner, I want a phrase that differs from the reply only in whitespace still found, so that line breaks do not drop good picks.
74. As a learner, I want picks the reply does not contain dropped, so that underlines always match real text.
75. As a learner, I want suggestions limited to terms or short phrases of one to six words, so that underlines are never whole sentences or sections.
76. As a learner, I want suggestions to pick terms the reply uses but does not explain, that matter for my question, so that underlines point at real gaps.
77. As a learner, I want terms the reply defines in place, everyday words, the topic of my own question and concepts I already know well skipped, so that underlines are not noise.
78. As a learner, I want low-familiarity concepts preferred, so that suggestions follow what I actually do not know.
79. As a learner, I want no fixed cap on the number of suggestions, so that a dense reply can still get every useful underline.
80. As a learner, I want concept and concept-link extraction for the knowledge graph to keep working, so that familiarity keeps updating.
81. As a learner, I want evidence that the new suggestion format costs less and picks better on my own saved replies, so that the change is proven and not assumed.

## Implementation Decisions

### Delivery order

One Beads epic with eleven tasks, implemented in this order: default models; phrase-matched suggestions with the comparison run; sidebar and tree list; settings window; bubble tint; chat-style conversation nodes; hidden-branch stubs; focused chat layout; inherited context section; draggable divider; diagram and video enlarge. The two cost fixes go first. Bubble tint precedes the two chat-style tasks that use it. The rest are independent of each other.

### Default models

- The Claude provider always passes a model to the CLI. When a conversation has no stored model, it passes the provider's default (`sonnet`), so the learner's Claude Code configuration never chooses the tutoring model. The Claude model list stays Opus, Sonnet and Haiku; Fable is not added.
- The Codex provider's default is `gpt-6.1-terra` when the account's model list contains it; otherwise the account default from the model list. The models response flags the fallback so the picker can show a note.
- A new conversation stores the resolved default model at creation, so the stored model, the picker and the billed model agree. Existing conversations with a null model resolve the same default on their next reply.
- The suggestion model setting and its own cheap-model defaults are unchanged.

### Suggestions

- The suggestion request sends the reply once. The word-offset table is removed from the request.
- Output contract: `{"suggestions":[{"text":"<exact phrase>","concept":"<optional>"}],"concepts":[...],"links":[...]}`. No offsets. Suggestions are listed in reading order. Concepts and links are unchanged.
- The server computes offsets. For each phrase in order:
  1. find the first occurrence at or after the end of the previous match;
  2. otherwise the first occurrence anywhere that does not overlap an earlier match;
  3. otherwise a match that treats any run of whitespace in the phrase as any run of whitespace in the reply;
  4. otherwise drop it.
  A matched span must still pass the existing exact-slice and surrogate-boundary check before it is kept. Stored suggestions keep their exact start, end and text, so branches, underlines and corrections are unchanged.
- Prompt rules: terms or short phrases of one to six words; used but not explained in the same reply; relevant to the learner's question; skip terms defined in place, everyday words, the question's own topic and concepts at familiarity 0.8 or higher; prefer low familiarity, then centrality. No count cap. Numbered section headings and whole sentences are no longer picked.
- Unparseable output still fails the call. Individually unmatched or overlapping phrases are dropped. Usage is still recorded on success and failure.
- A one-off comparison runs the old and new prompts on about five saved tutor replies from local data and records picks, input and output tokens and dropped-pick counts as verification evidence.

### Sidebar, tree list and Knowledge

- The top Learning/Knowledge tab row is removed. Knowledge becomes a sidebar entry that opens the knowledge graph as a full view in the workspace; leaving it returns to the previous learning tree.
- The sidebar is open by default above the mobile breakpoint, collapsed by default below it, and its open state is stored in browser storage like the existing Vim preference.
- Settings, Connections and map help leave the sidebar. The map menu's "Learning trees" item becomes the sidebar toggle; "Settings" and "Help" open the settings window.
- Tree list grouping uses the stored creation time of root learning trees. Group boundaries are calendar days in the learner's local time. Branch count is the number of descendant conversations, derived from data already loaded. No schema change.
- A small pure module provides grouping and counting so it can be tested without a browser.

### Settings window

- A modal dialog component from the design system, large on desktop and full-screen on mobile, with vertical side tabs.
- Tabs and contents: Models (suggestion model settings, concept-matching cost warning); Connections (Claude sign-in status and check, Codex/ChatGPT connect, custom endpoint settings); Interface (bubble tint, Vim canvas bindings, map help); Usage (today's usage).
- Existing settings components are reused inside the tabs and restyled; their behavior and API calls do not change.
- The window can open on a given tab with a given control focused. Existing shortcuts to custom endpoint settings open Connections with the endpoint form focused.

### Bubble tint

- About six presets mapped to design-system color tokens (accent, blue, green, purple, amber, neutral). No raw colors and no free color picker.
- Stored in browser storage. Applied through one CSS custom property consumed by both conversation nodes and the focused chat.

### Conversation nodes

- Preview rows keep chronological order. Question rows align right in the tint bubble; reply rows align left. Per-message branch handles stay on the reply rows. Screen-reader "Question:"/"Answer:" prefixes stay.

### Hidden-branch stubs

- Folding stays per conversation node and still hides every descendant.
- A folded node renders, for each hidden direct child, a short edge from that child's passage handle to a small marker node holding an eye-slash icon button. The marker's accessible name gives the child title and the count of further hidden descendants. Activating any marker expands the fold.
- The text line "N hidden branches" is removed.
- Marker computation lives with the existing hierarchy logic and is testable without a browser.

### Focused chat layout

- Uses the existing chat message components. Learner messages: right-aligned tint bubble, no sender label. Tutor replies: no bubble, header "Tutor · model", capped reading width.
- Per reply order: text with suggestion underlines, artifacts, status. The usage line moves to a footer visible on hover and on focus-within, always visible on devices without hover.
- Turn grouping: a question and its reply share a tight gap; turns are separated by a larger gap.
- Selection, "Ask about selection", underlines, child links and passage corrections keep their behavior.

### Inherited context section

- Shown only in child conversations, collapsed by default, at the top of the focused chat message list. Label: "Inherited from *parent title*". Body: the passage, the learner's branching question and the condensed snapshot as plain text. Read-only.
- The conversation response already carries the branch passage, question and snapshot; no API change is expected.

### Draggable divider

- Replaces the fixed chat panel width. Default 26rem. Clamped to a 22rem minimum and 70% of the workspace maximum. Stored in browser storage. Double-click resets to the default. The divider is a focusable separator with arrow-key resizing and correct value attributes.
- Map-only and expanded chat modes remain. The divider is hidden on mobile, where the chat takes the full width as today.
- The clamp and step math is a small pure function so it can be tested without a browser.

### Diagrams and videos

- Inline diagrams fit the panel width, keep their aspect ratio and are never upscaled past their natural size. The fixed-height scroll box is removed.
- The diagram image is a button. Activating it opens a near full-screen modal with zoom and pan. The same modal pattern gives videos an "Open large" view.
- Mermaid source stays a collapsed section, open by default only on render failure. Rendering stays in the browser as a sanitized SVG image; no server-side image step.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests exercise external behavior through the highest existing seam: HTTP requests against the app with fake provider launchers, or exported pure functions. They do not assert component internals, class names or prompt wording beyond the documented contract.
- Seam 1, the HTTP app with fake providers (prior art: suggestion, model and branch tests):
  - new Claude conversations send `sonnet` to the CLI even when the environment's Claude configuration names another model;
  - Codex uses `gpt-6.1-terra` when listed and the account default plus a fallback flag when not;
  - the stored model matches what was sent;
  - the suggestion request no longer carries a word-offset table;
  - phrase-only output is anchored correctly in order, for repeats, for whitespace differences and for overlaps, and unmatched phrases are dropped;
  - concepts, links and usage are still saved;
  - child conversation responses carry passage, question and snapshot.
- Seam 2, pure UI logic modules run under the Node test runner (prior art: canvas, layout and layout-save tests):
  - tree list date grouping across day boundaries and branch counts;
  - divider clamp, reset and arrow-key steps;
  - hidden-branch marker computation for folded nodes, including nested folds.
- Visual and interaction work (sidebar, settings window, tint, bubbles, chat layout, enlarge views) has no automated browser or end-to-end tests. Each such task is checked with the type-checked production build, the design-system doctor on the built output and one screenshot pass, recorded as verification evidence.
- The suggestion comparison run is recorded verification evidence, not an automated test.

## Out of Scope

- A cap or user setting for the number of suggestions.
- Section headings or whole sentences as suggestions.
- Adding Fable to the Claude model list.
- Editable tutor instructions, or any change to how the Claude CLI is isolated.
- An API-key path for Claude.
- Ordering or grouping learning trees by last activity, or any message timestamp schema change.
- Search in the tree list.
- A free color picker or custom tint colors.
- A non-modal or draggable settings window.
- Per-branch folding; folding stays per conversation node.
- Swapping the map and chat sides.
- Server-side diagram rendering.
- Inherited context shown on conversation nodes, or editing it.

## Further Notes

- Domain terms follow the glossary: learning tree, conversation, conversation node, focused chat, branch, passage, suggestion, suggestion model, inherited context.
- The default-model fix addresses a live cost bug: the Claude CLI was falling back to the learner's own Claude Code default model.
- The suggestion change keeps stored suggestion data and branch anchors exactly as they are; only the model contract and the server-side anchoring change.
- UI tasks use the Impeccable skill with Astryx components and tokens, following the project's no-raw-div and no-raw-color rules.

title: Keep growing nodes unobscured and large maps responsive
description:
## What to build

Nodes now grow as their conversations continue. Keep boxes readable: a box that grows must not cover its neighbours, and a map with many long conversations must stay smooth.

## Work order

1. When a visible node's measured height grows into another box, move the covered boxes down by the overlap, each together with its own descendants so subtrees keep their shape. Save the new positions through the existing layout saver; the one-write-per-minute rule is unchanged. Never move the growing node itself or a box the learner is dragging. Write the rule as a pure function beside `placeBox` in src/canvas.ts, with tests in test/canvas.test.mjs.
2. Folded and hidden nodes take no space. Unfolding must not leave boxes covering each other.
3. Bound the cost. Measure with a seeded tree of about 200 conversations with 20 turns each. Keep the preview payload bounded per message. Use React Flow's `onlyRenderVisibleElements` if panning or zooming drops frames. A streaming chunk must not re-render every node.
4. Selecting a tall node still brings it into view beside the chat panel, and Fit tree still works.
5. Add a seeded fixture script and record the measured timings, with the machine they were taken on, under docs/verification.

## Start here

PRD.md "Canvas and conversations" (placement and offset rule) and acceptance criterion 5. src/TreeOverview.tsx (placement and reveal effects), src/canvas.ts, src/layoutSave.ts.

## Out of scope

Automatic re-layout of the whole tree, and any new layout preference.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Continue a conversation whose box sits above another box until it would overlap: the lower box and its subtree shift down, no boxes overlap, and the shifted positions persist after the layout interval and a restart.
- Boxes that are not covered do not move, and a box being dragged is never moved by the rule.
- Streaming into one node does not re-render unrelated nodes; record how this was checked.
- On the seeded 200-conversation tree, pan, zoom, fold and open stay interactive; the recorded numbers and machine are in the evidence note.
- Layout writes remain at most one per minute when changed and none when idle.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixtures pass.

title: Show every message of a conversation in its map node
description:
## What to build

Each map node shows its whole conversation: every question and answer in order, each as a compact preview. A long message is truncated with an ellipsis, but no message is left out. This replaces the latest-question and latest-answer preview.

## Work order

1. Server: change `Store.previews` and `GET /api/previews` to return, for each conversation, its messages in order as `{ id, role, text, status }`, with each text cut to a bounded length. Keep the current 512-code-point cut and ellipsis unless a different bound reads better; record the choice. Read from the messages table every time and add no preview table or column. Keep the 500-id request bound.
2. Client: render the list in `Conversation` in src/TreeOverview.tsx. Question and answer rows are visually distinct, each clamped to a few lines with an ellipsis and a screen-reader role prefix. Give every row a stable `data-message` attribute holding the message id; the next task anchors branch lines to it. The node grows with its conversation. Do not add a scroll area inside the node, so the wheel keeps zooming the map.

title: Attach each branch line beside its source message
description:
## What to build

A branch connection leaves its parent box beside the message the branch was created from, rather than from a list of passages at the bottom of the box. New children are placed to the right, level with that message.

2. Re-measure handles with `useUpdateNodeInternals` whenever the transcript changes height: a new message, streaming text, or a fold. Edges must follow their row.
3. Child auto-placement already reads the handle's offset. Confirm new children land level with the source message and that `placeBox` still avoids occupied space. Folding a parent hides its child edges as it does today.
4. Fallback: if a saved branch's message is missing from the node, attach the edge at the middle of the node's right side instead of dropping it.
5. Update scripts/verify-canvas-positions.mjs, scripts/verify-tree-overview.mjs and test/canvas.test.mjs as needed. Record evidence under docs/verification.

title: Open New chat as a visible root that titles itself
description:
## What to build

Replace named tree creation with a single New chat action. Choosing it creates a learning tree at once, with no name prompt, and opens its map showing one root conversation box, with that conversation open in the chat side panel and the composer focused. The root shows the placeholder title "New chat" until the first question is sent, then takes its title from that question, the same way a branch already takes its title from its question. The sidebar entry, the map node and the chat header all update without a reload.

## Work order

1. Server: `POST /api/trees` no longer requires a title; the store creates the root with the placeholder. When the first user message of a root that still has the placeholder is saved, set the title from the trimmed question, reusing the 200-character rule in `Store.branch`. Deliver the new title to the open page through the existing `saved` stream event or the state refresh that follows it.
2. Client: in src/ChatPage.tsx remove the tree-name form, the empty-map Start conversation state and the `started` gate, so the root box is on the map from creation. The sidebar keeps the saved-chat list under one New chat button. Choosing New chat while an unstarted chat already exists opens that chat instead of creating another.
3. Keep layout restore, the three panel modes, narrow-window chat and keyboard access working for an unstarted root. A root with no messages restores after reload as the same box.
4. Update every test and fixture that creates trees by name or expects the empty map: test/app.test.mjs, scripts/verify-first-conversation.mjs, scripts/verify-keyboard-journey.mjs and other callers found by grep. Add a short evidence note under docs/verification.

## Start here

PRD.md "Canvas and conversations" and acceptance criterion 10. src/ChatPage.tsx (`create`, `starter`, sidebar form), server/app.mjs (`/api/trees`, message handler), server/store.mjs (`create`, `list`).

## Decisions already made

The title is the first question's text; no extra model call. One unstarted chat at a time. Existing saved trees keep their titles. Renaming and deleting chats are separate later work.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. acceptance_criteria:

- Choosing New chat again before asking anything returns to the same unstarted chat; no second empty tree is stored.
