title: Board polish: the tutor draws small pictures live on the board, stroke by stroke
description:
Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bpl.9.html

## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

The tutor can make a drawing: a few SVG paths it writes inline, drawn stroke by stroke, in colours the app's theme offers, so the learner watches a picture being made (ADR 0030). Drawings are never taken from the piece library.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `drawing w=W h=H` opens a drawing; `path "d" ink=NAME fill=NAME in DR` adds a path in the drawing's own 0-100 units, scaled into its box; each path is a board item.
- [ ] `ink=` and `fill=` accept only blue, green, pink, yellow, ink and muted, each mapped to the theme's colour tokens; `fill=` may be left out; any other value is a parse error.
- [ ] Path data accepts only SVG path commands, numbers, spaces and commas within a length limit; anything else skips the path and logs it. A drawing takes at most 24 paths.
- [ ] Each path draws its stroke, then fades its fill in.
- [ ] The rendered drawing carries no raw colour values, and it re-tints when the theme changes.
- [ ] The prompt offers drawings, allows these colour names on them only, and asks for about 12 paths.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bpl.9.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: ink= left out draws in ink; path data max 600 chars; default drawing box 600x600; drawing op takes 0 ms (sets the box), a path 450 ms at 1x; colour roles map to --rabbithole-ink-N by the mockup's family lines (blue 1, yellow 2, green 3, pink 4) since the --color-text-<hue> slots hold the lines in another order; page index shows 'dr drawing (N paths)' as the mockup's pages list does.
PR #219 opened; GitHub reports it CONFLICTING with master, so no CI ran. Handed over for the merger to resolve.

title: Board polish: the tutor writes a code block on the board line by line
description:
Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bpl.8.html

## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

The tutor can write code on the board: a code component whose lines arrive one per sentence part, each a board item the spotlight, the pointer, the pen and erase can reach. Code is highlighted with Prism (already in the app) in the theme's colour tokens and keeps its indentation.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `code lang="py" w=W h=H` opens a code block; `line "..." in CB` adds its lines in order; each line is a board item with its own id.
- [ ] Lines keep leading spaces, sit top-aligned in the board's monospace font, and draw in left to right at about a component child's length.
- [ ] Lines are syntax-highlighted in the theme's colour tokens, never fixed colours; an unknown `lang` renders plain.
- [ ] Long lines shrink to a minimum size, then clip with an ellipsis, and stay inside the box.
- [ ] A malformed line, a missing parent or a bad parameter is skipped and logged; the box follows the overlap and off-board rules of other components.
- [ ] The prompt offers the code block and asks for about 12 lines per block and a new page beyond that.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bpl.8.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: code box defaults 900x640; lang is any name matching [\w+#-]{1,20}, default plaintext; unknown to Prism renders plain. A line is a code line only with 'in CB' (a bare line stays a stroke). Line text keeps leading spaces, trailing trimmed; "" is a blank row; strings inside use single quotes (prompt says so, op strings cannot hold double quotes). Block size: largest 30..20 where longest line fits across at 0.6em per char and all rows fit down (baseline+0.2s+36 <= bottom); at 20 long lines clip with …, rows past the bottom are left out and the server skips them with 'no room for ID in CB'. Each line is tokenized alone. Spotlight: a line lights only itself; code panel never dims.

title: Board polish: quiet room tone and pen sounds fill the board's silences
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

While the tutor speaks or pauses within a reply, a very quiet room tone sits under the voice, and a soft pen sound plays while each item draws, so the board never drops into dead silence. Both are made in the browser with no asset files.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Room tone: soft filtered pink noise, about 40 dB below the voice, plays through a reply and fades out when the board waits for the learner.
- [ ] Pen: a soft band-passed stroke sound for each drawn op, lasting the op's draw-first length, about 26 dB below the voice; erase gets a softer wipe about 32 dB below; page, open and pointer make no sound.
- [ ] Muting the board silences both; pausing suspends both; the learner speed changes pen-stroke lengths along with the drawing.
- [ ] No new setting is added.
notes: Fills live in src/board/fills.ts behind streamedVoice (room/pen on Voice). Levels relative to a -22 dBFS voice (prototype's measured mean). The board has no mute control: Web Audio shares the page's output, so a muted tab or system silences room and pen with the voice. Pen keeps its first length when an op is re-squeezed.

title: Board polish: a filler plays when the next sentence's voice is late
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

When the next sentence (or joined group) is due but its voice has not arrived, the learner hears a short filler instead of silence. The board's filler clips grow to include short connectors. The filler before a reply's first audio keeps working as today.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] When the next sentence or group is due and its audio has not started after about 1 s of board time, a filler clip plays.
- [ ] A filler never repeats the one before it, never overlaps a sentence, and the sentence's first audio cuts it off.
- [ ] Fillers never appear in the transcript or in what is stored for the reply.
- [ ] The filler set adds short connectors such as "So...", "Right," and "Mm." in the board voice, cached like the existing ones.
- [ ] The filler before a reply's first audio behaves as before.
notes: Defaults: the board player reports { type: 'progress', sentence, phase: 'late' } once when a sentence after the turn's first is due (after its pause) and its voice is still 'waiting' after 1000 board ms; the session answers with a filler only once the turn's first audio was heard (the first-audio filler keeps its own server timer). Opening fillers stay Hmm./Okay./Good question.; late fillers pick only from the new connectors So.../Right,/Now,/And.../Mm. No silence trimming of clips.

title: Board polish: sentences between pauses are spoken as one stretch of joined speech
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

Sentences between two pauses are voiced as one edge-tts request, so they flow with natural intonation instead of each ending as if it were the last. The first sentence of a reply is still voiced alone so the start is as fast as today. Inside a joined stretch, the caption, the draw-first ops and the spotlight still move on at each sentence, timed from edge-tts word boundaries.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A reply's first sentence is voiced alone.
- [ ] Later sentences are grouped until a sentence carrying a `pause` op, a change in prosody rate, the end of the reply, or 4 sentences, whichever comes first; each group is one edge-tts request, and voicing stays one group ahead of playback.
- [ ] The edge-tts client requests word-boundary metadata and reports word offsets with the audio; the session sends each sentence's start offset inside its group clip.
- [ ] When boundary metadata is missing or a word cannot be matched, offsets are split by each sentence's share of the group's characters.
- [ ] The board starts each sentence at its offset: its caption shows, its ops start with draw-first timing measured to the next offset or the clip end, and the spotlight moves to it.
- [ ] Cutting in during a group stops its audio and drops its remaining sentences; a failed group falls back to captions with estimates.
- [ ] Stored replies keep one line per sentence; replaying a saved board is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: joined text is the sentences joined by one space at the first sentence's rate. Offsets go down as { type: 'offsets', id, ids, at } (ms of audio) only for groups of 2+, sent before the group's audio-end; fallback sends share (fraction of the clip before each sentence) and the player multiplies by the clip length once known. A group with no audio sends audio-end for each of its ids. A joined sentence whose clip ended or failed plays by its estimate.

title: Board polish: the tutor chooses the pauses; the app adds none
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

The board stops adding fixed pauses (the beat after every sentence and the longer pause before a page or component or after a key sentence). The tutor writes a `pause S` line after a sentence, rarely, only where an idea needs a moment; without one, the next sentence follows straight on. A key sentence stays slower in voice but no longer pauses by itself. The prompt takes the prototype's variant B pause wording and asks for natural connectors ("So,", "Okay, now", "Right,") where they fit.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `pause S` is read as an op of the sentence above it, in seconds of board time, clamped to 0.2-2; a malformed pause is skipped and logged and draws nothing.
- [ ] Without a `pause` op the next sentence starts straight after the one before; the fixed beat and the longer change/key pauses are gone.
- [ ] A key `!> ` sentence keeps its slower rate and gets no pause unless the tutor wrote one.
- [ ] A pause counts from the end of its sentence and overlaps any wait for the next sentence; cutting in drops it; the reply's last line gets none; the learner speed scales it; pausing the board holds it; captions without voice keep it.
- [ ] The prompt tells the tutor to pause rarely, after an idea that needs a moment, with the length chosen by weight, and to start sentences with natural connectors where they fit, never on every line; the key-sentence line no longer promises a longer pause.
- [ ] The prompt warns in one line each against a `sequence` message without `on ID` and against escaped quotes inside a label.
notes: pause S is read in scriptSentences (not ops.mjs): it sets sentence.pause in ms (clamped 200-2000), is not saved in board op lines, and the reply's last sentence drops it server-side. A line whose first word is 'pause' is always read as a pause. Prompt example gets 'pause 1' after the key formula and one connector.

title: Board polish: the board draws first, then talks: a sentence's ops finish early in the sentence
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

A sentence's ops start when the sentence starts and draw one after another, each at its own length by size, so the picture lands before the tutor finishes explaining it. They are squeezed to finish within the first third of the sentence's audio (or caption estimate) and never stretched across it. Starting lengths at 1x, from the prototype (tune freely): page/open 400 ms, a component box 900 ms, a component child 400 ms, text/dot/point 250 ms, pointer/erase 300 ms, math 500 ms, box/circle/line/arrow/plot 450 ms.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Ops of a sentence start with the sentence and run one after another at their own lengths.
- [ ] When their total would pass the first third of the sentence, they are squeezed to end there; they are never stretched longer than their own lengths.
- [ ] When the real audio length arrives after the estimate, the ops not yet finished are re-squeezed to it.
- [ ] The learner speed divides every op length; pausing the board freezes drawing mid-op and resuming carries on.
- [ ] A sentence without voice uses the caption estimate the same way.
notes: Op lengths from the spec's drawMs at 1x, converted to board time by /DEFAULT_SPEED so speed divides them. Re-squeeze keeps the entering op's start and refits it plus the rest into what's left of the first third.

title: Board polish: the highlight op is removed and the pointer glides quickly and fades with its sentence
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

The slow grey highlight wash goes: the spotlight is the one way the board shows what the tutor is talking about. The tutor no longer has a highlight op; saved boards that used it still replay. The pointer glides to its item quickly and fades when the sentence it belongs to ends, instead of lingering on its own timer.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The board prompt no longer offers `highlight`.
- [ ] A `highlight` line, new or replayed from a saved board, draws nothing and logs no error, and later ops that name the highlighted item still resolve.
- [ ] The highlight wash and its styles are gone from the board renderer.
- [ ] `pointer` glides to its item in about 250 ms at 1x, scaled by the learner speed.
- [ ] A pointer fades when its sentence ends: when the next sentence starts or the tutor stops and waits, and on cut-in or pause it behaves like the rest of the spotlight.
- [ ] A saved board replays without a pointer left on screen.
notes: Defaults: old highlight lines read as {} (no item, no error); an erase naming a dropped highlight skips that id. Pointer glide 250ms/1.5 board time (board time runs at 1.5x). Passed pointer fades as an erased item over 300ms board time; marked passed on next sentence show, idle (stop/wait) and cut-in; pause freezes it like the spotlight.

title: Board polish: the caption always shows under the board while the tutor speaks
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-bpl

## What to build

The sentence the tutor is saying shows on the caption line under the board whenever the tutor speaks, whether the transcript rail beside the board is open or collapsed. The rail keeps the history. No new component: the existing caption line stops hiding while the rail is open.

Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bpl). Prototype evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] While the tutor speaks, the caption line under the board shows the current sentence with the transcript rail open and with it collapsed.
- [ ] The caption changes when the next sentence starts and mutes when the tutor stops and waits for the learner, as it does today with the rail collapsed.
- [ ] With the voice off, the caption keeps its estimated timing.
- [ ] The transcript rail still lists what was said; the caption never adds to it.

title: Board polish: caption always on, draw first then talk, code and drawings, tutor-chosen pauses and joined speech
description: The caption shows under the board whenever the tutor speaks, transcript open or not. Each sentence's ops start with it at their own pace and finish in its first third, never stretched, so the picture lands before it is explained. New board components: a code block written line by line with Prism highlighting in theme tokens, each line a board item; and a drawing, a few model-written SVG paths in 0-100 units drawn stroke by stroke with ink/fill from the theme roles blue, green, pink, yellow, ink, muted (path data validated at the parse boundary). The highlight op is removed (old lines replay as nothing); the pointer glides in about 250 ms and fades at its sentence end. The app adds no fixed pauses: the tutor writes 'pause S' (0.2-2 s) rarely, and uses natural connectors. Sentences between pauses are spoken as one edge-tts request with word-boundary offsets per sentence; a reply's first sentence is spoken alone, later groups are capped at 4. Filler clips also play when the next sentence's voice is late. Quiet Web Audio room tone and pen sounds fill the silence. Spec: docs/board-polish-spec.md. Evidence: local branch prototype/board-pacing. Decisions in force: ADR 0028, ADR 0029, ADR 0030. The code block and drawing need a mockup before their tickets.

title: Board sketches: the tutor builds a comparison, a message sequence or a labelled equation piece by piece
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

The last three chat sketch kinds come to the board, following the pattern of the first sketch ticket (spec: Sketch kinds as board components). The prompt's sketch guidance gains a comparison, an exchange and a formula.

| Component | Parent | Child |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compare` | `vs="A\|B"`, box | `aspect "name" values="a\|b" in ID`, one value per side |
| `sequence` | `actors="A\|B\|C"`, box | `send "message" by=A to=B in ID`; without `to=` it is a note on its actor |
| `equation` | `"symbols separated by spaces"`, box | `symbol "s" means="…" in ID`, `s` one of the equation's symbols |

An actor not in the sequence, a symbol not in the equation and a compare row without one value per side are invalid. A sentence whose ops draw an `equation` or its `symbol` children gets the slower math rate from the key-sentences ticket.

- Each kind is a board component: the parent op gives its box (`at`, `w`, `h`, default box per kind), and each child op adds one piece `in` it. Each child is a board item with its own id, so `highlight`, `pointer`, `erase`, pen marks and the board pages list reach it.
- The client lays every kind out from all its children drawn so far, as it does for flow, tree, table and Venn: a new child reflows the earlier ones inside the box with animation (the reduced-motion fade otherwise). Pieces stay inside the box; past about eight children they shrink to a minimum size rather than overflow.
- Board style, chat geometry: the arrangement follows the chat sketch kind of the same name, drawn as board items in the board's strokes, fonts, theme colours and draw-on animation. Pure layout helpers are shared with chat sketches only where they split out without changing chat's output; chat sketch tests stay unchanged and passing.
- A child whose component is missing, of another kind or on another page, a value out of its kind's range or a missing required argument is skipped and logged. The guard treats the sketch's box like any component's box.
- Children support `look=` like any drawn item.
- The board pages list describes a sketch by its kind and its children's labels.
- The prompt's OPS lists the kinds and children in the existing entries' style. Op names are the spec's; a later benchmark may tune them.

Parked with needs-human until the owner adds the mockup; remove the label once the file exists.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bsk.6.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The tutor's compare, sequence and equation ops draw their component, and each child arrives with its sentence and reflows the earlier ones inside the box.
- [ ] An unknown actor, an unknown symbol and a compare row without one value per side are skipped and logged.
- [ ] A sentence drawing an equation or its symbols is synthesized at the math rate.
- [ ] Highlight, pointer, erase and the pen reach a single child; the board pages list shows each sketch's kind and child labels.
- [ ] A saved board reopens with its sketches as drawn; chat sketches draw exactly as before.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bsk.6.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: compare needs exactly two sides; sequence needs at least two distinct actors (matched case-insensitively); send to= must differ from by=; equation tokens split at spaces, a token with a letter is a symbol (superscript after ^), symbol matches a token's base or whole token; default boxes compare 1100x500, sequence 1200x700, equation 1200x500 (mockup). Layout in src/board/sketchRows.ts. Formula uses the generic math font family (token lint bans named families).

title: Board sketches: the tutor builds bars, a pie, a spectrum or a quadrant piece by piece
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

Four quantity kinds of the chat's sketches come to the board, following the pattern of the first sketch ticket (spec: Sketch kinds as board components). The prompt's sketch guidance gains quantities, two scales, shares and a range.

A slice's ring piece is a line part, so highlight/pointer/pen reach a slice through its legend row (mockup pointer s2 does this).

title: Board sketches: the tutor builds a cycle, stack, timeline or parts diagram piece by piece
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

The first four of the chat's sketch kinds come to the board as components (spec: Sketch kinds as board components). Pieces stay inside the box; past about eight children they shrink to a minimum size rather than overflow.
- Board style, chat geometry: the arrangement follows the chat sketch kind of the same name, drawn as board items in the board's strokes, fonts, theme colours and draw-on animation. Pure layout helpers are shared with chat sketches only where they split out without changing chat's output; chat sketch tests stay unchanged and passing.
- A child whose component is missing, of another kind or on another page, a value out of its kind's range or a missing required argument is skipped and logged. The guard treats the sketch's box like any component's box.
- Children support `look=` like any drawn item.
- The board pages list describes a sketch by its kind and its children's labels.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bsk.4.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The tutor's cycle, stack, timeline and parts ops draw their component, and each child arrives with its sentence and reflows the earlier ones inside the box.
- [ ] More than eight children still fit inside the box.
- [ ] Highlight, pointer, erase and the pen reach a single child; the board pages list shows each sketch's kind and child labels.
