title: Spotlight: while the tutor speaks, what it talks about stays bright and the rest of the page dims
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

While the tutor speaks, the board shows the learner where to look; when it waits, the whole page comes back (spec: Spotlight; GLOSSARY: Spotlight).

- Lit items: the top-level items on the tutor's open page that the most recent sentence with ops drew or named. Naming covers `highlight`, `pointer`, a connector's two ends and a child's `in`/`on` component; an `erase` lights nothing. A child keeps its whole component lit. A sentence without ops, or with only an `erase`, keeps the lit set it inherited.
- Every other top-level item on that page dims to reduced opacity with a short fade. Items whose look is `muted` keep their muted look and are not dimmed further. Learner pen strokes never dim.
- Full page: when the tutor's reply ends (a `?> ` question and a `~> ` check-in end it too), while the learner has the board paused, from the moment the learner cuts in, and whenever a saved board is shown not playing. A page the learner views on their own mid-reply shows in full. The spotlight comes back with the next sentence that draws or names something.
- With reduced motion on, dimming and undimming happen at once.
- The spotlight lives only in the board player and renderer: it never changes an item's saved look, the stored board, the board pages list, the history the model sees, page thumbnails or snapshots. There is no setting for it.

Parked with needs-human until the owner adds the mockup; remove the label once the file exists.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bsk.3.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] While the tutor speaks, the items its latest sentence with ops drew or named stay lit and the other items on the page dim; a sentence without ops keeps the lit set.
- [ ] A child keeps its whole component lit, a connector lights its two ends, and an erase lights nothing.
- [ ] Pen strokes never dim and muted items do not dim further.
- [ ] The whole page shows at reply end, at a question or check-in, while paused, from a cut-in, on a saved board and on a page the learner views on their own.
- [ ] With reduced motion the change is instant.
- [ ] Saved looks, the board pages list, model history, thumbnails and snapshots are unchanged by the spotlight.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-bsk.3.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: highlight, pointer and connector server items carry names (the items they name) so the client can light them; litBy in useBoard computes each sentence's lit set; dimmed in Board.tsx decides per item (child -> component, wash -> its item; pointer, stroke, muted never). Cut-in = sending mid-reply, as the app already defines it. Items carry data-item={id}, as in the mockup.

title: Key sentences and a calmer voice: the tutor says less and its key ideas land slowly
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

The tutor can mark the sentence that carries a part's key idea, formulas are said slower, and the prompt asks the tutor to say less (spec: Pacing, Board prompt).

- A new spoken line kind starting `!> `, read as a spoken sentence marked key. It is stored and replayed like the other line kinds. `?> ` and `~> ` lines are never key.
- The edge-tts client takes a per-sentence prosody rate instead of the fixed `+0%`: about `-15%` for a key sentence, about `-10%` for a sentence whose ops draw `math`, the slower of the two when both apply (never the sum), `+0%` otherwise. The learner's speed still multiplies on the client, and the caption estimate before audio length is known follows the same rate. Filler clips keep their pace.
- A key sentence is followed by the longer pause from the pauses ticket.
- Prompt: FORMAT replaces "Keep it under 20 words" with wording that asks for short, plain spoken lines that say less than writing would and let the drawing carry the rest, with no word count and without asking for single words. FORMAT adds the `!> ` line, used sparingly. PACING and BOARD ask softly for about seven top-level items per page (a component counts as one), erasing finished items or opening a new page beyond that, and for labels of a few words. No hard caps: the guard refuses nothing new.
- Prompt wording is not benchmarked here (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A `!> ` line plays as a spoken sentence, is saved and replays like the other line kinds, and is followed by the longer pause.
- [ ] A key sentence is synthesized at about -15%, a sentence drawing math at about -10%, one that is both at the slower rate, and every other sentence at +0%.
- [ ] The learner's speed still scales key and math sentences, and their caption estimate before audio length is known is longer to match.
- [ ] The board prompt has no word-count rule for spoken lines, describes the `!> ` line, and asks softly for about seven items per page and short labels.
- [ ] An eighth item on a page and a long label are still drawn.
notes:
Rate rule lives in server/board/session.mjs sentenceRate (math kind only; the equation ticket adds its kinds). Sentence messages carry key and rate (percent); the player divides its caption estimate by 1+rate/100 and pauses 900 ms after a key sentence.
sentenceRate and sentence building moved to server/board/script.mjs scriptSentences (session.mjs hit the 550-line cap).

title: Pauses between sentences: the board leaves room to take each sentence in
description:
Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bsk). Decisions in force: ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates), ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages).

The board player leaves a pause between sentences instead of starting the next one at once (spec: Pacing).

- A beat of about 300 ms of board time after each sentence.
- About 900 ms before a sentence whose ops open a page (`page`, `open`) or start a new top-level component (any kind in the board's component set, so later sketch kinds get it too). Where two pauses would apply, the longer one, never the sum.
- Pauses are board time: the learner's speed scales them and pause holds them; resume continues the same pause.
- A pause counts from the end of the sentence; a next sentence that arrives after the pause has passed starts as soon as it is ready.
- Cutting in drops any pause still to come with the sentences after it. A reply's last sentence gets no trailing pause.
- Captions without voice keep the same pauses.
- The values are starting defaults in one place; the rules are what tickets test.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After each sentence the next one starts about 300 ms of board time later, and about 900 ms later when it opens a page or starts a new component; never the sum of both.
- [ ] At 2× the pauses are shorter in proportion; pausing mid-pause and resuming keeps the remaining pause.
- [ ] A sentence that arrives after its pause has passed starts at once.
- [ ] Cutting in drops the pending pause; the reply's last sentence has no trailing pause before the board waits.
- [ ] Caption-only sentences keep the same pauses.
notes: Pause is measured from the previous sentence's end in board time and held as one timer before the next sentence; stop() resets it. Component kinds mirrored in src/board/player.ts COMPONENT_KINDS, kept equal to server COMPONENTS by a test (src does not import .mjs).

title: Board sketches, spotlight and pacing: sketches build piece by piece, the board shows where to look, and the voice breathes
description: The board gets the chat sketch kinds it lacks (cycle, stack, timeline, bars, compare, parts, sequence, quadrant, pie, spectrum, equation) as board components: the tutor gives the box, adds one child per sentence, and the sketch lays out and reflows its pieces in the board's own style. Each piece is a board item the tutor can highlight and the learner can circle. While the tutor speaks, a spotlight keeps the items it talks about bright and dims the rest of the page; the whole page comes back when the tutor waits (reply end, question, check-in) or the learner pauses or cuts in. The voice breathes: a beat after each sentence, longer pauses before a new page or component and after a key idea, formulas and key sentences (new '!> ' line) said slower through a per-sentence edge-tts rate. The prompt asks the tutor to say less without a word count, and softly for about seven items per page and short labels; no hard caps. Spec: docs/board-sketches-spec.md. Decisions in force: ADR 0028, ADR 0029. The sketch kinds and spotlight need a mockup before their tickets.

title: Page strip and back chip: the learner moves between board pages
description:
Spec: docs/board-pages-and-check-ins-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-pgs). Decisions: ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages), ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates, now per page).

The learner sees every board page and opens any of them; asking from a page gets the answer there.

- A thin strip along the top of the board holds page titles in creation order, each side page placed after its parent with a small "from" mark, and the page on screen marked. Clicking a title opens that page.
- A side page shows a "back to <parent title>" chip that opens the parent page.
- Opening a page sends `{ type: 'view', page }` up; the session remembers it for the learner's next message and sends nothing to the model on its own.
- When the learner asks from a page other than the tutor's open page, the session saves an `open` op among that learner message's op lines (as it saves pen strokes), the message ends with `page: <id>` after any `pen:` line, and the tutor's items land on that page. Replay matches what the learner saw.
- While the tutor draws, the view follows its open page: a learner who opened another page is brought back on its next drawn item, as a learner who scrolled away is today. When the tutor is idle or waiting, the learner's chosen page stays.
- The pen hit-tests only items on the page on screen.

Parked with needs-human until the owner adds the mockup; remove the label once the file exists.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-pgs.4.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The strip lists every page title in creation order, side pages after their parent with a from mark, the page on screen marked, and clicking a title opens that page.
- [ ] A side page shows a back-to chip naming its parent, which opens the parent.
- [ ] Asking from another page than the tutor's adds a `page:` line to the message, saves an `open` op with it, and the tutor's next items land on that page, also after reopening.
- [ ] While the tutor draws, the view returns to its page on the next drawn item; while it is idle the learner's page stays.
- [ ] The pen marks only items on the page on screen.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-pgs.4.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: a learner's view becomes a p<n> 'open' op held with the pen's pending lines (server/board/pen.mjs); a view straight back to the tutor's page drops it. Mid-reply the view waits until the reply ends. Brought back by a tutor item, the client sends {type:'view'} with no page. The open item comes down as a 'stroke' message. A page the learner opens slides in over 400 ms. The tab corner uses --radius-inner (4px) since the token lint bans the mockup's literal 6px.

title: Page index: the tutor knows every board page and reuses them
description:
Spec: docs/board-pages-and-check-ins-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-pgs). Decisions: ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages), ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates, now per page).

The model gets only spoken captions back from a conversation's history, so it cannot reuse a page it cannot see. Every turn now tells it what pages exist, and the prompt encourages side pages and reuse.

- Every turn sent to the model, no-answer turns included, starts with a short page index: one line per page in this conversation with its id, title, parent and `from` item, then its items, with the id and text of each item that has text (labels, text, math source, step and node labels) and the id alone for one with none. Kinds and coordinates are left out. The open page is marked.
- The index is built from the session's own replay of the saved op lines, so it holds after the model process restarts.
- Prompt wording, to encourage, never require: the tutor has a pool of pages. When a side question would crowd or derail the page it is on, it can explain on a new page made from the item asked about, then say it is going back and `open` the page it came from once the side question is clear. A quick answer stays on the current page. When the index shows a page that already explains what is asked, it can `open` that page and point at the part that answers, adding to it if the question goes further. It judges for itself when a page feels cramped, and titles each page with its idea in a few words.
- This wording replaces "answer it on the same board" and "when the board is getting full, start fresh space with clear". The example grows to show a side page made from an item and `open` back. The speak-first block stays unchanged.

Untested: the index's size on a long board and its cost to the first-sentence latency; log the index length per turn.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Each turn sent to the model, including no-answer turns, starts with the page index listing every page's id, title, parent, from item and item ids with their text, and marks the open page.
- [ ] After the board's model process restarts, the next turn's index still lists every saved page.
- [ ] The board prompt encourages side pages, going back and reusing a page from the index, and no longer says to answer on the same board or to clear when the board is full.
- [ ] The prompt's example shows a side page made from an item and opening the first page again.
- [ ] Each turn logs the page index length.
notes: Defaults: index is a 'BOARD PAGES (* marks the open page)' block, one line per page: id "title" parent= from=: items; erased items and marks (highlight, pointer, erase, page, open) are left out; table rows list their cells joined by |; an empty board says '(none yet)'. The index goes before the learner text, separated by a blank line, and is not saved with the message. Logged as index=<chars> on the model finished line.

title: Check-ins: the tutor checks the learner is following, in every mode
description:
Spec: docs/board-pages-and-check-ins-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-pgs). Decisions: ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages), ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates, now per page).

Check-ins are the default in every mode: now and then the tutor asks, in its own words, whether the learner is following, and waits however long they take. Never a quiz, never graded.

- A line starting `~> ` is a spoken check-in: voiced and captioned like a `> ` line, and it ends the reply.
- After a check-in the session starts no timer and sends no no-answer turns; the next turn is the learner's own message. The check-in's caption stays and the board's waiting cue keeps pulsing until the learner speaks, types or sends, reusing the look of a `?> ` question waiting for its answer (no mockup).
- Quiz questions (`?> `) keep today's wait: about 4 s after the learner goes idle, a hint, 4 s more, then carry on; typing, speaking or drawing holds the wait open.
- Board settings gains **Check-ins**: Off, Now and then (default), Often, remembered in the browser like the other Board choices, and reaching the session the way the learner-led or tutor-guided mode does. It joins the existing Board section in its current look.
- The board prompt, worded to encourage, never to require: check in after a big idea and before going back from a side page, never after small steps, never twice in a row, always in fresh words. "Not really" means explain that part again another way; "yes" means carry on. The level sets how strongly this is encouraged: Off leaves the block out unless the learner asks with "check on me more"; Often encourages it after each idea. "Stop checking in" and "check on me more" switch it for this board, handled by the model like "quiz me as we go". In tutor-guided its after-each-part questions already check understanding, so check-ins are rarer there.
- Learner-led drops "don't ask the learner questions" for "don't quiz the learner". The prompt's format rules document `~> `, and its example gains a check-in.
- A check-in answer is an ordinary learner message, so familiarity evidence as today.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A `~> ` line is spoken and captioned and ends the reply, and no no-answer turn follows however long the learner stays idle.
- [ ] While a check-in waits, its caption stays and the waiting cue shows until the learner speaks, types or sends.
- [ ] A `?> ` question still brings a hint after about 4 s of idle and the explanation carrying on after about 4 s more.
- [ ] Board settings has Check-ins with Off, Now and then (default) and Often, remembered, and the board prompt carries the chosen level, with no check-in block for Off.
- [ ] The board prompt asks learner-led not to quiz (instead of not to ask), documents `~> `, and its example has a check-in.
- [ ] An answer to a check-in is saved as an ordinary learner message.
notes: Defaults: level rides the board socket as check-ins=off|sometimes|often (default sometimes), localStorage rabbithole.check-ins. The waiting pulse (.board-waiting) now also shows while idle with waiting:true, for both ?> and ~>, cleared by typing, speech or send. Check-in ending the reply is prompt-enforced, like ?>.

title: Board pages: the tutor opens and moves between titled pages
description:
Spec: docs/board-pages-and-check-ins-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-pgs). Decisions: ADR 0029 (a board is a pool of pages), ADR 0028 (board items placed by coordinates, now per page).

The board stops stacking areas downward and holds titled board pages, each its own 1600x900 space, shown one at a time.

- `<id> page "title" [from=<item id>]` opens a new page and makes it the open page. Its parent is the page open when it was made; `from=` names the item on that page it explains, and is optional. A page with no title shows as "Page N". Page ids share the item id space and are never reused.
- `<id> open <page id>` makes an existing page the open page. Back is `open` of the parent. An unknown or non-page id is skipped like any broken op.
- A board starts with no page: the first drawing op on an empty board with no `page` before it starts an untitled page. `clear` stays readable as a new untitled page whose parent is the page open at the time, so boards saved before pages replay unchanged.
- New items land on the open page. Highlight, pointer, connectors, `on`/`in` parents and `from=` reach items on the open page only; `erase` reaches any page. The guard checks a new item only against items on its own page.
- Pages are op lines: saving needs no new columns, and replaying every op line rebuilds each page and the open page at every reply. The saved-board message sent on open carries each reply's items with their page and the open page per reply.
- The player gives `page` and `open` a share of their sentence's time, as `clear` has today, and the view slides to that page in it (a cross-fade with reduced motion). The pointer starts at the centre of a page it lands on. Scrolling through stacked areas goes.
- Reopening a board shows the page open at the end of the latest reply. The chat snapshot of a board reply renders the page open at the end of that reply.
- The board prompt's op list documents `page` and `open` and stops teaching `clear`. The when-to-use wording comes in a later ticket (the page index ticket); here the prompt only says what the ops do.

No new UI part: the page strip is a later ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A script with `page` and `open` ops draws each page in its own 1600x900 space, shows one page at a time, and slides to the open page (cross-fades with reduced motion).
- [ ] The first drawing op on an empty board starts an untitled page; a page without a title shows as "Page N"; a reused page id is skipped.
- [ ] Highlight, pointer and connectors reach only the open page's items, erase reaches any page, and the guard only moves an item away from items on its own page.
- [ ] A saved board replays its pages; reopening shows the page the latest reply ended on, and the chat snapshot shows the page its reply ended on.
- [ ] A board saved before pages, with `clear` ops, replays each fresh space as an untitled page in order.
- [ ] The board prompt documents `page` and `open` instead of `clear`.
notes: Defaults: pages stack as 900px slots (page N's top = (N-1)*900), the view shows one slot and slides between them; the implicit first page has id 'first'; page/open/clear items carry top, title, parent, origin (from=); items keep their old shape, the page each sits on is tracked inside the op reader and the board message gives each reply's open page as 'page'. Pen stroke crop now uses the stroke's own page.

title: Board pages and check-ins: a pool of pages the tutor moves between, and check-ins in every mode
description: A board holds a pool of titled board pages instead of one strip of stacked areas. The tutor opens a side page when a side question would crowd or derail the page it is on, goes back once it is clear, and reopens an earlier page when it already explains what the learner asks. It is encouraged by the prompt, never forced: no item budget, no limits in code. The learner sees every page in a strip and can open any of them; asking from a page gets the answer there. Now and then the tutor checks in, in its own words, after a big idea or before going back from a side page, and waits for the learner as long as they take. Check-ins are the default in every mode and never quizzes; the learner sets how often (Off, Now and then, Often). Tutor-guided keeps its short questions with hint and carry-on. Spec: docs/board-pages-and-check-ins-spec.md. Decision: ADR 0029.

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/45937446357. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Slow failure was a stale test: branch previews now follow the child's model (4a282ee6). Also fixed three master breakages that CI hit: board test read animationDuration instead of --board-ms, sketch.ts over the size cap (split into scales.ts), and Palette.hairline missing in sketchDrawnAt. Slow run 45938932440 green.

title: Sketches fit every reply layout
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

A sketch can sit anywhere a paragraph can, inside every reply layout (plain flow, figure beside text, image gallery, side-by-side comparison, steps, stages, key terms, callout, timeline, check and wide), and fits each at narrow and wide widths.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.5.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A sketch inside each reply layout fits it at narrow and wide widths, with nothing overflowing.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.5.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: a sketch measures its own box (ResizeObserver, before paint) and draws at that width at scale 1; a hidden box (0px, e.g. a closed check answer) keeps the last width. Flow goes vertical below 120px per rank (160 with a fork), per the mockup geometry. Arrow labels wrap too, estimated at 6.4px/char (13px) beside the existing 7px/char for 14px labels, which reproduces the mockup's wrap points. A build-in ends after 500 ms, so a later redraw at a new width or a check answer opened later shows the sketch whole instead of replaying the fade. The figure's stack estimate counts sketches at their own height, since they don't reflow like text; without this, a figure with a sketch stayed stacked. Spacing as drawn: check answer 12px, callout keeps the sketch's own 8px (the mockup's callout rule does not match, so it draws 8 and not 12), wide 20px under its visual. The title's reserve for the controls box (164/44px padding) and the controls themselves are left to Rabbithole-skt.7, which builds the controls; the mockup's extra 44px under each sketch is that controls row on devices that cannot hover.

title: Sketch kinds for quantities: line, quadrant, spectrum
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Adds the line, quadrant and spectrum kinds to the sketch module, so these blocks draw in replies like flow and bars. Their lines, from the spec (prototype syntax):

- line: first line `range: min..max`, then `value: label`; a number line.
- quadrant: lines `x: low .. high` and `y: low .. high`, then `item: x, y` with x and y from 0 to 10.
- spectrum: first line `ends: low .. high`, then items in order along it, `item: note`.

The local branch prototype/sketch (prototypes/sketch/sketch.js) has a stand-in renderer that parses every kind; reuse its parsing, not its look.

This ticket builds the line, quadrant and spectrum drawings of the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.3.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A valid body of each of line, quadrant and spectrum draws in a reply with one item per drawn element, each carrying its label; the title line and *star* focus carry through.
- [ ] A line places values within its range; a quadrant places items by x and y from 0 to 10 under its axis labels; a spectrum spaces items in order between its ends.
- [ ] A body that matches no line of its kind, or a value out of its range, is an error: the reply hides that sketch and logs its kind and reason.
- [ ] Each kind draws in the light and dark theme palettes.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.3.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: line labels estimate text at 0.6em (8.4px/char), as the mockup does, for edge clamping and crowding; a fourth crowded line label shares the top row; a sketch's frame of reference (range, axes, ends) follows the title in the figure's aria-label. Mockup geometry diffed element by element against drawSketch for every line/quadrant/spectrum figure: identical.

title: A stroke in free space goes to the tutor as an image
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A finished pen stroke over no board item goes with the next learner message as a cropped image of that area, only when the chat model reads images. Other models get no image.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] A stroke in free space goes with the next question as a cropped image, only to models that read images.
notes: Defaults: each free-space stroke (no mark) becomes its own PNG, rendered server-side with sharp from its points: crop = stroke bbox + 40 board px, clamped to the 1600x900 board, dark ink (6px, round caps) on white; only the learner's ink, not board items reaching into the crop. Sent only when ctx.readsImages({provider, model}) is true; the pen line gains ' · images of p<n> attached'. Files live in a mkdtemp under ctx.dir for the turn only. Board process ask(text, emit, signal, images=[{type,path}]): Claude sends base64 image blocks after the text, Codex sends localImage inputs.

title: Board settings: Voice language
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The Board section gains Voice language, English by default. A language other than English loads Whisper base at int8 (about 77 MB) instead of Moonshine on the next mic press, with the same download progress, and picks that language's voice from the voice table. The tutor speaks in the voice language.

Look: the Voice language row of the Board section mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.12.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Board section has Voice language, English by default.
- [ ] Choosing a language other than English recognizes speech in that language, downloading its model on the next mic press with progress.
- [ ] The tutor speaks in the chosen voice language's voice.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.12.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: voice-language stored per browser (localStorage rabbithole.voice-language, en default) and sent as ?lang= on the board socket; unknown codes fall back to en. Voice table: en Aria, zh Xiaoxiao, nl Colette, fr Denise, de Katja, it Elsa, ja Nanami, pt-BR Francisca, es-ES Elvira (the mockup's list). Names via Intl.DisplayNames. Whisper base pinned to onnx-community/whisper-base@27a07b4b (encoder+merged decoder int8, 76.9 MB), told the language, chunk_length_s 30. Non-English boards get no fillers (English words). Prompt gains a VOICE LANGUAGE line. GET /api/settings/voice-models?lang= reports whether the models are on disk (size check) for the Settings line.

title: Speaking cuts in on the tutor
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The mic now listens while the tutor speaks.

- When voice detection hears about 150 ms of speech while the tutor is speaking, the server stops the tutor at once (the interruption from the typing ticket). About 300 ms of silence then ends the question, as before.
- The tutor's own voice from the speakers does not count as the learner speaking.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the mic on, about 150 ms of speech while the tutor speaks stops it at once, and the question is sent after about 300 ms of silence.
- [ ] Played-back tutor speech alone does not trigger a stop.
notes: Defaults: cut-in applies whenever a turn runs (thinking or speaking), at the 5th voiced frame (160 ms, the same MIN_FRAMES that separates a click from a question). Tutor's own voice: left to the browser's echo cancellation (already on in src/board/mic.ts); no server-side echo guard. The stop reuses the typed cut-in's stop(turn), whose idle the client already treats as the stop signal.

title: The board keeps what the learner heard
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

- The player reports up when each sentence starts and ends playing, so the server knows the spoken point. Leaving mid-reply saves every sentence that started playing, with its ops, and drops the rest.
- The first audio byte times out after 2.5 s, with one retry. When speech still fails, the sentence plays as a caption only, timed by its length, and a notice says the voice is unavailable. The board carries on.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Leaving the board mid-reply saves every sentence that started playing and drops the rest.
- [ ] A first byte slower than 2.5 s is retried once; if speech still fails the sentence shows as a caption only, a voice-unavailable notice shows, and the board carries on.
notes: Defaults: the 2.5 s first-byte timer runs from speak() (it covers connecting), and a timed-out socket is dropped so the retry opens a fresh one. Retry happens only when no chunk arrived yet, so audio is never doubled. Once both tries fail, the rest of that turn is captions only (no further 5 s waits per sentence), with one notice per turn; the next turn tries speech again. Save-on-leave and progress reports already shipped with brd.7/brd.20 (test/http/board.test.mjs 'leaving mid-reply saves only shown sentences').

title: A reopened board shows its drawing
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A board reply stores its op lines with the reply. Reopening a board replays every op up to the latest reply and shows the final board at once, with no entry animation.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A board reply stores its op lines.
- [ ] Reopening the board shows the final board instantly, with the items of every reply.
notes: Defaults: op lines that parsed are saved raw as a JSON array in a new messages.ops column, only for sentences that started showing (saved with each streamed save and at the end). On open the board session replays every saved line through the op parser, so later replies can still join earlier ids, and sends {type:'board', items} once; the client draws them with a 0ms entry. Ops of a sentence never shown are dropped, so a later connector to one of their ids is skipped on replay.

title: Board items enter by hand
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

Board items stop fading in and enter the way a hand draws them, keeping the look the first drawing ticket built.

- A stroke draws on, a dot grows, text writes in left to right, each over its share of its sentence. Nothing pops in.
- With reduced motion on, every entry is a plain fade.
- A theme or appearance switch redraws the board in the new colours.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Strokes draw on, dots grow and text writes in; nothing pops in.
- [ ] With reduced motion on, each item fades in instead.
- [ ] A theme or appearance switch redraws the board in the new theme's colours.
notes: Defaults: entry is CSS only (src/styles/board.css) keyed by --board-ms per item: strokes use pathLength=1 + stroke-dashoffset (arrows draw shaft then head as one path), dots scale up from their centre, text reveals with clip-path inset right-to-left edge; a circle/box label writes in alongside its stroke over the same share. Easing ease-in-out cubic. Reduced motion swaps every animation for the opacity fade. Theme redraw needs no code: colours are light-dark theme tokens via currentColor. No new test: jsdom cannot run CSS animations and a markup check is a banned render-only test.

title: Board release check
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The release ticket for the board. A browser smoke script plays one scripted board in real Chromium with fake model output: a typed question, a reply that draws shapes, math and a component while it speaks (fake speech), a typed interruption, and the saved reply in normal chat. The privacy note in the data and privacy guide already covers boards; check it still matches what shipped.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A scripted board plays in real Chromium: it draws, speaks, takes an interruption, and saves the reply.
- [ ] The data and privacy guide matches what the board sends where.
notes: Defaults: fake speech is real WebM Opus tones made with system ffmpeg at script start (third sentence 20 s so the typed cut-in lands while it plays); script added to the smoke set as verify-board.mjs and run by npm run verify.

title: Boards on Codex
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A conversation whose chat model is on Codex gets a board too, on the existing long-lived Codex app-server, at low effort, with the same board prompt, shared history and thinking log as Claude. It is slower (first sentence about 1.2–1.7 s in `prototype/model-latency`); the waiting cue and fillers cover that.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A board on a Codex conversation answers typed questions with the board prompt at low effort.
- [ ] Board turns on Codex join the conversation's history both ways.
- [ ] Leaving the board stops the Codex turn.
notes: Defaults: the Codex board reuses Codex.generate on the shared app-server (tree.system overrides the tutor prompt); effort 'low' is sent as-is; close() leaves the shared app-server up, so the 10-minute idle stop does not apply; the no-board notice now names Claude or Codex.

title: Board replies fit the rest of the app
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

Everything said on a board is an ordinary reply in the conversation.

- After each board reply, the quick thinking model judges familiarity and records concepts in the knowledge graph, as for chat, and skips suggestion marks and next questions.
- Learner messages on a board, spoken or typed, are familiarity evidence like any message.
- Board turns count in usage history like chat turns.
- The normal chat view shows a board reply's spoken text plus a small snapshot of the board, rendered from its ops.

Look: the snapshot is designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.16.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A board reply records familiarity and concepts, with no suggestion marks or next questions.
- [ ] Board questions count as familiarity evidence.
- [ ] Board turns appear in usage history.
- [ ] In normal chat a board reply shows its text and a small snapshot of the board at that reply.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.16.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: the server attaches each board reply's snapshot (items replayed from every saved op line up to it) to the message in store.tree; a board reply with an empty board shows none. Concepts come from the existing suggestions job's naming path with no marks (graph and memory edits only, no suggestions row, no next questions); its call is recorded in usage history. Familiarity: the verdict job judges the board question after each completed board reply. Usage: each asked board turn records a chat usage event under the conversation's provider and model. Snapshot margins 11px/14px reproduce the mockup's measured 15px/14px gaps inside the reply's 4px flex gap.

title: Transcript rail and branching from the board
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A narrow transcript rail beside the board shows what was said, as captions in the rail. The learner can collapse it; when collapsed, the one-line caption under the board shows instead.

Selecting a passage in the rail branches as in chat. The board pauses, and the child conversation opens in normal chat without a board.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup, open and collapsed.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.15.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A board shows a transcript rail with the conversation's questions and replies, captioning the current sentence as it plays.
- [ ] Collapsing the rail shows the one-line caption under the board instead.
- [ ] Branching from a passage in the rail pauses the board and opens the child conversation in normal chat without a board.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.15.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: rail opens by default, not remembered (mockup open by default; spec silent). Rail reuses the chat's Passage and BranchForm; the spoken sentence is painted with a CSS highlight (board-now). Session turns carry their message ids from the server's thinking state. Send from the rail pauses at once; a turn in flight is ended first (leave, saved up to the sentence shown) because the branch route refuses while the reply slot is held, so a board reply left halfway is now a valid branch anchor (anchorOf). Ask here asks on the board, disabled while the tutor is busy. Differences from the mockup: state 6 — returning to the parent opens normal chat (focused chat keeps board state per conversation); turning Board on shows the saved board up to the spoken sentence with the branch mark, not Paused with Resume, since leaving ends the turn (spec story 6/7). The passage question field is the chat's one-line input, not wrapping; Ask about selection is the chat's Astryx sm button (168x28 vs 159x30); Ask here disabled while speaking.
Owner decision needed (PR #195, CI green). Mockup state 6 'Back on the parent: paused where it was' differs. What the app does: going back to the parent opens normal chat, because the focused chat keeps board state per conversation. Turning Board on shows the saved board up to the spoken sentence, with the explored-passage mark in the rail, but no 'Paused' and no Resume. Why: the branch route refuses while the board's reply holds the reply slot, so Send from the rail ends the turn first (saved up to the sentence shown, as spec stories 6 and 7 require when leaving). Options: (a) approve as built; (b) keep the parent's board session alive and paused while the child is open: Board stays mounted across the switch, and the branch route must accept a branch while a board reply holds the slot (a larger server change, and against story 6's 'switch conversation stops the tutor'); (c) only reopen the parent's board on return (lift board state out of FocusedChat), still without Resume. Smaller differences: the passage field is the chat's one-line input, not wrapping; Ask about selection is the chat's Astryx sm button (168x28 vs 159x30); Ask here is disabled while the tutor speaks.

title: The learner draws on the board with a pen
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A pen on the board toolbar lets the learner draw, circle and point to show what they mean.

- The learner's strokes are board items of their own, in their own look, and the tutor may erase or keep them.
- A finished stroke is hit-tested against the board items, and the next learner message carries references such as "circled `t1`".
- The pen alone sends nothing: strokes go with the next spoken or typed question.
- A learner message stores its strokes and references, so reopening the board shows them.

Strokes over no item are the next ticket.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.14.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The pen draws strokes on the board; drawing alone sends nothing.
- [ ] A question after circling an item tells the tutor which item was circled.
- [ ] The tutor can erase the learner's strokes with an erase op.
- [ ] Strokes are saved with the learner's message and show again when the board reopens.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.14.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: a finished stroke goes up at once ({type:'stroke', points} in board px); the server names it p<n> (next free id), hit-tests it and sends back {type:'stroke', item, mark}. A closed loop (ends within max(60px, 30% of its diagonal)) circles the items whose centres it encloses; otherwise it points at the item nearest its end within 40px. Pending strokes go with the next ask: the model gets 'pen: circled t1 · pointed at t3 · strokes p1, p2' appended; the learner message keeps their words and stores the stroke op lines (with circled=/pointed= refs) in messages.ops, so replay restores them. New erase op 'e1 erase ID ...' removes items from the board (server and on replay) and fades them out on the client over its share of the sentence. Pill counts strokes that mark an item; strokes over no item still draw and save but are left to the next ticket. Learner ink is the conversation's family ink (inkStyle), so a root conversation draws in paper, the same colour as look=focus.

title: Tutor-guided boards
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

Learner-led or tutor-guided is an app-wide setting in the Board section, learner-led by default. The board prompt tells the tutor which applies. A spoken or typed request ("quiz me as we go", "stop asking") switches it for the current board, and the model handles that itself.

- A `?> ` line is a spoken question for the learner. After it, whichever mode applies, the board waits about 4 s.
- If the learner says nothing, the session sends a no-answer turn and the tutor gives one hint. After about 4 s more of silence, a second no-answer turn has the tutor carry on teaching, with no comment on the silence.
- No-answer turns are system turns: not learner messages and not familiarity evidence.
- Answers are never graded.

Look: the setting row joins the Board section mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.13.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The Board section has learner-led or tutor-guided, learner-led by default, and the board prompt carries the choice.
- [ ] After a `?> ` question, about 4 s of silence brings one hint, and about 4 s more brings the explanation carrying on.
- [ ] An answer within the wait cancels the hint.
- [ ] No-answer turns are not saved as learner messages and are not familiarity evidence.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.13.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: mode stored per browser (localStorage rabbithole.board-mode = guided), sent as ?mode=guided on the board socket and read into the board prompt at warm-up, so a change applies from the next board opened. Wait starts when the question's caption ends (turn completes) and the last sentence is a ?> line; hint turn always waits once more; carry-on waits only if it ends on ?> again. Typing ({type:'typing'} on first character), speech detected, push-to-talk hold and a pen stroke all cancel the wait (holds it open until sent). No-answer turns: no user message, no verdict; concepts still recorded against the learner's last question. Pen code moved to server/board/pen.mjs for the 550-line cap.
PR #201 open, CI green.

title: Board settings: push-to-talk
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A new Board section in Settings with push-to-talk, off by default. With it on, voice detection is replaced by holding Space or the mic button: speech while held is the question, and releasing sends it.

The section will also hold Voice language and learner-led or tutor-guided from later tickets; this ticket builds the section and its push-to-talk row only.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.12.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Settings has a Board section with push-to-talk, off by default.
- [ ] With push-to-talk on, only speech while Space or the mic button is held is sent, and voice detection doesn't cut in.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.12.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: push-to-talk stored per browser (localStorage rabbithole.push-to-talk), read on each board render. Protocol: {type:'hold', on} up the board socket; hold stops the tutor and buffers audio without voice detection, capped at 60 s; release recognizes the whole buffer. The mic stream stays open after the first hold (no re-ask latency); frames go up only while held. A first hold that is still held when the models finish starts recording then. Space ignored in input/textarea/select/contenteditable and while the board is hidden; window blur releases. Voice language left to its own ticket per the description.
PR #199 open, CI green. Mic component tests moved to test/board/mic.test.mjs (file size cap).

title: Ask on the board by voice
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

A mic button on the board toolbar turns on hands-free voice questions. Speech recognition and voice detection run in the local server, so every browser and the desktop app behave the same; the learner's voice never leaves the machine.

- The first mic press downloads Moonshine base at int8 (about 63 MB) and Silero voice detection (about 1 MB) through `@huggingface/transformers` from a pinned revision, like the knowledge-graph embedder. Progress shows on the mic button, and typing works meanwhile.
- The browser captures the mic at 16 kHz mono with echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain on, and sends frames up the board socket.
- About 300 ms of silence after speech ends the question; it is recognized and sent as the learner's message.
- In this ticket the mic does not listen while the tutor speaks; speaking over the tutor is the next ticket.
- The desktop app grants the mic permission to the app's own page.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup, including the downloading, listening and off states of the mic button.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.11.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The mic is off when a board opens and turns on with one press.
- [ ] The first mic press downloads the speech models with progress on the mic button, while typing still works; later presses don't download again.
- [ ] With the mic on and the tutor silent, about 300 ms of silence after speech sends the recognized question.
- [ ] While the tutor speaks, the mic does not listen.
- [ ] No audio leaves the machine; only the recognized text goes to the provider.
- [ ] The mic works in the desktop app.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.11.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: Silero int8 (0.64 MB) with Moonshine base encoder+merged decoder int8 (~67 MB with tokenizer), pinned commits and SHA-256 in server/board/hearing.mjs. VAD threshold 0.5, 32 ms frames, end after 10 silent frames (320 ms), under 5 voiced frames (160 ms) is a click, 3 frames lead-in. Mic frames are float32 at 16 kHz resampled in public/mic-worklet.js (AudioContext at device rate, as Firefox refuses mixed rates). The server drops mic audio while a turn runs (thinking or speaking). Progress shows only when bytes download; a cached load turns on with no progress. Desktop: setPermissionRequestHandler grants audio-only media to the app origin, other permissions keep Electron's default.
PR #197 opened; GitHub reports CONFLICTING with master, so no CI ran. Left for the merger.

title: Cut in on the tutor by typing
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The learner can cut in mid-reply.

- Typing doesn't stop the tutor; sending does.
- On an interruption the server sends a stop: audio stops at once, the item being drawn jumps to its finished state in about 150 ms, and sentences and ops not yet started are dropped.
- The reply is saved with every sentence that started playing and its ops; the rest is dropped.
- The provider already received text the learner never heard, so the next turn tells the model where it was cut off, naming the last sentence heard, and says the rest was not heard.
- The tutor answers the question on the same board, then picks the topic up again in its own words (board skills).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Typing on a board while the tutor speaks doesn't stop it; sending the question does.
- [ ] On sending mid-reply, speech stops at once and the half-drawn item finishes within about 150 ms; nothing more from that reply plays.
- [ ] The interrupted reply is saved with every sentence that started playing and nothing after.
- [ ] The next model turn names the last sentence the learner heard and says the rest was not heard.
notes: Defaults: the cut-off note goes at the head of the next question's prompt (not the saved message), derived from the tree (last board reply interrupted with text), so it also covers leaving mid-reply and reopening. Sending is allowed while speaking or paused, held while thinking. The client stops playback on send without waiting for the server and drops sentences until the server's next state; the server's existing idle is the stop signal (no new message type). A reply already shown in full when cut in saves as completed, as on leave. A stopped item mid-entry ends 150 ms (board time) after the stop.

title: Waiting cue and filler clips
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The board is never still and silent for more than a second while the tutor answers.

- Within about 200 ms of a learner turn the board shows that the tutor heard: the tutor's pen moves to free space, or a soft pulse shows. With reduced motion on it is a plain fade.
- A few short filler clips ("hmm", "okay", "good question") are synthesized once per voice and kept locally. One plays only when a turn's first audio hasn't started after 1 s. They vary and never play twice in a row.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The board shows a waiting cue within 200 ms of a sent question.
- [ ] A filler clip plays only when a turn's first audio hasn't started after 1 s.
- [ ] No filler plays on a turn whose audio starts within 1 s.
- [ ] The same filler never plays on two turns in a row, and fillers are not saved in the reply.
notes: Defaults: waiting cue is a soft paper-coloured pulse at the board's lower-right corner (1544,844) while state is thinking, a 200 ms fade with reduced motion. Fillers: 'Hmm.', 'Okay.', 'Good question.' synthesized on first board open per voice into <data dir>/board-fillers/<voice>/*.webm (separate edge-tts client, retried next board on failure). Server sends a filler as binary frames under id 'filler' + audio-end when no audio chunk or audio-end for the turn's first sentence within 1 s; random among clips except the last one played this session. Client plays it only when no sentence is playing; the first sentence's speech cuts it off. createApp options fillers (off in tests) and boardClock (fake in tests).

title: Speed control and pause on the board
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The board toolbar gains speed and pause.

- Speed is applied on the client with `playbackRate` and `preservesPitch`, so a change is instant; animation durations scale with it. Default 1.5×, and the learner's choice is remembered in the browser.
- Pause stops audio and animation; resume continues from the exact sentence and item. Generation keeps buffering while paused.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup. The toolbar will also hold the mic and pen from later tickets; this ticket builds only speed and pause.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.8.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Speech plays at 1.5× by default.
- [ ] Changing the speed changes speech and drawing at once, without restarting the sentence.
- [ ] The chosen speed is still set after a reload.
- [ ] Pause stops speech and drawing; resume continues from the same sentence and item.
- [ ] A reply still arriving while paused plays in full after resume.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.8.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: board time stays at the default 1.5× (estimates, op shares, voice durations); a paced clock in the player scales it by speed/1.5 and freezes it on pause, retiming pending timers, so speed changes mid-sentence without restart. Item entries are CSS animations whose WAAPI playbackRate = speed/1.5; pause sets animation-play-state: paused. Speech: audio.playbackRate + preservesPitch, pause/play on the element. Speed saved as localStorage rabbithole.board-speed (1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2). Pause enabled only while state is speaking (or paused). Tool order: mic, pen, speed, pause. Menu uses the shared Astryx menu: 40px rows and 4px offset vs mockup 34px/6px, same as the composer effort menu.

title: The tutor speaks on the board
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The tutor's sentences are spoken aloud with edge-tts, in step with the drawing.

- A small edge-tts client of our own, reusing the library's protocol pieces (the library opens a socket per request and returns only whole clips). It opens the socket as soon as a turn starts, streams each sentence's audio in chunks and synthesizes one sentence ahead of playback.
- Audio chunks go down the board socket with their sentence id. Playback starts on a sentence's first chunk, and a sentence now lasts as long as its audio plays; its ops share that time. The estimate stays for the time before the audio length is known.
- Prove chunked MP3 playback in Chrome and Firefox before building on it (untested in the prototypes). If one of them can't play streamed chunks, stop and record it as a blocker. Safari is the owner's check, not this ticket's.
- The voice is `en-US-AriaNeural`, from a small table keyed by Voice language; videos keep their own voice.

Reporting what was heard, saving on leave and the speech-failure fallback are the next ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A board reply is spoken aloud sentence by sentence, each sentence's drawing lasting as long as its audio.
- [ ] Speech for a sentence starts playing on its first audio chunk.
- [ ] Chunked playback works in Chrome and Firefox, or the failing browser is recorded as a blocker.
notes: Chunked playback proof (headless Chrome 158, Firefox 160, MediaSource, real edge-tts clip fed in 4 KB and 120-byte chunks): Firefox's MediaSource refuses audio/mpeg (isTypeSupported false), so streamed MP3 can't play there. Both play WebM Opus streamed chunks: playing 30-75 ms after the first chunk (Chrome) and 31-54 ms (Firefox), ended on time at 1.5x. Default chosen: the board asks edge-tts for webm-24khz-16bit-mono-opus (the service accepts it; ogg is refused); videos keep MP3. Other defaults: speech frames are binary WS messages (1 byte id length, id, audio) plus {type:'audio-end', id}; sentences carry voiced:true when speech is on; speech is off in tests (createApp speech=null) and on in server/main.mjs; speech plays at 1.5x via defaultPlaybackRate+preservesPitch; a failed synthesis sends audio-end without chunks and the sentence plays by its estimate (timeout/retry/notice stay for Rabbithole-brd.21); voice table has English only until Voice language exists (Rabbithole-brd.23).

title: Flows, trees, tables and Venn diagrams grow one piece at a time
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The remaining components, on the component layout from the graphs ticket:

- `flow` + `step`: one step and its arrow at a time.
- `tree` + `node`: one node and its edge at a time.
- `table` + `row`: one row at a time.
- `venn` + `item`: two or three sets, one circle at a time, then the items.

Each reflows its earlier children inside its box when a new one arrives.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.6.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A flow adds one step and its arrow at a time.
- [ ] A tree adds one node and its edge at a time.
- [ ] A table adds one row at a time.
- [ ] A Venn diagram draws one circle at a time, then its items in the right regions.
- [ ] Each component reflows its earlier children inside its box when a new one arrives.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.6.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: brd.6 components are validated server-side (server/board/components.mjs) and laid out on the client from every drawn sibling (src/board/layout.ts), so a later child reflows earlier ones; parts move by CSS geometry (x/y/width/height/d/translate) with 400ms transitions. Syntax follows the board prompt: step/node/row/item "label" in ID, node under ID (or under=ID), row "a|b|c", item set=A+B (names, case-insensitive). A second root node, an unknown under, a row with more cells than cols, or an unknown set is skipped; a short row pads empty cells. Defaults: flow 1200x260 dir=right (down: rows, 260-wide boxes, at most 110 high), tree 1200x640, table 1100x420, venn 1100x620. Flow arrows stop 16 short of both boxes per the mockup rule (frames 2-3 draw 20). Node width = label chars x 18.75 + 60, rounded to even (mockup measured text, within 2px). Venn geometry scales the mockup's drawn positions by min(w/1100, h/620 or 800).

title: Graphs and number lines build up on the board
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

The first components: items that lay out their own children inside a box the tutor gives.

- `axes` + `plot`: the axes draw first, then each curve traces left to right.
- `numberline` + `point`: the line draws, then one point at a time.
- Children are `on` their component and use its units, such as points on the axes.
- A child arriving later reflows the earlier ones within the box, with animation. The prototype sized children from the whole script, which a live stream doesn't have.
- The guard treats a component as one item at its box.
- A child naming an unknown parent is skipped and logged.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.5.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Axes draw first and each plot then traces its curve left to right in the axes' units.
- [ ] A number line draws, then each point appears one at a time at its value.
- [ ] A child that arrives later reflows the earlier ones inside the component's box, animated.
- [ ] A child naming an unknown parent is skipped and logged.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.5.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: geometry computed server-side in board px (server/board/components.mjs), as connectors are; point label rows computed on the client from drawn points (labelRows in src/board/player.ts) so a later point reflows earlier labels. Missing ranges default to -5..5; axes default 800x600, numberline 1000x240. Default ticks: fewest even whole steps (5,4,6,8,10,3 pieces) that hit both ends and 0, else halves. Plots sample every 10 board px, cut at the axes' edge. Point value is a number or fraction word; label from "label", label=, else the value as written. dot X,Y and text on axes are also children (prompt advertises them). Children are not guarded and cannot be connector ends. Unknown parent -> skipped with cause 'unknown parent ID', logged by the existing 'op skipped' warn.

title: Math, highlight, pointer, erase and fresh space
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

More board kinds:

- `math`: KaTeX that appears term by term. Bad math is skipped and logged like any broken op.
- `highlight`: a sweep over an item.
- `pointer`: glides to an item, then fades.
- `erase`: the named items fade out.
- `clear`: the camera pans to a fresh 1600×900 area below; earlier areas stay on the board and the learner can scroll back to them.

The learner can also scroll back through the board's earlier states, one per reply, replayed from the stored ops.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.4.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A math op writes its formula in term by term; invalid math is skipped and logged.
- [ ] Highlight sweeps over its item, and pointer glides to its item and fades.
- [ ] Erase fades out the named items.
- [ ] Clear pans to a fresh area below, and earlier areas stay reachable by scrolling.
- [ ] The learner can step back through the board as it stood at each earlier reply.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.4.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: math validates on the server with KaTeX (display style, strict off); bad math is skipped and logged WARN 'board op skipped' with KaTeX's message. Terms = children of each .katex-base except struts and spaces, each writing in over an equal share. Math bounds (for highlight/pointer) are estimated from the LaTeX (shortcut comment in ops.mjs). Highlight/pointer take one id, erase any number (it may erase a highlight); marks cannot be named by later ops. The pointer starts at the centre of the current area and its tip stops 12px right of its item. clear adds 900 to every later y; the client grows the SVG one area per clear, pans with rAF ease-in-out (cross-fade with reduced motion), and a later live item scrolls back to the latest area. On open the server sends {type:'board', replies:[{caption, items}]} (store.boardReplies replaces boardOpLines); the stepper shows from 2 replies, is off while busy, and stepping or asking shows items without entry. Fixed board.test's reopen check, which read animationDuration instead of --board-ms since brd.19.
ralph-afk --pr: CI after the review failed 3 times; see .ralph-tui/pr-logs/.

title: Board items never overlap or fall off the board
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

After parsing, a guard checks each new item against the items still on the board. An item that overlaps another, or leaves the 1600×900 board, is moved to the nearest free spot and kept.

What counts as an overlap comes from the prototype's measure: bounding boxes intersecting by more than 4 px; a label inside a shape doesn't count; a line counts only when it crosses text or math; a connector counts when it crosses anything but its own endpoints. Speak-first runs had small label-on-arrow collisions in 6 of 16 runs, so the guard is required (ADR 0028).

Moves are logged so prompt regressions show up.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An item placed over another item is drawn at the nearest free spot instead.
- [ ] An item placed partly or wholly off the board is drawn at the nearest free spot on it.
- [ ] A label inside a shape, a line crossing only shapes, and a connector touching only its own endpoints are left where the tutor put them.
- [ ] Every move is logged with the item id.
notes: Defaults: guard runs in boardOps().read (server/board/ops.mjs) with the prototype's measure. Dots never count as overlaps (as in the prototype) but must stay on the board. Containment exempts only a strictly smaller item, so a box stacked exactly on an equal box still counts. Connectors are never moved (they stay joined to their ends); items placed later move off them. Free spots are searched on a 10 px grid, nearest by distance; a full board keeps the nearest on-board spot. Moves log INFO 'board item moved' id=<item id>.

title: The tutor draws shapes and labels as it speaks
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

Op lines under each sentence now draw on the board, one small change per sentence, timed with the caption.

- A plain op parser reads `<id> <kind> <args> [key=value]` lines, each belonging to the `> ` sentence above it. Kinds in this ticket: circle, box, dot, line, arrow, text. Top-level items take `at X,Y`, their centre on a fixed 1600×900 board; sizes are `r=`, `w= h=` and `size=s|m|l`; lines and arrows take board points, and a connector may run `from <id> to <id>`. `look=focus|muted|good|wrong|new` maps to theme colours in light and dark; the model never writes colours.
- An op that doesn't parse or names an unknown id is skipped and logged; the board carries on and the learner never sees op text or an error.
- Ops go down the board socket tagged with their sentence id.
- A new plain board player module turns sentences and ops into a timeline: a sentence lasts its estimated time (15 characters per second at 1.5×, as in the prototype) and its ops share that time in order. Later tickets add hand-drawn entry, saving, audio timing, speed, pause and interruptions to the same module.
- The renderer is SVG with clean marker strokes in theme colours. In this ticket every item enters with a plain fade; the next ticket adds hand-drawn entry.

The local branch `prototype/board-placement` has the op syntax the prompt teaches and a stand-in renderer; reuse its parsing rules, not its look.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup, as its finished items. Entry animation and saving the board are later tickets.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Circle, box, dot, line, arrow and text ops draw on the board at their coordinates, each fading in over its share of its sentence.
- [ ] Looks map to theme colours in light and dark.
- [ ] A malformed op, or one naming an unknown id, is skipped and logged; the rest of the board still draws and no op text shows.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.2.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: each sentence goes down with its ops in one event ({type:'sentence', id, text, ops}), sent once its op lines are complete (the next '>' line begins or the reply ends), so the player can split the sentence's time equally; the server can still start speech on the sentence line later. Ops are parsed and validated on the server (server/board/ops.mjs); skipped ops log WARN 'board op skipped' with the reason only, not the op line. A duplicate id, an unknown look or size, a non-positive size, or an op before its sentence is skipped too. Sizes default to r=90 and 280x160; a circle or box label renders inside it at size s. Known ids last for the board session (saving the board is a later ticket, so a reopened board starts empty).

title: Board opens and answers typed questions in captions
description:
Spec: docs/board-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-brd). Decision: ADR 0028 (board items are placed by coordinates).

This is the tracer bullet: a learner switches a conversation to a board, types a question, and reads the tutor's spoken sentences as a caption. Nothing is drawn or spoken aloud yet.

- A Board toggle in the focused chat header switches the conversation to its board. While the board is open it takes the full content width and the map is hidden. It opens empty and waits for the first question; the mic is off.
- One board session per open board, on the server, talking to the browser over one WebSocket (`ws` becomes a direct dependency; chat replies stay on server-sent events). This ticket carries typed questions up and session state (idle, thinking, speaking), sentences with ids, and notices down.
- Claude only here. The session starts one long-lived Claude Code CLI process with `--input-format stream-json` when the board opens, resuming the conversation's own session with the board system prompt and effort forced to low, so board turns join the conversation's history both ways. It stops when the board closes or after 10 minutes idle, like the quick thinking runner.
- The board prompt is isolated from chat: none of chat's media rules (visuals, videos, sketches, markers, discussions, reply layouts, suggestion marks, next questions), no tutor tools. It carries the board skills from the spec, the speak-first PACE block word for word, the learner's tutor style, the inherited context, the memory note, and explored concepts with familiarity.
- The model's output is the spec's line-based stream. This ticket reads only `> ` sentence lines; op lines are ignored until the next ticket.
- Each sentence shows as a one-line caption under the board, held for an estimate of 15 characters per second at 1.5×.
- The learner's question and the tutor's sentences are saved as an ordinary learner message and assistant reply in the conversation. Reopening the board shows the conversation as it was.
- Toggling the board off, switching conversation or closing the tab stops the tutor at once and saves the reply up to the sentence being shown.
- Thinking tokens of every request are logged.

Look: designed with Impeccable to the mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The focused chat header has a Board toggle; turning it on shows an empty full-width board with the map hidden and the mic off, waiting for a question.
- [ ] A typed question on a board gets the tutor's sentences back one at a time as a caption under the board.
- [ ] A Claude board keeps one CLI process for the whole board, started when the board opens and stopped when it closes or after 10 minutes idle.
- [ ] Board turns run at low effort with the board prompt: the speak-first block, the board skills and the learner's tutor style, and none of chat's media rules or tutor tools.
- [ ] A later chat turn in the same conversation sees what was said on the board, and a board turn sees earlier chat.
- [ ] Board questions and replies are saved as messages in the conversation.
- [ ] Turning the board off, switching conversation or closing the tab stops the tutor and saves the reply up to the sentence shown.
- [ ] Every board request logs its thinking tokens.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-brd.1.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: a non-Claude conversation's board shows a notice (Codex is brd.17); an unset tutor style adds nothing to the board prompt (chat's default style is written for reading); explored concepts come from the neighbourhood of the title, branch passage and last two learner questions at board open; saved reply text joins sentences with spaces and the reopened caption is its last sentence; messages gain a board flag (needed for the empty-board hint); no real-CLI slow test, since tickets never call a real model; the board composer draft is local to the board.
