title: Board: a voice tutor that talks the learner through an idea while drawing it
description:
A conversation can switch to a board: the tutor talks the learner through an idea aloud in short sentences and draws it one small piece at a time, in step with its words. The learner watches and listens, and cuts in by voice or typing; the tutor answers on the same board and picks the topic up again. Learner-led by default, tutor-guided by choice; speech at 1.5× by default. Board items are placed by coordinates with a guard (ADR 0028). Everything said on a board is an ordinary reply in the conversation. Spec: docs/board-spec.md. Evidence: local branches prototype/edge-tts-latency, prototype/model-latency and prototype/board-placement.

## Notes

The board is a new screen, designed with Impeccable. The owner makes each new-ui child's mockup at docs/mockups/<issue-id>.html before that child runs.

## Decisions so far

All decisions are in the spec. Claude Sonnet at low effort was approved by the owner from manual runs.

## Fog

- Streamed MP3 chunk playback in Chrome, Firefox and Safari is unproven; Rabbithole-brd.7 proves it first.
- How long Microsoft keeps an idle edge-tts socket open is unknown.
- The 1.0–1.4 s latency budget for a spoken question is summed from separate benchmarks, never measured end to end.
- Defaults not tuned with the owner: 2.5 s speech timeout, 4 s tutor-guided waits, 150 ms cut-in, 300 ms end of speech.

title: The tutor writes sketches
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

The chat prompt gains the accepted (v10) sketch rule, word for word as the spec gives it, with its bars example and the 17 kinds, inserted after the visual guidance and before the Visual frequency sentence. The app's visual rules stay word for word; no rule balances sketches against visuals and no kind is capped. "…; never write a fenced media block." becomes "Draw a sketch in a ```sketch <kind> block; request a visual with a visual marker, a video with make_video and a discussion with a discussion marker."

Visual frequency governs sketches too:
- Often keeps its sentence and gains "Sketches sit alongside these visuals, so draw visuals as you normally would and add sketches wherever a section has a shape."
- Sparing becomes "draw a visual or a sketch only where it clearly helps".
- Only when asked becomes "draw no visual or sketch unless the learner asked for one"; the sketch rule stays in the prompt.
- Whenever the learner asks for a sketch, the tutor draws one.

The accepted prompt is the prototype branch's prototypes/sketch/integrated/sys-v10.txt.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The chat prompt carries the spec's sketch rule word for word, with the 17 kinds, before the Visual frequency sentence.
- [ ] The app's visual rules are unchanged.
- [ ] The media-block sentence is the positive one from the spec; "never write a fenced media block" is gone.
- [ ] Often, Sparing and Only when asked each carry their sketch wording from the spec, and asking for a sketch always gets one.
notes:
Defaults: the sketch rule (SKETCH_RULE) goes in every chat prompt path (app tools, text tools, no tools) right before the Visual frequency sentence. 'Whenever the learner asks for a sketch, draw one.' is a new sentence at the head of the shared asked-sentence in all three settings; the rest of Often matches sys-v10 word for word (diffed).
master's src/sketch/sketch.ts was 569 lines (over the 550 cap, red CI); moved line/quadrant/spectrum to src/sketch/quantities.ts, no behaviour change.

title: Expand a sketch into a visual in place
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Each sketch offers "Expand into visual". Expanding sends a normal visual request built from the sketch's title and items and the text it sits beside; the visual replaces the sketch in place. The sketch stays one switch away, as a replaced version does with a new version. The visual is an ordinary visual artifact tied to the sketch's place in the reply, so it comes back when the conversation reopens, with its visual parts and new versions like any visual. The control is in the sketch mockup.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] "Expand into visual" on a sketch sends a visual request built from the sketch's title, items and neighbouring text, and the visual draws where the sketch was.
- [ ] A switch moves between the expanded visual and its sketch.
- [ ] An expanded sketch shows its visual when the conversation reopens.
- [ ] The expanded visual has visual parts and new versions like any visual, and counts in the Figures list.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.1.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: the expanded visual is a row in artifacts with sketch='hidden'|'shown' at the sketch block's start offset; the switch flips it server-side so a reopen shows whichever showed last. A second Expand on the same sketch returns the existing visual (no new request). The request's intent/description list the sketch's screen-reader items; excerpt is ~half the excerpt limit of plain text on each side. Overview mode keeps no inline media, so no expand control there. Button weight follows the house Button (500) rather than the mockup's ld.css 600.

title: Ask about a sketch item
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Every drawn item of a sketch can be pointed at and asked about, the way a visual part can. Asking opens a branch from that item, carrying the sketch's title and the item's label.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.6.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Pointing at a sketch item shows it can be asked about, by mouse and by keyboard.
- [ ] Asking about a sketch item opens a branch carrying the sketch's title and the item's label.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.6.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: a sketch item branch stores start..end of its whole sketch block plus the item label (no artifact); the server re-parses the block and accepts only a drawn label, rebuilding the passage as 'title › label' (title 'Sketch' when absent). Briefs for sketch items are not saved (offsets shared with the whole sketch). Keyboard: one Tab stop per sketch, arrows/Home/End move, Enter asks. Mockup states 8 (Sending), 9 (New branch opens) and 11 (Touch) reuse the existing branch form, child conversation and :hover-after-tap, so no separate pairs were recorded.
Merged master (skt.5 build-in): Sketch splits into Sketch + SketchDrawing so the build choice is made when the fence closes; the build test now skips the ask hit areas. PR #175 green.
Reviewer defaults (PR #175): (1) Only kinds that draw hit areas can be asked about: flow and bars, the two the mockup draws. The kinds merged from skt.4/skt.9 (line, quadrant, spectrum, plot, sequence, equation, grid and later ones) only draw; without this, Enter on their items threw. The spec says every drawn item of a sketch can be asked about, so each other kind still needs a hit area shape (owner: mockup or a rule) and a follow-up ticket. (2) Going back to a sketch item's source now focuses the item; it used to report the source as unavailable. (3) Explain briefly is disabled while a branch is sending, as mockup state 8 draws (shared branch form). (4) Pairs for states 8, 9 and 11 recorded; in state 8 the app shows the house loading button where the mockup writes 'Preparing context…' as text, as for a visual part.

title: Sketches build in with the reply
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

A sketch fades in one item after another over about 0.5 s; with reduced motion it appears at once. Sketches follow the reply's reveal the way the text around them does. The look stays as the first sketch ticket built it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A sketch fades in item by item over about 0.5 s.
- [ ] With reduced motion a sketch appears at once.
- [ ] A sketch appears in step with the reply's reveal of the text around it.
notes: Defaults: only a sketch that arrives while its reply streams builds in (decided at mount); a saved reply's sketches show at once, like its text. Reduced motion is read with matchMedia at mount. Build: items start 300 ms apart in total (--step = 300/(n-1) ms), each fades 200 ms, so ~0.5 s. Flow lines and chevrons appear with the first item; each flow station, its label and its incoming arrow label are one item group.

title: Sketch kinds for maths and exchanges: plot, sequence, equation, grid
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Adds the plot, sequence, equation and grid kinds to the sketch module, so these blocks draw in replies like flow and bars. Their lines, from the spec (prototype syntax):

- plot: one or two `y = …` lines in x (+ - * / ^, sin cos exp log sqrt), then `x: min..max`.
- sequence: first line `actors: A | B | C`, then `A -> B: message` or `A: note`; who sends what, in order.
- equation: first line `eq: …` with symbols separated by spaces, then `symbol: meaning`.
- grid: rows of cells separated by spaces; `name:` above a grid captions it; a line holding only ×, =, + or → joins two grids, as in image × kernel = output.

The local branch prototype/sketch (prototypes/sketch/sketch.js) has a stand-in renderer that parses every kind; reuse its parsing, not its look.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.4.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A valid body of each of plot, sequence, equation and grid draws in a reply with one item per drawn element, each carrying its label; the title line and *star* focus carry through.
- [ ] A plot draws each curve over its x range and treats an expression outside its grammar as an error, never evaluating it as code; a sequence draws each actor once and each message in order between them; an equation links each annotated symbol to its meaning; a grid draws joined grids with their join sign and captions, and *star* cells as the focus.
- [ ] A body that matches no line of its kind, or a value out of its range, is an error: the reply hides that sketch and logs its kind and reason.
- [ ] Each kind draws in the light and dark theme palettes.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.4.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes: Defaults: grid lines are exempt from the eight-item limit (rows are cells, not items); each grid caps at eight rows. Text widths are estimated in the plain module (7.5px/char for 15px curve names, 8.5px/char for 14px sequence labels), so the plot area's right edge can differ from the mockup by a few px. Mockup differences left as artifacts: its .tbl grids carry a 16px margin from the shared line-diagram/ld.css table rule (app does not); the steep-plot curve name sits 4px higher in the mockup than the centred rule gives. Dark pairs in docs/verification/Rabbithole-skt.4/.

title: Sketch kinds for comparisons: compare, venn, pie
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Adds the compare, venn and pie kinds to the sketch module, so these blocks draw in replies like flow and bars. Their lines, from the spec (prototype syntax):

- compare: first line `vs: A | B`, then `aspect: A's value | B's value`.
- venn: two lines `set name: item, item`, then `both: item, item`.
- pie: `label: number`; shares of one whole.

The local branch prototype/sketch (prototypes/sketch/sketch.js) has a stand-in renderer that parses every kind; reuse its parsing, not its look.

This ticket builds the compare, venn and pie drawings of the mockup; line, quadrant and spectrum are the next ticket.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.3.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A valid body of each of compare, venn and pie draws in a reply with one item per drawn element, each carrying its label; the title line and *star* focus carry through.
- [ ] A pie shows each share as a percentage of the whole; a venn puts both-items in the overlap; compare draws one row per aspect under its two names.
- [ ] A body that matches no line of its kind, or a value out of its range, is an error: the reply hides that sketch and logs its kind and reason.
- [ ] Each kind draws in the light and dark theme palettes.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.3.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: venn wraps items at 8px/char (reproduces the mockup's wraps) but fits rings at flow's 7px/char (reproduces its 80px and ~132px ring heights within 1px); real text is not measured. A bar before any colon ends a compare aspect (pipe form). A repeated venn 'both' line merges. Unitless (or %) pie values summing to 100 are shown as written. A focused pie share stays muted, as in the mockup. Compare's vs: line does not count toward the 8-item limit. Palette gains a hairline role (--color-border) for compare row seams. Screen-reader name adds each kind's frame after the title. sketch.ts is at 460 of the 550-line check-size limit: the next three kinds will need a split.
Merged master (skt.5 build-in): compare rows, venn items and pie slices/rows carry --i so they build in item by item; the compare names, venn rings and set names come with the first item.

title: Sketch kinds for structure: cycle, stack, tree, timeline, parts
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

Adds the cycle, stack, tree, timeline and parts kinds to the sketch module, so these blocks draw in replies like flow and bars. Their lines, from the spec (prototype syntax):

- cycle: one stage per line, in order; the last leads back to the first.
- stack: one layer per line, top first, `name: note`.
- tree: an indented outline, two spaces per level.
- timeline: `when: event`, in order.
- parts: first line `whole: name`, then `part: what it does`.

The local branch prototype/sketch (prototypes/sketch/sketch.js) has a stand-in renderer that parses every kind; reuse its parsing, not its look.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A valid body of each of cycle, stack, tree, timeline and parts draws in a reply with one item per drawn element, each carrying its label; the title line and *star* focus carry through.
- [ ] A cycle leads its last stage back to the first; a stack draws its first line on top; a tree nests by two spaces per level; a timeline keeps its order; parts draws its whole with each part and what it does.
- [ ] A body that matches no line of its kind, or a value out of its range, is an error: the reply hides that sketch and logs its kind and reason.
- [ ] Each kind draws in the light and dark theme palettes.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.2.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: new kinds measure text with a 14px Atkinson Hyperlegible Next advance table (focus words +5%, non-ASCII 7px) instead of flow's 7px/char, so columns land within 1-3px of the mockup; flow untouched. Wrapped labels balance their lines (cycle-8 mockup). A cycle needs 2+ stages; parts needs a whole and 1+ part; every line must match. 'left: right' splits at the first colon not followed by a digit (10:30 stays whole). Cycle height is last baseline + 10 (mockup's 8-stage draws 160, app 162). Tree items carry level; the screen-reader list nests.
Merged master (skt.5 build-in): each new kind's item is one <g style=--i:k> (ring + labels; parts' whole is item 0), stack li carries --i and .sketch-stack > * joins the build selector.

title: Sketches draw in replies: flow and bars
description:
Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-skt). Decision: ADR 0027.

A ```sketch <kind> block in a reply draws as a sketch the moment its fence closes, with no model call. This tracer bullet supports two kinds:

- flow: `A -> B` or `A -> B: arrow label`; steps, cause and effect; may branch and rejoin.
- bars: `label: number`, with an optional unit after the number.

A body has one item per line, an optional first line `title: …` and one or two words wrapped in *stars* as the focus. A new plain sketch module turns a kind, a body and the theme palette into a drawing with one item per drawn element (its label), or an error naming what is wrong: an unknown kind, an empty body, lines matching nothing, or values out of range. Later tickets add the other 15 kinds to it.

Reply rendering shows a sketch instead of a code block: no copy button, never the source. While the fence is still open it shows a placeholder the size of a small sketch. A broken sketch is hidden and logged. Screen-reader text comes from the title and items. Colours come from the theme tokens visuals receive, light and dark, and a theme switch redraws sketches. Sketches are not in the Figures list or Fig N numbering.

Look: sketches blend into the chat and stay compact, since a reply carries many; designed with Impeccable to the mockup. The local branch prototype/sketch (prototypes/sketch/sketch.js) has a stand-in renderer that parses every kind; reuse its parsing, not its look.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A ```sketch flow or ```sketch bars block in a reply draws a sketch with its title, focus and items; no code block or copy button shows.
- [ ] A sketch block whose fence is still open while the reply streams shows a placeholder, then the sketch once it closes.
- [ ] A sketch with an unknown kind, an empty body, lines matching nothing or out-of-range values is hidden, its source never shown, and logged with its kind and reason.
- [ ] A screen reader reads each sketch from its title and items.
- [ ] Sketches take the current theme colours in light and dark and redraw on a theme switch.
- [ ] Sketches are not counted in the Figures list or the Fig N numbering.
- [ ] Matches the mockup at `docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.1.html` in layout, elements, copy, sizes and spacing, with its colours mapped to theme tokens by role; the owner approves any difference.
notes:
Defaults: palette passed as theme CSS variables (role mapping from the mockup: ground=background-body, ink=text-primary, muted=text-secondary, seam=border-emphasized, focus=rabbithole-paper), so a theme switch recolours live. Any line that fails makes the whole sketch an error (hidden). Negative bar values are out of range. Flow label wrap estimates 7px/char. The Expand into visual control in the mockup belongs to skt.7 and is not built here. Gap above a sketch keeps the app's 16px paragraph rhythm (mockup renders 15px).
PR #168 is open. Its CI is red only on node scripts/check-size.mjs, which fails on origin/master too: src/chat/Passage.tsx 557, src/shell/ChatPage.tsx 558, src/styles/media.css 585 and src/styles/states.css 744 lines. title: Sketches: small diagrams the tutor writes, drawn instantly
description:
The tutor writes sketches, fenced ```sketch <kind> blocks from 17 fixed kinds, and the app draws them instantly in its theme with no model call (ADR 0027). Sketches cover the smaller points inside a section, about 30 tokens each, beside the visuals that carry the main ideas; the app's visual rules stay unchanged and Visual frequency governs both. Learners can ask about any sketch item and expand a sketch into a visual in place. Spec: docs/sketches-spec.md. Evidence: local branch prototype/sketch.

## Notes

The sketch look is new UI, designed with Impeccable to blend into the chat and stay compact. The owner makes the mockup at docs/mockups/Rabbithole-skt.1.html before Rabbithole-skt.1 and Rabbithole-skt.7 run.

## Decisions so far

All decisions are in the spec; the tutor wording is the owner-accepted v10.

## Fog

- Release condition (owner): a Codex benchmark of the accepted rule with all 17 kinds has zero failed sketches, judged with the owner in a planning session, not by a ticket.
- The Sparing and Only when asked wording is a default, not benchmarked.

title: Give the i-have-adhd skill to every tutor reply
description:
## What to build

Every chat reply follows the i-have-adhd skill (github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd, the skills/i-have-adhd SKILL.md, MIT). Add it as a fixed tutor skill beside the teaching and natural writing skills, using the SKILL.md body as written. Leave out only the YAML frontmatter, which is install metadata.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
design: Store the skill text the way the natural writing skill is stored, and add it to the tutor skills that precede the tutor style, so it reaches the tool, text-tool and no-tool prompts and child branches through the same path. Keep the upstream MIT copyright notice in the repo next to the stored skill text, not in the prompt. The skill adds about 2,400 Claude tokens to every chat request; this was accepted.

- Every chat system prompt contains the i-have-adhd skill text exactly once: with app tools, with text tools, without tools, and in a child branch.
- The skill sits with the other tutor skills, before the tutor style, and the learner-edited tutor style still comes last.
- The stored text matches the upstream SKILL.md body apart from the removed frontmatter.
- The upstream MIT copyright notice ships with the stored skill text.
notes: Pinned upstream ayghri/i-have-adhd at f3e783bae5f4820416492091b3abeb670616c23a (HEAD on 2026-11-25). Stored as server/media/prompts/i-have-adhd.md (body only) with i-have-adhd-LICENSE.txt; ADHD_SKILL sits after HUMANIZER_SKILL in TUTOR_SKILLS. Tool-path budget test allows ADHD_SKILL.length on top.

title: ADHD-friendly reading skill for the tutor
description:
Add the i-have-adhd skill (github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd, MIT) to the skills every chat model gets, the same way the natural writing skill is given.

Decisions so far: the owner compared 12 single-turn learning questions on Claude Sonnet and Codex gpt-6.1-terra with and without the skill. Claude replies were about a third shorter and easier to scan; Codex wording got simpler. The skill goes in as written, not adapted, always on, and reply layouts stay at the model's discretion (no layout triggers added).

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Eval note: the comparison appended the skill after the tutor style on the no-tool prompt path, single turn. The owner chose the humanizer-style placement (before the tutor style) anyway and skipped a re-run.

title: Codex usage-limit error ends the reply right away
description:
When the ChatGPT account hits its usage limit mid-reply, the chat spins forever (until the 5-minute stall timeout) with no message, so the learner thinks the app is broken.

Evidence (Rabbithole's Codex log, turn 01a2121e-5428-7161-b189-0d80844c3632, 2026-11-25 09:51:47-09:52:34): Codex treated the limit as a stream disconnect ('stream disconnected before completion: The ChatGPT user has reached their Subscription Sharing usage limit. Ask the user to try again after their usage limit resets or use an API key instead.'), retried 5 times, and sent an app-server 'error' notification after each attempt. It never sent turn/completed afterwards. The Codex provider ignores 'error' notifications and only reports failures from turn/completed, so nothing reached the chat.

What to build: when Codex sends an 'error' notification for the active turn that is a usage limit, or says it will not retry, the reply fails at once and the chat shows Codex's own short reason, like other Codex failures do. Retryable errors that are not limits keep waiting as today.
design: Fail on the first usage-limit error, not after Codex's retries: retrying a usage limit cannot succeed (decided with owner). Capture one real 'error' notification payload first; the log shows the event name but not its fields (expect error.message, possibly codexErrorInfo and willRetry). Prefer a structured limit flag if present, fall back to the message text. Claude provider is out of scope: the same hang there is unconfirmed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A usage-limit 'error' notification for the active turn ends the reply immediately with status failed and an error naming Codex's reason; no wait for turn/completed or the stall timeout.
- An 'error' notification Codex will not retry ends the reply the same way.
- A retryable non-limit 'error' notification does not end the reply; a later turn/completed still finishes it normally.
- 'error' notifications for another thread or turn are ignored.
- The partial reply stays saved after the failure.
- A test replays the logged sequence (repeated 'error' notifications, no turn/completed) and sees the failure with the limit message.
notes:
Real payload check: the logged turn's final error had codex_error_info 'other' with the limit only in the message, so the provider fails on willRetry === false, codexErrorInfo 'usageLimitExceeded', or /usage limit/i in error.message. On failure it interrupts the turn so Codex stops retrying. Test extends the existing Codex failure test in test/providers/codex.slow.mjs (Codex adapter tests are slow-suite).
PR #166 open, CI test+secrets green. Slow-tests workflow triggered on the branch; codex.slow.mjs passed locally (9/9).

title: Oversized PDF attachments are refused with a clear message
description: Text attachments over 1 MB are refused, but the PDF path returns before that check and has no page or image limit. A 600-page textbook under the 50 MB upload cap sends all its text and every page image in one prompt, holds every page image in memory while preparing, and saves the text with the message. The reply then fails at the provider after a long wait.
design: Check the page count early, before rendering pages. Reuse the existing 1 MB text limit and pick an image cap the supported providers accept.
acceptance_criteria:
- A PDF whose extracted text is over the text attachment limit is refused with a 400 asking the learner to attach the pages they need.
- A PDF with more page images than the cap is refused the same way, before all pages are rendered.
- A refused send saves no message and no attachment, like an oversized text file.
- PDFs under both limits attach as before.
notes: Defaults: image cap 100 per PDF (Anthropic API max images per request; Codex accepts more). Text limit reuses the 1 MB text-file limit, counted over the PDF's extracted text parts. Limits are checked after each page, so pages past the crossing are never rendered. Cap is per PDF, not per turn.

title: Audit fixes (2026-11-25): Windows endpoints, PDF limits, small server bugs, dedupe
description:
Fixes from the 2026-11-25 whole-repo audit. All children are independent and can run in any order.

Decisions so far:
- Rolling TinyTeX without a checksum and the Windows hard kill with its 10 s stale lock stay recorded shortcuts, not tickets.
- The Windows endpoint bug was simulated on Linux by removing process.getuid; no Windows machine was used.

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/45578578862. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Only failure: openai-switching.slow.mjs compared the whole root tree before/after branching; rrp.2 added branchPreviews (derived from children). Ignore branchPreviews like branch-compaction.test.mjs does.

title: Move existing Windows data into the install folder
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "Windows install folder".

On first launch, when `data` holds no database and `%APPDATA%\rabbithole` exists, the app moves the old folder's contents into `data` before the server starts: a rename on the same drive, otherwise a copy that is checked before the old folder is deleted. If the move fails, the app logs it, keeps the old folder and uses it for this run. Window layout and preferences survive, since the old folder also held Electron's profile.
acceptance_criteria:
- An upgrade from a version that kept data in `%APPDATA%\rabbithole` opens with every learning tree, add-on and preference in place.
- The old folder is deleted only after the data is safely in `data`.
- A failed move leaves the old folder untouched and the app still opens with the learner's data.
notes: Defaults: move lives in desktop/shell.mjs moveOldData, run before app.setPath('userData'). Copy only on EXDEV (other rename errors such as a locked file fall back to the old folder). Copy goes to data.moving, checked by entry and size, then renamed into data, so a half copy never leaves trees.sqlite in data. An empty data folder gives way; a non-empty one without a database makes the move fail (old folder used). No move when RABBITHOLE_DATA_DIR is set. Failure to delete the old folder after a good move is logged only.

title: Choose the Windows install folder; data lives inside it
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "Windows install folder".

Per ADR 0025: the NSIS installer becomes assisted and per user, letting the learner change the location, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Rabbithole`, and always installs into a folder named Rabbithole there (a path already ending in Rabbithole is used as is). The install folder holds the app files and `data`; the desktop app passes `data` to the server, so add-ons go there too. Electron's profile moves inside `data`, set before Electron starts. Uninstall removes app files and offers "Also delete my learning trees, videos and add-ons", ticked by default; a silent uninstall deletes `data`; the uninstall the updater runs never deletes `data`. The Windows smoke test follows the new folder and also installs, writes a file in `data`, installs again silently as an update, checks the file survived, uninstalls silently and checks the folder is gone. Linux is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- The installer lets the learner choose a location and installs into a Rabbithole folder there, defaulting to today's location.
- Learning trees, add-ons and the app's own profile live in the install folder's `data`.
- An update keeps `data`; an uninstall with the box ticked removes the whole install folder; unticked keeps `data`.
- The Windows smoke test proves the update and the uninstall.
- Linux installs behave as before.
notes: Defaults: own folder page via customPageAfterChangeDir (not allowToChangeInstallationDirectory, whose StrContains check would install straight into any path merely containing 'Rabbithole'); suffix rule skipped on updates so old Programs\rabbithole-desktop installs update in place. Electron userData = data itself (it shared %APPDATA%\Rabbithole with the server before, so ins.6 can move one folder). RABBITHOLE_DATA_DIR env still wins over the install data folder. Uninstall keep-data path deletes top-level entries except data in place instead of electron-builder's rename-into-TEMP busy check (that would move gigabytes and fails across drives).

title: First-launch progress bar while the app starts
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "First-launch progress bar".

The starting page shows a thin progress bar under "Starting…" only when the data folder held no database before this start. It eases toward 90 % over about 20 seconds, slowing near 90 %, and jumps to 100 % when the server is ready, before the window shows the app. The status line stays the polite live region; the bar has a progressbar role without a value. Reduced motion advances it in a few steps without animation. A start failure hides the bar and shows the existing failure text.
acceptance_criteria:
- A first launch shows the bar moving toward done and completing when the app opens.
- Later launches show no bar.
- A start failure shows the failure text with no bar.
- Under reduced motion the bar changes without animating.
notes: Defaults: first launch = no trees.sqlite in the data folder (RABBITHOLE_DATA_DIR or dataDir()) checked before spawn; main.mjs adds body classes 'first'/'ready' to starting.html like showError does; bar is CSS-only (20s ease-out keyframe to scaleX(.9), steps(4) under reduced motion, hidden when pre#status shows).

title: Windows install check runs first in the Desktop build workflow
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "Windows check in the Desktop build workflow".

A new first job on a Windows runner, needed by every other job, runs the app's own install code for Claude Code and Codex as the server would, then confirms the tool finder finds each and that `--version` runs, failing the run at once otherwise. It does not sign in. The owner pushes and triggers the workflow (AGENTS.md); agents edit it locally.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every other Desktop build job waits on the Windows install check.
- The check fails the run when either install fails or the app cannot find the installed tool.
notes: Defaults: check lives in scripts/install-check.mjs (cliInstaller + findCli + launchArgs, no server start); job install-check on windows-latest with Node 24; wheels-check needs it, and every other job already descends from wheels-check, whose failure() gate skips them when the check fails. Not run locally (would install both CLIs on the owner's machine); first proof is the owner's next Desktop build run.

title: Sign in to Claude without a terminal
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "Installing Claude Code and Codex".

A Sign in button for an installed but signed-out Claude Code, in first-run setup and Settings Connections, runs `claude auth login` in the background, opens the sign-in address it prints in the default browser and polls `claude auth status` until signed in, then reloads models. If the command needs a terminal (not yet proven), the button falls back to showing the command to run. The "Run claude in a terminal" copy goes. Codex sign-in is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pressing Sign in opens Claude's sign-in page in the browser and setup moves on once signed in.
- If sign-in cannot run without a terminal, the learner sees the command to run instead.
- No copy asks the learner to run claude in a terminal.
notes: Defaults: probed 'claude auth login' without a TTY (throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR): it runs, opens the browser itself with a localhost-callback sign-in, prints a short claude.ai/oauth/authorize link and waits ('Paste code here if prompted'). So the app does not open the printed link too (would give two tabs, and that link may be the paste-a-code flow); it shows it as an 'Open the sign-in page' fallback link. No address within 20 s, or an exit before one, falls back to showing 'claude auth login'. Client reloads models every 3 s while waiting (models() runs claude auth status). Model menu now points to Settings; signed-out reply error and startup log hints no longer ask to run claude in a terminal.

title: Install Claude Code and Codex from the app
description:
Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-ins), Implementation Decisions, "Installing Claude Code and Codex".

A server route installs `claude` or `codex` by running its official installer without a terminal and reports through the existing downloads model, one install per tool at a time. Commands: Claude `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` (PowerShell) or `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`; Codex `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex"` or `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh`, both with `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`. Output goes to the server log; the row shows indeterminate progress that completes on exit. Success clears the cached tool lookup and the client reloads models; failure shows the last output line and Retry. The tool finder also searches `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin`, and finds a tool installed while the app runs. First-run setup and Settings Connections show Install, the command for the learner's system (PowerShell on Windows) and the official page link. The startup log hint for a missing Claude Code points at Install. No administrator rights.
acceptance_criteria:
- Install for a missing tool runs its official installer for the learner's system and shows progress like a download.
- When the install finishes, setup moves on without pressing Check again.
- A failed install shows its last output line and a Retry button.
- The shown command is PowerShell on Windows and shell on Linux.
- Codex installed by its Windows installer is found without a restart.
notes: Defaults: route is POST /api/downloads/install/<claude|codex>; it runs beside the add-on queue (downloads.now) so an install never waits behind a video-tools download, and Retry on its row re-runs it at once. No explicit cache clear: cliPath already re-detects a missing CLI on every call, so a finished install is found on the client's model reload. Progress is plain indeterminate (installers report no percent). Shown command comes from the server (installCommand) in /api/models providers.<id>.command. Codex startup hint also switched from npm to its official installer.

title: One-click Claude and Codex, a first-launch progress bar and a chosen Windows install folder
description:
First-run setup and Settings install Claude Code and Codex with a button running the official installers in the background, and sign in to Claude without a terminal (ADR 0024). The Desktop build workflow first checks those installs on a Windows runner. First launch shows a progress bar. The Windows installer lets the learner choose the location of one Rabbithole install folder holding app and data, kept on update, deleted on uninstall unless unticked (ADR 0025).

Spec: docs/one-click-providers-and-windows-install-folder-spec.md

title: Buttons for short settings
description:
Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-vis), Implementation Decisions, "Settings buttons".

Rule: a fixed choice of five options or fewer shows as buttons (the design system's segmented control, as the library panel uses); more than five shows as a dropdown. Video mode (Quality, Saving) becomes buttons. Effort pickers in chat, smart model and suggestion settings follow the rule by the selected model's option count, including Default and Custom; choosing Custom opens the typed effort field as today. Lists of the learner's own items, such as model profiles and models, stay dropdowns. Labels, saving and error states are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- Video mode shows Quality and Saving as buttons and saves the one pressed.
- An effort picker with five or fewer options shows buttons; with six or more, a dropdown.
- Choosing Custom still opens the typed effort field.
- Model profile and model lists stay dropdowns.
notes: Defaults: shared src/settings/Choice.tsx counts every option (Follow, Provider default, unavailable saved effort, Custom…) and shows SegmentedControl (hug layout) for <=5, Selector otherwise. Buttons sit in a design-system Field so Video mode keeps its visible label and description and the effort error status stays. Visual frequency (spec) has no setting in code yet, so not touched here.

title: Changed pulse and crossfading scene changes
description:
Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-vis), Implementation Decisions, "Play".

While a continuing step runs, the step helper watches the root for changed attributes and text and, once the motion settles, briefly outlines the nearest visual part of each changed element. Scene changes crossfade: a still copy of the old scene sits over the root while `show` redraws, then fades out as the new scene fades in. No pulse animates under reduced motion. The visual worker prompt tells stepped visuals to show each step's change in the picture, with at most a short label per step.
acceptance_criteria:
- After a continuing step, the visual part of each changed element is outlined briefly.
- During a scene change the old scene stays visible until the new one fades in.
- Under reduced motion nothing pulses or fades.
- The visual worker prompt asks for picture-first steps with at most short labels.
notes: Defaults: pulse = a 900ms fading accent ring (.tt-pulse, sandbox.html) laid over the nearest data-part ancestor-or-self of each changed node, or the changed element itself when it has none; only after an animated continuing step settles (ms > 0), none when the next step interrupts. Crossfade = root clone (data-part stripped, inert, aria-hidden, keeps root id for styles) absolutely placed over root inside .tt-steps (now position: relative), both fading over the full step duration; show runs at once. Canvas content copies blank (shortcut noted).

title: Play for stepped visuals
description:
Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-vis), Implementation Decisions, "Play".

The step helper adds Play/Pause beside Previous and Next with the same keyboard wiring. Play starts only on the learner's click, never on render, scroll into view or a new version. Each step's motion lasts about 1.5 to 2.5 seconds, chosen from what the step changes, then holds about 1 second; Play stops on the last step and starts again from the first. Previous and Next animate with a shorter eased transition (default about 0.6 seconds). Previous, Next or a step key during Play pauses it. With reduced motion durations are 0 but Play still holds each step for the full step time. Play pauses when the visual leaves the viewport or the page is hidden.
acceptance_criteria:
- Steps advance on their own only after Play is clicked, and Play stops on the last step.
- Pause, Previous, Next or a step key stops Play.
- Steps receive longer durations during Play than when stepped by hand.
- Under reduced motion Play still pauses on each step with duration 0.
- Play pauses when the visual is out of view or the page is hidden.
notes: Defaults: manual step 600ms; Play motion = 1500ms + 100ms per node the step changes (counted with MutationObserver.takeRecords during the measuring pass), capped at 2500ms; hold 1000ms. Play sits below Previous (grid row 2, col 1) beside the Step n of m indicator, no CSS change. Pressing Play moves to the next step at once. tt-show (host opening a picked step) also pauses Play.

title: Visual display controls and a leaner visual worker prompt
description:
Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-vis), Implementation Decisions, "Visual controls".

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-vis.1.html (every control and variant, light and dark; covers this ticket and its display-controls sibling).

Adds the display controls in the same style as the input controls: readout (label and live value with unit), result card (correct, incorrect, neutral), status (info, success, warning), legend (swatch and label per series, using the series inks) and table (styled like reply tables). The visual worker prompt drops its guidance on building and styling controls, keeping only the catalogue; a worker may still build a control the kit lacks with the same variables.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each display control renders in light and dark and is announced sensibly by screen readers.
- A readout updates when its value changes.
- The visual worker prompt no longer carries the old control styling guidance and lists every control in the kit.
notes: Defaults: rh-result title comes from label (not title, which would add a tooltip); display controls expose value (readout value, result/status text); result and status are role=status aria-atomic and set variant/label live; reset restores readouts, results and statuses (incl. initial variant/label); legend inks in order blue, yellow, pink, green, cycling; rh-table only adds a caption from label and styles the worker's native table like reply tables (no numeric alignment class); rh-readouts groups readouts.

title: Visual input controls for every visual
description:
Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-vis), Implementation Decisions, "Visual controls".

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-vis.1.html (every control and variant, light and dark; covers this ticket and its display-controls sibling).

The sandbox defines custom elements, globals like `stepThrough`, rendering native elements in the light DOM, configured by attributes (`label` required, `variant`, range or options), exposing `value`, firing `input` and `change`, keeping values across a theme change, never parts. This ticket: button (primary, secondary, quiet; button group), toggle, switch, slider with value and unit, number with stepper, choice list (segmented up to five, radio list beyond), text field and reset (restores every control and fires `reset` on the root). Base sandbox CSS styles them with the theme variables and fonts, light and dark, focus rings, disabled states, wrapping at phone width. The visual worker prompt gains their catalogue entries. Saved visuals render as before.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each input control renders with its label, reports its value, fires input and change, and works by keyboard with a visible focus ring.
- Controls follow a theme change without losing their value and are never picked as visual parts.
- Reset restores every control in the visual and fires reset on the root.
- The visual worker prompt lists these controls, their variants, attributes and events.
- Visuals saved before the kit render as before.
notes: Defaults: rh-button has no value (fires native click); reset fires one bubbling 'reset' on #visual (reaches window) and no per-control input/change; choice value is the option text; number clamps on change; all rh-* elements skip part picking; fonts via --font-family-body and --rabbithole-font-reading tokens (token lint bans literal names); display controls (readout/result/status/legend/table) left to vis.2.

title: Visual controls, Play for steps and buttons for short settings
description:
Every visual gets a kit of ready-made visual controls, styled by the app, so visuals appear sooner and controls look the same. Stepped visuals get Play beside Previous and Next with slow readable motion, a short hold, a "this changed" pulse and crossfading scene changes. Settings shows any fixed choice of five or fewer as buttons.

Spec: docs/visual-controls-play-and-setting-buttons-spec.md

title: Going back to a parent lands on the branched passage
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Back to the passage".

The back button, origin chip and each ancestor breadcrumb open the parent with a target: the passage of the child on the path from that ancestor to the current conversation. The parent scrolls it into view, lights it up as a reveal does, and moves focus to it. The target uses the existing multi-frame hold for message and figure targets, so the chat's scroll-to-bottom cannot win. A free branch targets the parent reply that was latest when it was created. A missing passage falls back to its reply, then to today's behaviour. Contents and the map are unchanged. Reduced motion shows the light-up without fading.
acceptance_criteria:
- Back, the origin chip and a breadcrumb each land on and light up the passage leading toward the current conversation, and focus moves there.
- The view stays on the passage after the parent finishes loading and laying out.
- Going back from a free branch lands on the parent reply that was latest when it was branched.
- A passage no longer in the reply lands on its reply instead.
- Contents and the map open conversations as before.
notes: Defaults: back, origin chip and breadcrumbs pass the child's reply as the message target alongside its passage; the existing 12-frame message hold prefers the revealed mark/[data-reveal] (or the visual/discussion [data-artifact]) inside that reply and falls back to the reply when absent. Reduced motion: the reveal light-up is a static highlight with no fade today, so nothing changes. The existing 'Saved source passage is unavailable' notice stays when falling back.

title: One-off cleanup of meta and "none" explored concepts
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Ghost trees".

A one-off cleanup, recorded in the cleanups table like earlier ones, re-names the explored concept of every root conversation whose explored concept is "Lecture learning" or "none", using the new naming with its first question and attachment text. The two concepts are deleted once no conversation or evidence uses them. Today that is the deadlocks and parsing lecture trees and the Prolog tree.
acceptance_criteria:
- After startup, no conversation has "Lecture learning" or "none" as its explored concept, and both concepts are gone.
- The deadlocks and parsing lecture trees no longer show each other as ghost trees.
- The cleanup runs once and never again.
notes: Defaults: cleanup runs at every startup until recorded (cleanups row 'rename-activity-explored-concepts'); needs the quick thinking model, else it warns and retries next start. Only the explored concept changes, titles stay. Names compare case-insensitively. A root whose re-naming fails stops the run unrecorded; already-fixed roots stay fixed. Bad names are filtered from nearestConcepts and from replies. Concepts dropped only when no tree, evidence or observation row uses them (aliases, topics, links go with them).

title: Explored concepts name the subject, never the activity
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Ghost trees".

Two lecture PDF trees (deadlocks, parsing) both got the explored concept "Lecture learning" because the title job saw only the typed question, so a ghost tree joins them; another tree got a concept named "none". The title job receives the first message's attachment text, up to the first few thousand characters, from text already extracted at send. Its naming prompt says the explored concept is a subject of study, never the activity (avoid "lecture learning", "homework help", "explaining a file"). "none" or an empty name means no explored concept; no concept named "none" is created. Nearest-concept reuse stays, so real same-subject trees still link.
acceptance_criteria:
- A root conversation whose first message attaches a PDF gets its explored concept from the PDF's subject, not from "help me learn this lecture".
- A naming reply of "none" leaves the conversation with no explored concept and creates no concept.
- Two trees on truly the same subject still share an explored concept.
notes: Defaults: attachment text for the title job = first message's non-image prepared parts joined, cut to 4000 chars; it also feeds the nearest-concept lookup; 'none' (any case) as concept is treated as no concept.

title: Visual frequency setting: Sparing, Often or Only when asked
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Visual frequency".

A new app-wide setting stored like video mode: `sparing`, `often` (default) or `only-asked`, read and written through a settings route, shown in Settings next to Video mode as three buttons (the design system's segmented control). The tutor's visual marker rule gains one sentence chosen by the setting: Often encourages a visual for each distinct concept a picture helps in a longer reply, never forcing one; Sparing keeps today's guidance; Only when asked draws none unless the learner asked. An explicit request is honoured at every level. Videos and the video offer are untouched. A change applies from the next reply, like a tutor style edit.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh install reads Often; a saved choice survives a restart.
- Settings shows the three choices as buttons and saves the one pressed.
- The tutor instructions for the next reply carry the sentence for the saved choice.
- Video behaviour is unchanged at every level.
notes: Defaults: the frequency sentence is its own 'Visual frequency:' paragraph right after the tutor rules (both marker and fenced-block paths), before the verdict/discussion rules, so it stays in the cacheable fixed prefix; tutorSystem without the field uses Often. Settings section 'Videos' renamed 'Visuals and videos' holding Visual frequency above Video mode. Prompt size budget test allows the Often sentence on top.

title: Plainer explanations: familiarity-first teaching and plain brief explanations
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Teaching skill".

Replace the teaching skill's "Aim for what the idea is and why it exists…" line with the spec's guidance word for word (pitch to familiarity, intuition before the textbook version for new ideas, varied openings, analogies only now and then, formal terms once the idea has landed, precise version for those who know it). Same for every provider; the default tutor style is unchanged. The single brief and brief batch prompts share one rule: two or three short sentences every time, plain everyday words, explain the term in context rather than summarise the reply, no unexplained jargon; the "target, not a hard limit" wording goes. The brief call is told the learner's familiarity with the suggestion's concept when known; unknown means write for a newcomer. Briefs stay on the quick thinking model. Not measured in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every provider's tutor instructions carry the new teaching guidance, and the old "Aim for…" line is gone.
- Single briefs and brief batches use the same plain-words, two-or-three-sentence rule.
- A brief for a suggestion with a known concept familiarity passes that familiarity to the brief call.
notes:
Defaults: kept 'Once they understand, say so and point at what comes next.' after the replaced Aim-for sentence. Softened analogy.md to 'now and then, never by habit' so it no longer contradicts the new guidance (spec story 3, glossary). Known familiarity = concept has at least one observation (an unobserved concept's 0.3 prior and neighbour guesses count as unknown → newcomer). Brief batches carry no familiarity: they start from the tutor's marks before quick thinking names concepts, so none is known yet. Tutor prompt size budget test allows the +525 chars.
PR #144 green. First CI run failed only in test/media/video-runaway.test.mjs (fake-timer flake, unrelated, passes locally); rerun passed.

title: Suggestion marks may name their concept
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Concept marks".

Tutors write wiki-style aliases such as `[[safe state|safe]]` and the reply shows `safe state|safe`. Per ADR 0023, `[[concept|shown]]` is an official suggestion mark for every provider: the reply shows only the shown words, underlined, and the concept is stored as that suggestion's concept. The parser splits on the first `|` or `\|` (tables); an empty side makes it a plain suggestion of the other side. Streaming and saving strip the concept and the bar, so offsets and passages use shown text only. Quick thinking names concepts only for marks without one. The notes rule in the tutor prompt describes when to use the form. The fallback marking path uses the same parser.
acceptance_criteria:
- `[[a|b]]` and `[[a\|b]]` show `b`, underlined, with concept `a` stored for that suggestion.
- `[[a]]` shows `a` and leaves its concept to quick thinking, as today.
- Streamed text never shows a bar or a concept, even when a chunk ends inside a mark.
- A mark inside a Markdown table row renders the table cleanly.
- Quick thinking is asked to name concepts only for marks without one.
notes: Defaults: a mark cut off at its line end with a bar also shows only its shown words; [[|]] (both sides empty) leaves no text and no passage; the concept is bounded like other note names (noteName). Fallback path needs no change: it reads the same diagramReply/stripMarkers output.

title: The usage table records concept merges
description:
Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tex), Implementation Decisions, "Merge recording".

Every merge confirmation fails because the usage table's task check has no `merge`, so ADR 0022's automatic merges and its one-time cleanup have merged nothing (0 merges, 0 aliases). A schema migration rebuilds the table to accept `merge`, keeping every existing row, as earlier migrations rebuilt it. The one-time cleanup was never recorded as finished, so it reruns at the next startup by itself.
acceptance_criteria:
- An existing database keeps every usage row after the upgrade and then accepts a merge row.
- A confirmed merge after a reply merges the two concepts and keeps the other name as an alias.
- Usage history shows the merge calls under "Concept merges".
notes: Default: fresh databases create usage_events with 'merge' in the task check; existing ones get a rebuild after the ended column, keeping all 13 columns by name. Criterion 3 needs no code: UsageDashboard already labels merge 'Concept merges'.

title: Plainer teaching, more visuals, concept marks, honest ghost trees and back to the passage
description:
The teaching skill pitches every explanation to the learner's familiarity, intuition first for new ideas, the same for every provider. Brief explanations are always two or three short sentences of plain words. A Visual frequency setting (Sparing, Often by default, Only when asked) encourages more visuals. `[[concept|shown]]` becomes an official suggestion mark (ADR 0023). The title job names a subject, never an activity or "none", and a cleanup fixes the bad ghost trees. Merges are recorded so ADR 0022 runs. Going back to a parent lands on the branched passage.

Spec: docs/plainer-teaching-concept-marks-and-return-to-passage-spec.md

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/45352957541. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Only failure: endpoint-switch.slow.mjs expected Claude/Codex prompts without look_up_concept; the app now offers it (LOOKUP_RULE). Updated the expectation, matching test/http/tutor-style.test.mjs.

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/45349187578. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Only failure was endpoint-switch.slow.mjs: test expected tool list lacked look_up_concept (LOOKUP_RULE added in mkg.2). Test-only fix; slow run 45351439307 green. PR #137.

title: Settings shows the app version and clearer web search add-on copy
description:
Spec: docs/search-window-version-and-map-cleanup-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nav), Implementation Decisions, "App version; Web search add-on copy".

The version appears only in the update banner. Settings' foot shows "Rabbithole <version>"; in the desktop app it adds "· Latest is <version>" and an Update button that does what the banner's Install does when a newer version exists, or "Up to date" when the launch check found nothing newer, and nothing extra after a failed check. In a browser the version comes from the server with no update controls. The web search add-on's enables text becomes the spec's wording.
acceptance_criteria:
- Settings' foot shows the running version in the desktop app and in a browser.
- With a newer version it shows the latest version and an Update button that installs it like the banner.
- With nothing newer it shows "Up to date"; after a failed check nothing extra; in a browser no update controls.
- The sidebar rail's Settings dot is unchanged.
- The web search add-on says exactly the spec's text; the custom endpoint offer and Search settings text are unchanged.
notes: Defaults: version comes from /api/state for both browser and desktop; the desktop shell passes app.getVersion() as RABBITHOLE_VERSION because CI stamps only desktop/package.json. Launch check 'update-not-available' becomes update stage 'current' (no banner, no rail dot). Settings foot shows 'Latest is X' for every non-current stage, Update button only when Install is valid (available, failed). Copy change has no test (constant).

title: The map's corner list is removed
description:
Spec: docs/search-window-version-and-map-cleanup-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nav), Implementation Decisions, "Map corner list".

The map's top-left list of the trunk and its direct children cannot be clicked, shows no deeper conversations and can cover a quarter of the map. InkLegend and the data function only it uses are removed with their styles and tests. The sidebar's Contents stays the list of conversations.
acceptance_criteria:
- The map renders without the corner list.
- Nothing left uses the removed component, its data function or its styles.

title: Floating search window over every conversation
description:
Spec: docs/search-window-version-and-map-cleanup-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nav), Implementation Decisions, "Search window (Window, Opening a result)".

The Astryx command palette becomes a floating window, centred, about 760 px wide and up to 80% of the viewport's height, opened with Ctrl+K or the sidebar's Search button. Results are grouped by learning tree with address, title and highlighted snippet. It traps focus, moves with Up and Down, opens with Enter and closes on Escape, returning focus. An empty query shows the six most recent learning trees. Opening a result opens the conversation in the focused chat scrolled to the matched message with the words briefly highlighted.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-nav.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Ctrl+K and the sidebar's Search button open the window; Escape closes it and returns focus.
- Results show grouped by learning tree with address, title and a highlighted snippet.
- Up and Down move through results and Enter opens one at the matched message; title and passage matches open at the top.
- An empty query shows the six most recent learning trees, and no match shows a clear message.
- A screen reader hears the result count and the selected result.
notes: Defaults: kept the Astryx CommandPalette as the window (it already traps focus, moves with Up/Down via aria-activedescendant, opens with Enter, closes on Escape returning focus and announces the result count), sized min(760px, 100vw-32px) by 80vh and restyled per the mockup. Ctrl+K or Cmd+K opens it from anywhere, composer included, like Ctrl+Shift+O. Recent = six newest-created roots with day and conversation count; Enter on one reopens the tree as saved (like the Library). A match opens its conversation in the focused chat: reply matches scroll to and focus the message, title/passage/question matches scroll to the chat title; matched words get a CSS Custom Highlight for 2 s (no fade: ::highlight cannot transition). Group headings are the tree title, the current tree suffixed ' · This tree'; same-titled trees share a heading (shortcut). Visible count line is aria-hidden since the palette's own live region announces the count. Sidebar button renamed 'Search conversations' (tooltip names Ctrl+K).

title: Search finds every conversation's text
description:
Spec: docs/search-window-version-and-map-cleanup-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nav), Implementation Decisions, "Search window (Index, Matching, Route)".

Search matches root titles only. An FTS5 trigram table holds each conversation's title, passage and branch question and each completed message's plain text with markers removed, kept up to date in the same transactions and built once by a migration. Words of 3+ characters match anywhere in any order; shorter words match titles by prefix; a trigram-overlap fallback forgives typos. Title matches rank first and the current tree's results first. The route returns up to 50 grouped results with address, titles, matched field, a ~160-character snippet with match ranges and the message id. The existing palette shows these results with their snippet; the client waits 120 ms after typing and cancels stale requests. Confirm FTS5 trigram works under the desktop build's Electron Node.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parts of words in any order match, and a small typo still matches through the fallback.
- Branch titles, passages, questions and reply text are all found; markers are never matched or shown.
- Deleted conversations are absent and new conversations and replies are found once saved.
- Results group by learning tree, title matches first, the current tree first; snippet ranges point at the match.
- Existing data is indexed by a migration, and the index works in the desktop build.
notes: Defaults: one result per conversation (its best row: title first, then FTS5 rank, newest on ties); groups ordered current tree first, then by best result. Short words (<3 chars) must prefix a title word for title rows and are ignored for passage/question/reply rows. Typo fallback keeps texts sharing >=50% of the query's trigrams. Index = search_texts content table + external-content FTS5 trigram table; SQL triggers keep titles, branch passages/questions and deletes in step, JS indexes completed messages (plainText of stripMarkers) in the same transaction. Desktop server runs on the bundled Node 24 (scripts/desktop-stage.mjs), not Electron's Node; CI's Node 24 runs the FTS5 test. Palette picks open the branch via openTree(root, focus); scroll-to-match is Rabbithole-nav.2.

title: A search window for every conversation, the app version, a cleaner map and clearer web search copy
description: Search finds only learning tree titles. A SQLite FTS5 trigram index searches every conversation's titles, passages, questions and replies, fuzzy and as the learner types, shown in a floating search window. The map's corner list is removed, Settings shows the app version with update state, and the web search add-on's copy says which models need it. Spec: docs/search-window-version-and-map-cleanup-spec.md.

title: Typing stays open while the tutor answers
description:
Spec: docs/reply-reading-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-rrp), Implementation Decisions, "Typing while the tutor answers".

The composer's text box is disabled while a reply is in flight. It stays editable; Send is disabled and Enter does nothing until the reply ends. The draft is kept and never sent automatically. Attach stays disabled during a reply and Stop is unchanged. The first-question screen follows the same rule.
acceptance_criteria:
- During a reply the learner can type in the composer; Send is disabled and Enter sends nothing.
- The draft is unchanged when the reply ends and is not sent automatically.
- Attach stays disabled and Stop stays available during a reply.
- The first-question screen behaves the same way.
- A screen reader announces the box as editable and Send as unavailable.
notes: Defaults: in the focused chat Stop keeps taking Send's place during a reply (Stop unchanged), so Send is unavailable there by absence; the first-question screen shows a disabled Send. Enter is held via onKeyDown (Shift+Enter and IME commit untouched). useAttach.add refuses while disabled so paste/drop into the now-editable field cannot attach. A send now clears the draft only if it still equals the sent question, and the first question's typed-ahead text moves to the new conversation's draft.

title: Branch preview shows the question and the start of the child's reply
description:
Spec: docs/reply-reading-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-rrp), Implementation Decisions, "Branch preview".

Pointing at a branched passage shows little, and nothing for the learner's own selections. The client receives each branch's question as well as the start of the child's first reply. Any branched passage shows a card with the question on one line, then the first paragraph of the child's first reply cut at about 280 characters at a word boundary with "…". While the child has no reply, the card shows the brief if one exists, otherwise only the question.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pointing at any branched passage, from a suggestion or a selection, shows the question and the child's first-reply excerpt.
- A long first paragraph is cut at about 280 characters at a word boundary with "…"; a short one is untouched.
- While the child has no reply the card shows the brief, or only the question when there is none.
- Clicking still opens the branch's conversation; overlapping branches keep their picker.
notes: Defaults: tree payload carries branchPreviews keyed by child ({question, preview}); suggestion passages no longer carry preview. Excerpt takes the first top-level markdown paragraph (falls back to the whole reply), cut at 280. Question line truncated by CSS ellipsis. Brief lookup now matches any underline by start/end.

title: Reply usage sits behind a closed Usage button
description:
Spec: docs/reply-reading-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-rrp), Implementation Decisions, "Usage disclosure".

Every reply shows a line of token counts. It is replaced by a muted "Usage" button in the reply footer that expands the same line, closed by default and on every visit. Visual progress text shows only while a visual is pending or failed, in the focused chat and the map's conversation nodes.
acceptance_criteria:
- A finished reply shows a closed "Usage" button instead of the token line; expanding it shows the same line.
- The button is closed again after reload or navigation.
- No lasting visual success text remains in the focused chat or conversation nodes; pending and failed text stays.
- Token stats in the conversation details are unchanged.
notes: Defaults: Usage button is an Astryx ghost sm Button in the reply footer, disclosure via aria-expanded; open state is plain useState so it resets on remount (reload/navigation). Visual footer/node count already shows only while a visual is pending (visualsReady); failed state stays on the visual's own badge. The visual frame's 'Interactive' badge is kept: it is the frame's state badge (tutor-tools spec story 55), not footer progress text.

title: Bolded terms and briefed selections become suggestions
description:
Spec: docs/reply-reading-polish-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-rrp), Implementation Decisions, "Suggestion marking; Briefed selections become suggestions".

NOTES_RULE's suggestion paragraph gains the spec's sentence about marking a term it would bold. When a brief explanation is saved for a learner-selected passage, the passage becomes a ready suggestion of that reply with the brief attached and an empty concept, so opening it records no familiarity evidence. A passage matching an existing suggestion adds nothing.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- The notes rule's suggestion paragraph contains the spec's sentence; nothing else in the rule changes.
- Saving a brief for a selected passage adds a ready suggestion with that brief and no concept.
- A passage that matches an existing suggestion adds nothing and keeps that suggestion's brief.
- The briefed passage underlines like any suggestion, shows its brief on hover and opens the branch box on click; overlapping marks still work.
notes: Defaults: a passage matches an existing suggestion by exact start/end. A briefed selection is added only to a ready suggestions row, or a new ready row when a finished reply has none (suggestions off); a pending row is skipped because finishSuggestions replaces its passages; a failed row stays failed. Reopening an already-saved brief for a selection also adds it. The brief route returns the reply's updated suggestions row so the client underlines at once. The tutor prompt size guard in test/media/tutor-style.test.mjs grows by exactly the new sentence.

title: More suggestions, branch previews, quiet usage and typing while the tutor answers
description: Long replies arrive with few suggestions because the tutor bolds terms instead of marking them; the notes rule gains a loose sentence, and a briefed selection becomes a suggestion. Pointing at a branched passage shows the question and the start of the child's first reply. Token counts move behind a closed Usage button, and the message box stays editable while the tutor answers. Spec: docs/reply-reading-polish-spec.md.

title: Stats panel under the knowledge graph
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Stats panel".

Nothing under the graph shows how knowledge grows. A new panel shows (a) concepts met and known over time, (b) topics ranked by mean familiarity, (c) fading concepts, (d) misconceptions newest first with whether they cleared, and (e) an activity heatmap of learner messages per day. One read-only route computes them from existing tables. Choosing a concept selects it in the graph and opens its detail.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-mkg.7.html
acceptance_criteria:
- The panel shows the five sections with figures matching the stored data.
- Known means familiarity at or above the level the graph draws as full; fading means once known and now below it.
- Choosing a concept anywhere in the panel selects it in the graph and opens its detail.
- No new stored data; the route is read-only.
notes: Defaults: learner messages per day = recorded 'chat' usage events whose reply message still exists (messages carry no timestamp; no new stored data). 'Met' = earliest evidence or observation per concept; concepts with no recorded time count as met from the start. Growth points are weekly, ending now. Known = rounded familiarity >= 0.8 (the graph's full ring), shared as KNOWN in server/familiarity.mjs. A misconception clears on a later observation at level 3 (Explains it) or above. Choosing a concept selects it and focuses its detail (mockup). Topic swatches skipped: hues land with Rabbithole-mkg.6. Misconception rows show the learner message text instead of the mockup's branch chip.

title: Knowledge graph shows topic colours, hulls and related topics nearby
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Graph colour, hulls and placement".

Topics are same-coloured circles pinned evenly round a circle. The server sends a 2D anchor per topic from a PCA of topic centroids, scaled to the map, with the even circle as fallback for topics without embeddings. The force layout uses these anchors. Each concept takes its first topic's hue; hues spread round the wheel in anchor-angle order and mix toward the theme's ink. Each topic draws a soft, low-opacity hull with its label behind its concepts.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-mkg.6.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Topic anchors are deterministic and related topics sit near each other; a topic without embeddings falls back to the even circle.
- Each concept wears its main topic's hue; concepts without a topic stay neutral.
- Neighbouring topics get neighbouring hues, readable on light and dark variants.
- Each topic has a soft hull with its label behind its concepts; familiarity keeps its ring fill.
notes: Defaults: server sends unit-scale PCA anchors only for topics with embeddings (graph.anchors); the client scales them by its existing ring radius and keeps the even-circle slot for topics without one. PCA via Gram-matrix power iteration, embeddings of another dimension skipped, fewer than two placeable topics place none. Hues from 250deg in anchor-angle order (mockup). Hull = convex hull of members plus the topic centre so the centre label sits inside, 44px round stroke, opacity 0.14 in both variants (CSS light-dark cannot vary opacity). Labels moved before concepts in DOM so they sit behind. Key gains 'Colour: topic'.

title: Duplicate concepts and topics merge automatically
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Automatic merge (ADR 0022)".

When the post-reply call records new concepts or topics, each new name is compared by embedding with existing ones; pairs at or above 0.85 become candidates. One quick thinking tool call per reply confirms, per pair, whether they name the same concept or topic. Confirmed pairs merge through the existing store merge, keeping the name with more evidence (older on a tie) and storing the other as an alias; topics move their concepts to the kept topic. The "Merge concepts" button, dialog and route are removed. Tune the threshold against the owner's pairs in the spec's Further Notes.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models). Blocked by the memory ticket only because both change the post-reply job.
acceptance_criteria:
- Candidate pairs from one reply reach a single confirmation call; unconfirmed pairs stay apart.
- A confirmed concept merge keeps the name with more evidence, or the older on a tie, and keeps the other as an alias.
- A confirmed topic merge moves its concepts to the kept topic.
- Each merge is logged with both names and the kept one, and the call is metered.
- The "Merge concepts" button, its dialog and its route are gone; the knowledge page renders without them.
notes: Defaults: thresholds tuned on the owner's graph with the local MiniLM embedder: concepts 0.85 (7 of 9 known duplicates; Artemis/Artemis program 0.74 and Perseverance/Perseverance rover 0.66 missed; 46 of 655 names get a candidate, 150 at 0.75), topics 0.70 (3 of 4 known pairs; Orbital mechanics/Astrodynamics 0.42 unreachable; 8 candidate pairs over 74 topics). Evidence for the kept name: a concept's evidence + observation rows, a topic's concept count; older = lower id. Topic merges keep the old name in a new topic_aliases table so addGraph resolves it. Topic names are embedded on each check (only when the reply adds a topic), not stored. Confirmation: confirm_merges quick tool returning pair numbers in 'same'; runs after the suggestions row settles, metered as task 'merge' attributed to the reply (Usage label 'Concept merges'); failures log WARN 'merge skipped' and merge nothing. Logs: INFO 'concept merged'/'topic merged' with names and kept fields (added to the log field allowlist). Without the local embedder nothing merges.

title: One-time cleanup merges existing duplicate concepts and topics
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Automatic merge (one-time cleanup)".

655 concepts and 74 topics hold plain duplicates. A one-time background cleanup after startup backs up the database file, then checks every existing concept and topic through the automatic merge path in batches, and records that it ran.
acceptance_criteria:
- The database file is backed up before any merge.
