- Existing duplicates confirmed by the quick thinking model are merged with aliases, in batches, without blocking the app.
- The cleanup never runs again once recorded.
notes: Defaults: cleanup runs only from main (createApp mergeCleanup option, off in tests like briefs), needs the local embedder and suggestions enabled. Candidates use the same thresholds as per-reply merges over every concept and topic; confirm calls hold up to 20 pairs, metered as task 'merge'. Quick model: chat default's quick thinking model, same subscription rule as suggestions. Backup trees.sqlite.backup-merge-<date>-<id>.sqlite via VACUUM INTO, taken only when pairs exist, before the first call. merge_cleanup table records completion; a failed run logs WARN 'merge cleanup skipped', is not recorded and retries next startup.

title: Messages embed in the background so recall answers fast
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Background message embedding".

Each search_conversations call embeds up to 256 pending messages before searching, taking about 30 seconds. A background job embeds each message when it completes, chunked as recall does today; a startup job embeds older unembedded messages in small batches, yielding between batches. search_conversations embeds only the query; still-unembedded messages are found by keyword only.
acceptance_criteria:
- A completed message is embedded in the background without delaying the reply; a failure logs a warning and leaves it unembedded.
- On startup older unembedded messages are embedded in batches until none remain.
- search_conversations embeds only the query and finds unembedded messages by keyword.
notes: Defaults: batch size 16 (BATCH in server/tools/recall.mjs), setImmediate yield between batches; one 'embeddings' job in ctx.jobs so stop/settled cover it. Trigger: every reply finish (embeds the learner message and a completed reply) plus app startup. A failed batch logs 'message embedding failed' and ends the run; the next trigger retries.

title: look_up_concept covers several concepts in one call
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Concept lookup".

The graph reaches the tutor only through names in the typed message, so an attachment's concepts are never looked up. look_up_concept takes concepts, a list of 1 to 10 names or short descriptions, and returns per item the nearest concepts with familiarity (or a guess, or unknown), topics and links. The tutor rule gains the spec's loose sentence. Offered only where the tool is offered today.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- look_up_concept accepts 1 to 10 concepts and refuses an empty or longer list.
- The result has one entry per requested item; an item with no match returns unknown.
- The tutor rule contains the spec's sentence about looking up concepts the neighbourhood does not cover.
- The automatic concept neighbourhood is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: result shape {lookups:[{query, concepts}|{query, familiarity:'unknown'}]}; items looked up one embed call each (shortcut noted in recall.mjs); LOOKUP_RULE appended like MEMORY_RULE only when look_up_concept is in tree.tools; lookUpConcept in neighbourhood.mjs (also used by title job) unchanged.

title: The quick thinking model edits the memory note after a reply
description:
Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mkg), Implementation Decisions, "Memory note writing".

The post-reply quick thinking call gains an optional memory field: a list of edits in the shape update_memory_note takes (add, rewrite, delete). Its input gains the current note, the memory rule's limits and the spec's instruction. Edits go through the same editor, so MEMORY_NOTE_LIMIT (8,000 characters) applies. Each write records the message that caused it, and that reply's footer shows a muted "Memory updated" mark that opens the memory note in Settings. When suggestions are off the call does not run; the tutor's tool stays.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- A memory edit returned by the post-reply call changes the note and records the message that caused it.
- An empty or missing memory field changes nothing; an edit that grows the note past the limit is refused.
- A reply with a recorded write shows a muted "Memory updated" mark, without note text, that opens the memory note in Settings.
- The tutor's update_memory_note tool and rule are unchanged, and its writes also show the mark.
- Memory edits are logged and the call stays metered as today.
notes: Defaults: writes recorded as messages.memory flag (additive nullable column), set by saveMemoryNote(text, message) for the tutor tool (turn.reply) and the post-reply call; learner saves pass none. Memory edits run in both post-reply variants (naming and full marking), applied before the suggestions row settles so the poll shows the mark. Mark is a ghost sm Button 'Memory updated' in the reply footer opening Settings > models focused on #memory-note. Logs: INFO/WARN 'suggestions memory edit [refused]' with id, conversation, cause; never note text. MEMORY_LIMITS split out of MEMORY_RULE with identical text, shared with the call.

title: Memory note writing, concept lookup, fast recall and a clearer knowledge graph
description: The memory note was never written in 234 replies: the quick thinking model now may edit it in the call it already makes after each reply, and a reply that changed it shows "Memory updated". look_up_concept takes several concepts and the tutor is told loosely to use it for concepts the neighbourhood misses, such as an attachment's. Messages embed in the background so search_conversations stops taking about 30 seconds. Duplicate concepts and topics merge automatically (ADR 0022) with a one-time cleanup. The graph gets topic colours, hulls and PCA-placed topics, and a stats panel. Spec: docs/memory-recall-and-knowledge-graph-spec.md.

title: The tutor knows a video's narration and leans on visuals for hard ideas
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "Narration in later turns; Visual rule".

After a video the tutor knows only its id, title and description. The artifact metadata later turns carry for a ready video gains a narration field with the full narration script as plain text; cut code and plan details stay out. The visual marker rule and the legacy visual rule each gain the loose sentence from the spec about leaning on more visuals for ideas that are hard to grasp.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- Later turns carry a ready video's full narration script as plain text, and no cut code or plan details.
- Visuals' metadata is unchanged.
- Both visual rules contain the spec's sentence about hard ideas, word for word, and nothing like a quota.
notes: Default: narration joins each cut's narration with a blank line, read from the saved plan; a video with no readable saved plan carries an empty narration.

title: A video records how long it took to make
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "Video time".

The elapsed clock lives only in memory. The video job's start time and the time it became playable are saved on the artifact, and each stage's start and end are saved with its usage rows. A Retry or new version overwrites them; export does not. The video's Usage shows "Made in 6 min 12 s" above the table and gains a Time column per stage.
acceptance_criteria:
- Start and playable times survive a restart and end at playable, not at export.
- A Retry or new version restarts the clock.
- The video's Usage shows a "Made in …" line above the table and a Time column per stage.
- A video made before this change shows no time line.
notes: Defaults: 'playable' = the video saved ready (finishVideo), the moment every cut plays live; the start is the job start in runVideo (same instant as the in-memory startedAt), so Retry, new version and tool-wait resume all restart it. Columns artifacts.started/playableAt (ms), usage_events.ended (moves with each record). Stage time = last call end - first call start per stage+model row. Format '42 s' / '6 min 12 s'.

title: The piece writer reuses, improves or draws a new piece with a recorded reason
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "Piece reuse".

The piece writer keeps one call per object and now receives the chosen piece's full source. It returns reuse (no new output), improve (a new version of the same piece) or new, with a one-line reason. Improve stores a new version under the same piece identity: future videos get the newest, saved videos keep the version they were made with. Each choice is saved with the video and logged with its reason, so the reuse rate can be counted per video.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- The piece writer's input holds the full source of the saved piece the plan chose.
- Reuse creates no new piece; improve creates a new version of the same piece; new creates a new piece.
- Saved videos keep drawing the piece version they were made with after an improve.
- Every choice is saved with the video as piece, choice and reason, and the log line names the choice and reason.
notes: Defaults: 'one call per object' read as keeping today's single set-piece call per video (no extra calls). The plan's adopted piece is carried as recurringObjects[].pieceId (resolved from find_pieces matches) and offered first in that object's library matches, marked chosen, with full source. 'variant' is replaced by 'improve'; every choice needs a one-line reason. Improve updates the pieces row (name, look, source, forms, roles, true colours, parts, embedding) after copying the old row into new table piece_versions; the audit improve path archives too. Saved videos keep their version because each video's data.pieces holds its own module. Choices saved as data.pieceChoices [{piece, choice, reason}] only when the library was offered; log line 'media piece piece= choice= reason='.

title: One-time cleanup folds duplicate pieces into one each
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "Piece reuse (one-time cleanup)".

Earth, Moon, MarsGround and six engine parts each exist twice. A one-time cleanup, run at startup after the migration, folds pieces sharing a name into one piece: newest as the current version, the others as older versions, video links repointed. It backs up the database file first and records that it ran.
acceptance_criteria:
- The database file is backed up before the cleanup changes anything.
- Pieces sharing a name become one piece holding every version, newest current.
- Videos that used any of them still play with the version they were made with.
- A second start changes nothing.
notes: Defaults: 'sharing a name' = exact name match. 'Newest' = latest improved time (tie: later saved). Folded pieces' current rows and their own piece_versions move under the newest piece; their piece_videos links move to it; parts lists in pieces and piece_versions repoint, and a part folded into its own piece is dropped so pieceTree cannot recurse. Run record: new table cleanups(name, at) with row 'fold-duplicate-pieces'; its absence triggers the cleanup. Backup (same VACUUM INTO as the upgrade backup, logged by main.mjs) is taken only when duplicates exist, reusing an upgrade backup made on the same start.

title: The video planner sees the nearest saved pieces before writing looks
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "Piece reuse".

Pieces duplicate because the plan writes every recurring object's look before the library is searched. Matching moves before looks are written: for each recurring object the server takes the 5 nearest pieces by name and role, as nearestPieces does now, and gives the planner their names and short looks, never their source. The planner's rule: adopt a saved piece's look when it is the same real object; describe a new look only for a different object or when the saved look cannot serve this video.
design: The prompt wording in the spec is a proposal, not benchmarked. Use it as written; tests check the rule text and the call input, never a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).
acceptance_criteria:
- The planner input lists, per recurring object, up to 5 nearest saved pieces with name and short look and no source.
- The planner rule tells it to adopt a matching saved piece's look and name it as the piece to start from.
- With an empty library the planner input and behaviour are as today.
notes: Defaults: matching runs through a new planner tool find_pieces(name, role), offered only when the library has pieces and an embedder works; it embeds 'name: role' and returns the 5 nearestPieces as {name, look} (look as saved, untruncated). add_object gains optional 'piece' (validated against that object's matches) and refuses a look until find_pieces ran for the object. Text-mode planners get no tool results, so they keep today's tools and write looks as before. Embed failure warns and returns no matches.

title: A video's new version follows the learner's instruction
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "New version of a video".

The video card's menu gets the same "Try a new version…" item and box. The video's planner receives the current plan and the instruction, or the different-approach line, and cuts are redrawn from the new plan. The current playable cuts, plan and narration move into the single previous slot so the switch brings them back without redrawing. Video mode is read when the new version starts, as for a Retry.
acceptance_criteria:
- The video card's menu offers "Try a new version…" with the same optional instruction box.
- The planner receives the current plan and the instruction, or the different-approach line when there is none.
- The previous playable cuts, plan and narration are kept and "Previous version" switches back without redrawing.
- The new version uses the video mode in force when it starts.
- Exported MP4 files are untouched.
notes: Defaults: the previous slot JSON now stores {id,attempt,source,title,description,duration} for both kinds; a video's switch swaps its id and attempt back, so its library entry, cut folder, usage and any exported MP4 (all keyed by id/attempt) follow it with nothing redrawn or moved. Switch allowed only on a ready video, as for visuals. The planner gets the current plan as currentPlan inside its JSON task, plus a note; instruction line mirrors visuals. The video card's existing ArrowPath button became the trigger of a small Versions menu (Try a new version…, Previous version) using the shared useNewVersion box; no mockup since the look is kept. Video mode is already read at job start in generateVideo.

title: A visual's new version follows the learner's instruction
description:
Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvv), Implementation Decisions, "New version of a visual".

"Try a different version" redraws blind: the old source is wiped before the call and the learner cannot say what to change. The menu item becomes "Try a new version…" and opens a small inline box with an optional instruction (at most 500 characters), "Make new version" and Cancel. The regenerate route accepts the instruction, validated at the trust boundary. The current source, title and description move into a single previous slot before the redraw; the model receives the current source plus the instruction, or the existing "take a different approach" line when there is none. A "Previous version" switch swaps current and previous.
acceptance_criteria:
- "Try a new version…" opens an inline box with one optional instruction field, keyboard accessible, submitting with Enter.
- The visual call receives the current version's source and the learner's instruction; with an empty instruction it receives the different-approach line instead.
- The replaced version is kept in a single previous slot; a second new version replaces it.
- "Previous version" appears in the visual's menu while a previous version exists and swaps current and previous, so the next new version builds on the one the learner chose.
- Visual parts, steps and branches follow whichever version is current.
- An instruction over 500 characters or of the wrong type is refused; the validation retry path is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: previous slot is a nullable artifacts.previous JSON column {source,title,description}, filled only for visuals (videos keep their id-change path for nvv video ticket). Clients see only hasPrevious: true. Switch is POST /artifacts/:id/previous, allowed only on a ready visual with no drawing job. Instruction validated on trimmed length (<=500) and type string; absent/null/empty means none. The current source reaches the model as raw lines after 'currentVersion:' on the first call only; the validation patch retry is unchanged. Badge state mapping moved into visualProgress.visualBadge to keep VisualFrame under the 550-line cap.

title: New versions, piece reuse, video time and more visuals for hard ideas
description: "Try a new version…" on a visual or video takes an optional instruction and is made from the current version, keeping one previous version a switch away. The video planner sees the nearest saved pieces before writing looks, and the piece writer reuses, improves or draws new with a recorded reason; a one-time cleanup folds the 9 duplicated piece names. A video records how long it took to make, later turns carry its narration, and the visual rule gains a loose sentence that hard ideas deserve more visuals. Spec: docs/new-versions-pieces-and-video-time-spec.md.

title: Notes rule splits into groundwork, suggestion and end section paragraphs
description:
Spec: docs/brief-batch-markers-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bbm), Implementation Decisions, "Notes rule".

The tutor wrote wiki-style marks such as [[Prolog facts|fact]], so the reply showed "A Prolog facts|fact states a relationship". The cause is the groundwork rule "use its name exactly", which sits at the end of the one-paragraph notes rule and reads as a rule for every mark. NOTES_RULE becomes the benchmarked text in the spec, word for word: an opening paragraph, then "Groundwork notes:", "Suggestion notes:" and "End section:" paragraphs. The groundwork naming sentence moves into the groundwork paragraph, and the suggestion paragraph gains "Inside the brackets write only words of the reply, nothing else." It keeps its leading blank line in the tutor instructions. In replays of the Prolog turn on Terra this text gave 0 of 24 replies with pipe marks; paragraphs without that sentence gave 3 of 8. The marker stripper does not change: [[x|y]] is not an intended format and is not parsed.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tutor instructions for every provider carry the notes rule exactly as written in the spec: an opening paragraph, then labelled Groundwork notes, Suggestion notes and End section paragraphs.
- The groundwork paragraph holds the rule to use a concept neighbourhood name exactly; no other paragraph mentions neighbourhood names.
- The suggestion paragraph says to write only words of the reply inside the brackets.
- Marker stripping and reading are unchanged, including [[x|y]], which keeps its words as written.

title: Brief batch streams marker text and retries missing terms once
description:
Spec: docs/brief-batch-markers-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-bbm). Decision: ADR 0021.

The brief batch stops calling the write_briefs tool and becomes a plain text quick thinking call. For each term, in the order given, the model writes one line [[brief: term]] with the term exactly as given, then its paragraph. The batch prompt keeps its style and data sentences and its term list, and replaces the tool instruction with the benchmarked sentence, word for word: "For each term, in the order given, write one line [[brief: term]] with the term exactly as given, then its paragraph on the following lines. Write nothing else." The server reads the stream and saves each brief explanation as soon as the next marker line, or the end of a completed call, closes it. After the call ends, whether it completed, failed or was cut off, any requested term without a saved brief is asked for once more in a new batch call holding only those terms. A term still missing after that is written on demand when its suggestion is opened, as today. The write_briefs quick tool is removed; every other quick thinking job stays a tool call.
acceptance_criteria:
- A brief batch saves each brief explanation while the call is still streaming, once the next [[brief: term]] line closes it; the last brief is saved when the call completes.
- A marker is a whole line [[brief: term]]; its paragraph runs to the next marker line, trimmed. Text before the first marker, a term that does not exactly match a requested term, and an empty paragraph save nothing.
- Each brief is saved under every suggestion of the reply whose term matches, and never replaces a saved brief or one being written on demand.
- A batch that fails, is cut off, or completes without some terms keeps every brief it closed, then makes one retry call asking for only the missing terms, read and saved the same way. There is no second retry.
- A suggestion whose brief is still missing after the retry gets one on demand when opened; opening during a running batch starts the on-demand call as today.
- Every batch call, the retry included, is metered as brief usage, and the batch records no familiarity.
- A batch that leaves terms unsaved after its retry logs a warning with the cause.
- The write_briefs quick tool no longer exists; marking suggestions, recording verdicts and naming conversations still answer through their tool calls.
notes: Defaults: batch uses the plain-text INSTRUCTIONS of on-demand briefs (no tool wording); marker lines are matched after trimming the line; items join with newline; the unsaved-after-retry warning reads 'left briefs unsaved' and logs a count, not term names, to keep learner text out of logs; a term whose suggestion got an on-demand brief meanwhile is not retried.

title: Brief batch markers and a structured notes rule
description: The brief batch stops calling the write_briefs tool and streams [[brief: term]] text (ADR 0021): each brief explanation is saved as soon as the next marker or the end of a completed call closes it, and terms a batch missed, after a failure, a cut-off or a skip, are retried once before falling back to on-demand briefs. This fixes the 2026-11-23 failure where Codex Luna could not find the write_briefs tool hidden inside Codex's exec tool and saved nothing, and lets the first briefs land within seconds instead of after the whole 7 to 15 second call. The tutor's notes rule becomes three labelled paragraphs (groundwork, suggestion and end section) with the benchmarked wording in the spec, which stops the groundwork naming rule from leaking into suggestion marks as [[Prolog facts|fact]]. Pipes stay unparsed. Spec: docs/brief-batch-markers-spec.md.

title: Depth stops on the conversation node
description:
Spec: docs/fork-inks-and-depth-stops-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fki).

Each conversation node on the map shows depth stops under its address chip: one porcelain ring per level below the trunk, joined by a line, the last ring filled, like a transit stop row. Depth is the number of address parts after the trunk (1.2.3 is depth 2). The row has no cap, no run-in line and no number; it grows with depth. Sizes from the mockup: 6px rings with a 1.5px porcelain stroke, 11px apart, a 1.5px porcelain joining line. The row is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the address chip stays the exact place.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fki.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Every conversation node below the trunk shows one ring per level under its address chip, joined by a line, with the last ring filled; the trunk shows none.
- A depth-9 node shows nine rings; there is no cap, run-in line or number.
- The row does not make the card band wider or taller.
- The depth-1 marker is visibly distinct from the "Responding" activity dot.
- The row is hidden from assistive technology.
- The rings read clearly in every theme in light and dark.
notes: Defaults: stop row is absolutely positioned 3px under the chip (out of flow) so the band never grows; fits the 8px band padding even with a one-line title on a 28px sm button. Ring fill is the card surface (--color-background-surface), strokes --rabbithole-paper, matching the mockup's raised/paper.

title: Sibling lines get their own vertical run
description:
Spec: docs/fork-inks-and-depth-stops-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fki).

Branch lines leaving one card currently share the vertical run at the gutter centre, so the line drawn last covers its siblings. Each sibling line whose vertical run would overlap another gets its own lane beside it. Lanes are ordered by the current vertical position of the child cards, so lines never cross, and are recalculated live while the learner drags a card. Routing keeps its shape (sideways, 45 degree turn, vertical run, 45 degree turn, sideways), 7px lines and round caps. Lane assignment needs all siblings' positions, so it is computed where the map knows every node position and handed to each line.
acceptance_criteria:
- Branch lines from one parent whose vertical runs share a gutter each take a separate vertical run, so no line covers another.
- Lines from one parent never cross each other; dragging a child card past its sibling swaps their lanes.
- Lanes update live while a card is dragged and stay correct after the drop and after reopening the map.
- A lone line, or a line in a gutter of its own, keeps the gutter centre as today.
- Lines to a child left of its parent and to a child stacked above or below it in the same column also get separate lanes.
- Lines keep 7px weight, round caps and 45/90 degree turns, and lanes never let two 7px lines touch.
notes: Defaults: lane spacing LANE=12px (7px line + 5px gap), lanes centred on the mean of the overlapping runs; lane assignment computed by MeasureLanes inside ReactFlow from the store (handle rings + card boxes), shared to Branch through a Lanes context; ghost lines share it. Lanes are not squeezed to fit narrow gutters (shortcut comment).

title: Each child takes its own ink at every fork
description:
Spec: docs/fork-inks-and-depth-stops-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fki).

Siblings at every fork take different branch inks. Children of the trunk keep taking inks 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, ... in address order. Below the trunk, the children of a conversation on ink p take "the three inks other than p in ascending order, then p" by sibling index, repeating; an only child keeps its parent's ink. Ink stays derived from the existing address walk, so every surface that reads it follows: map branch lines, card bands and address chips, fold stubs, passage underlines and their chips, the Contents route strip, ghost-tree dots and visual-part outlines. The map's line key keeps listing the trunk's direct children with their inks, relabelled from "Branch family inks" to "First branches". Themes keep four inks.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fki.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- The trunk's children take inks 1, 2, 3, 4, 1 in address order, as today.
- Children of a conversation with siblings take the three inks other than their parent's in ascending order, then the parent's, repeating: under ink 2 a fork of three gets 1, 3, 4; under ink 3 a fork of four gets 1, 2, 4, 3.
- An only child keeps its parent's ink, so a chain without forks stays one colour; once it gains a sibling, both take the fork rule.
- Adding a later sibling never changes the ink of earlier siblings that already had a sibling.
- Map branch lines, card bands, address chips, fold stubs, passage underlines and their chips, the Contents route strip, ghost-tree dots and visual-part outlines all show the conversation's new ink.
- The map's line key lists the trunk's direct children with their inks under the label "First branches".
- Existing learning trees show the new inks with no data migration.
notes: Defaults: library volume spine uses the same fork inks (kept in sync with conversationAddresses, as its test requires). Contents route strip code unchanged: third-column siblings still continue their elder sibling's line in the elder's ink; each station keeps its own ink.

title: Fork inks and depth stops
description:
Inks are chosen at every fork instead of once per branch family, so siblings on the learning tree map always read apart, like the trunk's children do today. An only child keeps its parent's ink, so a chain without forks stays one line. Themes keep four branch inks. Sibling lines leaving one card each take their own vertical run, ordered so they never cross, and follow the cards while dragging. Each conversation node shows depth stops under its address chip: one porcelain ring per level below the trunk, the last filled, with no cap. Lines stay 7px and full colour at every depth. See the spec.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fki.1.html (panel C is the chosen design; panel D records the rejected cap).

title: The same run rebuilds and re-pins the Linux wheels
description: The one-button Desktop build run (upd.3) also keeps the Linux wheels current. Unlike the sandbox pin, the installed app reads the wheel pins when it installs video tools, so they must be in the commit the installers are built from. First the run compares the pycairo and manimpango versions the setup scripts pin with the wheels on the fixed wheels release, and rebuilds them only when they differ, reusing the wheels workflow rather than copying it. When the wheels were rebuilt, it commits their URLs and SHA-256 hashes, taken from the uploaded files, and builds the installers from that commit; upd.3's sandbox pin and release tag follow on top. The wheels release keeps the wheels of older versions, so an app that pins them can still install video tools; the wheels workflow therefore adds new files to that release instead of deleting and recreating it. The wheel pin commit lands on master even if master moved, the same way as upd.3's pin, and stays there if the installers then fail, since the wheels it names exist.
acceptance_criteria:
- When the pinned pycairo or manimpango version differs from the released wheels, the run rebuilds the wheels before building the installers.
- When the versions match, the run does not rebuild the wheels and leaves their pins as they are.
- After a rebuild, the wheel URLs and SHA-256 hashes from the uploaded files are committed before the installers are built, and the installers are built from that commit.
- The wheels of older versions stay on the wheels release, so an installed app that pins them still installs video tools.
- A failed wheel build publishes nothing and changes no pin.
- The wheels workflow no longer deletes the wheels release; a run adds the new wheels and their hashes beside the old ones.
- If the installers fail after a wheel rebuild, the wheel pin commit stays on master and the next run does not rebuild the wheels.
notes:
Defaults: the pinned versions live in LINUX_WHEELS file names (scripts/manim-setup.mjs); the wheels workflow reads them with sed, so it has no version env. scripts/linux-wheels-pin.mjs 'missing' compares package-version-cp312 prefixes with the release assets (a missing release counts as all missing); 'pin' rewrites names and hashes from the release SHA256SUMS. Desktop build: wheels-check (master only) -> wheels (workflow_call of linux-wheels.yml, only when missing) -> wheel-pin (commit, push to master, else cherry-pick onto moved master) -> linux/windows/release check out the wheel pin commit. If master moved before the wheel pin, the installers build from moved master plus the pin, since the direct pin commit sits on no ref the build jobs can fetch. Wheels release: created once if missing, new file names uploaded without --clobber, existing names skipped, SHA256SUMS merged and re-uploaded. Versions present but pin hashes stale is left as is (spec: matching versions leave pins).
Reviewed, fixed and green, but the merge is blocked by missing access: `gh pr merge 111 --squash` fails with "refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow .github/workflows/desktop-build.yml without workflow scope". The gh token has no `workflow` scope and this PR changes two workflow files. Tried: the squash merge once, after CI passed (test and secrets pass, PR is MERGEABLE, head b47c947). Options: (1) owner merges PR #111 in the GitHub UI with squash and subject "task: Rabbithole-upd.4 The same run rebuilds and re-pins the Linux wheels"; (2) owner runs `gh auth refresh -s workflow` and restarts the reviewer. Nothing else is open: the review comment on the PR lists the three findings, all fixed in b47c947.
Owner refreshed the gh token with workflow scope (2026-11-22). Access blocker resolved: the reviewer can squash-merge PR #111.

title: Desktop build publishes when every job passes and re-pins the sandbox
description:
The owner releases with one manual run of the Desktop build workflow and pushes nothing by hand. The run builds and smoke-tests both installers as today. When every job passes it publishes the release instead of leaving a draft; this replaces upd.1's draft rule. If any job fails, nothing is published and no pin changes.

Before publishing, the run commits the Windows sandbox pin that npm start uses to master, as the GitHub Actions bot. The pin moves only when the sandbox crate, which builds the launcher and both helpers in the zip, or its lockfile changed since the commit of the release it points to now, because every build gives the sandbox zip a new hash even when its code is unchanged. The new pin names this run's own release tag, known before publishing, and the SHA-256 of the zip the run built and uploads, never a value typed in or copied from a log. The pin commit sits directly on the built commit and the release is tagged on it, so its source download carries the pin to its own zip; the pin commit differs from the built commit only in pin values, which the installers do not read. A run that moves no pin makes no commit and tags the built commit. If master moved during the run, the same pin change lands on master as its own commit, while the tag stays on the commit built from, so the release never contains code the run did not build. If the pin change cannot be pushed, nothing is published. Only one run of the workflow goes at a time. The published release is marked latest, so the README download links and the update banner find it.

AGENTS.md gains the rule that master may also change through this workflow's pin commit, and that the owner pulls before the next Ralph run. That commit does not pass the local trufflehog hook, so it changes only pin values.
acceptance_criteria:
- One manual run builds and smoke-tests both installers with no other step by the owner.
- The release is published only when every job passes; a failed job publishes nothing and changes no pin.
- When the sandbox source changed since the pinned release, a commit on master sets the sandbox pin to this run's release tag and the SHA-256 of its uploaded zip.
- When the pin moves, the release is tagged on the pin commit, so the release's source carries the pin to its own zip.
- When the sandbox source did not change, the pin is left as it is, the run makes no commit and the release is tagged on the built commit.
- If the pin commit cannot be pushed, nothing is published.
- The pin commit touches only pin values and lands on master even if master moved during the run.
- The release tag never contains a commit the run did not build and test.
- A second run waits until the first one finishes.
- The published release is marked latest, and the README download links fetch its installers.
- The workflow never deletes a release that a pin points to.
- AGENTS.md says master may change through this pin commit and that the owner pulls before the next Ralph run.
notes: Defaults: pin moves when git diff <pinned tag> HEAD -- desktop/sandbox is non-empty (a missing tag counts as changed); SHA-256 computed in the release job from the downloaded zip artifact; order is tag push -> draft release with assets -> pin push to master (ff, else cherry-pick onto moved master) -> publish with --latest, so a failure before the pin push leaves only a draft; workflow-level concurrency group desktop-build without cancel-in-progress; no workflow step deletes releases.

title: Switching Settings pages keeps the scroll
description: Switching pages from the Settings nav scrolls the new page's heading into view, so the window jumps and stutters even when the learner was at the top. Switching pages must leave the scroll where it is and move focus to the new heading without scrolling. Opening Settings at a named section or control, as other parts of the app do, still scrolls to it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Switching Settings pages never moves the scroll.
- After a switch, focus is on the new page's heading.
- Opening Settings at a named section or control still brings it into view.
notes: PR #99: nav switches focus the heading with preventScroll and no scrollIntoView; requests still scroll. New test test/shell/settings-window.test.mjs. CI green.

title: Branded desktop loading screen
description:
The desktop starting page becomes a branded page: the Rabbithole logo and a looping animation, in the house light or dark colours following the system theme, calmed under reduced motion. It shows no real progress and the server stays unchanged. Start errors still replace it with their text.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-dpl.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Opening the desktop app shows the logo and an animation in the system's light or dark theme while the server starts.
- With reduced motion the animation is still or calmed.
- A server that fails to start still shows its error text.
- The screen follows the mockup.
notes: Defaults: page CSS copied from the mockup with .boot moved onto body and .still replaced by @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce); color-scheme: light dark on :root so light-dark() follows the system; caption 'Starting…' as in the mockup; no web fonts loaded (file:// page, falls back to system fonts); main.mjs unchanged since its showError swap already triggers the :has(pre#status) error state. No test per spec (static markup).

title: Video mode setting with a Saving mode
description: A new app-wide setting, Video mode, with Quality (default) and Saving, stored with the other server settings and set on the Models page next to the smart model. When a video starts, the pipeline reads the mode once. In Saving mode it skips the cut audit and its fix for every cut, starts no piece improvement and fetches no reference photos; it keeps the plan, exhibits, set pieces, cut writing, narration and the repair of a cut that fails to render, limited to that failure. A Retry uses the mode at the time of the Retry; finished videos keep how they were made.
acceptance_criteria:
- Settings offers Video mode with Quality and Saving, and Quality is the default.
- A video made in Saving mode calls no cut audit, audit fix, piece improvement or reference photo, and is saved playable.
- In Saving mode a cut that fails to render is still repaired.
- In Quality mode videos are made as today.
- Changing the mode affects only videos started or retried afterwards.
notes: Defaults: Video mode stored in its own one-row table video_mode (no row = quality), routes GET/POST /api/settings/video-mode {mode}. UI: VideoMode selector in a 'Videos' section directly after the model profile table on the Models page (app-wide, not per profile, so not a row inside the profile table). Saving mode still shoots each cut's stills (no model call) so a crash goes to its repair; repairs keep today's prompt. Cuts finished in Saving are marked audited (cut-state needs it to be playable), so a later Quality Retry keeps them unaudited. Planner prompt unchanged: in Saving any referenceQuery is ignored, and a Retry in Saving drops the prior attempt's reference photos.

title: Desktop releases carry versions and updater files
description: The desktop build workflow stamps the app version as 1.0.<run_number> before building, tags the release v1.0.<run_number>, and uploads the updater's metadata files and blockmaps with the installers. Installer artifact names are set to the fixed README names directly, so the metadata and files agree and README links keep working. Releases stay drafts until the owner publishes them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each desktop build has the version 1.0.<run_number> and a matching tag.
- The release carries the updater metadata and blockmaps for both installers.
- The installers keep their fixed README names.
- The release is still created as a draft.
notes: Defaults: publish provider github Thomastienn/Rabbithole in desktop/package.json (needed for electron-builder to write latest*.yml and app-update.yml); build runs with --publish never so CI never uploads itself; version stamped with npm version --no-git-tag-version in desktop/ (updates package.json and lock); AppImage blockmap is embedded, so Linux uploads only AppImage + latest-linux.yml.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Owner action: after this merges, run Desktop build. Releases are then tagged v1.0.<run_number>. Keep the desktop-build-9 release, or set SANDBOX_RELEASE to the new tag and the SHA-256 that the Windows job prints.

title: Update banner in the desktop app
description:
The desktop shell checks this repository's published releases once on launch with electron-updater, with no automatic download or install on quit. A newer version shows an in-app banner, "Rabbithole X.Y.Z is available", with Install. Install downloads with progress; when the update is ready, Restart runs the existing pending-layout save, then quits and installs. A failed check stays quiet; a failed download shows a short reason with Retry. The update decision is a plain function or state machine in the shell module.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-upd.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- On launch the app shows the banner only when a newer published release exists.
- Nothing downloads until the learner clicks Install, and the banner shows download progress.
- Restart saves the pending map layout before installing.
- Being offline never shows an error on launch; a failed download offers Retry.
- The banner follows the mockup.
notes: Defaults: electron-updater 6.8.11 pinned as desktop runtime dependency; bridge is a sandboxed preload (desktop/preload.cjs) exposing rabbitholeDesktop.update(get|install|restart) + onUpdate over one ipc channel, accepted only from the server origin; Restart saves the layout, stops the server, then quitAndInstall so the new version finds the data folder free; card sits inside the sticky sidebar foot above Downloads/Settings; the mockup's x hides card and rail dot for this launch (page state); failed-download reason is one of two short sentences (connection vs other).

title: Desktop installer ships without bundled tools
description: The desktop build stops staging uv, LaTeX, Python, Manim, yt-dlp, the offline Python packages and the video browser, and drops its check for missing bundled tools; the foreign-binary check stays. The desktop shell points the tool root at a tools folder inside the data folder, so add-ons install there and the app never writes into its own folder. The installer keeps the pinned Node, the app and, on Windows, the sandbox launcher and its helpers. The owner runs the desktop build to confirm the size.
acceptance_criteria:
- The staged desktop resources hold no video tools and no offline Python.
- The desktop app installs add-ons into the data folder.
- A fresh desktop install chats with no add-on installed.
- The desktop smoke test still passes without bundled tools.
- The README and the setup guide describe add-ons installed on request instead of tools bundled in the installers.
notes: Defaults: shell sets RABBITHOLE_TOOLS_DIR to <data>/tools via toolsDir() in desktop/shell.mjs, using the staged app's server/desktop.mjs dataDir (relative RABBITHOLE_DATA_DIR resolves from the server cwd, like server/main.mjs). Offline Python add-on now lists uv before python (its setup runs uv venv; a fresh desktop has no uv) and video tools share it. Browser step writes an empty package.json into a tool root without one, else Remotion downloads to <root>/.remotion instead of node_modules/.remotion. Smoke test asserts no bundled tools and no add-on on a fresh install, then installs video tools (offline Python first) via the API, 30 min cap, before its render and run_python checks; Windows runs sandbox setup before the install since detectPython needs it. Linux workflow drops the Cairo/Pango apt step. uv's managed Python stays in uv's default folder (outside the data folder); app folder is never written.

title: Linux installs Manim from the project wheels
description: Point the Linux Manim install at the wheels from the wheels workflow, with their URLs and SHA-256 hashes pinned, so video tools install on Linux without a compiler or development packages. Windows keeps PyPI's wheels. Needs the owner to have run the wheels workflow; if its release does not exist yet, record the external blocker on this ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- On Linux the Manim install uses the pinned project wheels of pycairo and manimpango and builds nothing.
- A wheel whose hash does not match is refused.
- Windows installs keep using PyPI's wheels.
- The Linux check for Cairo and Pango development packages no longer blocks installing video tools.
notes:
Unblocked 2026-11-22: Linux wheels run 45070063269 passed and published the linux-wheels release (pycairo 1.29.2 and manimpango 0.7.1, cp312 manylinux_2_28 x86_64, built from dc4eeda). Pin the URLs and SHA-256 hashes from its SHA256SUMS.
Defaults: wheels pinned in scripts/manim-setup.mjs LINUX_WHEELS (hashes from linux-wheels SHA256SUMS, re-checked by downloading the assets); Node downloads them into <toolRoot>/.tools/wheels and checks SHA-256 (uv --find-links verifies no hashes), then uv pip install --find-links <dir> --only-binary pycairo --only-binary manimpango (uv pip has no --no-build-package; dry run confirmed it resolves the local wheels and refuses to build without them). Only Linux x64 uses them (the wheels are x86_64); Linux arm64 still builds from PyPI. Linux pkg-config check dropped from checkManimDependencies and the first-run Linux line now asks only for bwrap; macOS keeps its check. desktop-stage left alone (aon.8 removes bundled tools).

title: Workflow builds Linux wheels for pycairo and manimpango
description: PyPI has no Linux wheels of pycairo and manimpango, which Manim needs, so installing video tools on Linux would need a compiler and the Cairo and Pango development packages. Add a manually triggered GitHub workflow that builds manylinux x86_64 wheels of both at the versions Manim pins, for the Python the add-ons use, repairs them with auditwheel so they carry their libraries, and attaches them to one fixed GitHub release. Agents edit the workflow locally; the owner pushes and triggers it (AGENTS.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- The workflow runs only when triggered by hand.
- It builds manylinux x86_64 wheels of pycairo and manimpango at the pinned versions and repairs them with auditwheel.
- It attaches the wheels and their SHA-256 hashes to one fixed release, replacing earlier copies.
notes: Defaults: pycairo 1.29.2 and manimpango 0.7.1 (what uv resolves for manim==0.22.1 on Python 3.12, matching the local .venv); CPython 3.12 (cp312, as manim-setup/python-setup use); manylinux_2_28 container (glibc 2.28); fixed tag linux-wheels, deleted and recreated each run so earlier copies go, marked --latest=false so it never shadows the desktop release; hashes in SHA256SUMS. Workflow not run: the owner triggers it after merge (workflow_dispatch registers from master).

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Owner action: after this merges, run the Linux wheels workflow, then pin the wheel URLs and SHA-256 hashes it publishes in the setup scripts. Rabbithole-aon.7 needs those pins.

title: A waiting video offers to install video tools
description: A video asked for while video tools are not installed is still created and planned as today. Its card shows "Video tools aren't installed" with an Install button and the download size instead of waiting silently, and it renders once the tools are ready. The existing "Video tools are still downloading (n%)" state stays for an install in progress.
acceptance_criteria:
- A video requested without video tools is kept and its card offers Install with the size.
- Install from the card installs video tools and offline Python.
- The video renders once the tools are ready, without asking again.
- While the tools download, the card shows the existing downloading state.
notes: Defaults: reason text "Video tools aren't installed (about 500 MB)." carries the size (from the add-on list) so the card needs no extra fetch; the job still fails fast before planning with that reason and the card shows Install video tools. Card Install posts /api/trees/<id>/artifacts/<aid>/install (installs video-tools, which queues offline Python first). live() rewrites a stored tools reason to the current one; /api/state lists waiting videos' conversations while video tools download so cards poll. When videoWaiting() turns null, every video failed with a 'Video tools ...' reason is retried automatically (also covers the older downloading state). Removed the now-unused video:true tool flag.

title: Installed add-ons update themselves
description: After an app update pins a newer version of a tool inside an installed add-on, such as Manim, that add-on downloads again in the background and shows Updating in the sidebar and on the Add-ons page. Add-ons the learner never installed are never checked or downloaded.
acceptance_criteria:
- An installed add-on whose pinned version no longer matches downloads again on launch and is reported as updating.
- An add-on never installed is not checked or downloaded after an update.
- An add-on whose versions match does nothing on launch.
notes: Defaults: an add-on remembered in addons.json before this launch, whose tool fails its readiness check at start, is queued with update:true; the add-on list reports state 'updating' (with percent) and the sidebar says Updating. An interrupted first install also reads as Updating on the next launch (no per-tool version record). Only Manim's check compares a pinned version today; uv, LaTeX, Python and the browser check presence.

title: First-run setup offers add-ons
description:
First-run setup gains a last step after the provider and chat model steps. It lists the same add-ons with what each enables and its size, with Install per row, Install all and Skip, and says the Add-ons page in Settings has them any time. Leaving the step never waits for downloads; they run in the background while the learner chats.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-aon.3.html
acceptance_criteria:
- First-run setup ends with an add-ons step listing every add-on.
- Install on a row, or Install all, starts the downloads, and the learner can leave the step at once.
- Skip leaves every add-on uninstalled, and the step says where to install them later.
- The sign-in step asks for Claude or Codex: once one is connected, the other shows as optional, not as an error.
- The button that leaves setup reads Start chatting, not Start asking.
- The step follows the mockup.
notes: Defaults: add-on rows use the server's add-on copy and sizes (GET /api/downloads/addons), not the mockup's sample copy; the step polls that list every second while open (no add-on stream); Install all posts each not-installed add-on in list order; the leave button reads Skip until any add-on is installing/installed/failed, then Start chatting; the Linux video-packages section stays in step 1 until Rabbithole-aon.7 lands the wheels; connections never show an error state, a missing CLI reads Not set up with its install line; the step's row component is its own (src/shell/FirstRunAddOns.tsx) since the Settings Add-ons page (aon.2) is in flight in parallel.

title: Add-ons page in Settings
description:
A new Settings page, Add-ons, beside Interface, Models, Connections and Usage. Each row shows an add-on's name, what it enables, its size and its state (Installed, Not installed, Downloading n%, Updating, Failed) with Install or Retry. Video tools say they need offline Python. The last row is the existing sandbox status (bwrap on Linux, the Windows sandbox). No Remove action.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-aon.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Settings has an Add-ons page listing video tools, offline Python and web search with their state.
- Install and Retry start the add-on's download, and the row follows its progress.
- The video tools row says it needs offline Python.
- The page shows whether the code sandbox is ready.
- The page follows the mockup.
notes:
Defaults: page AddonsSettings.tsx, rows reload GET /api/downloads/addons on each /api/downloads stream message. 'Waiting for <dependency>' is derived client-side (add-on downloading while its dependency downloads). Downloading meta estimates 'n of N MB' from percent x approximate size. 'updating' state rendered if the server ever reports it (aon.1 never does; upd epic). Sandbox row: /api/setup/sandbox status now reports bwrap presence off Windows (probe bwrap --version); Linux missing shows apt command + Check again. SandboxSettings moved off the Models page; it stays as the first-run Windows step (firstRun prop dropped), useSandbox() hook shared. Add-on 'enables' copy updated to the mockup's.
PR #104 green. First CI run failed test/media/video-runaway.test.mjs (timing flake, passes locally, unrelated); rerun passed.

title: Add-ons install only on request
description: The download manager queues every video tool automatically once first-run setup ends. Group its tools into three add-ons with stable ids: video tools (uv, LaTeX, Manim with clips, the video browser), offline Python and web search. Every add-on becomes on request, as web search already is. Installing video tools queues offline Python first, since they share it. The data folder remembers which add-ons the learner installed. The downloads API lists the add-ons with name, what each enables, approximate download size, dependency, state and percent, and installs or retries one by id. The sidebar downloads keep working. Under npm start the project folder stays the tool root, so the owner's installed tools count as installed.
acceptance_criteria:
- After first-run setup no add-on downloads unless the learner installs it.
- The add-on list reports each add-on's state (installed, not installed, downloading with percent, failed) and its dependency.
- Installing video tools also installs offline Python, offline Python first.
- Installing or retrying an add-on by id queues its downloads; an unknown id is refused.
- Which add-ons the learner installed survives a restart.
- Tools already present in the tool root count as installed and never download.
notes: Defaults: add-on ids video-tools, offline-python, web-search; sizes ~500/50/40 MB (compressed estimate of owner's installed .tools/.venv); remembered in <data>/addons.json; API GET /api/downloads/addons, POST /api/downloads/addons/<id>[/retry] (retry = install, re-queues only failed tools); old POST /api/downloads/<tool> removed (SearchOffer moved to add-on route). Never-requested add-ons get a quiet readiness look at start (never queues) so tools already in the tool root show installed; web search is not looked at (its check launches SearXNG). Legacy searxng folder still counts as requested.

title: Desktop loading screen and Settings scroll
description: Two pieces of polish. The desktop app shows "Starting Rabbithole…" as plain text on white while its server starts, which looks like a broken build. Switching pages in Settings makes the scroll jump down and stutter even when the learner was at the top.

title: Desktop app updates on request
description: The desktop app has a fixed version and never learns about a newer build; the learner has to find the release page and reinstall. After this epic each desktop build carries its own increasing version, and the app checks published releases on launch and offers the update in a banner: one click downloads it, another restarts into it. Only releases the owner publishes reach learners.

title: Video mode: Quality or Saving
description: Every video pays for cut audits, their fixes, piece improvements and reference photos. After this epic the learner chooses a Video mode in Settings: Quality, the default and today's behaviour, or Saving, which skips those steps and keeps only what a playable video needs.

title: Add-ons installed on request
description:
The desktop installers are about 1 GB because they bundle Python, Manim, TinyTeX, the video browser and the offline Python packages, which a learner who only chats never uses. ADR 0020 replaces that bundle with add-ons: video tools, offline Python and web search, installed only when the learner asks, from a last first-run setup step, a new Add-ons page in Settings, or a waiting video card. Installed add-ons update themselves when an app update needs newer versions. Add-ons come from upstream with every version pinned, plus our own manylinux wheels of pycairo and manimpango so Linux needs no compiler.

After this epic the base installer only chats and is a few hundred MB.

Decisions so far: see the spec and ADR 0020.

title: Targets and map view state move to their owners
description:
Two more groups of state sit in the shared chat state object though one consumer each really uses them. The figure, message and passage to scroll to, and whether the composer should take focus, are consumed by the chat targets hook. The folds of a learning tree map, the ghost tree marks and the map width are consumed by the map.

After this ticket the chat targets hook owns the first group and the map's own hook owns the second.
design: Folds are also held inside the map view and copied up through a callback; give them one home in the map's hook and let layout saving read from there. Keep the map width in local storage under the same key.
acceptance_criteria:
- The chat targets hook owns the figure, message and passage targets and the composer focus request; other code asks it to go to a target.
- The map's hook owns folds, ghost tree marks and the map width; folds have one home.
- Opening a resource, a search result or a ghost tree still lands on the same conversation, message or figure as before.
- Folds, positions and the map width are still saved and restored as before.
- The composer still takes focus in the same situations as before.
notes: useChatTargets owns reveal (passage), figure and message targets, the composer ref and the focusComposer request; exposes goTo(id, source, artifact, message), jump(conversation, message) and drop(ids). useMapViewState owns folds, ghost marks and map width (same localStorage key). Defaults: both are composed inside useLearningTrees like useLayoutSaving (they need its open conversation and app state), and other hooks reach them as trees.targets / trees.map. Folds' one home: the map hook keeps folds the learner changed for the current root and otherwise shows the folds saved in that root's layout; TreeOverview takes folded/setFolded props instead of its own state, and layout saving reads map.folded.

title: No hook or view takes the whole chat state
description:
What remains in the shared object after the earlier tickets is view state: map or focused chat, expanded, tab, drawer, narrow screen, the statistics panel, view transitions, renaming and the shared error notice. Hooks and views still receive whole objects and pick fields out of them, so a test has to know which fields a view reads and build a partial object by hand, and the hook test kit mounts every hook to test one.

After this ticket the remaining object is the view state and nothing else, hooks take the owners they need, and views receive the values they read.
acceptance_criteria:
- The remaining shared hook holds only view state and the shared error notice.
- No hook takes the whole set of hooks; each takes the owners it needs, and dependencies run one way.
- The focused chat, the reply thread and the map view receive the values they read, not whole hook results.
- A test can mount one hook with fakes for the owners it needs.
- No test builds a partial copy of another hook's result by guessing which fields are read.
- The page behaves as before on wide and narrow screens.
notes: Defaults: hooks keep their owner arguments but type each as Pick<Owner, fields read>, so a fake is built to the declared type; nested targets/layout/map stay reached through trees. Views (FocusedChat, ChatThread, MapView, LibraryPanel, ModelMenu, DeleteDialog) take flat props; FocusedChat passes a ThreadProps bundle on to ChatThread. Live turns map is owned by useLearningTrees (trees.live) and written by useReplyStream instead of the stream assigning its map into trees each render. Kit: mountHook(t, use); pending-branch tests now mount useBranchForm alone; test/support/thread-props.mjs gives complete ThreadProps defaults.

title: Branch form owns its state
description:
Which branch form is open, the element that gets focus back when it closes, and the message the learner is selecting a passage from live in the shared chat state object. The tree actions reset them from outside.

After this ticket the branch form hook owns them and offers one way to close the form.
acceptance_criteria:
- The branch form hook owns the open branch form, its focus return target and the message being selected from.
- Other hooks close the branch form through the hook; none clears its state directly.
- Focus returns to the same control as before when the branch form closes.
- Branching from a passage, a suggestion, groundwork and a free branch all work as before, from the focused chat and from the map.
notes: useBranchForm owns branch, selectingMessage and branchOrigin; exposes branch, setQuestion, selectingMessage/setSelectingMessage, closeBranch and drop(ids). Defaults: ChatPage builds the branch form before the tree actions (epic direction), which take it as a fourth argument. Deletion calls branchForm.drop(ids): closes a form whose parent is deleted and clears the passage selection of a deleted open conversation, without refocusing, as before; closeBranch stays the learner's close (Escape/outside click) with the same focus return.

title: Reply stream owns live turns, drafts and pending attachments
description:
Live turns, running streams, the busy flag, the draft of each conversation and its pending attachments live in the shared chat state object. The reply stream hook, the branch form hook and the tree actions all write them.

After this ticket the reply stream hook owns them. Other hooks ask it to send, to stop, or to clear what belongs to a conversation that is going away.
acceptance_criteria:
- The reply stream hook owns live turns, running streams, the busy flag, drafts and pending attachments.
- No other hook writes them directly; deleting a conversation or starting a new chat asks the reply stream to drop what it holds for them.
- A draft and its pending attachments still survive switching to another conversation and back.
- A reply that is streaming in a conversation the learner left still finishes and shows when they return.
- Stopping a reply works as before.
notes: useReplyStream owns drafts, pendingFiles, busy, streams and turns; API: drafts/setDraft, pendingFiles/setFiles, busy, isLive(id), drop(ids), send, create, stop. Defaults: create (first question) moved from tree actions into the reply stream since it owns busy and the first draft/files. useLearningTrees reads live turns through trees.live, a read-only ref the reply stream points at its map (learning tree data is built first). The branch question offered on reopen moved from select into a reply stream effect on tree id. New chat drops nothing: the left conversation keeps its draft and running reply. Delete calls drop(ids), which now also clears those conversations' pending files.

title: Learning tree data and its stale-answer check have one owner
description:
The app state from the server, the open conversation and its previews live in the shared chat state object, and every hook writes them. Whether a server answer is still current is decided by three counters (the selected conversation, a request number and a checkpoint number) that each hook reads and bumps itself: the selected conversation is read at 29 places in six files. "Leave the open conversation" is written out three times in the tree actions.

After this ticket the learning trees hook owns that data and those counters. Other hooks ask it to load, to apply a change to a learning tree, or to leave the open conversation; none touches the counters.
design: The learning trees hook already owns refresh, select and opening a tree or conversation; the data and counters move in beside them. Offer one operation that runs a request and applies its answer only while it is still current, and use it at every place that compares the counters by hand today. The locally removed and renamed lists move too, since refresh is what applies them.
acceptance_criteria:
- The learning trees hook owns the app state, the open conversation, previews, addresses, the loading flag and the counters that say whether a server answer is current.
- No other hook or view reads or changes those counters.
- The check for a stale server answer is written once.
- A server answer that arrives after the learner opened another conversation, or after a newer request for the same one, is dropped in every case where it was dropped before.
- Leaving the open conversation is written once and used by delete, new chat and every other place that did it.
- A learning tree the learner just deleted or renamed still does not reappear or revert when the next refresh arrives.
notes: useLearningTrees(c) owns state, open tree, previews, addresses, loading, visibleIds, removed/renamed and the selected/request/checkpoint counters. One check: since(id) (current while id open and request unchanged; unchanged=true also needs no local change). reload(id, apply, unchanged) runs a tree fetch through it; change(update?) marks a local change; show(tree) opens a tree already in hand; leave() leaves the open conversation (newChat, empty first question, delete with nothing next); retitle/forget/isRemoved for renamed and removed lists; openId() for 'is this still open' checks. useLayoutSaving is now called inside useLearningTrees with the data (trees.layout), since refresh applies unsaved layout. Default: changeView and returnToTree moved with visibleIds into useLearningTrees (both need tree data and view state comes first); stats panel scroll effect moved into FocusedChat. videoAction's reload now also drops on a newer request for the same conversation (was selected-only).

title: Break up the chat state bag
description:
One hook holds all the state of the chat page and returns 69 values. Six more hooks each take that whole object, plus what the earlier hooks return, so the seven are one closure spread over seven files: inlining them back into the page would change nothing but file length. A state change usually needs edits in several of them, and the test kit has to mount all seven to test one.

After this epic each group of state has one owner, and no hook or view receives the whole object.

Decisions so far

- Ownership. Learning tree data: the app state from the server, the open conversation, previews, addresses, the loading flag, the lists of locally removed and renamed trees, and the three counters that tell whether a server answer is still current. Reply stream: live turns, running streams, the busy flag, drafts and pending attachments. Branch form: the open branch form, the element it returns focus to, and the message being selected from. Targets: the figure, message and passage to scroll to, and the composer focus. Map view state: folds, ghost tree marks and the map width. View state: everything left, which is what is shown (map or focused chat, expanded, tab, drawer, narrow screen, statistics panel, view transitions, renaming) and the shared error notice.
- Direction. Dependencies run one way: view state and learning tree data first, then reply stream, then branch form, then the tree actions. A hook takes the owners it needs, never the whole object.
- The check for a stale server answer is written once, by the owner of learning tree data. It is timing logic, so each ticket keeps the same answers dropped as before.
- The request function leaves the object in Rabbithole-sva.3, which blocks this epic.
- The tickets form one chain, because every one of them edits the page and the tree actions.

From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 5.

title: Diagrams module split by concept
description:
One module near the cap holds five concepts: the tutor's instructions for media, the parser for media requests in a reply, the tutor's context about earlier media, compaction of media for inherited context, and the Mermaid worker. 37 files import it; 3 use its diagram generator. A separate small file holds reply request code that was moved out of it for size.

After this ticket each concept has a module of its own.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the five concepts has its own module, named for it; the reply request code sits with the concept it belongs to.
- Each importer imports only the module it uses.
- No re-export keeps the old import path alive.
- Behaviour is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: modules tutor-instructions.mjs (rules, tutorSystem, VERDICT_SHAPE moved here since it is instruction text), reply-parser.mjs (diagramReply + LIMITS; reply-requests.mjs folded in, jsonEnd/inMediaLayout now private), tutor-context.mjs, compaction-messages.mjs, diagram-generator.mjs (renamed from diagrams.mjs). Shared modelMessage moved to server/attachments.mjs next to withAttachments. Function names unchanged.

title: Fold the cut submit handler back and drop re-exports that hide owners
description:
The handler for a submitted cut was moved unchanged into a file of its own to get its owner under the cap. The two halves share one mutable object. Several media modules also re-export names from other modules so that old import paths keep working, and tests import through them, which makes the owning module hard to find.

After this ticket the handler is back with its owner and every import names the module that owns what it imports.
acceptance_criteria:
- The cut submit handler lives in the module that owns it, and the pass-through file is gone.
- No module re-exports another module's names only to keep an old import path working; callers and tests import from the owning module.
- No file is over the cap.
- Behaviour is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: cutSubmission folded into video-cuts.mjs (its only caller) as a private function. Dropped media re-exports in video-cuts (auditReport/auditFix), videos (playable, SANDBOX), diagrams (readVerdicts, VERDICT_SHAPE); callers now import from audit-answers, video-cuts, video-sandbox, reply-requests. Kept video-kit.tsx re-exports: they are the ./kit surface generated cuts import, not an old path. Non-media re-exports (markdown.ts, attachments, openai, test/support kits) out of scope.

title: The size check says how to answer a cap hit
description:
When the size check fails, nothing says what a good answer is, so the cheapest one wins: move a block unchanged into a new file, or squeeze lines.

After this ticket the rule is in the agent docs and the check's failure message points to it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The agent docs state the rule: when a file reaches the cap, deepen a module or split it by concept; never move code unchanged into a sibling file, and never fold lines or inline a named value to get under.
- The size check's failure message points to that rule.
- The cap itself is unchanged.
notes: Rule lives in docs/agents/testing.md under '## File size cap', next to the existing cap bullet; failure message names that section. Copy-only change to the CLI message, no new test.

title: Answer the size cap with depth, not sibling files
description:
The file size check fails any hand-written file over 550 lines. It has been met by moving code unchanged into a sibling file, by folding lines and by inlining named constants. Each of these adds an interface, or removes a name, without making any module deeper: the halves share mutable state, and re-exports hide where the code now lives.

After this epic the rule for answering a cap hit is written where agents read it, the files that only pass through are folded back, and a module that holds several concepts is split by concept.

From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 9.

title: Views call the server access module; the request prop goes
description:
The request function is still passed as a prop to 20 places, most of them in Settings, and its type is re-declared 22 times with differing return types. Eight test files replace the global fetch and match URLs in a chain of conditions.

After this ticket views and hooks call the server access module directly, and tests swap in a fake adapter.
acceptance_criteria:
- No view or hook receives the request function as a prop; each calls the server access module.
- The request function's type is declared once.
- Tests replace the server with a fake adapter of the module; none replaces the global fetch.
- Settings, the focused chat and the learning tree map behave as before.
notes: Views/hooks import request from src/serverAccess.ts (aliased 'api' in hooks where a 'request' ref already exists). firstQuestion, prepareBranch and treeSearchSource import it too instead of taking it as a parameter. Seam: setAdapter(next) in serverAccess swaps the fetch-shaped adapter and returns the old one; test/support/fake-server.mjs fakeServer(t, answer) installs it per test (JSON body or Response-like reply; a throw rejects like a dropped connection). request returns any, so the per-view return types went with the props. test/scripts/tools-setup.test.mjs still stubs global fetch: it fakes internet downloads for a Node script, not the app server.

title: One reply stream reader with typed events
description:
Reading a streamed tutor reply (for a new question and for a retry) and reading streamed replies inside a discussion are two copies of the same read loop. The events have no type on the client: their names exist only as strings on both sides, so a renamed or new event fails without an error.

After this ticket one reader in the server access module serves all three, and the events are typed once.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sending, retrying and replying in a discussion read the stream through one reader in the server access module.
- Stream events have one type declaration on the client, covering every event the server sends.
- Stopping a reply and a dropped connection behave as before.
- Keepalive lines are still ignored.
notes: replyStream(path, init) in src/serverAccess.ts: POSTs, throws the server message on !ok, returns an async iterable of StreamEvent (releases the reader lock when done). StreamEvent union + sseFrames moved there from chat/turn.ts. applyStreamEvent typed; returns event.type !== 'error' (same set as the old list).

title: Server access module owns requests and the CSRF header
description:
The client's request function lives inside the chat state hook. Export, downloads, the live player and video usage call fetch themselves, each building the CSRF header its own way. The token for that header sits in a variable in the export button's module and is written from the chat state hook.

After this ticket one plain module sends requests, and those four use it.
design: A plain module, not a hook. It holds the CSRF token once the app state has loaded. The chat state hook's request function delegates to it for now, so the prop keeps working until the last ticket of this epic. Reads that are not JSON, such as a cut's code for the live player, go through it too.
acceptance_criteria:
- One client module sends requests, adds the CSRF header and turns a failed response into an error carrying the server's message.
- Export, downloads, the live player and video usage use that module and no longer call fetch themselves.
- The CSRF token is held in one place.
- The error messages the learner sees are unchanged.
notes: Module at src/serverAccess.ts: setCsrf, serverFetch (raw Response, adds CSRF header when init given) and request (JSON GET/POST, throws Error with server message + data). useChatState imports request as api so the prop keeps working. useReplyStream also uses serverFetch so the token lives only in the module; stream reading stays for sva.2.

title: One client module for talking to the server
description:
The client's request function is a closure inside the chat state hook, handed down as a prop to 20 places and re-declared as a type 22 times. Nine direct fetch calls in six files go around it. The CSRF header is built in five places. The loop that reads a streamed reply exists twice, and its events have no type. Tests replace the global fetch and match URLs by hand.

After this epic one client module owns the URLs, the CSRF header, error parsing and the reply stream, with a fake adapter for tests.

From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 6.

title: One owner for the order of the video pipeline
description:
The order of the pipeline is split. One module plans the video, fetches exhibits, detects Manim and finishes. Another writes set pieces, writes and narrates cuts, runs each cut audit, and fixes and repairs cuts. They exchange option bags of 24 and 26 fields, nine of them functions built inline, and the second returns seven fields of which two are used. Neither is tested directly.

After this ticket one module shows the order from plan to finished video and takes one set of dependencies.
design: The dependencies are the model call (epic Rabbithole-mdc), the engine, the cut state, the workspace, the store, narration and the clock. Steps may stay in modules of their own behind the pipeline; nothing outside the pipeline calls them. A file that was split from its owner only to meet the size cap folds back as part of this work.
acceptance_criteria:
- One module shows the order of the pipeline from plan to finished video.
- The pipeline takes one set of dependencies, passed the same way throughout.
