- A test drives the pipeline with a fake model call and a fake engine, without a server or HTTP.
- Playback still starts when the first cut is playable, and cuts are still written, narrated and audited in parallel.
- A failed cut is still repaired, and a cut audit's issues are still fixed before the cut plays.
- Retrying and regenerating a video behave as before.
notes: Defaults: the pipeline is generateVideo({ dir, artifact, previous, signal }, deps) in videos.mjs; deps (DEPS documents them) = call/write (videoCall over a provider), writerCapable, readsImages, engines(job) (videoEngines), store, narrate, timeout (the clock's budget; raced timers stay real), embed, stills, search, exhibit, clips, mcp, onPhase/onStage/onWarning. Undefined deps fall back to the real ones. Steps take (video, deps): planVideo, keptCuts, progress, finish (videos.mjs), drawPieces/improveSaved (video-pieces.mjs), startCuts/makeCut (video-cuts.mjs). writeSetPieces, videoMedia and fetchExhibit keep their focused signatures as leaf helpers. No file was found that was split from its owner only for the size cap, so nothing folded back.

title: One module owns the video workspace layout
description:
Where a video's working files live (its work folder, the files of each cut, the saved cut source) is spelled out as path strings at about 25 places: in the jobs, the routes, export and conversation delete. The saved cut source is parsed in four modules.

After this ticket one module answers where those files are and reads and writes a cut's saved source.
acceptance_criteria:
- One module answers where a video's working files are, and reads and writes a cut's saved source.
- Jobs, routes, export and conversation delete ask that module; none builds these paths itself.
- Existing saved videos are found where they were; nothing on disk moves.
notes: Defaults: server/media/video-workspace.mjs owns the layout (workRoot, videoWork, attemptWork, legacyWork, cutWork, cutAudio, cutClip) and the saved source (readSaved -> data or null, writeSaved). store.videoData writes through writeSaved. The relative clip path stored in saved source (cut-N/public/manim.mp4) stays a literal: it is saved data. mediaPath (exported MP4) stays in videos.mjs: not a working file. Tests keep literal paths so they pin the on-disk layout.

title: A cut's state is named in one place
description:
Whether a cut is being written, narrated, audited, fixed, playable or failed is not stated anywhere. It is worked out from six fields in three places (the playable check, the saved cut rows and the progress report), beside a separate list of phases in the job code. A change to the pipeline has to keep all of them in step.

After this ticket one definition says which states a cut can be in and how it moves between them.
acceptance_criteria:
- One definition says which states a cut can be in and how it moves between them.
- The progress the learner sees, the check that a cut is playable and the saved cut rows all read that definition.
- The learner sees the same progress steps as before.
- Videos saved before this change still load and play.
notes: Defaults: server/media/cut-state.mjs holds CUT_STATES (state -> job phase + next states), job PHASES and cutState/playable, all derived from the existing saved cut fields (no new persisted field, so old videos load). cutRows, report() and the playable route read it. A failed cut now shows as 'failed' in rows and reports no phase. A kept audited cut under repair is no longer playable while it is repaired.

title: Remotion and Manim behind one engine seam
description:
A cut is drawn by one of two engines, Remotion or Manim (ADR 0001). The pipeline tests which engine a cut uses at 21 places in six modules, and checks whether Manim is available at seven more. Only Manim's half can be replaced in tests.

After this ticket there is one interface with two adapters, and the pipeline picks an adapter once for each cut.
design: The interface covers what the pipeline asks of an engine: the instructions for writing a cut, the check of written code, the still frames for the cut audit, the audit instructions and making the cut playable. Manim being unavailable is the Manim adapter's answer, not a separate check at each place.
acceptance_criteria:
- The pipeline chooses an engine adapter once for each cut; no other code tests which engine a cut uses.
- Remotion and Manim cuts are written, checked, audited and made playable as before.
- A video that needs Manim when Manim is unavailable fails with the same message as before.
- A test can supply a fake engine for either kind of cut.
notes: Defaults: seam in server/media/cut-engines.mjs. ENGINES holds the static adapters (pictures, playable, instructions, audit, source, stage); cutEngines() adds a job's ready/check/play/stills. generateVideo picks each cut's engine once and passes the per-cut array to writeCuts; tests pass fakes by kind via generateVideo({ engines }). Manim unavailable: the Manim engine warns once and stops the job with its message (no per-site checks); the stopped cut is no longer marked failed, so Retry keeps its code. Manim's availability check now runs before exhibit fetching. Plan validation (video-plan cutProblem, plan-calls add_cut/add_exhibit) still names engines: it checks the planner's choice, outside the pipeline's 21 sites. validateOutput moved to video-sandbox.mjs to avoid an import cycle. Manim audit-fix code is now unfenced like written code (was trim).

title: A cut pipeline with an engine seam
description:
Making a video crosses about 19 modules. The order of the pipeline is split over two of them, which exchange option bags of 24 and 26 fields. A cut's state is worked out from fields in three places. Callers branch on the engine (Remotion or Manim) at 21 places in six modules. No test drives the pipeline directly; about 21 test files start the whole app to test one step.

After this epic one cut pipeline module owns the order, the cut state and the workspace layout, and Remotion and Manim are two adapters at one engine seam.

ADR 0001, 0002, 0004 and 0006 stay as they are. From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 4.

title: Artifact slots live inside the reply turn
description:
The code that tracks a reply's visuals, discussions and videos (its artifact slots, and the bounded queue of media work) sits in its own module but reaches back into the send function through four callbacks: whether the reply has finished, what its status is, how to emit an event and the abort controller. It also hands its internal collection to the caller, which loops over it in three places.

After this ticket the artifact slots are part of the reply turn.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reply's artifact slots and media queue are part of the reply turn; nothing outside reads its internal collections.
- No callback asks the route whether the reply has finished or what its status is.
- Visuals and discussions still appear at their markers, and a video still stands alone, as before.
- The limit on media work running at once for one reply is unchanged.
notes: Defaults: reply-artifacts.mjs stays its own file (merging would pass the 550-line cap) but is created only by replyTurn and takes {emit, signal} instead of send/controller/isFinished/getStatus. Interface: prepare(output), draw(output, status), end(output, status), cancel(), showVisual, makeVideo, startDiscussion, hasMedia. drawDiagrams and the stop/cancel loops moved inside; the slots map is no longer returned. Pending-diagram cancel now runs inside end(), before stopToolCalls (store-only, emits nothing).

title: Reply turn owns stream state, saving and finish order
description:
While a tutor reply streams, the send function keeps its collected text, status, usage, inline notes, next questions, the periodic save and that save's trailing update in twelve variables shared by nested functions. The order of work after a reply finishes lives in the same function.

After this ticket a reply turn module holds that state and that order. The send route passes it the model's events and writes what it emits.
design: The reply turn takes the events of the model call, a way to save and a way to emit; it does not know HTTP. The save interval and the clock are passed in, so tests need no real timers. Request preparation (retry and attachments) stays in the route.
acceptance_criteria:
- One module holds a tutor reply's state from first token to finish; the send route holds none of it.
- The module can be driven in a test without a server, HTTP or real timers.
- Partial text is saved at the same interval as before, and a late save error still fails the reply where provider errors do.
- Suggestions, groundwork and next questions reach the learner at the same moments as before.
- Work after a reply finishes starts in the same order as before.
- A stopped or interrupted reply keeps its partial text.
- The send route is well under the size cap.
notes: Defaults: replyTurn(ctx, {id, tree, user, reply, body, job, emit, saveEvery, clock}) in server/http/reply-turn.mjs returns {finished, stream(generate), runAppTool, fail, finish}. It builds replyArtifacts and appCalls itself (rpt.2 folds the slots in) and runs the legacy diagram loop after the stream. The route closes the response and heartbeat when it emits 'done'. Clock = {now, setTimeout, clearTimeout}, defaulting to real timers. Two HTTP tests in stream-updates (trailing update, late save error) moved to test/http/reply-turn.test.mjs.

title: A module for the reply turn
description:
Sending a question is one function of about 540 lines, held exactly at the file size cap; its last five changes each had to trim it back under. It parses the request, prepares attachments, handles retry and then tracks a tutor reply from first token to finish in twelve mutable variables. Every test of that behaviour starts the whole app and reads the event stream over HTTP.

After this epic a reply turn module owns a tutor reply's state and the order of work when it finishes. The route parses the request and writes events.

From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 3.

title: Video jobs, drawings and exports join; the old lists go
description:
Video jobs, visual drawings and exports are the last kinds of background work with collections of their own. Once they move, the three hand-kept lists (await, stop, delete) have nothing left to name.

Deleting a conversation today aborts five of the collections and leaves title, verdict, suggestion and brief explanation jobs to notice later that their conversation is gone. After this ticket deleting a conversation stops every kind of job that belongs to it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Video, drawing and export work is tracked by the background jobs module.
- The server context holds no collection for one kind of job.
- Awaiting all background work, stopping the server and deleting a conversation are each one call on the module.
- Deleting a conversation stops every kind of background job that belongs to it, including title, verdict, suggestion and brief explanation jobs.
- Deleting a conversation still waits for its video jobs to end before their files are removed.
- Export progress and a failed export are still reported to the learner as before.
- A new kind of job needs no edit to the await, stop or delete paths.
notes:
Defaults: kinds 'video' and 'drawing' (key artifact id) and 'export' (key library id, conversation null, kept while failed). Module gains settled(key?) and stop(conversations?); start option settle:false (replies, prepared compactions) replaces the settled() skip list. Delete and server stop abort without a reason; STOPPED dropped since ctx.stopping is set first. Delete now awaits every job of the deleted conversations, not only videos.
CI round 1: delete awaiting every job hung on replies and compactions whose providers ignore abort. Added start option files:true (video jobs); stop(conversations) waits only for those, stop() still waits for all.
CI round 2: test/media/artifacts-stop.test.mjs failed once (inline diagram path, 30 ms deadline vs. duplicate POST under CI load; untouched here, passed 3/3 locally); rerun green.

title: Compactions, discussions and replies in flight join the background jobs module
description:
Compaction is tracked in one map under two kinds of key: a child conversation's id, and a discussion's id with a prefix. Compactions prepared when the branch form opens, running discussions and replies in flight each have a collection of their own.

After this ticket all of them are tracked by the background jobs module.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compaction, prepared compaction, discussion and in-flight reply work is tracked by the background jobs module.
- Compaction for a child conversation and compaction for a discussion are separate kinds, not two key formats in one map.
- A prepared compaction is still reused on submit while its key matches, and dropped otherwise.
- A failed compaction of a branch created before its inherited context was ready is still kept for retry, and removed on success.
- Stopping a reply from the focused chat still works.
notes: Defaults: kinds 'reply' (also held by model change and branch submit), 'discussion', 'compaction' (child), 'discussion-compaction', 'prepared-compaction' (key parent; fields input, passage, failed). Module gains start(..., { keep, controller }) and remove(job): kept jobs (compactions, prepared) stay after settling until removed; a reused prepared compaction hands its controller to the child's job. settled() still skips replies and prepared compactions, stop() still awaits only discussions and compactions, delete still cleans only these five kinds (bgj.3 unifies). app returns jobs instead of active.

title: Background jobs module owns the quick jobs
description:
This ticket adds the background jobs module and moves the first four kinds of job to it: title, verdict, suggestion and brief explanation. Each of them keeps its own collection today.

After this ticket those four are started through the module. Awaiting all background work and stopping the server ask the module for them, and still read the old collections for the kinds that have not moved yet.
design: For each job the module records its kind, its key, its conversation, its abort controller and its done promise. Each kind keeps its own rule for sharing or replacing a running job; for example, concurrent requests for the brief explanation of one passage share one call.
acceptance_criteria:
- Title, verdict, suggestion and brief explanation jobs start through one module and no longer have collections of their own.
- Awaiting all background work and stopping the server cover these four kinds through the module.
- Concurrent requests for the same brief explanation still share one call.
- Stopping the server aborts these jobs as before.
notes: Default: server/http/jobs/background.mjs backgroundJobs() on ctx.jobs: start(kind, key, conversation, run) -> job {kind,key,conversation,controller,done}, get(kind,key), list(kind?). Sharing/replacing stays at call sites (brief shares via get; verdict aborts then replaces). A settled job leaves only if not replaced (before: title/suggestion/brief deleted unconditionally). Batch briefs keep kind 'brief' with key batch:<message>. stop() still aborts these four without awaiting them, as before.

title: One owner for background jobs
description:
Background work (titles, verdicts, suggestions, brief explanations, compaction, discussions, replies in flight, videos, drawings and exports) is tracked in eleven separate collections on the server context. Three hand-kept lists must each name them: the one tests await, the one that stopping the server aborts, and the one that deleting a conversation cleans up. The three do not name the same collections, and a new kind of job needs an edit in each.

After this epic one module owns starting, awaiting, stopping and per-conversation cleanup of background work, and each kind of job registers with it once.

From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 2.

title: Media test fakes answer by role
description:
Fake providers in the media tests decide what to return by matching prompt wording, for example whether the prompt starts with the planner's opening words. A prompt edit breaks tests that have nothing to do with it, and every fake has to know every prompt.

After this ticket the shared fakes route by the call's role name, and the media tests use them that way.
design: Add role routing to the shared fakes in the test support folder first, then move the media tests over. Tests that assert on what a prompt contains keep doing so; only the routing changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fake providers used by the media tests choose their answer from the call's role name.
- No media test routes a fake by prompt wording.
- Tests that check what a prompt contains still check it.
notes: Defaults: fakes route video calls by tree.stage (plan, pieces, improve, audit, fix, repair, cut) and other calls by tree.role (visual, suggestions, verdict, compaction, video). Patch vs whole-source requests (repair, improve) are told apart by the input format via asksPatch(text) in test/support/video-kit.mjs, since both share one stage. The custom-endpoint wire fake in videos-jobs routes by the frozen request field, as roles do not reach the wire. Prompt-content asserts unchanged. Non-media tests (test/http, test/usage) still route by wording; out of scope.

title: Remaining test fakes answer by role
description:
After the media tests, the tests of the other areas (requests, chat, providers) still route their fake providers by prompt wording.

After this ticket they route by role name through the same shared fake.
acceptance_criteria:
- No test routes a fake provider by prompt wording.
- One shared fake serves the media tests and the other tests.
- Tests that check what a prompt contains still check it.
notes: Defaults: in-process fakes route by tree.role/tree.stage. The discussion turn request now carries role 'discussion' (adapters ignore it, log redaction already drops role) so fakes can tell it from the tutor reply. Single vs batch brief (both role 'brief') told apart by the task's 'terms' field. Wire fakes (OpenAI endpoint, CLI protocol fixture) see no role, so they route by the JSON task's fields via taskOf in test/support/model-task.mjs: visual = request, suggestions = answer, compaction = messages. Call filters used only for prompt-content asserts (suggestion-kit suggestionCalls, videos-jobs planner check) keep their wording: they check prompts, not route fakes.

title: Video usage reads the call's named role
description:
The usage meter for videos decides the stage of a call (plan, pieces, improve, audit, repair, fix or cut) by testing how the prompt starts or ends, in a chain of seven tests. Prompt wording, and the order in which prompt parts are joined, are therefore hidden rules: rewording a prompt can file usage under the wrong stage without any error. The cut number reaches the meter as a sixth positional argument that exists only for the meter.

After this ticket each video model call states its stage and its cut where the call is made, and the meter reads them.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every video model call states its stage, and its cut where it has one, at the call.
- The usage meter never reads prompt text to decide a stage.
- Usage history records the same stage and cut for each call as before.
- Rewording a prompt changes no stage.
notes: Defaults: video calls take (instructions, input, { stage, cut, onText, images, tools }); stage and cut ride on the request beside role (adapters ignore them) and the meter in server/http/jobs/media.mjs reads request.stage/request.cut. The sixth generate argument is gone. video-models test fake now reads tree.stage instead of matching prompt text.

title: Visual and diagram calls use the video call path
description:
The video pipeline has one function that calls a model, collects the stream, bounds the output and meters the call. Visuals and the older Mermaid diagrams each re-implement it, with their own race between the time limit and an abort, and their own wiring of the text tool instructions for models without tool calls.

A fix to one of the three does not reach the other two.

After this ticket all three kinds of media call go through one path, and each call names its role.
design: Grow the existing video call function into the one media call path; do not add a second beside it. The time limit and the output bound of each kind stay as arguments. The role name travels on the request as in the quick thinking calls.
acceptance_criteria:
- Visual, diagram and video model calls share one call path; the race between time limit and abort and the output bound are each written once.
- Each call carries a role name.
- A visual or diagram that times out, overflows or is aborted ends with the same message and state as before.
- Models without tool calls still receive the text tool instructions as before.
notes:
Defaults: videoCall renamed to mediaCall in server/media/media-call.mjs; each kind passes { role, bytes, overflow, tooManyItems?, incomplete, failed(reason) }. Roles: 'video', 'visual', 'diagram' (request field role; video stages are mdc.3). The race is raced(controller, promise, budget, timedOut) in the same module, wrapped around the whole visual/diagram run (so validation stays under the time limit) and used by the video wait. Text tools: tools = { capable, textTools, ...native }; mediaCall appends textTools to the end of the instructions when not capable, so the visual TEXT_TOOL line moved from after the fixed rules to the end. Diagram overflow now waits for the stream to end instead of aborting it at once; same message. A visual no longer blanks its partial at the moment of overflow; the retry blanks it as before.
CI fix: mediaCall checked status before overflow, so a diagram that overflowed and then ended unfinished said 'did not complete' instead of the old overflow message (old diagrams aborted at once). Added kind.overflowFirst, set only for diagrams; videos and visuals keep 'incomplete wins' since their overflow triggers a retry. Tests now expect role on the request.

title: Quick thinking calls share one path
description:
Six places call the quick thinking model with the same block of about 40 lines: choose the quick thinking model for the conversation, check it can be used, attach the answer tool, call with no thread, check the status and read the answer. They are the title job, the verdict job, the two brief explanation calls, compaction and the suggestion fallback.

A change to how a quick thinking call is made needs six edits, and one missed copy behaves differently from the rest.

After this ticket one module makes the call, and each of the six names its role when it calls.
design: Put the module beside the model role code. It uses the stream collecting helper from Rabbithole-au3.9. The role name travels on the request, so the usage meter and test fakes can read it; provider adapters ignore it. Callers keep their own prompts and their own handling of the answer. The six callers join collected text with different separators today: keep each one as it is, and record any that looks like a mistake in a comment on this ticket instead of changing it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The six quick thinking calls go through one module, and none repeats the model choice, the usability check, the call and the status check.
- Each call carries a role name that the usage meter can read.
- Titles, verdicts, brief explanations, inherited context and fallback suggestions come out the same as before for the same model output.
- An unusable quick thinking model, a failed call and a stopped server are each handled as before in all six.
notes: Default: server/http/quick.mjs holds quickCall(provider, role, quick, opts) (request with role, optional quick tool, collectText, aborted/status/empty check) and quickCalls(ctx) -> ctx.quickModel(tree, unset) (quickFor + throw; unset=true lets suggestions keep a provider-default null model) and ctx.askQuick(role, quick, opts) (metered + toolCapable). suggest() now takes the resolved quick model; the subscription-provider check for an unset model moved to the suggestion job. Log redaction skips request.role like tool definitions. Separators kept: title ' ', verdict '', brief '\\n', batch briefs '', compaction ' ', suggestions '\\n\\n'. None looks wrong; '' (verdicts, batch briefs) can glue two text items but both read JSON or tool calls, so it is harmless. Title's warn cause now carries quickFor's 'Quick thinking cannot prepare this chat's context.' prefix (log only). A suggestion call whose generate throws now carries any usage already reported (before: only status and parse failures did).

title: One module for asking a model
description:
Every place that asks the chat model, the smart model or the quick thinking model builds the call itself: it picks the model, sends the request, collects the stream and reads the usage. The video usage meter works out which kind of call it is metering from the wording of the prompt.

After this epic one module takes a named role and a prompt and returns the text and the usage. The provider's generate call stays the seam beneath it, with its three adapters (Claude, Codex, custom endpoint) and the test fakes.

This builds on Rabbithole-au3.9, which makes the stream collecting rule exist once. From the architecture review of 2026-11-21. Candidate 1.

title: The memory note can grow without limit
description:
The memory note is one text about the learner. The tutor adds lines to it with its memory note tool, and the learner edits it in Settings. The whole note goes into every chat prompt and every discussion prompt.

Nothing limits its size. Case: 500 added lines are about 50 KB, roughly 12,000 extra tokens on every reply. Past 100,000 bytes the Settings save hits the JSON body limit and answers "Message too long", so the learner cannot trim the note by hand.

After this ticket the memory note has a limit of 8,000 characters. A tutor edit that would pass it fails with a message that tells the tutor to rewrite or delete entries. A Settings save over the limit is refused with a clear message.
design: One constant for the limit. Check the resulting length where the tutor's edit is applied (it covers add and replace) and where Settings saves the note. A note that is already over the limit must stay loadable, and a save that makes it shorter must pass, so the learner can get back under the limit.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tutor edit that would take the memory note past 8,000 characters is refused; the tutor is told to rewrite or delete entries, and the note is unchanged.
- A Settings save of a note over the limit is refused with a message that names the limit.
- A memory note saved before this change that is over the limit still loads, and the learner can save a shorter one.
- A note at or under the limit saves as before, from the tutor and from Settings.
notes: Default: an edit is refused only when the result is over 8,000 chars AND longer than the current note (tooLong in server/tools/memoryNote.mjs). So an over-limit note saved before this change loads, and any shortening save (tutor delete/rewrite or Settings) passes, per the design. Store layer is unchanged.

title: Windows npm start downloads the sandbox launcher from the published release
description:
On Windows, `npm start` downloads the sandbox launcher that runs model-written code. The setup script names release tag `desktop-build-4`, which does not exist, and its SHA-256 is a placeholder of 64 zeros, marked as a shortcut. So on a Windows `npm start`, videos and offline Python stay off, though the README says startup downloads the launcher.

After this ticket, setup uses the real tag and hash of the release published in the blocking ticket.
design: Set SANDBOX_RELEASE in the tools setup script to the tag and SHA-256 recorded in the comment on the blocking ticket, and remove the shortcut comment. Keep Git local: no push and no release run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setup names a published release tag and the launcher's real SHA-256; no placeholder hash remains.
- A downloaded launcher whose hash does not match is still refused.
- The README sentence about the Windows launcher download is true.
close_reason: SANDBOX_RELEASE set to desktop-build-9 and its real launcher SHA-256; shortcut removed; mismatch test still refuses bad zips

title: Map layout is lost when the window closes within a minute
description:
The map keeps node positions, folds, the viewport and the selected conversation in memory and writes them at most once per minute (decided in TreeTutor-b1z.17). Nothing writes them when the page or the desktop window closes.

Case: drag some conversation nodes, quit the desktop app 20 seconds later, open it again. The map is back in its old place. This is a normal quit, not a crash. The usage guide also says the layout saves "when leaving the tree"; no code does that.

After this ticket, closing the page, reloading it or quitting the desktop app saves the pending layout. The one-minute batching stays for normal use.
design: On `pagehide`, flush the layout saver with a request that outlives the page: fetch with `keepalive: true`. sendBeacon does not fit, because the save needs the CSRF header. Check that the desktop shell lets that request finish on quit. Make the guide sentence and the behaviour agree: either flush when the learner switches to another learning tree too, or correct the sentence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Moving a conversation node and closing the page within a minute keeps the new position after reopening.
- The same holds for a fold, the viewport and the selected conversation.
- Quitting the desktop app within a minute of a layout change keeps the change.
- Closing the page with no pending layout change sends no layout save.
- The usage guide's sentence on when the layout saves matches the behaviour.
notes: Defaults: guide sentence corrected (no flush on switching learning trees; the minute batch still covers that). Page flushes on pagehide with fetch keepalive; desktop window close awaits window.rabbitholeSaveLayout (3 s bound) before closing, and before-quit closes the window before SIGTERM so Cmd+Q/menu quit also saves.

title: Publish the desktop release so the README download buttons work (owner)
description:
The README download buttons link to `releases/latest/download/<installer>`. At audit time (2026-11-21) GitHub had one release, `desktop-build-3`, and it was a draft. "latest" skips drafts, so both buttons answer 404. This is the first thing a visitor clicks.

Publishing is the owner's step: AGENTS.md keeps pushes and release runs with the owner. An agent does not work this ticket.
design: The owner runs the release workflow and publishes the release. The Windows job prints the SHA-256 of the sandbox launcher; the follow-up ticket needs that value and the release tag.
acceptance_criteria:
- A published (not draft) release holds the Windows installer, the Linux installer and the Windows sandbox launcher.
- Both README download buttons download an installer.
- A comment on this ticket records the release tag and the SHA-256 of the sandbox launcher.
notes: PR worker stopped without changes: the description says an agent does not work this ticket, and AGENTS.md leaves release runs to the owner. Checked 2026-11-21: the only release, desktop-build-3, is still a draft. Owner steps: (1) run the desktop release workflow or publish desktop-build-3 if it already has the Windows installer, the Linux installer and the sandbox launcher; (2) check that both README buttons download an installer; (3) comment the release tag and the SHA-256 of the sandbox launcher (the Windows job log prints it) on this ticket. Then close it so the tag/hash follow-up can start.
close_reason: desktop-build-9 published; README buttons download installers; tag and hash recorded in comment

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Release desktop-build-9 published 2026-11-22 with the Linux AppImage, Windows installer and rabbithole-sandbox-windows-x64.zip. Sandbox launcher SHA-256: 2b0f5b4f4e0d29624e8330e2bbb0ca847d0383f3b49094bd4c50007136b4544b (GitHub asset digest and a local download agree). Both README download buttons answer 200.

title: Free-branch + on conversation nodes on the map
description:
Spec: docs/free-branch-and-interactive-visuals-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fbv).

A conversation node on the learning tree map shows a subtle + on hover and on keyboard focus, only when that conversation has a completed tutor reply. The + opens the existing branch question box beside the node with no passage. Sending creates a free branch from that conversation and opens the child. The map's branch line already attaches by reply, so it needs no layout change.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fbv.3.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Hovering or focusing a conversation node with a completed tutor reply shows a subtle +; a node without one shows none.
- The + opens the branch question box beside the node with no passage; sending creates a free branch and opens the child's focused chat.
- The new branch line attaches at the parent's latest completed tutor reply.
- The + is a labelled control reachable by keyboard, and Escape closes the question box.
notes:
Defaults: map + is a new FreeBranchForm (BranchForm is bound to passage anchors), opened to the right of the node, header 'Ask on the side, after its latest reply' per mockup. + shows only when the node preview has a completed assistant reply. askFromMap posts {free:true, question} and opens the child if the learner is still where they were; parent drafts stay untouched. Escape/close returns focus to the +; outside click closes without refocus; a refused branch keeps the box and question.
The + carries its label (aria) but no hover tooltip: the mockup names only the label, and an Astryx tooltip hangs the clamped-rows map test's scrollHeight fake.

title: General interactive-visual principle in the visual guidance
description:
Spec: docs/free-branch-and-interactive-visuals-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fbv).

In the visual writer's guidance, replace the sentences that make interaction the default when an idea has a meaningful variable with this principle: "Treat a visual as something the learner plays with, not a picture to look at. When what it shows depends on values the learner could vary, start from a sensible example, let them change those values, typing their own where that makes sense, and show the result follow. Make plain what they can change. Leave it static when nothing meaningful varies." The surrounding input-validation and control rules stay. There is no host change: controls and drags already never pick a visual part.
acceptance_criteria:
- The visual guidance states the principle above in place of the old interaction-default sentences.
- The input-validation, reset and control rules around it are unchanged.

title: Free-branch chips at the bottom of their reply
description:
Spec: docs/free-branch-and-interactive-visuals-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fbv).

In the parent's focused chat, each tutor reply that free branches hang off ends with a row of them. Each entry is the branch's address chip in family ink, reusing the existing address chip look as explored groundwork chips do, followed by the branch title. Entries are in address order and the row wraps when full. A long title truncates; the chip never does, and the full title stays in the entry's label. On the latest reply the row sits between the reply and its next questions. Choosing an entry opens that child.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fbv.2.html
acceptance_criteria:
- After two free branches from one reply and one from a later reply, each reply ends with its own chips, in address order and family ink.
- A row with more chips than fit its width wraps without overflowing.
- On the latest reply, the chip row sits above the next questions.
- Choosing a chip opens that child's focused chat; chips are reachable and labelled for keyboard use.
- Deleting a free branch removes its chip and renumbers later siblings as other branches do.
notes: Defaults: free-branch row renders inside the reply after ReplyFeedback and before NextQuestions (Astryx ChatMessage draws the copy/usage footer after its children, so the row sits between reply and next questions as the spec says). Chips derive in ChatThread from state.trees (parent + messageId, no artifact, passage === ''), sorted numerically by address, inked via conversationAddresses. Entry is a secondary Astryx Button: address chip as icon, title as label (Astryx truncates the label; the icon box does not shrink), aria-label 'Open <address> <title>'. Row starts with the origin-ring station mark.

title: Free branch from the focused chat
description:
Spec: docs/free-branch-and-interactive-visuals-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-fbv).

The focused chat's question box gains "Ask on the side" beside Send. It sends the typed question as a free branch: a child conversation with no passage, groundwork or visual part. The server hangs it off the parent's latest completed tutor reply, chosen on the server, and saves it with no offsets, no visual and an empty passage text. There is no schema change. The child's compaction has no passage, and its tutor context has no selected passage. The child opens in its focused chat, like any branch. The compaction starts at creation, as for groundwork, with no form-open preparation.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-fbv.1.html
acceptance_criteria:
- Ask on the side creates a child conversation from the typed question and opens it; the child inherits the parent conversation up to that moment with no passage.
- The child hangs off the parent's latest completed tutor reply, takes the next address and its family ink, and survives reopening the app.
- Ask on the side is unavailable before the conversation's first completed tutor reply, while the conversation is responding, when the question box is empty and when the question has attachments.
- The server rejects a free branch with 400 before the parent has a completed tutor reply, and when it mixes free-branch fields with passage offsets, groundwork or a visual part.
- Ask on the side is a labelled control reachable by keyboard.
notes: Defaults: free-branch request body is {free: true, question}; any passage, groundwork, visual or messageId field with it is 400. freeAnchorOf sits beside anchorOf so prepare/brief never accept a free form. Compaction prompt for a free branch drops the two passage sentences and the passage field; tutor context uses a free-branch intro with snapshot only. Ask on the side uses ChatComposer sendActions (left of Send), aria-disabled with the reason as tooltip; not drawn before the first completed reply. Origin line reads 'Asked on the side of <parent>, after its latest reply' per mockup; Inherited context omits the empty Passage row.

title: Free branches and interactive visuals
description: The learner can start a branch with their own question, with no passage: a free branch. They use "Ask on the side" beside Send in the focused chat, or a subtle + on a conversation node on the map. It inherits the parent conversation up to that moment, hangs off the latest completed tutor reply and opens like any branch. Its address chip sits at the bottom of that reply. A learning tree keeps one root, so there is no forest. Visual guidance changes to a general principle: a visual whose result depends on values starts from a sensible example and lets the learner change or type those values. It shows the result follow and stays static when nothing varies. See the spec.

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/44965302476. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Root cause: au2.3 moved the Claude prompt to a per-turn --system-prompt-file; openai-switching.slow.mjs now captures args via inlineArgs. Also inlined PROMPT_RESOURCES in send.mjs to pass check-size (552>550). PR #58, slow run 44965642679 green.

title: Web search readiness: a real search runs before every reply, and a crashed SearXNG still reports ready
description:
Two faults in how the server knows whether web search works.

First, before every reply the tool runner asks the search status to decide which tutor tools to offer (server/tools/runner.mjs). That status check runs a full search for the word Rabbithole on the real search engines, with a 30 second limit (server/tools/searxng.mjs). Video jobs do the same (server/media/videos.mjs). Each reply starts later, and the engines block the instance sooner.

Second, the server watches its own SearXNG process for an exit only while it starts (server/searxng.mjs). If the process dies later, the state stays ready and launch returns early, so it is never started again. Search tools then fail or vanish with no reason shown.

After this ticket deciding which tools to offer costs no outside request, and a SearXNG process that exits after startup is reported as not ready and can be started again.
design: For the managed instance use its own ready state. For a SearXNG address the learner typed in, reuse the last probe result for about a minute.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ten replies in a row cause at most one outside probe search; a test with a counting fake search shows it.
- The explicit check in Settings still runs a real probe.
- When the managed process exits after startup, the status is not ready with a message for the learner, and the next launch starts a new process; a unit test with a fake child process shows it.
notes: Defaults: added searxngSearch.ready() for tool offering (runner, video jobs); managed instance answers from its own state, a typed URL reuses its last probe for 60 s keyed by URL. Settings keeps status(), which always probes. Fault 2 was already handled on master: the startup 'close' listener stays attached, so a post-startup exit sets ready:false with stderr, and searxngDownload.launch then starts a new process; added a fake-child test proving the restart, no code change there.

title: A custom endpoint model can call tools without end
description:
The tool loop for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (server/providers/openai.mjs) runs until the model stops asking for tools. A comment there says it has no call limit. A small local model that keeps repeating the same web_search call never stops, and every round sends a longer history. In a background job (a video, a compaction, a discussion) nobody watches, so a paid endpoint keeps charging until someone notices.

After this ticket the loop stops after a fixed number of rounds and the learner sees a clear error that names the limit.
design: 30 rounds is a reasonable limit. The existing comment records that having no limit was a choice; this ticket replaces that choice, so update the comment.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a fake endpoint that always answers with a tool call, the reply ends with a clear error after the limit and no further request is sent.
- A normal reply with several tool rounds under the limit is unchanged.
- Text already streamed before the limit is kept, as with other errors in the middle of a reply.
notes: Limit counts model calls: 30 calls per reply; the 31st is never sent and the reply fails with an EndpointError naming the limit. The check sits after the end-section (ENDED) break so a finished reply still ends normally.

title: Reply images from any address load by themselves and can leak private text
description:
The page loads every http or https image the tutor writes in a reply, with no click (the image node in src/markdown/markdown.ts; the page's security policy allows any image host). A PDF, attachment or web page with hidden instructions can make the tutor write an image whose address carries private text, for example the memory note or part of the conversation, to a stranger's server. The browser then sends it.

After this ticket an outside image loads by itself only when its address came from a find_images result in the same reply. The map of those addresses already exists (imageSources in src/markdown/ReplyImage.tsx). The app's own images (attachments, generated assets, data: addresses) load as today. Any other image address is shown as a plain link with its alt text, so nothing is requested until the learner clicks.

Out of scope: the read_page tutor tool stays a second path for the same leak when it is switched on.
design: This changes what learners see when the tutor writes an image address from memory or from a web_search result: a link instead of a picture. That is the intended trade. No new screen or component, so no mockup.
acceptance_criteria:
- An image whose address a find_images call returned in the same reply is shown as today.
- The app's own images are shown as today.
- Any other http or https image appears as a link with its alt text, and the page makes no request for it.
- A component test covers a listed address and an unlisted one.
notes:
Defaults: gate lives in renderMarkdown's image node (listed = address is a key of the find_images sources map). Unlisted http(s) image renders as <a target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer> with alt text (URL when alt empty); inside an existing link it renders the alt text only, so anchors never nest. App images (attachments, assets, data:) never pass through Markdown image nodes, so they are untouched; no same-origin exception added. CSP img-src left as is.
CI: first run failed only in test/media/video-runaway.test.mjs (unrelated, passes locally, 'Cannot interpolate an input which is not a number'); rerun green. Likely flaky.

title: Release workflow builds both installers and smoke-tests them
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Workflow, Smoke test).

The hand-triggered desktop build workflow switches from Tauri to electron-builder on Ubuntu 22.04 and windows-latest and uploads both installers to a draft release, as today. After building, each job starts the bundled server from its own build output on an empty temporary data folder and checks it answers; on Windows it runs the sandbox's one-time setup (runners have admin rights); then it renders one fixture cut through the video sandbox to a validated MP4 and runs one fixture run_python call in the sandbox. No models, no accounts, no network for the checks. A failed check fails the job and the release. README's install section describes the AppImage, the Windows installer, the SmartScreen warning and the bubblewrap line. Agents edit the workflow locally; the owner pushes and triggers it (AGENTS.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- The workflow builds both installers with electron-builder and keeps manual trigger only and the draft release.
- Each job runs the smoke test on its own build output and fails on any failed check.
- The smoke test uses only fixture data and no provider or account.
- The smoke script runs locally on Linux against the staged build and passes.
- README describes installing and first launch on Linux and Windows.
notes:
Defaults: smoke script scripts/desktop-smoke.mjs <resources> (desktop/stage, extracted AppImage resources, or installed Windows resources). Linux job opens the AppImage with --appimage-extract (no FUSE/display) and installs bubblewrap; Windows job installs the NSIS setup with /S and finds resources via LOCALAPPDATA/Programs/*/resources/node.exe. The fixture cut renders through the server's own export route (POST /api/videos/<id>/export) from a seeded saved video with test/fixtures/narration.mp3; Windows runs POST /api/setup/sandbox; run_python runs the build's pythonTool in-process (no HTTP route reaches it without a model). Blocker: the local run against desktop/stage was denied by the agent's permission classifier (staging and starting the server); the owner runs: node scripts/desktop-stage.mjs && node scripts/desktop-smoke.mjs desktop/stage
Also fixed master's send.mjs line count (553 > 550 after au2.6 + au2.9) so CI passes; same behaviour.

title: Windows desktop installer with bundled tools and the sandbox
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Bundled tools, Installers and release: Windows resources).

The staging step and electron-builder also build on Windows: a per-user NSIS installer into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs with no admin rights, the pinned Windows Node 24, Windows standalone Python with the same packages, TinyTeX and Remotion's Windows headless Chromium. The sandbox launcher and its Codex helpers ship beside each other in the resources, and the shell passes the launcher's location to the server. The Windows sandbox's read rules cover the install folder that holds Node, the server and the tools. Windows tickets cannot run on the Linux machine Ralph uses: acceptance is that the config and staging code are complete for the Windows target and their unit tests pass; Windows behaviour is proven by the workflow smoke test.
acceptance_criteria:
- The staging step and electron-builder config have a complete Windows path (Node, tools, sandbox launcher and helpers, per-user NSIS).
- The shell passes the sandbox launcher's location on Windows.
- The sandbox's read rules include the install folder; covered by a unit test of the launcher arguments.
- Linux builds and tests still pass.
notes: Defaults: NSIS oneClick + perMachine:false (electron-builder's per-user %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs install, no elevation), icon icons/icon.ico, unsigned. Install-folder read rule: on Windows sandboxCommand prepends --read <dirname(RABBITHOLE_SANDBOX)>, the resources folder holding node.exe, app and tools (holds no learner data). Windows stage makes no .venv-python link (NSIS carries no links); pythonVenv falls back to the bundled tool root's .venv when .venv-python is absent (never for the project folder). tools-setup's tar runs as System32 bsdtar on Windows, like the Node unpack.

title: Electron desktop app for Linux replaces Tauri
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Shell, Installers). ADR 0019.

A separate desktop package holds Electron and electron-builder, so npm ci in a clone never downloads Electron. Electron's main process starts the bundled Node 24 on the server entry with port 0, shows a short Starting Rabbithole page, reads output until the Rabbithole: <url> line, then loads it; if the server exits first the window shows its output as the error. The app runs in place from the AppImage mount: no copy step. Quitting stops the server; on Linux the server gets SIGTERM if the shell dies. Window locks: no Node integration, context isolation, sandboxed renderer, no preload API, navigation only to the server's origin, other http(s) links and new windows go to the default browser, other schemes refused. Page downloads (exported MP4) open the native save dialog. The shell passes the tool root to the server. electron-builder makes an unsigned AppImage with the existing app icon. The Tauri shell, its config, launcher page and staging go; the Windows sandbox launcher crate stays. npm run desktop:build builds the new app.
acceptance_criteria:
- The AppImage opens the app within a few seconds of launch, first launch included, with no files copied into the data folder.
- The app shows its icons and matches npm start in Chromium.
- A reply link to another site opens in the default browser; the window never leaves the server's origin.
- Exporting a video opens a save dialog and writes the MP4 where chosen.
- Closing the window stops the server; a second copy shows the already-running message.
- No Tauri code or config remains; npm start and npm ci in a clone are unaffected.
- The shell's decisions (address from output, navigation allow-list, early-exit error) are plain functions with unit tests (seam 2).
notes: Defaults: desktop/ is its own npm package (electron 45.4.1, electron-builder 26.18.0, exact pins, own lockfile); root npm ci never sees it. Shell = desktop/main.mjs (ESM main) + desktop/shell.mjs (serverUrl, navigation, startError; tested in test/desktop/shell.test.mjs so root CI runs it). Resources: electron-builder extraResources copies desktop/stage as-is (checked app-builder-lib 26.18: no default excludes for extraResources, symlinks kept, so .venv-python stays a link and __pycache__/.pyc survive). Linux PDEATHSIG via /usr/bin/setpriv --pdeathsig SIGTERM (Node spawn has no prctl); plain spawn when setpriv is missing. Downloads use Electron's default will-download path: no save path set, so the native save dialog opens. Menu bar auto-hidden (Alt shows it). New windows always denied; their http(s) links go to the default browser. Windows: RABBITHOLE_SANDBOX passed; NSIS config left to elx.6. Workflow: Tauri caches/prereqs replaced by Electron caches and Cairo/Pango headers; full switch + smoke test stay with elx.7.

title: First-run setup asks only for bwrap when tools are bundled
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (First-run setup in the desktop app).

When the server runs with bundled tools, first-run setup's Linux line asks only for what is missing at runtime: sudo apt install bubblewrap when bwrap is absent, with Check again. It no longer checks pkg-config or headers. Under npm start the existing full line stays. Windows' one-admin-prompt sandbox step is unchanged. In the desktop app the Downloads icon only ever shows web search.
acceptance_criteria:
- With bundled tools and bwrap present, setup shows no Linux install line.
- With bundled tools and bwrap missing, setup shows only the bubblewrap line and Check again.
- Under npm start the full line appears as today when packages are missing.
- Covered by unit tests of the setup decision (seam 3) and a component test where the setup screen changes.
notes: Defaults: 'bundled tools' means RABBITHOLE_TOOLS_DIR points away from the project folder (toolRoot !== projectRoot). Bundled Linux line: 'sudo apt install bubblewrap' on Debian/Ubuntu, words 'bubblewrap' elsewhere; pkg-config/headers not probed. UI copy unchanged (screen renders whatever /api/setup/system returns). Downloads showing only web search comes from elx.1's tool-root readiness; no change here.

title: Linux desktop build bundles Node, the app and every video tool
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Bundled tools).

A staging step builds the desktop resources for Linux: the pinned official Node 24 (SHA-256 checked, as today), the built app with production dependencies only, and a tool root holding a relocatable standalone Python (from uv) with Manim at its pinned version, the offline Python packages and yt-dlp installed straight into it, TinyTeX with Manim's documented LaTeX packages and dvisvgm, and Remotion's headless Chromium. Other OSes' native binaries are removed (above all onnxruntime-node's) and build-only packages left out. If the Manim and offline Python pins clash, ship two standalone Pythons. Cairo and Pango come from wheels or system runtime libraries, never build headers. Not bundled: the Claude Code and Codex CLIs, SearXNG, ffmpeg.
acceptance_criteria:
- The staging step produces the resources on Linux and fails if they contain another OS's native binaries or miss a bundled tool.
- The server started on the staged Node with the staged tool root and an empty data folder reports every video tool ready and queues no download.
- A sandboxed Manim clip and a sandboxed run_python call work from the staged tools after the staged folder is moved to another path.
- The staged size is recorded in the ticket's close comment.
notes:
Defaults: scripts/desktop-stage.mjs stages desktop/stage/{node, app/, tools/} as plain folders (no app.tar: the shell runs in place; the Tauri desktop:build that reads app.tar is replaced by elx.5). tools/ keeps the project layout: .tools/uv (pinned uv), .tools/TinyTeX (+ MANIM_TEX_PACKAGES via existing ensureLatex), .venv = uv's standalone CPython 3.12 with manim, yt-dlp and PYTHON_PACKAGES installed straight in (--break-system-packages, --compile-bytecode; pins resolve together so one Python), .venv-python = relative symlink to .venv, node_modules/.remotion/chrome-headless-shell/linux64. pycairo/manimpango have no Linux wheels: they build at stage time against the build machine's Cairo/Pango headers and link only system runtime libs (libcairo2, libpango). pip is uninstalled from the bundle (carries Windows .exe launchers). onnxruntime-node's other OS/CPU folders are removed; the stage then fails on any PE, Mach-O or other-CPU ELF file, and on any bundled tool that does not run by its own path. Build-only packages = npm ci --omit=dev. Tool staging on Windows is left to elx.6.
Staged size: 2492 MiB (92,625 files) on linux-x64 after pruning (2752 MiB before dropping onnxruntime CUDA/TensorRT providers). Node 122M, TinyTeX 548M, Python 759M, Chromium 243M, uv 37M, app ~1.0G. Evidence in PR #51.

title: Server finds every video tool from one tool root
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Running in place: Tool root, Download manager). Prefactor for the desktop app.

The server resolves uv, TinyTeX, the Manim Python, the offline Python, yt-dlp and the video browser from one tool root. By default it is the project folder, so npm start behaves exactly as today; an environment setting from the desktop shell points it at bundled tools. Python is run as an interpreter (venv or a standalone Python) with python -m, not through venv scripts, so a relocatable Python without a venv works. The video browser's path follows the OS (it is fixed to the Linux build today). The download manager reads readiness from the tool root, so a tool root with every tool present queues no video tool download.
acceptance_criteria:
- With no tool root set, npm start finds and downloads its tools exactly as before.
- With a tool root set, Manim, offline Python, clips, LaTeX and the video browser are all looked up there, and nothing is looked up in the project folder.
- A standalone Python with no venv at the tool root is used for Manim, clips and run_python.
- The video browser path is correct for Linux and Windows.
- A tool root with every video tool present makes the download manager queue no video tool; web search can still be queued.
- Tool resolution and the download manager behaviour are covered by unit tests with a fake filesystem and platform.
notes: Defaults: env RABBITHOLE_TOOLS_DIR sets the tool root (empty/unset = project folder). The tool root keeps the project folder's layout: .tools/uv, .tools/TinyTeX, .venv (Manim + yt-dlp Python), .venv-python (offline Python), node_modules/.remotion/chrome-headless-shell/<os>/... for the video browser; each Python dir may hold a venv or a standalone Python (bin/python|bin/python3, Scripts/python.exe|python.exe). yt-dlp runs as python -m yt_dlp. Browser readiness is a file check at that path (browser-setup --check removed); a browser download runs with the tool root as cwd, so a tool root without package.json would download into <root>/.remotion - the bundle must ship the browser. start.mjs still calls ensureBrowser in the project folder (npm start unchanged).

title: Server runs from a read-only app folder
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md (Running in place: Read-only app folder).

At runtime nothing is written under the app folder or the tool root. Every write the server, Remotion, Python, Manim or LaTeX makes goes to the data folder or a job's own workspace: Remotion bundles, Python bytecode, LaTeX font and format caches (TinyTeX's variable data points at the data folder), Manim media, temporary files.
acceptance_criteria:
- The server started from a read-only copy of the project, with a temporary data folder, opens, lists saved trees and serves a saved video's cut.
- Making a video, a Manim clip, an export and a run_python call write nothing outside the data folder and the job workspaces.
- npm start still works from a normal writable clone.
- Covered by one integration test running the server from a read-only copy (seam 5 in the spec).
notes: Defaults: Python processes run outside the sandbox (Manim/offline-Python readiness probes, yt-dlp) get -B so no __pycache__ lands in the tool root (-I ignores PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, so the flag, not the env). The video sandbox sets TEXMFVAR=<workspace>/tmp/texmf-var: TinyTeX's texmf.cnf points TEXMFVAR at its own texmf-var, so LaTeX caches now go to the job workspace and prebuilt formats still resolve from TEXMFSYSVAR (checked with kpsewhich). Clip downloads use the job workspace's tmp instead of os.tmpdir(). The read-only test is test/http/read-only.slow.mjs (it spawns the server, so slow tier per docs/agents/testing.md); it copies server/src/scripts/package.json plus a stub dist, links node_modules, chmods the copy read-only, and asserts the copy's file snapshot and an empty TMPDIR are unchanged. Setup stays unfinished there, so no downloads run; node_modules writes are not snapshotted (it is a link).

title: Electron desktop app with bundled video tools
description:
Spec: docs/electron-desktop-spec.md. ADR: docs/adr/0019-electron-desktop-with-bundled-video-tools.md (supersedes ADR 0011's Tauri shell).

Replace the Tauri shell with Electron showing the unchanged server's loopback address in the same Chromium the owner tests with. The app runs in place from its installer (no copy on launch, read-only app folder), ships Python, Manim, TinyTeX and the video browser so videos work on first launch, and keeps model-written code sandboxed (bwrap on Linux, codex-windows-sandbox on Windows). electron-builder makes an unsigned AppImage and a per-user NSIS installer; the hand-triggered workflow smoke-tests both with fixture data. npm start is unchanged.

Windows behaviour is proven only by the workflow's smoke test, which the owner triggers (AGENTS.md).

title: One store transaction helper instead of hand-written begin/commit/rollback blocks
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

Every multi-step database write goes through one transaction helper instead of about 15 hand-written begin, commit and rollback blocks across the store. The copies already differ: most take the write lock at once and one does not, and a later fix to one copy would miss the others. Learning trees, knowledge graph, media, model profiles and schema upgrades behave exactly as before. Expect about 70 fewer lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One store helper runs a block of writes, commits when it succeeds, and rolls back and rethrows when it fails.
- [ ] Every hand-written transaction block in the store uses it, with unchanged behaviour and return values.
- [ ] Schema upgrades that must switch foreign key checks off outside the transaction still do.
- [ ] A test shows a failure inside the helper leaves no partial writes.
notes: Store.transaction(write) lives on the Store class (server/store.mjs) and always takes BEGIN IMMEDIATE; layout() was the one plain BEGIN and now takes the write lock too. The inline 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE; ...; COMMIT;' schema upgrade strings also go through it, so a failing statement now rolls back instead of leaving the transaction open. The resources rebuild keeps PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF/ON as separate statements outside the transaction. deleteProfile's early ROLLBACK became a plain return false (nothing written yet).

title: Refuse a uv download that does not match its pinned hash
description:
## Parent

Rabbithole-aud (repo audit fixes, 2026-11-21)

## What to build

The uv download, which the Python and video tools need, is refused unless it matches a known hash. Today the app fetches a pinned uv version but never checks the archive before unpacking and running it. The desktop build already pins and checks a hash for the Node runtime, so follow that pattern. TinyTeX is out of scope: its rolling daily bundle is a recorded shortcut with a stated reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every platform's uv archive has a pinned SHA-256 kept beside the pinned version.
- [ ] An archive whose hash does not match is refused with a clear message, and nothing is unpacked or run.
- [ ] The TinyTeX download behaves as before.
- [ ] A test feeds an archive with the wrong hash and sees the refusal.
notes: Hashes from uv 0.13.9 release .sha256 files (linux-x64 cross-checked by downloading). Check lives in unpack() between download and extract, opt-in via sha256 so TinyTeX is unchanged. ensureUv takes hashes = UV_SHA256 as a test seam, like run/probe.

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/44854934065. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Only failure in run 44854934065: claude-runner.slow.mjs drives the real Claude Code CLI, which the GitHub runner lacks/isn't signed into. Default: skip it when CI is set; local test:slow (backlog gate) still runs it; claude-runner.test.mjs covers the flow over the fixture.

title: Suggestion buttons overflow a narrow chat column sideways
description: Found while fixing Rabbithole-mbp.7 (the horizontal scrollbar under the chat column; its cause differs from the page scroll). When the chat column is narrow (window 1024px wide: column ~300px), a suggestion button under a reply keeps its question on one line, so the button (432px for 'How does a reduction show that one problem is as hard as another?') is wider than the column and the chat layout (.astryx-chat-layout) scrolls sideways: scrollWidth 476 > clientWidth 300. Seen in Firefox and Chrome with npm run serve on a copy of real data. No mockup: a bug fix.
design: Let the suggestion label wrap or shrink inside the column (min-width: 0 / white-space on the label span) rather than clipping the chat layout's horizontal overflow.
acceptance_criteria:
- At any window width, suggestion buttons fit inside the chat column and the chat column never scrolls sideways.
- Each suggestion's full question stays readable.
notes: Default: next-question buttons wrap (white-space normal, auto height, min-height 28px sm size, 4px block padding) so one-line buttons keep their old 28px height; no truncation, so the full question stays readable. Checked in Chromium at 520/1024/1440px on a copy of real data: .astryx-chat-layout scrollWidth == clientWidth (was 476 > 312 at 1024px).

title: The page never scrolls after visiting Settings
description: Spec section: Still page. Owner repro: open Settings, come back; the app stays shifted up with an empty band at the bottom, a page scrollbar on the right and a horizontal scrollbar under the chat column. Leading suspect: a scrollIntoView in the Settings window that scrolls every ancestor, the document included. Reproduce with npm run serve, never npm start. No mockup: a bug fix.
design: Find and fix the cause at its source first. Clipping overflow on html and body is the fallback only if the cause cannot be fixed there; Settings content must then scroll inside its own area. Fix the horizontal scrollbar here if it shares the cause, otherwise file it as its own ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
- After opening Settings and coming back, the app sits in place with no empty band and no page scrollbar.
- Settings, the chat and the map still scroll inside their own areas.
- No horizontal scrollbar appears under the chat column, or a separate ticket records its own cause.
notes:
Cause: .sidebar scrolls (overflow-y:auto) but was unpositioned, so its sr-only usage text (absolute) took body as containing block and made the document 12px taller than the window whenever the sidebar outgrew it (Firefox 1280x720 on the owner's data; Chrome at shorter windows). Same class as 66b5341 for .knowledge-panel. Fix: position: relative on .sidebar. Settings' scrollIntoView left unchanged: with nothing stretching the page it only scrolls the settings panel. Horizontal scrollbar has its own cause (suggestion buttons wider than a narrow chat column), filed separately.
PR #30 open, CI green after merging master (master's 3b6b9d0 fixed the Mermaid worker test failures that also hit this branch). Horizontal chat-column overflow filed as Rabbithole-mbp.8.

title: Write brief explanations ahead of time
description: Spec section: Ready brief explanations. Opening a suggestion must show its brief at once (target under one second), so briefs for every suggestion of a reply are written in the background once the reply's suggestions are final.
design: One quick thinking call per reply, after the end section (or after quick thinking marks suggestions for a reply without one), returning every brief through one tool call (ADR 0013). Separate from the hidden-notes call so concepts are not delayed. Metered as brief usage. Never overwrites a saved brief. No backfill of old replies. Selected passages and visual parts stay on demand.
acceptance_criteria:
- After a reply's suggestions are final, every suggestion has a saved brief without the learner opening it.
- Opening a suggestion with a saved brief returns it with no model call.
- Opening a suggestion before its brief is saved writes one on demand, and the batch does not overwrite it.
- The batch records no familiarity evidence.
- A failed batch is logged and suggestions fall back to on-demand briefs.
- Batch calls appear in usage as brief work.
notes:
Defaults: batch = startBriefs in server/http/jobs/briefs.mjs, one quick thinking call with the write_briefs quick tool (terms matched by plain text), metered as 'brief'. Triggered after finishSuggestions for completed replies only: at once after [[end]] (beside, not inside, the hidden-notes call) or after quick thinking marks a reply without one. Stopped (interrupted) replies get no batch. Skips passages already saved; at save time skips any passage with an on-demand call running, and saveBrief stays INSERT OR IGNORE, so an early open is never overwritten. Batch never calls observeBrief. Failure logs 'warn brief saved nothing ahead'. No plain-text fallback beyond <tool_call> text.
createApp briefs option (default false, main.mjs true) like verdicts, so suggestion tests count no batch calls.

title: Visual parts follow objects and steps
description: Spec section: Visual part grouping. In the fusion visual of 2026-11-20 every nucleon was one part (Nucleons) and every label another (Labels), so the learner could not ask about one nucleus, and no part matched the merged or split nuclei.
acceptance_criteria:
- The visual writer's parts rule says a part is one object the learner would name, never a collection of like things such as all nucleons or all labels.
- It says a label sits inside the part it names.
- It says that when objects merge, split or change identity between steps, the script renames and regroups the parts at each step to match what that step shows.
- It says step captions and legends are not parts.
- Part finding in the frame is unchanged.
notes:
Default: rules added to the parts paragraph of server/media/prompts/visual.md with a fusion example; wording test reads the prompt file in test/media/visual-parts.test.mjs. No frame code touched.
CI fix: test/support/tsx.mjs slice guard ran inside the mermaid parse worker (env: {} hides CI) and exited 1 on CI runners; guard now main-thread only. Breaks every PR off master since 760e7c4.
video-runaway.test.mjs 'over 20 minutes still completes' failed once on CI (fake-timer timing flake, unrelated); passed on rerun.

title: Shorter brief explanations; familiarity counted when a brief is opened
description: Spec section: Ready brief explanations. Briefs are about two or three short sentences (GLOSSARY.md, Brief explanation). Today the weak familiarity evidence is recorded when a brief is saved; ticket 5 will save briefs nobody opens, so evidence must move to opening.
acceptance_criteria:
- The brief prompt asks for about two or three short sentences, as a target rather than a hard limit.
- Opening a suggestion's brief, whether saved or freshly written, records the weak familiarity evidence once per suggestion.
- Saving a brief records no evidence by itself.
- Briefs for selected passages and visual parts behave as before.
notes:
Defaults: evidence recorded by new store.observeBrief, called by the brief route after serving a saved or freshly written suggestion brief; keyed brief:<message>:<start>:<end> with INSERT OR IGNORE so it counts once per suggestion passage. saveBrief only saves. A failed write records nothing.
Also fixed test/support/tsx.mjs: the local-limit guard exited Mermaid parse workers (env {}) on CI, failing diagram-parser and artifact-render on every PR. The guard now runs only on the main thread.

title: Discussion markers end the reply; start_discussion removed
description: Spec section: Visual and discussion markers (ADR 0018). The tutor writes one line [[discussion: Name (level): voice | ... | Speaker > line | ...]] as the last thing before the end section: 3 or 4 classmates (name at most 60, level below/near/above, voice at most 500), then 4 to 8 opening lines (speaker an exact classmate name or Tutor, text at most 2000), the last a question to the learner.
design: Same parser and drop log as ticket 2. Repairs: lines past eight are cut; a line whose speaker is not a classmate or Tutor is dropped; a last line that is not a question is accepted. Drops (logged): fewer than three classmates, fewer than four lines after repairs, or not closed by the end of its line. Text after the marker, except the end section, is dropped, like text after [[end]]. Tutor prompt: the benchmark wording for the discussion marker; drop start_discussion and its started result.
acceptance_criteria:
- A valid discussion marker starts the discussion with its classmates and opening lines, and the reply ends there.
- Text after the discussion marker, other than the end section, never appears.
- Lines past eight are cut and lines with an unknown speaker are dropped.
- A marker with too few classmates or lines, or one not closed by the end of its line, starts nothing, leaves no text and is logged.
- start_discussion is no longer offered to any provider; discussions in history read as before.
notes: Defaults: marker parsed in server/media/markers.mjs readDiscussionMarker; classmate part 'Name (level): voice', line part 'Speaker > text' (first '>' splits). Repairs: fields cut to limits (name 60, voice 500, text 2000), control chars removed, classmates past four ignored, a classmate with no voice, a duplicate name or the name Tutor/Learner is dropped, unknown-speaker lines dropped then cut to eight; below/above spread and closing question not enforced. Any closed discussion marker (valid or not) ends the reply: text after it is dropped, only [[next]]/[[video offer]]/[[end]] are read. An unclosed one is removed and logged; text after it stays. Drop log message: 'discussion marker dropped' (visual drops still 'visual marker dropped'). Tool-path prompt gains DISCUSSION_MARKER_RULE (the start_discussion description reworded for the marker).

title: Visual markers carry their fields; show_visual removed
description: Spec section: Visual and discussion markers (ADR 0018). The tutor writes [[visual: name | title: ... | shows: ... | alt: ... | check: ...]] on one line where the visual goes; there is no show_visual tool. Limits as today: name 40, title 120, shows 280, alt 280, check 600.
design: Reuse the streaming marker stripper (ADR 0016/0017 marker family). The visual starts when its marker closes, with the reply so far as the writer's context. Repairs instead of errors: cut over-long fields, title falls back to name, alt to shows, strip control characters. Drops (logged via ticket 1): no shows, or not closed by the end of its line; an unclosed visual marker is removed rather than left as plain text. Tutor prompt: describe the marker, keep [ ] | and line breaks out of fields, math in words; drop all show_visual and queued wording; keep the existing when-to-visualise and check guidance.
acceptance_criteria:
- A closed visual marker starts drawing at once and the visual lands at the marker, including inside :::wide and :::figure.
- Over-long fields are cut to their limits; a missing title or alt falls back to the name or shows.
- A visual marker without shows, or one not closed by the end of its line, draws nothing, leaves no text in the reply and is logged.
- No text of a check's answer appears in a streamed or stored reply, even from a broken marker.
- show_visual is no longer offered to any provider; make_video still works as a tool call.
- The tutor prompt describes the visual marker and mentions neither show_visual nor a queued result.
notes:
Defaults: marker fields parsed in server/media/markers.mjs readVisualMarker; worker request keeps its old shape (title, shows, alt, check_answer, context). Title falls back to name, then to shows. Control characters are removed. A visual marker body may hold single [ or ] so a stray bracket cannot leak its check. An unclosed visual marker is cut whole and logged 'not closed by the end of its line'; one without shows logs 'no shows'; a repeated title logs 'title already shown in this reply'; a visual beside a video logs the besideVideo error. Removed store.moveArtifact (only used for marker moves) and the bare-JSON visualCall fallback. make_video description: dropped the 'queued' wording; text-tools rule no longer says 'treat it as queued'. The tool-path prompt-size budget test now counts prompt + app tool definitions against the pre-ADR-0018 total (9987+6121), since the visual rules moved from the show_visual description into the prompt (native prompt 12129 chars).
CI: first run failed test/media/artifacts-stop.test.mjs:37 (legacy diagram path, 30ms deadline races the duplicate POST under CI load; passes locally, untouched by this change). Rerun of the failed job passed.

title: Log dropped visual markers
description: Spec section: Dropped-marker logging. Today a [[visual: name]] marker with no show_visual call is removed silently (the fusion reply of 2026-11-20 lost its visual this way). Log every such drop so losses show up; ticket 2 and 3 reuse the same log for their drops.
acceptance_criteria:
- Removing a visual marker without drawing a visual logs a warning naming the conversation, the reply and the reason.
- A marker with a matching call logs nothing.
- Replies stream and store exactly as before.
notes:
Defaults: drop log is 'WARN chat visual marker dropped id=<reply> conversation=<tree> cause="no matching show_visual call"'; added 'conversation' to the log FIELDS allowlist; the marker name is not logged (model text); checked once at reply finish, so stopped replies log unmatched markers too; a repeated marker name with one call logs the extra marker.
CI fix: the npm-only guard in test/support/tsx.mjs (760e7c4) exited the Mermaid parser worker, which inherits --import but gets env {} so has no CI var; it broke artifact-render and diagram-parser on every PR. The guard now runs only on the main thread.

title: Media markers, ready brief explanations, visual part grouping and a still page
description: Spec: docs/media-markers-briefs-and-part-grouping-spec.md. Decisions: docs/adr/0018-markers-carry-visuals-and-discussions.md (supersedes the visual and discussion tool calls of ADR 0013 and the marker-plus-call pairing of ADR 0017). Terms: GLOSSARY.md (visual, visual part, step, discussion, classmate, suggestion, brief explanation, quick thinking model, familiarity). Model quality was settled by owner-approved Haiku benchmarks in the grilling session; no ticket calls a real model (docs/agents/testing.md, Real models).

title: Visual parts in 3D visuals
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).
