The visual writer names the meaningful objects of a three.js scene as visual parts, by object name plus a part flag, nested up to three levels.

On hover, the sandbox raycasts against the named objects and picks the smallest one under the pointer. It reports that object's on-screen bounds, so the host draws the same rectangle and name. Clicks that orbit or drag the camera never pick. Everything else works as for SVG visuals.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a new 3D visual, hovering an object draws a rectangle with its name that follows the object as the camera moves.
- One click asks about the object, and dragging to orbit never opens the ask box.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a6c08455eb179b30d (a5f7087). Part = three.js object with non-empty name and userData.part === true. Pick = nearest visible ray hit, then flagged ancestors, max 3. Bounds = bounding-box corners projected to screen, clamped to canvas. Sandbox's THREE copy has a WebGLRenderer subclass calling drew after each frame so the rectangle follows the camera; try/catch keeps picking errors from stopping the animation loop. A click >4px from pointerdown never picks (all visuals). Scene canvases pick despite their own orbit handlers. Visual prompt explains the part flag. Verified jsdom + real three.js raycast, and Chromium WebGL sandbox.html. Shortcut: corners behind the camera project wrongly, hidden by clamp. Scenes not using THREE.WebGLRenderer have no parts.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Branched visual parts stay marked
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).

A part the learner branched from keeps a subtle rectangle in its branch family ink on every step that draws it, the way a passage keeps its underline. The rectangle is thin, never filled, and never covers the part.

Returning to the source, or clicking the part's address chip, opens the visual at the stored step and brings the rectangle into view.

After Try a different version, the branches and their chips stay. The rectangle shows only where the new version has a part with the same trail.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-nvp.8.html
acceptance_criteria:
- After branching from a part, its rectangle shows in the branch family ink wherever the part is drawn, including later steps that continue the scene.
- Clicking the chip opens the visual at the picked step with the part marked.
- A different version keeps the branches, and the rectangle appears only on a part with the same trail.
notes:
Owner 2026-11-20: build without a mockup; docs/mockups/Rabbithole-nvp.8.html will not exist. Design from the spec, reusing the existing suggestion underline and Ask styles.
Implemented on branch worktree-agent-ad89ed6df3b7b97be (1094186), no mockup. Mark: 2px solid branch-ink line, 4px corners (--radius-inner), 3px outside the part, no label, never filled. Frame marks the first visible part whose trail matches; re-measures on change, resize, transition end. 'Address chip' = origin-strip chip in the child conversation; chips under the visual still open the child. Stored step opens once step controls exist. Same trail twice: first branch's ink. Mark reply validated (max 50 entries, valid trails, inside frame). A new version keeps the visual id, so branches stay. Fixture/jsdom/HTTP tests. Not done: 3D parts (.11) not marked; checkVisibility, step jump and look not checked in Chromium.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Pick visual parts from the keyboard
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).

The ask box opened by a visual's Ask button supports picking parts from the keyboard. The host knows the part tree that the sandbox posts.

Arrow keys move between parts at the current level, and the rectangle follows. Enter narrows to the focused part's children, the trail widens again, and the ask box's source follows the pick. Focus stays visible, and screen readers hear each part's name and trail.
acceptance_criteria:
- A keyboard user can pick any part of a new visual and ask about it without a pointer.
- The focused part shows its rectangle and name, and its name and trail are announced.
- Esc ends picking and returns focus to the Ask button.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a112af1f70cc50c00 (5236cae). Sandbox sends its part tree (DOM data-part + three.js userData.part, max 3 levels, visible only, with step) only while the box picks, via the measure schedule; three.js frames trigger it. Host accepts max 200 nodes / 3 levels inside the frame. Ask box gets a listbox of parts at the current level: arrows move and stop at ends; Enter narrows, on a leaf moves to the question; source follows focus; labels give name and trail; crumbs widen. Focused part reuses the hover rectangle and name. Ask button is the box origin so Esc returns to it. New pickPart(trail, step); widenPart uses it. Merge with .4 conflicted in BranchForm.tsx, useChatState.ts, branch-form.test.mjs (picker beside pending), both kept. jsdom only. Not done: keyboard picking from pointer-picked boxes; parts below level 3 or past 200 nodes; Chromium check.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts (c16b9db); full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Point at visual parts and ask
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp). Terms: visual part (GLOSSARY.md). Refines the visual asking and motion spec where it removed tagged parts.

The visual writer wraps every meaningful object of an SVG or HTML visual in a group carrying its visual part name, nested up to three levels. Names are short and in the learner's language, and controls are never named. This is required for every new visual and every Try a different version.

The sandbox reads the part tree and posts names, nesting and bounds to the host. Picking is always on:
- Hovering hit-tests the smallest named part under the pointer, and the host draws a subtle rectangle at its bounds with a small name label.
- One click opens the floating ask box with that part as the source, like clicking an underline.
- Buttons, inputs, selects, sliders, elements with their own pointer handlers, and the step-through Previous and Next never pick.

The ask box shows the trail, such as "Nuclear plant > Reactor > Control rods". Choosing an earlier entry widens the source to that ancestor. The whole-visual Ask button stays.

The sandbox is untrusted. The host accepts only bounded part messages: at most three names per trail, bounded length, no control characters, and bounds inside the frame.

Branches gain the picked part's trail and step as nullable fields, and the label is the part's name. The child's source is the part's name, its trail, and the visual's title and description. A brief explanation for a part comes only on request.

Older visuals without parts, Mermaid diagrams and plain canvas visuals keep only the whole-visual Ask. Visuals have no native text selection.

Mockup: docs/mockups/Rabbithole-nvp.8.html
acceptance_criteria:
- In a new SVG visual, hovering a detail draws a subtle rectangle with its name; hovering a component's own area outlines the component.
- One click on a part opens the ask box for that part, and the trail widens it to a larger part.
- Sliders, buttons and Previous and Next keep working and never open the ask box.
- A question about a part starts a child whose tutor knows the part, its trail and the visual.
- Malformed or oversized part messages from a visual are ignored.
- Old visuals, Mermaid diagrams and canvas visuals behave as before.
notes:
Owner 2026-11-20: build without a mockup; docs/mockups/Rabbithole-nvp.8.html will not exist. Design from the spec, reusing the existing suggestion underline and Ask styles.
Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a4a354dd5a7bfdc24 (b2bde76), no mockup. Parts marked data-part="Name". Rectangle: 2px dotted muted outline like the suggestion underline; name on a neutral chip inside the box near the frame top. Trail reuses .crumbs. A pick floats the ask box over the part; from the enlarged view it closes and opens inline. Branch explanation = visual's description, set server-side. New additive trail (JSON) and step columns. Pointer cursor on parts; no text selection in visuals. Prompt asks for parts; server does not reject visuals without them. Fixture/jsdom/integration tests plus a Chromium sandbox.html check. Not done: Explain briefly for parts (briefs keyed by text offsets); rectangle kept after pick; origin line showing the part name.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Select inside formulas like text
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).

Math in a reply carries source offsets from KaTeX's parse tree, instead of one atomic span for the whole formula.

A drag inside a formula maps to the smallest LaTeX span covering the selected symbols. The span widens to whole groups: fractions, roots, scripts, \left...\right pairs and environment rows. The highlight snaps to the widened span, and the passage is that LaTeX substring. A selection that crosses text and formula applies the same rule at each end. A branch from part of a formula underlines just that part.

KaTeX's parse tree is internal, so pin the version and cover the mapping with unit tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dragging over mc^2 in E = mc^2 asks about mc^2, not the whole formula.
- One row of an aligned derivation can be selected and asked about on its own.
- A selection that cuts through a fraction or superscript widens to the whole term, and the highlight shows the widened span before the learner asks.
- A selection from a sentence into a formula works.
- A branch from part of a formula underlines just that part on return, and existing branches from whole formulas still underline the formula.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-aea85e0093aa62437 (55ad208). Selecting one part of a group (base, numerator, superscript) keeps that part; ∑ alone gives \sum; selecting every symbol takes the whole formula with its $ signs. Braces count as a group. Parts KaTeX gives no offsets for widen to a group, at worst the whole formula (e.g. 12^2). Formula underlines reuse the suggestion style (selector u.suggestion -> .suggestion). katex pinned to 0.19.1 (already in lockfile). Fixture/jsdom tests; native MathML drag not browser-tested. Known gap: reveal on return highlights the whole formula, not the part.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Short brief explanations in markdown
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).

The brief explanation prompt asks for one paragraph of a few short sentences that a learner can skim in a second or two. It says what the term is, or why it holds in this reply. Bold, italics, inline code and inline math are allowed; headings, lists and links are not. There is no word count.

Brief explanations render with the reply's inline markdown renderer, both in the suggestion popup and above the branch question box. Saved brief explanations stay as they are.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new brief explanation is a few short sentences in one paragraph.
- Bold, italics, inline code and inline math in a brief explanation render both in the popup and above the question box.
- Headings, lists or links from the model never render as blocks or clickable links.
- Saved brief explanations look as before.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-ae1b22ebbf034aadc (d6502aa). New src/markdown/inlineMarkdown.ts renderInline reuses parse and mathMarkup (markdown.ts is near the 550-line cap). Block content runs on as one line; links show as plain text; display math shows inline. Prompt names $...$ as math delimiter. Only saved briefs render as markdown; the child-reply preview fallback stays plain text. Fixture tests; inline math look inside .brief-tip/.branch-brief not checked visually.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Quick thinking is always ready
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp).

On any provider, a quick thinking call never waits for a model start-up. Each call starts with clean context and names its own model and effort.

Only the provider of the chosen quick thinking model keeps a runner, and switching to another provider closes the old one:
- Codex already meets this, with one app-server and a fresh thread per call.
- Custom endpoints need nothing.
- Claude keeps one headless CLI process started ahead of time, waiting for its first message.

Check whether Claude Code can clear a session and switch models inside a running process. If it can, reuse the process. If not, replace it in the background after each call. Where a runner's system prompt is fixed when it starts, the task's instructions move into the call's message.

Calls a learner waits for take the ready runner first: brief explanations, and the compaction for a branch being created. A background call (hidden notes, titles, verdicts) uses the runner when it is free, or starts its own process as today. The runner closes after 10 minutes without a quick thinking call. Record the Claude runner's measured idle memory in the ticket notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- With Claude as the quick thinking provider, a brief explanation requested after the app has been idle for less than 10 minutes does not wait for a CLI start-up.
- Two quick calls in a row each see only their own task, never the previous call's text.
- Changing the quick thinking model or profile applies to the next call, without the learner waiting for a restart.
- A brief explanation requested while hidden notes are running is not delayed behind them.
- After 10 minutes without a quick call no runner process remains, and the next call still works.
- Codex and custom endpoint quick calls behave as before.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-ae39f76f6ec8f560a (d364201). Live (Claude Code 2.1.329): a running process clears context (/clear, so the runner omits --disable-slash-commands; messages always start with app instructions) and switches model and effort. Idle runner ~200 MB, ~235 MB after 3 calls; warm calls ~1.0 s. urgent:true calls (briefs, compaction) take the runner; background calls never do; a busy runner falls back to a fresh process. Instructions travel in the message. Settings save and profile switch/delete close the runner; a stopped call kills it and a fresh one starts. Codex app-server unchanged. Risk: thread-less Claude calls with instructions reset the 10-min idle countdown.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Open and branch from a suggestion while the reply streams
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp). This is a chosen default recorded in the spec; the grilling session did not settle it.

Underlines now appear while the reply streams. Opening one before the reply finishes shows its brief explanation and the branch question box, the same as on a finished reply.

A question sent before the reply finishes waits, shown as pending in the box. It creates the branch when the reply completes, so the child's inherited context covers the whole reply. If the reply fails or is stopped, the question stays in the box for the learner to send again. Selecting other text mid-stream stays as it is today.
acceptance_criteria:
- While a reply streams, clicking an underlined suggestion opens its brief explanation and the question box.
- A question sent mid-stream creates its branch once the reply completes, with inherited context from the whole reply.
- If the reply fails or is stopped, the unsent question is kept.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-afbd2d122fb7a9a6b (6a25dba). Brief route runs before the 409 already-responding check, reading reply text saved so far. Send route saves reply text whenever a suggestion closes (otherwise the 250 ms save throttle gave 400s for an immediate click; tested). Mid-stream question kept as branch.pending: box shows 'Waiting for the reply…' / 'Sends when the reply finishes.'; outside clicks (incl. Stop) do not close it, Escape drops it. Branch context preparation waits for completion. On stop/fail/refusal the question returns to the box. Fixture tests only. Not done: hover tip needs a ready suggestion, so a mid-stream brief shows on hover only after completion.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: The end section ends the reply
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp). Decision: docs/adr/0016-tutor-marks-its-notes-inline.md.

Once [[end]] has streamed, the server runs any tool calls already in that model response. It then finishes the reply as completed, drops any text after [[end]] and aborts the provider run, so no further model round can answer again.

An adapter whose run the server ended reports the reply as completed, not interrupted. It records usage summed from each model message, because a stopped run reports no final summary.

After a stopped run, the next learner message must resume the conversation's session on Claude and on Codex. Check that a run stopped while a tool call was pending does not break resume. Custom endpoints simply stop streaming.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reply ends for the learner as soon as its end section is in, and the tutor's run does not continue afterwards.
- A show_visual call in the same model response as [[end]] still shows its visual.
- The reply's status is completed and its usage appears in usage history.
- The next question in that conversation continues the same session with earlier turns remembered, on Claude and on Codex.
- No reply repeats its text after the end section.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a560f93a0897f5548 (09975f3). Text after [[end]] cut in stripMarkers; a call written after [[end]] lands at the reply's end. Adapters emit {type:'response'} when a model response begins; once [[end]] is in, the send route aborts with reason ENDED (chatStream.mjs) after that response's calls ran. Codex: a response starts at a reasoning or agentMessage item; risk: reasoning between text and a tool call in one response would cut that call (item order not checked live). Adapters ignore lines after abort; ended runs log as finished. Live on Claude Haiku: per-message usage sum equals the final result; --resume after kill at next message and after kill with a pending tool call both remember context. Codex live check blocked by usage limit (resets 2026-11-21 03:18); covered by fake app server only.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts (3431df9); full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: The tutor marks notes inline and quick thinking writes the hidden notes
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp). Decision: docs/adr/0016-tutor-marks-its-notes-inline.md.

For every provider, the tutor marks its notes with the shared marker stripper:
- [[groundwork: a; b]] before any reply text, at most three; a later one is ignored.
- [[term]] around each suggestion where it writes it. The term stays, the brackets are stripped, and the passage is the term's place in the stripped text. A term is one to six words.
- [[next: question]] for up to three next questions, and [[video offer: question]] for the rare video offer.
- Always [[end]] to close, with no next questions after a casual turn.

Each marker reaches the client as it closes, through the existing groundwork, suggestion and next-question events. Groundwork shows above the reply as the reply begins, and underlines appear as their terms stream. Suggestions become ready when the reply finishes. The current notes reader's validation and limits apply to the markers, and the tutor still gets the concept neighbourhood.

record_turn is removed: its tool definition, its reader, its prompt rules, the forced tool_choice call for custom endpoints, the guard that refused app calls after it, and its section in docs/custom-endpoint.md.

After every completed reply, one quick thinking call writes the concepts with their topics, the links between them and the concept each suggestion names. The verdict keeps its own background call, which now runs for every reply. When a completed reply has no [[end]], that same call also writes suggestions, groundwork and next questions, through the existing notes path. GLOSSARY.md already describes this.
acceptance_criteria:
- Groundwork from a reply's first line shows above the reply before its text finishes streaming.
- A suggestion's underline appears on the exact term while the reply still streams.
- Next questions show after the text; none show after a casual turn that wrote [[end]] alone.
- No marker text reaches the learner, the stored reply text or copied text.
- Claude, Codex and a custom endpoint behave the same, and no reply makes a record_turn call or a forced extra request.
- The knowledge graph and familiarity still update after each reply.
- A completed reply without [[end]] still gets suggestions, groundwork and next questions afterwards.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a7e75d140a0b76cee (a0fcacb). Bare [[end]] is a marker kind in markers.mjs. Suggestions stream as a new 'suggestions' SSE event, status pending; underlines show while streaming but click only after completion (left for .4); screen readers announce the count on completion. After [[end]] tutor suggestions and groundwork save as ready; the quick call (prompt 'The tutor already marked…') adds concepts via store.nameSuggestions, keeping branch children made meanwhile. Fallback quick call also writes next questions. A stopped reply keeps suggestions/groundwork, no quick call. Notes blocks still hidden but no longer read; tutor prompt asks for markers in every mode. record_turn removed. Fixture tests, run file by file. Left for .3: text after [[end]] not dropped, run not stopped.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: A marker in the text places each visual, and a reply never repeats a visual
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-nvp). Decision: docs/adr/0017-visual-markers-place-visuals.md.

The tutor writes [[visual: name]] in its reply text exactly where a visual goes, and its show_visual call carries the same name: required, a short slug of at most 40 characters. show_visual loses after and side. The Hermes-style text fallback carries name too.

This ticket adds the shared streaming marker stripper to the reply parser; the note markers reuse it later. It removes [[...]] markers as deltas arrive and holds back an unfinished [[ at a delta's end until it closes. An unclosed marker at the end of its line stays as plain text without its brackets. Markers inside code spans, code blocks and math are left as text.

Placement: a visual lands at its marker, whether the marker came before or after its call. Until its marker arrives, a visual shows at the call's position, then moves to the marker. A marker with no call is dropped when the reply finishes.

:::wide holds one image or one visual marker, and :::figure sets an image or a visual marker beside its text. This undoes the images-only rules in the tool prompt rules and the show_visual description.

A show_visual whose title matches one already called in the same reply, ignoring case and whitespace, is not drawn. The same reply means every model response for one learner message. The tutor gets "already shown; continue your reply without repeating it", and the refusal is logged. The queued result wording stays. Stored visuals keep their saved position and side.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reply whose text holds [[visual: x]] mid-reply, with its show_visual call for x after all the text, shows the visual at the marker, never at the end.
- A call that comes before its marker shows the visual at the call's place, then at the marker once the marker streams in.
- A visual marker inside :::wide shows the visual at full width; inside :::figure it shows beside its text.
- The learner never sees marker text, even when a marker is split across stream chunks; [[ inside code or math stays as written.
- A second show_visual with the same title in one reply draws nothing and tells the tutor it was already shown; a later reply may reuse the title.
- A call without name gets a plain error naming name.
- Saved replies show their visuals where they were.
notes: Implemented on branch worktree-agent-a12df6e0581281e72 (4c74346). Marker stripper in server/media/markers.mjs: removes [[kind: value]] whole, keeps text of [[words]] (for .2); uses the renderer's markdown parse to skip code and math, parses only when [[ or trailing [ present. Names/titles match ignoring case and whitespace. name required on the <tool_call> text path too; weak models omitting it lose that visual. record_turn guard left for .2. Fixture tests only; test:affected 506/506.
close_reason: Merged into integration branch inline-notes-visual-parts; full suites and code review run at the end of the epic

title: Inline notes, visual markers and visual parts
description:
Spec: docs/inline-notes-and-visual-parts-spec.md. Decisions: docs/adr/0016-tutor-marks-its-notes-inline.md (supersedes record_turn from ADR 0013 and part of ADR 0008) and docs/adr/0017-visual-markers-place-visuals.md (supersedes ADR 0014). Terms: GLOSSARY.md (suggestion, groundwork, next question, brief explanation, quick thinking model, visual, visual part, step, passage).

Notes arrive while the learner reads: for every provider the tutor marks groundwork, suggestions and next questions inline, the end section ends the reply so the tutor never answers twice, and quick thinking writes the hidden notes. A marker in the text places each visual, a repeated visual title is refused, quick thinking never waits for a start-up, brief explanations are short markdown, formulas select like text, and visuals have nested visual parts the learner points at and asks about.

## Decisions so far
See the spec's Implementation Decisions.

## Fog
Whether Claude Code can clear context and switch models inside a running process; the memory a headless Claude runner uses; session resume after the server stops a run; per-message usage against the final summary it replaces. Branching from a suggestion mid-stream (the ticket for it) is a chosen default to confirm with the owner.
notes: Review fixes merged (0ed26ea), start-up crash fix dcb773c, c245bcc. npm test 956/956 (quick-runner fixed after run), test:slow 22/22. Codex live [[end]] check still pending its usage reset. Branch inline-notes-visual-parts not yet on master.
close_reason: All children merged into inline-notes-visual-parts; code review findings fixed; fast and slow suites pass

title: Fix test:slow failures
description: The slow-test workflow failed on master: https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/actions/runs/44632919088. Reproduce from the run log, fix every failure and open a PR.
notes: Default: launcher failure was the 20s waitFor bound expiring under 8-way CI load (passes in 8s locally); raised to 60s, still under 120s test timeout. Codex test expected usage without reasoning:4 the fixture emits since mpl.2.

title: Soft environment light and shadows in 3D scenes
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). The kit's Lights gains soft environment lighting generated in the kit, with no file, and soft ground shadows on a shadow-catching ground plane. Shadow and environment quality are fixed, chosen for smooth live playback. Nothing is downloaded.
acceptance_criteria:
- 3D cuts that use the kit's Lights show soft reflections and soft ground shadows.
- No file, loader or network request is used.
- Live playback of an existing 3D test cut stays smooth on the owner's machine.
notes:
Defaults: three RoomEnvironment via PMREM (env intensity 0.45, ambient 0.55->0.3); PCFShadowMap (PCFSoft removed in three 0.187) 1024 map, radius 6; kit sets castShadow on every mesh each frame so generated code needs no change; shadowMaterial ground (opacity 0.35) fixed at y=-2 (kit GROUND), named in the 3D cut prompt. Live smoothness on owner's machine not verified by agent.
Lights lives in server/media/video-stock.tsx (re-exported by the kit) to keep video-kit.tsx under the 500-line check.

title: Named finishes and house-style patterns for 3D objects
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). The kit exposes a material helper: a finish name (matte, plastic, metal, glass, glow), a colour expression (palette role, neutral or true colour) and an optional pattern name (wood, brushed metal, panel lines, fabric, stone, tiles, bands). It returns a material whose colour is the given colour and whose pattern is a soft, low-contrast greyscale texture drawn on a canvas inside the kit, multiplied by that colour, with matching subtle relief. Patterns are deterministic and generated once per name. Set-piece and cut 3D guidance tell writers to build materials with the helper, still forbidding loaders, files and their own textures. The house-style skill's 3D line names the finishes and patterns and keeps no photoreal textures, noise or clutter. The colour validator accepts the helper's colour argument through the palette, neutral and true-colour bindings it checks today. Set pieces keep their helper calls in their source, so reuse keeps finishes and patterns.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each finish and pattern name gives a material; the same name gives the same texture every time.
- The material's colour comes from the given colour expression.
- A colour outside the brief passed to the helper is refused as other colours are today.
- 3D guidance and the house-style skill name the finishes and patterns and still forbid loaders and files.
- A reused set piece keeps its finishes and patterns.
notes: Defaults: helper is finish(kind, colour, pattern?) in video-stock.tsx (re-exported by kit), returns a cached MeshStandardMaterial per kind|colour|pattern so per-frame calls reuse one. Patterns are 256px DataTextures computed from seeded lattice noise in code (no DOM canvas, so it also runs in node tests), grey 0.82-1, used as map and bumpMap (bumpScale 0.6). glass = transparent 0.35 opacity (no transmission pass, for live playback); glow = emissive in its colour. Unknown finish falls back to matte, unknown pattern to none. Validator checks finish()'s 2nd argument as a color style.

title: Pen marks in 3D cuts target set pieces
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Pen and cursor marks in 3D cuts name a target set piece, and optionally a named part point the cut writer exports, instead of x and y. The plan tool's mark accepts target for 3D cuts; the plan check rejects a 3D cut's mark without target with a plain error for that call; 2D cuts keep x and y. The cut writer resolves a target to a 3D point and draws the mark through the kit's projection, so marks follow the camera.
acceptance_criteria:
- A 3D cut's mark without target is refused with a plain error for that call.
- A 2D cut's mark with x and y is accepted as today.
- A 3D cut's mark with a target is drawn on that set piece and stays on it while the camera moves.
notes:
Defaults: 3D marks are {tool, sentence, target, part?, label?, shape?}; 3D sketch shapes circle/underline/arrow only (freehand needs pixel points), sized around the projected target (circle r~90px, underline 200px below, arrow from up-left). Cut components now receive an emphasis prop (rendered and live); the app overlay skips target marks and the 3D cut draws them with kit <Marks marks keys at fov>, at mapping 'Target' and 'Target.part' to a 3D point or f=>point; unknown part falls back to target; unknown target or behind-camera point draws nothing. Target names are not checked against recurring objects (cutProblem has no brief).
CI: test/media/visual-detach 'a visual that times out after the turn ended' failed on master too (50ms visual timeout fired before the ~200ms reply stream finished); raised to 3000ms in this PR.

title: Labels in 3D cuts stay pinned to their objects
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). The kit gains a pure screen projection: from the cut's camera keys, a frame, the canvas size and field of view, and a 3D point, it returns the point's place in the 1920x1080 frame and whether it is in front of the camera, reusing the existing camera path. The kit gains a Pin component for the HTML layer above the ThreeCanvas: it takes the camera keys and a 3D point, or a function of the frame for objects with idle motion, places its children at the projected position, and fades them when the point goes behind the camera or off frame. 3D cut guidance changes to pin every label to its object with Pin; titles and legends may stay unpinned. The cut audit gets a 3D addendum: flag a label or mark not on its object. The camera keeps moving.
acceptance_criteria:
- A point at the camera target projects to the frame centre.
- A point behind the camera reports hidden, and its Pin fades out.
- Projections follow the camera path frame by frame.
- 3D cut guidance tells writers to pin labels with Pin.
- The audit of a 3D cut asks for labels or marks off their objects.
notes: Defaults: screenAt(keys, f, point, {width=1920,height=1080,fov=75}) assumes the ThreeCanvas fills the frame (canvas size sets aspect only), fov 75 = r3f default, near 0.1; returns {x,y,front,opacity}, opacity fades over 60px at frame edge and is 0 behind/off frame. Pin hides (display none) at opacity 0. Audit addendum AUDIT_3D appended after AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS for dimension '3d' so stage detection by prefix still works.

title: Planner defaults to 2D
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). The planner rule becomes: default 2d; use 3d only for a cut whose point cannot be shown flat, such as rotation, hidden depth or 3D structure; 3D cuts cost more, since every set piece then needs a 3D form and renders are heavier. Explicit 2D and 3D asks keep their handling. The house-style skill's 2D line allows layered depth (parallax layers) or an isometric view where it helps, and says flat is fine.
acceptance_criteria:
- The planner's instructions state the 2D default, the cannot-be-shown-flat test for 3D and that 3D costs more.
- Explicit 2D asks still give all-2D plans and explicit 3D asks mostly-3D plans.
- The house-style skill allows layered depth or an isometric view in 2D and says flat is fine.
notes: Prompt-only change: planner 2D default + cost note; house-style 2D line allows parallax/isometric, flat fine. Explicit 2D/3D sentences unchanged. PR #7.

title: The tutor decides when to make a video, with a last-resort offer
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Decision: docs/adr/0015-tutor-decides-when-to-make-a-video.md. The server's learner-text check before make_video is removed with its refusal. make_video's description: start a video only when sure the learner wants one, in any wording or language; when the learner only hints at one or still does not follow after the explanation, do not start one, offer it instead as a next question, as a last resort. record_turn's next questions may include one video offer, worded as the learner asking for a video of the idea: at most one per reply, never in a reply holding a visual or discussion. Choosing it sends it as the learner's message, like any next question. Every refused app tool call (video, visual, discussion, record_turn) is logged at warn level with tool name, reply id and reason, without input values. The rules that a video stands alone in its reply stay.
acceptance_criteria:
- make_video starts a video for 'can u quicky a short video how to play, just 2d video' and for a request in another language.
- record_turn accepts one video offer among next questions and refuses a second, or one in a reply holding a visual or discussion, with a plain error.
- Choosing a video offer sends it as the learner's message.
- A refused app tool call writes a warn log line with tool, reply id and reason and no input values.
- A video still cannot share its reply with a visual or discussion.
notes: Defaults: video offer is a separate record_turn argument video_offer (string), appended to next_questions and counted in the three; a second offer, one beside any visual/discussion/video, or a fourth question is skipped and named in the result (record_turn stays tolerant, ADR 0013). Refusals log 'WARN chat app tool call refused' with id, tool, cause (input values redacted); record_turn skips log the same way. The legacy rabbithole-video block keeps asksForVideo (spec names only make_video's check; videos-jobs test covers it). New log field 'tool'.

title: show_visual places itself with after
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Decision: docs/adr/0014-visual-calls-carry-their-place.md. show_visual gains a required after: the last few words of reply text the visual follows, at most about 120 characters. When a native call arrives after text in the same model response, the visual's position is the end of the first match of after in that response's text: exact first, then ignoring case and runs of whitespace, then the end of that response's text. When the tutor stopped at the call, the position stays the text streamed so far, as today. The <tool_call> text path keeps its own position and uses after only when the call sits at the end of the text. The tutor prompt's reply-layout line stops mentioning visual blocks inside :::figure, and :::figure is described for images only.
acceptance_criteria:
- A custom-endpoint response that writes the whole reply and then calls show_visual places the visual after its anchored passage, not at the end.
- Several show_visual calls in one response each land at their own passage.
- An anchor differing only in case or spacing still matches.
- A misquoted anchor puts the visual at the end of that response's text.
- A tutor that stops at the call and continues after queued keeps today's placement.
- The tutor prompt no longer tells models to put a visual block inside :::figure.
notes:
Defaults: after is required for native calls (error goes back to the model) and optional on the <tool_call> text path, where nothing goes back; text-path calls use after only when at the end of the text. When the reply text ends with the anchor, the call position is kept (tutor stopped at the call). A model response starts at the reply length of the previous tool call; a call-only round after a text round searches that earlier text. The writer request does not carry after. :::wide wording left as is (out of scope).
PR #5 open; format and secrets green. The test job is red only on test/map/tree-list.test.mjs (tree grouping and DST tests), which this change does not touch. They pass locally on Node 26 with TZ=UTC, and the same tests fail on PRs #2 and #4: master's CI cannot switch process.env.TZ at runtime, even after e91d548 (Node 26). Options: fix the TZ handling on master (for example TZ in the workflow env, or the test setting TZ before Date is first used), then rerun run 44619227587; or accept the PR with that known failure. Every show_visual-related test passes in CI.
PR #5: all checks green (run 44623208129) after master's TZ/test fixes merged into the branch. Handed to reviewer.

title: Visuals sit beside a section with side
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). show_visual gains an optional side (left or right). The side is stored with the visual. With side, the visual shows beside the section that follows its position, using the existing figure rendering, including the narrow-screen fallback; without it, the visual sits in the flow. Reloading uses the stored values. Images from image search keep :::figure as today.
acceptance_criteria:
- A visual called with side right shows to the right of the section that follows it.
- A visual without side sits in the flow.
- On a narrow screen a sided visual falls back as figures do today.
- Reopening the conversation shows the visual in the same place and side.
- Images in :::figure layouts are unchanged.
notes:
Defaults: side is an optional enum on show_visual (invalid value errors back to the model), stored in a new artifacts.side column (ALTER on older DBs; null = flow). The 'section that follows' is the next top-level block plus following blocks up to the next heading, :::directive, rule or another visual; a leading heading joins it. Several sided visuals at one spot share the media column, side from the first. A sided visual before a directive or at reply end stays in flow. Narrow replies (<480px) render plain flow and wide ones stack via the shared Figure, as :::figure does.
PR #11: all checks green (run 44634902636). schema.mjs was at the 500-line limit, so interrupt() moved unchanged to server/store/recovery.mjs; the side column is added in open()'s additive section (migrate runs only on pre-v1 databases).

title: Find and fix why some endpoints skip record_turn
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Replies through some custom endpoints (seen on github/auto through Omniroute) arrive without the tutor's record_turn call, so every reply makes two extra quick-model calls (verdict and suggestions). Find the cause from stored replies, logs and a live run, such as prompt wording, tool ordering or an endpoint that drops the last tool call, then fix it. Until fixed, the quick-model fallback stays. Also update docs/custom-endpoint.md, which still says tool calls are out of scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- The cause is recorded as a comment on this ticket.
- After the fix, a reply through the affected endpoint carries its suggestions, next questions and verdict from record_turn, with no separate verdict or suggestions call.
- Replies without record_turn still fall back to the quick thinking model.
- docs/custom-endpoint.md describes tool calls on custom endpoints as they work today.
notes: Defaults: fix in the custom endpoint adapter only (Claude/Codex untouched). One forced round at most per reply, only when record_turn was offered, not yet called and text was shown. Text in the forced answer is dropped. The nudge goes as a system message; an endpoint rejecting it or tool_choice fails only the forced call, so the reply completes and quick thinking stands in. Test fake answers forced calls separately (fake.forced/fake.force, like probes) so existing call-count tests stay unchanged.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text: Cause: the model behind github/auto (Omniroute served gpt-5.6-luna) often just ends its text with finish_reason stop and no tool call. Not an endpoint dropping calls: raw SSE dumps showed no tool_calls deltas at all. Live runs with the real tutor prompt and app tools: 3 of 6 replies skipped record_turn, 4 of 5 skipped it in a second batch, mostly after a show_visual round. Moving RECORD_RULE to the end of the system prompt made no clear difference. Omniroute honours tool_choice naming record_turn (2/2 calls, mostly cache-read). Forced calls without a nudge came back sparse (concepts only, 5 of 6 without suggestions); with a system nudge naming next questions and suggestions, 6/6 had suggestions and 4/6 next questions. Fix: one forced record_turn round with that nudge in server/providers/openai.mjs; a failed forced call keeps the reply and quick thinking stands in.

title: Visual retries and set-piece repairs send patches
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). A visual retry sends the previous fragment and the failure and asks for a patch; a patch that fails falls back to a whole fragment, as cut repairs do. A set-piece module that fails its check is repaired by patch first and whole module second, matching cut repairs.
acceptance_criteria:
- A visual whose first fragment fails is retried with a patch, and a valid patch gives a ready visual.
- A visual patch that does not apply falls back to a whole fragment.
- A set-piece module that fails its check is fixed by a patch when the patch applies, and rewritten whole only when it does not.
notes:
Defaults: visual retry sends previousFragment as raw lines after the JSON task (withSource convention) and asks for a diff; a patch that does not apply gets one whole-fragment call within the same retry; an applied patch that still fails validation ends the visual as before (2 attempts). No patch when the first answer overflowed or was empty. Set pieces: a module that failed its check is patched first (PIECES_PATCH_NOTE), whole module second, within the same attempt; with library matches only the code field is patched and the previous piece choices are kept. Visual prompt line about validationError now says whole fragment unless asked for a patch.
PR #4 (https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/pull/4): everything is green except the test job. The only failure is test/map/tree-list.test.mjs 'learning trees group by local creation day, newest first, including midnight and week boundaries' (Older group missing; earlier also 'calendar days stay correct through both daylight-saving changes').
