title: Audit fixes send a patch only
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). An audit fix is one patch call. If the patch fails to apply or validate, the cut goes into its normal repair attempts with the audit's issues as the repair note. The whole-code-inside-JSON fallback is removed.
acceptance_criteria:
- A passing audit-fix patch changes the cut with one call.
- A failing audit-fix patch leads to the cut's normal repair attempts, carrying the audit issues, and no whole-code rewrite call is made.
- A cut that runs out of repairs fails as today.
notes:
Defaults: a fix answer that does not parse, apply or validate (cutSource; for Manim also the check) restores the pre-audit cut and calls rewrite() with 'The cut audit found: <where: what; ...>. Its fix patch failed: <error>' as validationError. A fix that validates but fails to render keeps the pre-audit cut as before (spec names apply/validate only). Fix call provider errors and manimUnavailable keep the cut as before. With no repair attempts left the cut fails via cutError, like the crashed-render path. auditFix now always takes a source and throws instead of returning null; FIX_WHOLE_NOTE removed.
PR #1 (https://github.com/Thomastienn/Rabbithole/pull/1) is open. Its code is complete; the format and secrets jobs pass, but the CI test job stays red for reasons this change doesn't cause. (1) test/map/tree-list.test.mjs fails 2 tests under Node 24, which is ci.yml's node-version and allowed by engines >=24. They pass under Node 26 locally, and this branch doesn't touch that file or src/map/treeList.ts. They also fail locally under Node 24 (npx node@24), so master's code fails the same way. (2) 'video HTTP requests route smart model and effort through the real Claude/Codex adapters' (videos-jobs) and 'claude visual workers get only load_skill' (visuals-prompts) time out on CI at concurrency 8 but pass locally under both Node 24 and 26. This looks like load flakiness. This is the repo's first CI run, so master has never been green. Options: (a) pin CI to Node 26 or fix treeList's local-day logic for Node 24 in a separate task, then rerun; (b) loosen the timeouts on the two flaky tests; (c) merge this PR on the evidence above. One rerun gave the same result.
Resumed: master's CI fixes (Node 26/TZ, tree-list local dates, longer until()) are now in the PR branch; format, secrets and test all pass on run 44621937436. Earlier CI concern resolved.

title: Usage shows reasoning tokens apart from output
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Usage records reasoning tokens as their own field: custom endpoints from completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, Codex from its reasoning output count, Claude where its usage reports them. Output keeps its current total meaning; existing rows have none. The video token breakdown and the usage history totals show reasoning beside output where known; the look otherwise stays the same.
acceptance_criteria:
- A custom-endpoint call reporting reasoning tokens stores them with the usage event.
- A Codex call reporting reasoning output stores it.
- The video token breakdown shows reasoning per stage beside output where known.
- Usage history totals show reasoning where known; older rows show none, not zero.
notes:
Defaults: reasoning is a nullable usage_events column (part of output, not added to totals). Claude CLI result usage reports no reasoning field, so Claude rows stay NULL. Custom endpoint sums reasoning across tool rounds only from rounds that report it. Video breakdown gains a Reasoning column after Output (— when unknown); usage history totals show 'N output (M reasoning)' only when some call in range reported it.
CI test job red on 4 tests unrelated to this change, identical on sibling branch Rabbithole-mpl.3 (run 44614214672): test/map/tree-list.test.mjs (2 date/TZ tests), test/media/videos-jobs.test.mjs 'video HTTP requests route smart model...', test/media/visuals-prompts.test.mjs 'claude visual workers get only load_skill...'. All 4 pass locally (also with TZ=UTC); a rerun failed the same way. Format and secrets green. Options: fix the CI-environment failures on master in a separate task, then rerun PR #2; or accept PR #2 with these known failures.
Resumed: CI fixes landed on the branch (TZ, Node 26, until timeout); all PR #2 checks green (run 44621941533). Handed to review.

title: Model calls stop only when the model stalls
description: Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-mpl). Every model call (Claude CLI, Codex, custom endpoint) ends only after 5 minutes without new output; the custom endpoint's hard 5-minute request limit becomes an idle limit reset by every streamed chunk, including reasoning and tool-call chunks. The whole-video deadline and its per-cut stretch go; a 2-hour runaway guard on the whole video stays, in the same place. Visuals and diagrams follow the same rule, and the app-level defaults that override the generator defaults are removed so one value applies. Sandbox render, snapshot, narration and Manim budgets are unchanged. A stalled call fails with a message saying the model stopped responding, shown inline on the video card; Retry keeps finished cuts as today.
acceptance_criteria:
- A custom endpoint that keeps streaming for 7 minutes finishes its reply.
- A custom endpoint that sends nothing for 5 minutes fails with the model-stopped-responding message.
- A video whose cuts take longer than 20 minutes in total still completes.
- A video still running after 2 hours fails with a message saying it ran over two hours.
- Visuals and diagrams in the running app follow the same stall rule; no 5-minute whole-run limit remains.
- The video card shows the stall message inline, and Retry keeps finished cuts.
notes:
Defaults: stall message 'The model stopped responding for 5 minutes. Partial reply saved; try again.' for Claude, Codex and custom endpoint; video runaway guard 2h with 'Video generation ran over two hours.' (shown inline on the card); visual/diagram whole-run limit defaults to the same 2h guard and keeps its 'timed out' wording; app.mjs no longer overrides visual/diagram limits. Custom endpoint idle timer resets on every SSE data event (content, reasoning, tool-call, usage).
PR #3 CI: format and secrets pass; test fails only on test/map/tree-list.test.mjs 'learning trees group by local creation day…' (expects an 'Older' group; gets 'Previous 7 days' and 'Yesterday'). It's unrelated to this change: the PR touches no tree-list code, the test passes locally on Node 26, and the same failure shows on Rabbithole-mpl.3's CI run 44614214672. CI uses Node 24, and the test changes process.env.TZ at runtime, so the likely cause is TZ/ICU handling on Node 24. Two other failures in the first run (videos-jobs real adapters, visuals-prompts claude workers) passed when the failed jobs were re-run, so they were flaky. Options: (a) fix the tree-list test or CI Node/TZ in a separate task and re-run PR #3; (b) merge #3 with the known-unrelated failure.
Resumed: master's tree-list TZ fix (064ad43, f971029) is merged into the branch (3a55198); CI on that head is green (secrets, format, test).

title: Media: pinned 3D labels, stall limits, finishes, visual placement, video offers, leaner output
description:
Spec: docs/media-placement-limits-and-lean-output-spec.md. Decisions: docs/adr/0014-visual-calls-carry-their-place.md (amends ADR 0013's placement), docs/adr/0015-tutor-decides-when-to-make-a-video.md. Terms: GLOSSARY.md (house style, focal object, next question, visual, cut, set piece, cut audit).

3D labels and pen marks drift because they sit at fixed screen spots while the camera moves; long or slow videos fail on a fixed 20-minute deadline and a hard 5-minute endpoint request limit; 3D objects are flat colour under one light; custom-endpoint visuals land at the end of replies; videos lean 3D; a server regex refuses real video asks; output tokens go unseen into whole rewrites. The kit pins labels and marks to 3D objects, calls stop only after 5 silent minutes (2-hour runaway guard), 3D gets soft environment light, shadows, five named finishes and seven house-style patterns, show_visual carries `after` and `side`, the planner defaults to 2D, the tutor decides about videos with a last-resort next-question offer, usage shows reasoning tokens, and audit fixes, visual retries and set-piece rewrites send patches. No new caps.

## Decisions so far

See the spec's Implementation Decisions.

## Fog

- Why `github/auto` via Omniroute skips record_turn (investigation inside the token work).
- Live playback cost of environment light, shadows and glass on slower machines.

title: Run the full test suites
description: Review and fix; do not file tickets for what you can fix. Run every full test suite the project's testing guide names and fix every failure, then rerun until all pass. Review the commits since the last gate (git log --grep 'Run the full test suites') for defects the suites miss and fix them. If one run cannot finish, record a checkpoint in the notes and leave this open. Mark it blocked only for a concrete external blocker.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every full suite passes
- [ ] Defects found in the commits since the last gate are fixed
notes: Gate 2026-11-19. Full suites: npm test 841/841 pass first run; npm run test:slow 20/21, test/providers/endpoint-switch.slow.mjs failed (stale expectation: since tcl.1/tcl.2 send.mjs offers APP_TOOLS natively to capable providers and as textTools to a non-capable custom endpoint, so the tutor prompt prefix changed). Fixed the expectation. Review of commits since last gate 05d8e5d (focused on the tcl tool-call epic: quickTools, recordTurn, app-calls, plan-calls/videos, openai stream usage, providerError, model search): found loggedProvider (server/log.mjs) treated tool schema strings on the request (to, text, name...) as private values, mangling every logged failure cause (e.g. "Cus[redacted]m endpoint", "Model [redacted]"). Fix: drop tools/textTools from the private values; regression test in test/http/log-format.test.mjs. Rerun: npm test 842/842, npm run test:slow 21/21, test:affected 473/473, format:check and check-size pass. All fixture/in-process checks; no live provider runs needed.

title: Full-suite gate
Fuzzy model search in every model picker
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

One shared model search used in every model picker: endpoint settings, the chat model menu, model profiles, and the smart and quick thinking model settings. Fuzzy subsequence matching ranked so contiguous and early matches come first, showing the top 50 results, no debounce, no new dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
- "son46" finds claude-sonnet-4-6.
- With thousands of models, at most 50 results are drawn and typing does not lag.
- The chat model menu has the search.
- Every model picker uses the same search.
notes: Done. Shared search: fuzzyScore/searchModels/searchGroups in src/settings/models.ts (subsequence match on label or id; rank = fewer breaks, earlier start, shorter text; cap SHOWN_MODELS=50; no debounce, no dependency). Shared UI: ModelSearch field + searchNote + ModelPicker in src/settings/ModelPicker.tsx. Used by EndpointModels, chat ModelMenu (DropdownMenu header search; providers without matches hide during a search), and ModelPicker replacing the hasSearch Selectors in ChatSettings, SmartSettings, SuggestionSettings (quick thinking) and FirstRunSetup. Model profiles pick models through those same role pickers (the profile Selector picks profiles, not models, so unchanged). Decision/tradeoff: Astryx Selector search is substring-only with no filter hook, so model pickers became DropdownMenu radio menus with a header search (trigger aria-haspopup=dialog, rows menuitemradio); search field is not autofocused so menu keyboard nav (Home/ArrowDown/Enter) is unchanged; loose rows (Follow chat default, unavailable) always show. Evidence (jsdom/unit, fixtures): test/shell/model-search.test.mjs (son46 -> claude-sonnet-4-6, 5000 models -> 50 shown under 50ms), test/chat/model-menu.test.mjs (menu search, 3002 models draws 50, no-match note); updated model-roles, chat-settings, suggestion-settings, first-run, endpoint-settings tests and verify-settings-window.mjs role (not run: browser). check-size, format:check, tsc, test:affected (59/59) pass.

title: The quick thinking model's JSON jobs move to tool calls
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

Under ADR 0013, the quick thinking model's structured jobs (the suggestion and verdict fallback and titles) return through plain tool calls validated by the server, with the text fallback for models without tool support, instead of JSON text.
acceptance_criteria:
- The suggestion and verdict fallback and titles work through tool calls with the same results as before.
- A model without tool support still produces them through the text fallback.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. server/tools/quickTools.mjs: name_conversation (title, concept), record_verdicts (verdicts) and mark_suggestions (suggestions, groundwork, concepts, links; schemas reuse record_turn properties) plus quickTool(tool, read, capable, mcp): native models get the one tool (tools + mcp + runTool, read throws a plain error the model fixes), others get it described as <tool_call> text (PLAN_TEXT_TOOLS + tool JSON) and the answer text is scanned for that call. title.mjs, verdicts.mjs and suggestions.mjs (suggest gains {capable, mcp}; job passes ctx.toolCapable(selection)) use it; prompts drop "Return only JSON" and "Do not use tools". Validation reuses titleCall/cleanTitle, readVerdicts and marks, so results match before. openai.mjs: a round whose calls are all accepted quick tools ends the reply with no further request and no "ended without text" error; a rejected one goes back for another round. mcp.mjs lets quick tools validate themselves. VERDICT_SHAPE moved to reply-requests.mjs (re-exported from diagrams.mjs) to break an import cycle.
Decisions/tradeoffs: a model that ignores the tool and writes the old JSON/plain text still goes through the old readers (readTitle, readVerdicts, parse) as a last fallback, so nothing that worked before breaks. Text-mode rejected calls are skipped (no result channel); a later valid call wins.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/http/quick-calls.test.mjs (unit quickTool native/text/fallback; app + fake Claude quick: all three jobs via runTool, bad call gets named error, title/concept/verdicts/suggestions saved; fake OpenAI endpoint tools:true -> name_conversation error then fixed, exactly 2 requests; tools:false -> <tool_call> text, no tools field, 1 request). Existing titles/verdicts/suggestions tests unchanged and pass. check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 464/464 pass.

title: Media usage recorded for custom endpoints
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

Media calls through custom endpoints (visual writer, plan, cuts, audit) record their reported usage. Today usage is read only when the call carries tools.
acceptance_criteria:
- A custom-endpoint call without tools that reports usage appears in usage history.
- Calls with tools still record usage once.
notes: Done. server/providers/openai.mjs: every custom-endpoint chat request sends stream_options.include_usage and reads usage chunks (previously only with tools); the stream reads on to [DONE]/end after finish for tool-free calls too. Media tasks (visual writer, plan, cuts, audit) use the same generate path, so roles.mjs records their usage. Test: test/providers/tool-loop.test.mjs 'a tool-free endpoint call asks for usage and records it once' replaces 'tool-free endpoint requests do not ask for usage'; tool-turn test now asserts exactly one usage event. Fixture (fake OpenAI server), no live endpoint. Tradeoff: endpoints that reject stream_options would now fail tool-free calls; OpenAI-compatible servers accept it and tool calls already sent it. Checks: check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 389/389.

title: Failed media shows the real provider error
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

A failed visual or video stores and shows the provider's first error line, shortened and with secrets redacted, instead of a generic line such as "Video provider failed to generate a composition." Repairs the writer recovers from stay silent.
acceptance_criteria:
- A provider error such as a model missing from the endpoint's catalog appears on the failed card.
- Keys and tokens in an error never appear on screen or in storage.
- A recovered repair shows no error.
notes: Done. providerError() in server/log.mjs: first non-empty line of errorCause (key/Bearer/sk-/JWT/api_key/token patterns + endpoint URLs redacted), withoutPaths, max 300 chars. Visual failure: 'Visual provider could not generate a result: <line>. Check Smart…'; video: 'Video provider failed: <line>' (VideoCard FAILURE_REASON allowlist extended). Custom endpoint HTTP errors now append 'Endpoint said: <error.message>' via responseError() in endpointSettings.mjs (key redacted), so a model missing from the catalog reaches the card and chat. Repairs: visual validation retries and video invalidOutput repairs unchanged (silent); test asserts a recovered visual has error null. Tradeoff: superseded tests that asserted upstream bodies stay hidden were updated to assert redacted detail instead. Evidence (fixtures only, no live provider): node --test log-format, visuals-failures, visuals-progressive, video-cuts, openai-stream, endpoints, openai-settings, card-states, video-cards pass; check-size ok; format:check ok; test:affected 549/549 (one earlier run showed 1 unidentified failure, two reruns clean).

title: The cut audit reports through tool calls; Remotion cuts get motion-design
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The smart model's cut audit reports with flag_problem (cut, problem), flag_poor_piece (piece, reason) and pass_cut instead of JSON text, assembled into today's issue shape so the fix flow is unchanged. Remotion cut writers always get the motion-design skill; their 3D skill still comes from the plan; Manim keeps its own skills.
acceptance_criteria:
- An audit that flags a problem leads to the same fix as a JSON issue list did.
- An audit that passes a cut makes it playable.
- A poor piece flagged by the audit is improved as before.
- Remotion cut prompts include motion-design.
notes: Done 2026-11-18. Audit reports by tool call: auditReport(offered) in server/media/audit-answers.mjs offers flag_problem(cut, problem), pass_cut and, only when libraryPieces exist, flag_poor_piece(piece, reason); each call is validated on arrival (error names the field; max 8 problems; piece must be an offered name) and assembled into the old {what, where} issue list and {name, why} pieces, so fix and piece-improve flows are unchanged. Problems outrank a pass; no verdict throws like an unreadable answer did. Native tools (Claude/Codex, endpoints with tools) go through videoCall (moved to server/media/video-call.mjs to keep video-cuts under the size limit) as {tools, mcp, runTool}; others get the tools as Hermes <tool_call> text appended to the audit prompt, and leaked/text calls are read from the answer. Audit stage metering now matches by prefix. Remotion cut writers always get MOTION_DESIGN_SKILL; 3D skill still per plan dimension; Manim unchanged. auditIssues/poorPieces removed. Evidence (fixtures): video-audit (fix after flag_problem, pass makes playable, unit checks of calls/errors/text mode), video-piece-improve (flag_poor_piece improves piece), video-cuts (motion-design in Remotion prompts), manim-audit; native runTool path exercised in 13 integration audits (codex fixture). check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 818/818 pass. No live provider run.

title: The video plan is built through tool calls
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The smart model plans a video with start_video (title, description), add_area, add_colour (palette role and ink, or true colour name and hex), add_object (name, look, position, optional colour role and reference query), add_term, add_cut (purpose, narration, engine, dimension, join, end state, optional emphasis), add_exhibit (cut, kind and that kind's fields) and finish_video. Each call is checked as it arrives against today's plan rules with a plain error naming the field. Cosmetic problems get defaults (bad join becomes a scene change; missing objects, terms or areas are empty; a 3D Manim cut becomes 2D). finish_video reports structural problems (no cuts, a cut without narration); a model that stops without a valid finish gets one retry with the problem stated, then the video fails with that problem. Calls assemble into today's plan shape, so set pieces, cut writing, narration and export are unchanged; the large plan JSON prompt and parser are retired for new videos.
acceptance_criteria:
- A plan built through valid calls produces a video as before.
- A call with a bad field gets an error naming it, and the corrected call is accepted without restarting the plan.
- A bad join becomes a scene change instead of failing the video.
- A plan with no cuts after its one retry fails with a message naming the problem.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. server/media/plan-calls.mjs: planBuilder({exhibits, clips}) offers start_video, add_area, add_colour (role + ink, or role + true colour name + hex), add_object, add_term, add_cut, add_exhibit (only when web search is ready; clip kind only with the downloader) and finish_video. Each call is checked as it arrives with the existing plan rules (cutProblem / planProblem, now exported from video-plan.mjs) and a bad call throws a plain error naming the field (for example 'engine must be "remotion" or "manim".'), which the native tool loop returns to the model; accepted calls stay. Defaults: a bad join/transition/direction (or cut 1 'continue') becomes a scene change with the fade; a 3D Manim cut becomes 2D; areas, roles, objects and terms start empty and may stay empty. finish_video reports structural problems ("The plan has no cuts; add what is missing..."). videos.mjs: capable smart models plan natively (tools + mcp + runTool, planning progress counts call characters); others get the tools as <tool_call> text (PLAN_TEXT_TOOLS) and builder.read runs them in order, collecting rejected calls for the retry note. No valid finish -> one retry with the problem stated in the instructions, then "Video plan is incomplete: <problem>." The assembled plan is today's shape, so set pieces, cuts, narration and export are untouched. videoPlan (JSON parser) and the JSON plan prompt are removed; PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS, EXHIBITS_NOTE and CLIPS_NOTE now describe the calls.
Decisions/tradeoffs: add_cut rejects a missing narration as a field error (the model fixes that call), so finish_video's structural check mostly catches "no cuts" and a missing start_video. The retry is a fresh plan (fresh builder), not a continuation, because each plan request is a new session. A plan that names an exhibit without search ready now drops that exhibit call instead of failing the video. A colorRole must name a role already added (error says to add_colour first). No cap on native cut count beyond the existing 64 KiB text limit for text mode.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/video-plan-calls.test.mjs (generateVideo with capable: native calls -> ready video with the same plan; bad engine gets the named error and the corrected call is accepted without restart; bad join becomes scene; no cuts -> exactly one retry whose instructions state "the plan has no cuts", then "Video plan is incomplete: the plan has no cuts."; retry can recover; text-mode rejected calls named). test/media/video-plan.test.mjs, video-emphasis, video-pieces, video-true-colours now validate through planThrough (plan -> calls). All media fixtures answer plans as <tool_call> text via test/support/video-kit.mjs planText/planCalls; videos-recovery expects the one retry; videos-jobs expects tools on the planner request.
Checks: node scripts/check-size.mjs ok; npm run format:check ok; npm run test:affected 832/832 pass.

title: GSAP in the visual sandbox
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

Bundle GSAP core (no plugins) in the visual sandbox beside d3 and three.js, with no network. Add a loadable gsap skill (core and timeline pattern, greensock/gsap-skills, MIT, source and licence recorded). The skill check also retries a visual that uses GSAP without gsap loaded, and GSAP animation counts as animation for motion-design. The step helper and d3 are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- A visual using gsap runs in the sandbox without network access.
- A visual using GSAP without loading gsap is retried once with the skill.
- Existing step-through visuals behave as before.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. gsap 3.15.1 (exact pin; npm licence: GreenSock standard no-charge, not MIT) bundled by Vite into src/media/sandbox.ts as the window.gsap core global (no plugins registered); visual.md lists it; validate() no longer bans gsap. New loadable skill gsap (server/media/prompts/gsap.md, rewritten excerpt of greensock/gsap-skills gsap-core + gsap-timeline SKILL.md @ aed9cfd3, MIT (c) 2026 GreenSock, gsap-skills-LICENSE.txt, README entry). SKILLS.gsap.uses = /\bgsap\s*\./; motion-design.uses also matches gsap., so a GSAP visual missing both skills is retried once with both. Step helper and d3 untouched.
Decisions: GSAP counts as animation for motion-design too (spec line 97), so loading only gsap still triggers one retry for motion-design. Excerpt excludes plugins/CustomEase/ScrollTrigger and tells the writer to scope selectors to the visual root.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/sandbox-gsap.test.mjs (sandbox imports bundled gsap core with no plugins; a gsap timeline in jsdom with the bundled package moves and hides the element); test/media/visual-skills.test.mjs (+2: loads gsap+motion-design over real MCP, accepted in 1 call; without gsap retried once with gsap and motion-design, not threejs). No-network is the existing sandbox CSP (test/http/app.test.mjs). step-through, visuals-failures pass. tsc --noEmit OK, check-size OK, format:check OK, test:affected 828/828. No live provider or browser run.

title: The visual writer loads skills by tool call
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The visual writer's prompt gains a text budget (at most a few short sentences, short labels) and makes interaction (slider, drag, click) the default when the idea has a meaningful variable, static when controls would add nothing. The writer gets one tool, load_skill(name); its prompt lists each loadable skill with a one-line description and says it must load the matching skill whenever that work applies. Add vendored MIT excerpts: threejs (quick start and common mistakes, CloudAI-X/threejs-skills) and motion-design (checklist, duration and easing tables, LottieFiles/motion-design-skill), recorded with sources and licences beside the existing vendored skills. House style and frontend-design stay always given. If output uses three.js without threejs loaded, or animation (d3 transitions, CSS transitions or keyframes) without motion-design loaded, the server rejects it once and retries the writer with the missing skills already in its prompt. Models without tool support use the text fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
- A writer that loads threejs gets its text, and its 3D visual is accepted.
- A 3D visual written without loading threejs is retried once with the skill in the prompt.
- An animated visual written without motion-design is retried once with it.
- The skills' sources and licences are recorded with the other vendored skills.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. Writer (server/media/visuals.mjs) gets one tool, load_skill(name: threejs|motion-design), when the conversation model is tool-capable (ctx.toolCapable; jobs/media.mjs passes ctx.mcp), so Claude/Codex use the per-attempt MCP server and endpoints the native loop. Prompt (visual.md) adds the text budget and interaction-by-default; INSTRUCTIONS append a loadable-skills list with one-line descriptions and "must load". House style, frontend-design and analogy stay always given. Vendored MIT excerpts prompts/threejs.md (CloudAI-X/threejs-skills 0e18186, threejs-fundamentals Quick Start/Cleanup/Performance/Common Mistakes, adapted to the THREE global) and prompts/motion-design.md (LottieFiles/motion-design-skill 2e1f3c0, quality checklist + timing/easing tables) with LICENSE files and README entries. Enforcement: after attempt 1, output matching THREE. (threejs) or .transition( / CSS transition*: / @keyframes (motion-design) without that skill loaded is rejected once; attempt 2 has the skill text in its instructions plus a validationError naming it. Validation errors share the same single retry; the final attempt is never rejected for skills.
Decisions/tradeoffs: text fallback (no tool support) describes load_skill as <tool_call> text; calls are stripped from the fragment and partials, and since no result returns, a requested skill counts as missing and triggers the same one retry with it in the prompt (costs one extra generation; an early abort on seeing the call was skipped). GSAP stays for tcl.9.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/visual-skills.test.mjs (load over real MCP returns skill text, 3D accepted in 1 call; 3D without threejs retried once with skill; @keyframes without motion-design retried once; text-mode call hidden + retry). Updated visuals-prompts adapter test (claude and codex both pass: only mcp__rabbithole__load_skill allowed) and show-visual-loop (count tutor calls only). check-size OK, format:check OK, test:affected 426/426. test/media/video-camera fails the same on HEAD when run bare (tsx loader). No live Claude/Codex run.

title: Lean tutor prompt for every model
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

Rewrite the one shared tutor prompt to roughly half its current size before learner data, for every model. The check-yourself paragraph shrinks to two or three lines; the teaching and humanizer skills are trimmed to their core rules; media rules already live in the tool descriptions. The math, memory and neighbourhood rules, the tutor style and the reply layout section stay. Fixed text stays first for prompt caching.
acceptance_criteria:
- The tutor system prompt before learner data and tool definitions is at most half its size before this epic.
- Layouts, math, memory, neighbourhood and tutor style guidance are still present.
- Existing tutor behaviour tests pass.
notes: Done 2026-11-19. Trimmed the shared tutor skills to core rules: server/media/prompts/teaching.md (4.9K→~2K with analogy), analogy.md, humanizer.md (3.9K→~1.6K, 26 rules folded into five one-line groups); README notes the trim. The tool-path rules already had media/check-yourself moved into tool descriptions (tcl.1/.4/.5); math, memory, neighbourhood, tutor style and the reply layouts are unchanged and fixed text stays first. Measured tutorSystem before learner data and tool definitions: pre-epic (8475eed^, tools update_memory_note+find_images) 20,265 chars; now native app tools 7,851 (39%), text-tool fallback 7,533 excluding the tool JSON. Decision/tradeoff: trimmed the .md skills in place, so the video planner (PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS) also gets the shorter skills; the legacy no-app-tools branch (unused in production, kept for older tests) shrinks too (19.5K→14.4K). New unit test in test/media/tutor-style.test.mjs asserts <= half for native and text paths and presence of math, layouts, memory, neighbourhood, skills+style. Checks: check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 9/9, plus video-models, video-plan, visuals-prompts, http/tutor-style, show-visual, media-calls 21/21. Fixture-level only; no live Claude/Codex reply-quality check run.

title: Lopsided figures stack
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

A figure reply layout whose text is much taller than its media (about twice the height) stacks text and media vertically instead of side by side, whichever model wrote it, including stored replies.
acceptance_criteria:
- A figure with text about twice its media's height or more shows media and text stacked.
- A balanced figure keeps its side-by-side arrangement and side choice.
notes: Implemented: src/markdown/layouts.ts Figure component measures .layout-text/.layout-media with ResizeObserver; plain rule stacks(text, media, stacked) stacks at text >= 2x media, unstacks only below 1.5x (hysteresis). While stacked, side-by-side heights are estimated from the last side-by-side column widths (text height scales inversely with width, media proportionally), so stacking reflow cannot flip it back; errors only make it stickier toward stacked. Stacked drops data-side/data-ratio and sets data-stacked (layouts.css single column), DOM order unchanged. Applies at render time, so every model and stored replies. Tradeoff: geometry is a fixed-width estimate, not a live re-layout; visuals whose height ignores width stay stacked slightly longer. Evidence (fixture/jsdom, stubbed geometry): test/chat/reply-media-layouts.test.mjs unit test of stacks and component tests for default and side=right ratio=wide (balanced keeps columns+side, 2x stacks, stays stacked after reflow, unstacks when text shrinks); mutation check fails 3 tests. check-size, format:check, tsc, test:affected (82/82) pass. No browser run (not named in acceptance).

title: Discussions and videos by tool call
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The tutor starts a discussion with start_discussion (classmates with name, level and voice; lines with speaker and text) and a video with make_video({topic}), replacing the rabbithole-discussion and rabbithole-video blocks. Their rules (discussion only when asked, video only when explicitly asked, a video request stands alone) move into the tool descriptions. The server gives the video planner the conversation context. Arguments are validated by the server with plain errors.
acceptance_criteria:
- A start_discussion call creates a discussion whose lines arrive one at a time as today.
- A make_video call starts a video planned from the conversation context.
- A make_video call alongside another media call in the same reply gets a plain error.
- The discussion and video block rules no longer appear in the tutor prompt; stored discussions and videos still open.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. make_video (server/tools/makeVideo.mjs, {topic} max 200) and start_discussion (server/tools/startDiscussion.mjs, classmates name/level/voice + lines speaker/text, validated by the existing readDiscussion) join APP_TOOLS (show_visual, make_video, start_discussion, record_turn): offered natively to tool-capable models (MCP for Claude/Codex, function calling for endpoints) and as <tool_call> text otherwise; MCP skips ajv for them so plain errors reach the model. Their rules (discussion only when asked, placed last; video only when explicitly asked, ask if unclear, stands alone) live in the tool descriptions; with app tools offered the tutor prompt drops DISCUSSION_RULE and the rabbithole-video sentences (legacy prompt without tools keeps them). make_video creates a pending video at the call position whose planner input keeps request/intent(=topic)/inheritedContext/sources and adds context = conversation turns plus reply so far (last 6000 chars); PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS names the context field. Plain errors: bad/over-long topic; make_video after a visual/discussion ("stands alone"); show_visual/start_discussion/make_video after a video ("cannot join a video"); learner did not explicitly ask (asksForVideo, as the block check); no smart model. start_discussion saves the opening as a ready discussion artifact at the call position (lines reveal one at a time in the client as before), result "started; end your reply now." Fenced discussion/video block parsing is unchanged so stored ones still open.
Decisions/tradeoffs: unasked videos and missing smart model are now tool errors rather than failed video cards; a legacy block visual in the same reply as a tool video is not cross-checked.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/media-calls.test.mjs (argument errors, context builder, prompt free of block rules for native and text tools; MCP make_video -> planner receives intent+context, show_visual/make_video after it errored; visual-then-video errored; unasked video errored; MCP start_discussion bad then good -> ready discussion at position with private levels/voices). Updated tool-list expectations in tool-loop, search-settings, show-visual tests. check-size OK, format:check OK, test:affected 434/434. No live Claude/Codex run.

title: record_turn replaces the hidden verdict and notes blocks
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The tutor ends each reply with one record_turn call carrying next questions, suggestions (text and concept), groundwork, concepts with topics, concept links and verdicts (concept, level, confidence), replacing the rabbithole-verdict and rabbithole-notes blocks (ADR 0013; ADR 0008 ownership unchanged). Next questions show as soon as the call arrives. Invalid entries are skipped and named in the result; no retry is asked for. For custom endpoints a round whose only calls are record_turn or start_discussion ends the reply with no further request. When a reply ends without the call, the quick thinking model stands in as today.
acceptance_criteria:
- After a reply with record_turn, next questions, underlined suggestions, groundwork, concepts, links and familiarity evidence are saved and shown as they were from the blocks.
- Next questions appear when the call arrives, without waiting for another request.
- A custom endpoint makes no further request after a final record_turn.
- A reply without the call still gets suggestions and verdicts from the quick thinking model.
- An invalid entry is skipped without losing the valid ones.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. record_turn (server/tools/recordTurn.mjs) is an app tool beside show_visual (server/http/app-calls.mjs APP_TOOLS): offered natively to tool-capable models (MCP for Claude/Codex, function calling for endpoints) and as <tool_call> text otherwise; never in tutor tool settings or tool activity. Arguments: next_questions, suggestions{text,concept}, groundwork, concepts{name,topics}, links{from,to,kind}, verdicts{concept,level,confidence}; the notes/verdict rules moved into its description and the prompt swaps VERDICT_RULE+NOTES_RULE for a one-line RECORD_RULE when it is offered. readRecordTurn keeps valid entries, names skipped ones in the result ("recorded; skipped suggestions[1] (needs text), ..."), no retry asked; MCP skips ajv for it. send.mjs: next questions stream as soon as the call arrives; at finish the call stands in for the blocks (notes -> marks/finishSuggestions/addGraph, verdicts -> observe), so no quick thinking; without a call the old block path or quick thinking fallback runs as before. openai.mjs: a round whose calls are all record_turn/start_discussion ends the reply with no further request.
Decisions/tradeoffs: repeat calls add up (questions capped at 3, last verdict per concept wins); suggestion anchoring still happens at finish via marks(), so a suggestion text not in the reply drops silently rather than being named; start_discussion is listed in the ending set ahead of its tool; discussion turns keep their verdict block (unchanged). App-call handling moved from send.mjs to server/http/app-calls.mjs to stay under the 500-line cap.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/record-turn.test.mjs (unit tolerance/naming; Claude-style MCP call saves questions, suggestion passage, groundwork, concepts/topics, link, observation, invalid entries skipped, questions event arrives before the reply ends, no quick thinking; a reply without the call triggers quick-thinking suggestions and verdicts; fake OpenAI: one request only after a record_turn round). Updated expectations: tool-loop, search-settings, tutor-style, http/verdicts, show-visual. check-size OK, format:check OK, test:affected 423/423. No live Claude/Codex run.

title: Tool support probe and Retest for custom-endpoint models
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The first time a custom-endpoint model is used for chat or media, the app sends one tiny tool call and saves whether a valid call came back, setting the model's existing tool flag; the app uses the native path when it worked and the text fallback otherwise. Settings offers Retest per model. Probing on first use avoids testing thousands of listed models nobody uses.
acceptance_criteria:
- A model whose endpoint returns a valid tool call to the probe uses native tool calls; one that does not uses the text fallback.
- The probe runs once per model, not on every turn and not for listed but unused models.
- Retest in Settings re-runs the probe and the next turn follows the new result.
notes: Done 2026-11-19. roles.toolCapable probes a custom-endpoint model on first chat/media use when it has no saved tool flag and /models reports no tools boolean (server/providers/toolProbe.mjs: one non-streamed ping tool call, 60s). Valid call -> uses_tutor_tools=true; answer without a call or a 4xx tools rejection -> false; connection/401/403/404/429/5xx saves nothing and probes again next use. Parallel first uses share one probe. Retest: POST /api/settings/endpoints/model/retest + Retest button per model (src/settings/EndpointModels.tsx, split out for the 500-line limit; statusError moved to endpointSettings.mjs and redactStream to chatStream.mjs to keep openai.mjs at 500). Decisions/tradeoffs: a reported capabilities.tools boolean is trusted (no probe); probe and the learner toggle share the same flag so Retest overwrites a manual choice; probe usage not recorded. Evidence (fixtures, fake OpenAI server): test/providers/tool-probe.test.mjs (3 pass), test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs Retest step; check-size ok, format:check ok, tsc ok, test:affected 821/821 pass. No live endpoint check.

title: Text tool-call fallback and tolerant media parsing
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

A chat model whose endpoint cannot call tools gets the same tools described in the prompt and writes each call as Hermes-style text: <tool_call>{"name": ..., "arguments": {...}}</tool_call>. The shared reply-stream parser recognises it, hides it from the learner and runs it like a native call; no result goes back to the model in text mode. The same parser catches native calls leaked into reply text in that shape. The old fenced-block parser stays and also accepts the broken forms seen in practice: :::rabbithole-visual {...}, :::rabbithole-video {...}, and :::wide or :::figure wrapped around bare request JSON, each treated as the request it meant.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reply from a model without tool support that writes a <tool_call> for show_visual gets that visual, and the learner never sees the call text.
- A native-capable model's call leaked into its text in that shape runs once and is hidden.
- Each broken form listed above becomes its visual or video instead of raw text.
- No reply shows raw request JSON or ::: request markup to the learner.
notes:
Done 2026-11-18. Parser: diagramReply (server/media/diagrams.mjs, helpers in server/media/reply-requests.mjs) now also reads <tool_call>{"name","arguments"}</tool_call> (arguments may be a JSON string) into output.calls (closed, or unclosed at the final parse), hidden while streaming including a partial "<tool_c"; :::rabbithole-<kind> {json} (JSON on the same or next lines, balanced-brace end, its own ::: close line consumed only outside a figure/wide layout); and bare JSON with a string title inside an open :::figure/:::wide, treated as a visual with the layout lines kept and the visual placed inside. A broken visual block holding show_visual arguments (alt, no description) runs as a show_visual call. Partial ":"/"::"/":::" lines hide while streaming. send.mjs runs each call once in order (ranCalls index) through the same visualCall path as native show_visual, at the call position with the reply text before it as context; nothing goes back to the model. Text mode: a non-tool-capable model gets textTools [show_visual]; tutorSystem uses TOOL_VISUAL_RULES with a text-tools rule (Hermes format + tool JSON) in place of "Do not use tools".
Decisions/tradeoffs: only app tools (show_visual today) run from text; other names and unreadable/invalid calls are logged (chat "text tool call skipped") and dropped, since text mode has no result channel. Bare JSON in a layout always means a visual (never a video). A bare JSON line without a title inside a layout is hidden while it streams, then shown as text. Video keeps its fenced block until tcl.5.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/media/tolerant-requests.test.mjs (unit: tool_call, colon, figure/wide, show_visual-shaped block, streaming prefixes never show JSON/markup, plain JSON stays text); test/media/show-visual.test.mjs (app + fake provider: non-tool endpoint writes <tool_call> across 7-char deltas -> visual at position, writer gets args+context, no streamed text shows the call; Claude leaked call runs once and is hidden). tool-loop expectation updated (tool-free endpoint request now describes <tool_call>). check-size, format:check, test:affected 414/414 pass (earlier runs had one timing flake each in artifacts-stop / visual-detach, both pass alone and on rerun).

title: The tutor asks for visuals by tool call
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md (epic Rabbithole-tcl). Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md.

The tutor requests a visual with a show_visual tool call (title, shows, alt, optional check_answer) instead of a fenced rabbithole-visual block. It is served like the existing tutor tools: through the per-turn MCP server for Claude and Codex and through function calling for custom endpoints, always present, never a learner-toggled tutor tool. The server places the visual at the reply position of the call, creates it pending and starts the writer at once with the reply text so far as context, then answers "queued" so the reply continues. A custom endpoint continues the reply in the next request; a continuation that repeats already-shown text has the repeated prefix dropped. check_answer makes a predict-then-reveal check whose answer stays hidden until revealed. The visual rules move from the tutor prompt into the tool description. The server validates arguments itself and returns a plain error naming the argument; no strict schema mode.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tutor reply that calls show_visual mid-reply shows the visual at that point, and the visual starts before the reply ends.
- The tutor receives "queued" and its continued text follows the visual; an exact repeat of already-shown text is not shown twice.
- A call with a missing or over-long argument gets a plain error naming it, and a corrected call succeeds.
- check_answer produces a check whose answer is hidden until the learner reveals it.
- show_visual never appears in tutor tool settings or the tool activity list.
- Stored replies with fenced visual blocks render as before.
notes:
Done 2026-11-18. show_visual (server/tools/showVisual.mjs) is appended after the learner tutor tools whenever the model is tool-capable (Claude, Codex, endpoint models with tools); not in TUTOR_TOOLS, so never in tutor tool settings; send.mjs drops its tool events so it never shows in tool activity or stored reply tools. The call creates a pending visual at the reply's current visible text length, queues the writer at once (replyArtifacts.showVisual) with request {title, shows, alt, check_answer?, context = reply so far, last 6000 chars}, and returns "queued". Validation is the server's: missing/empty/over-long/control-char argument -> "show_visual needs alt as non-empty text." / "show_visual title is 200 characters; shorten it to at most 120."; MCP skips its ajv check for this tool so the named error reaches the model. Custom endpoints: openai.mjs flushes the redaction buffer before running tools, and chatStream.roundText drops a continuation's exact repeat of shown text or the last round's text (held while it could still be a repeat; a partial repeat that ends is shown as written). Prompt: with show_visual offered, tutorSystem uses TOOL_VISUAL_RULES (visual and check-yourself block rules removed; the rules live in the tool description; video keeps its fenced block with explicit fields until tcl.5). visual.md reads alt, context and check_answer (answer inside closed <details> as before).
Decisions/tradeoffs: models without tool calling keep the old fenced-block prompt until tcl.2 adds the text fallback; the repeat check runs after every tool round, not only show_visual (only exact repeats drop). Fenced-block parsing is unchanged, so stored replies render as before.
Evidence (fixtures, not live): test/tools/show-visual.test.mjs (validation, prompt, repeat filter), test/media/show-visual.test.mjs (Claude-style call over the real per-turn MCP server: bad then corrected calls, position, writer starts before the reply goes on, check_answer reaches only the writer, no tool events), test/providers/show-visual-loop.test.mjs (fake OpenAI: error then "queued", continuation repeat dropped, visual at position). Updated tool-loop, search-settings, tutor-style, visuals-prompts expectations for the always-present tool. check-size OK, format:check OK, test:affected 410/411: the single failure changed between runs (videos-jobs adapter timeout, then visual-detach 50 ms visualTimeout); both flake the same way on a HEAD copy (visual-detach failed 3 of 4 runs there), so they are not caused by this change. No live Claude/Codex run was made.

title: Tool calls and a lean tutor prompt
description:
Spec: docs/tool-calls-and-lean-prompts-spec.md. Decision: docs/adr/0013-structured-output-only-through-tool-calls.md (supersedes the delivery part of ADR 0008). Terms: GLOSSARY.md (visual, video, cut audit, discussion, suggestion, next question, skill, reply layout).

Only frontier models make media today: replies juggle about six output formats under a 5K-token prompt, and the video plan is one large JSON object. Every model gets one shared tutor prompt about half the size; anything structured goes through plain tool calls (show_visual mid-reply, make_video, start_discussion, record_turn, plan and audit calls), validated by the server with no strict schema mode; models without native tool calling write Hermes-style <tool_call> text. The visual writer loads skills (threejs, gsap, motion-design) by tool call, visuals keep little text and favour interaction, lopsided figures stack, failed media shows the provider's real error, custom-endpoint media usage is recorded, and every model picker gets fuzzy search.

## Decisions so far
See the spec's Implementation Decisions.

## Fog
GitHub Models tool support; whether Claude and Codex can end a turn right after a tool call without one more short request.

title: Windows installer and release workflow
description: Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part C, "Per-OS builds", "Builds on GitHub Actions". The same Tauri app builds an unsigned NSIS installer on Windows. A desktop build workflow runs only on manual trigger, with one Linux and one Windows job, each building on its own OS with cached npm, Cargo and Tauri dependencies, and uploads both installers to a draft GitHub Release the owner publishes by hand. Agents edit the workflow locally only; the owner pushes and triggers it (AGENTS.md). The download page notes SmartScreen's "More info, Run anyway" step.
acceptance_criteria:
- The workflow runs only on manual trigger, never on push or pull request.
- One run produces an AppImage and an NSIS installer on a draft GitHub Release.
- Each job restores its dependency caches.
- The README's download section explains the unsigned SmartScreen warning.
notes:
Windows installer and release workflow done (Rabbithole-dsk.5).

Implementation:
- .github/workflows/desktop-build.yml: on workflow_dispatch only. A `linux` job (ubuntu-22.04 for older glibc, README apt list) and a `windows` job (windows-latest) each run npm ci + `npm run desktop:build` with setup-node npm cache, Swatinem/rust-cache (desktop and, on Windows, desktop/sandbox targets) and actions/cache for Tauri bundler tools (~/.cache/tauri, %LOCALAPPDATA%\tauri). Artifacts: the AppImage and nsis/*-setup.exe. A `release` job (needs both, contents: write) runs `gh release create desktop-build-<run> --draft` with both installers.
- Decision: a third release job creates the draft, because two build jobs creating one draft race. Tradeoff: one extra short job; the tag name is generic and the owner can rename it before publishing.
- desktop/tauri.windows.conf.json (Tauri merges it on Windows): nsis target, icon.ico, and rabbithole-sandbox.exe, codex-command-runner.exe and codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe as resources beside the app.
- scripts/desktop-stage.mjs: win32-x64 Node 24.22.3 zip pinned by SHA-256 (e612af99…, from nodejs.org SHASUMS256.txt), node.exe extracted with System32 bsdtar, npm run through a shell only on Windows (npm.cmd), the sandbox workspace built with cargo on Windows and the three exes copied to desktop/stage. Linux path unchanged.
- desktop/src/main.rs Windows fixes: the app unpacks into %LOCALAPPDATA%\rabbithole-app; node.exe; System32 tar.exe (Git's GNU tar reads "C:" as a host); CREATE_NO_WINDOW for tar and node; links open with explorer; on close the server is killed (no SIGTERM on Windows). Shortcut recorded in code: its lock goes stale after 10 s, so an immediate reopen can hit ELOCKED.
- README: Windows desktop app and Downloads sections, including SmartScreen's More info, Run anyway.

Evidence (local Linux, fixtures only for Windows):
- test/scripts/desktop-workflow.test.mjs 3/3 (only workflow_dispatch; each job has npm, Cargo and Tauri caches and uploads its installer; both go to one draft release).
- cargo test (Linux) 1/1. `cargo xwin check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` for the shell finished, with empty placeholder sandbox exes in desktop/stage that were removed afterwards (Tauri checks that resources exist). This shows the Windows config merges.
- check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 799/799.
- Not run here: the workflow itself (the owner pushes and triggers it), the NSIS build, the Windows sandbox helper build with MSVC, a Windows launch. Per the epic, Windows behaviour is proven on the owner's first run. Also untested: the Linux AppImage rebuild with the changed stage script (Linux logic is unchanged apart from the tar variable). Server child processes are not in a job object, so a killed server can leave a running render behind on Windows.

title: Windows sandbox step in first-run setup
description: Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part B, "Windows sandbox prompt". On Windows, first-run setup runs the sandbox's one-time elevated setup behind one UAC prompt. If declined, setup explains that video making stays off until it is enabled, and Settings offers to try again. Linux setup is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- On Windows, first-run setup asks once for admin rights to enable the sandbox.
- Declining finishes setup with an explanation, and video making reports unavailable.
- Settings can run the sandbox setup again.
- Linux first-run setup shows no sandbox step.
notes: Done 2026-11-19. Launcher: `rabbithole-sandbox --setup` runs codex_windows_sandbox::run_elevated_setup (one UAC prompt via its setup helper) with the same Restricted workspace-write profile, codex_home %LOCALAPPDATA%\rabbithole\sandbox; exits 0 once sandbox_setup_is_complete, non-zero on decline/failure; no-op when already set up. Server: windowsSandbox() in server/media/video-sandbox.mjs ({status, enable}; enable spawns `--setup` then re-probes `--check`), injected into createApp as ctx.sandbox; GET /api/setup/sandbox -> {windows, ready}, POST runs setup. Client: src/settings/SandboxSettings.tsx, rendered only when windows: first-run setup step "Video sandbox" with Enable sandbox; declined -> "Video making stays off until it is enabled; you can try again from Settings" and the button hides (asks once); Settings (tutor tab, after Tutor tools) shows the same with Try again. Video/run_python stay unavailable via existing sandboxMissing (dsk.2). Decision: the UAC prompt starts from an explicit Enable click in setup rather than on mount, so it never appears unexplained; tradeoff: a learner who ignores the step is not prompted (Settings covers it). Evidence (fixtures): test/media/windows-sandbox.test.mjs (linux no-op, declined, accepted), test/shell/first-run.test.mjs (Windows ask once + decline + finish; Linux no sandbox step), test/shell/sandbox-settings.test.mjs (Try again succeeds; Linux renders nothing), test/store/first-run.test.mjs (routes). cargo test 3/3; cargo xwin build x86_64-pc-windows-msvc ok; check-size ok; format:check ok; test:affected 434/434. Windows UAC behaviour unproven until the owner runs the desktop workflow.

title: Windows support in the server
description: Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part B "Finding CLIs" and part C "Data folder", "Manim on Windows", "Desktop actions". The data folder is %APPDATA%\rabbithole on Windows. "Show in folder" uses Explorer's /select, and Trash uses the Recycle Bin through PowerShell, both with argument arrays and no shell string. Manim's dependency check accepts Windows, where pycairo and manimpango install from wheels and LaTeX comes from the TinyTeX download. CLI detection adds %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA%\npm and %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin, and resolves npm's .cmd shims to their real executable or node script instead of using a shell.
acceptance_criteria:
- On Windows the app stores data in %APPDATA%\rabbithole.
- Show in folder and Trash use Explorer and the Recycle Bin on Windows, and Linux keeps its current actions.
- Manim setup proceeds on Windows without system packages.
- A Claude or Codex CLI installed through npm on Windows is found and launched without a shell.
notes:
Done 2026-11-19. server/desktop.mjs: desktopFor(platform) — win32 reveal = detached explorer.exe ['/select,', path] (explorer exits 1 on success, so detached like xdg-open); trash = powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command <fixed script> with the path in env RABBITHOLE_TRASH (never script text), Microsoft.VisualBasic FileSystem DeleteFile/DeleteDirectory SendToRecycleBin. Linux gdbus/xdg-open/gio unchanged. dataDir(): %APPDATA%\rabbithole on win32, $XDG_DATA_HOME/rabbithole (~/.local/share) otherwise; main.mjs uses it (RABBITHOLE_DATA_DIR still wins). findCli: win32 searches PATH, %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA%\npm, %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin for name.exe then name.cmd; a .cmd shim is parsed for its last "%dp0%\<target>" (skipping node.exe) and returns the target only if it exists. launchArgs(bin,args) runs .js/.cjs/.mjs targets as [process.execPath, [script,...]]; Claude (auth status + replies) and Codex launches use it, no shell option anywhere. manim.mjs: checkManimDependencies accepts win32 and skips pkg-config there (pycairo/manimpango wheels), still requires latex+dvisvgm; texBin win32 = .tools/TinyTeX/bin/windows; detectManim python = .venv/Scripts/python.exe on win32. tools-setup: uv win32-x64/arm64 zip (uv.exe at zip root, so no --strip-components); TinyTeX win32-x64 = TinyTeX-1-windows.exe, a 7-Zip SFX run as `<exe> -y -o<part>` with inner TinyTeX folder renamed into place; tlmgr on Windows is a .bat, so it runs as tlpkg/tlperl/bin/perl.exe texmf-dist/scripts/texlive/tlmgr.pl install ... (asset names and archive layout checked against the live release: uv zip listing, 7z listing of TinyTeX-1-windows.exe incl. perl.exe, tlmgr.pl, bin/windows/latex.exe and tlmgr.bat contents).
Decisions/tradeoffs: tlmgr.bat also sets PERL5LIB to tlperl\lib; skipped since runner has no env option and TL's perl is relocatable — first thing to check if Windows tlmgr fails. Windows npm global prefix is assumed %APPDATA%\npm (custom npm prefix not queried; `npm` itself is a .cmd). TinyTeX has no Windows arm64 bundle (error message). Not touched: npm start's browser open (xdg-open) and clips' .venv/bin/yt-dlp on Windows; Codex env passes only PATH/CODEX_HOME/ACCESS_TOKEN, which may need SystemRoot on Windows — check in the first Windows run.
Evidence (fixtures, Linux host; Windows behaviour is proven when the owner runs the Windows workflow, per the epic): test/media/desktop-actions.test.mjs (Explorer /select, PowerShell Recycle Bin with path only in env, Linux gdbus/xdg-open/gio unchanged, data folder per OS); test/providers/find-cli.test.mjs (Windows folders, npm cmd-shim script and exe targets, gone target = null, launchArgs, Codex launches a resolved .js under process.execPath); test/scripts/manim.test.mjs (win32 ensureManim installs into .venv/Scripts/python.exe with pkg-config missing; LaTeX still required); test/scripts/tools-setup.test.mjs (win32 uv zip URL/no strip, TinyTeX exe URL/-y -o, tlmgr via perl). Live Linux: findCli still finds ~/.local/bin/claude and linuxbrew codex; dataDir = ~/.local/share/rabbithole. Checks: check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 464/464.

title: Windows sandbox launcher
description: Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part C, "Windows sandbox". A small launcher executable built from the Tauri workspace using OpenAI's codex-windows-sandbox crate from openai/codex, as a git dependency pinned to a Codex release tag; its Apache-2.0 notice ships in the app's licences file. Elevated mode, with rules matching bwrap: no network, the learner's home and app data hidden, writes only to the job's workspace, reads of the workspace and runtime folders. On Windows, Remotion renders and stills, Manim and run_python run through it with the argument shape they already pass; when it is not set up they report unavailable, while chat, visuals and diagrams work. Linux keeps bwrap unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
- The launcher builds for the Windows target with the crate pinned to a Codex release tag.
- On Windows, the server chooses the launcher for every model-written code run; on Linux it still uses bwrap.
- Without the sandbox set up, video making and run_python report unavailable, and chat keeps working.
- The crate's licence notice is in the app's licences file.
notes:
Result (verified 2026-11-19):
- desktop/sandbox: separate Cargo workspace `rabbithole-sandbox`, codex-windows-sandbox/codex-protocol/codex-utils-absolute-path pinned to openai/codex tag rust-v0.170.0 (Windows-only deps, so the Linux app never fetches Codex). Elevated mode, NetworkSandboxPolicy::Restricted, writes only to --workspace, reads = --read paths + workspace + platform defaults, env only --env plus SystemRoot/windir, TEMP/TMP=workspace. `--check` exits 0 once one-time setup is complete; a run never triggers UAC.
- Windows build: `cargo xwin build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` produced PE32+ rabbithole-sandbox.exe and codex-command-runner.exe. codex-windows-sandbox-setup compiled but its link step needs mt.exe to embed its UAC manifest, which this Linux host lacks (no llvm-mt); MSVC on the Windows runner provides it (dsk.5 builds/bundles the helpers).
- Server: sandboxCommand() picks bwrap on Linux (unchanged args, env {}) and $RABBITHOLE_SANDBOX on win32 with launcherArgs() translating the existing bwrap argument shape; used by sandboxProcess (Remotion render/still, Manim) and runPython. sandboxMissing()/detectPython report unavailable on Windows until `--check` passes; VideoCard shows it as unavailable. Tauri main.rs sets RABBITHOLE_SANDBOX on Windows; LICENSES.md (Apache-2.0 + Codex NOTICE) bundled as a resource.
- Decision: hidden home/app data come from the separate sandbox account rather than explicit deny paths; PATH is dropped on Windows (POSIX folders). Tradeoff: Windows behaviour is unproven until the owner runs the workflow.
- Checks: node --test test/media/windows-sandbox.test.mjs test/shell/downloads.test.mjs 8/8; cargo test 3/3; check-size ok; format:check ok; test:affected 520/520. Added desktop/sandbox/target/ to .gitignore.

title: Linux desktop app
description: Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part C, "Shell", "Data folder", "Webview", "Export save dialog". A Tauri 2 app that bundles a Node 24 runtime and the built app, starts the server on a free loopback port, points the webview at it once it listens, and stops it when the window closes. The server's Host, Origin and CSRF checks apply unchanged. Linux ships an AppImage using the system bwrap and keeps the existing data folder. Webview downloads open a native save dialog. Assume the Remotion player and WebGL visuals work in WebKitGTK; no manual webview check.
acceptance_criteria:
- Building on Linux produces an AppImage.
- Opening it shows the app with no terminal, using the same data folder as npm start.
- Closing the window stops the server.
- A file download from the app opens a native save dialog.
notes:
Linux desktop app done (Rabbithole-dsk.1).

Implementation:
- desktop/: Tauri 2 shell (src/main.rs, tauri.conf.json, icons, ui/index.html loading page). `npm run desktop:build` = scripts/desktop-stage.mjs (dist, server, scripts, src, `npm ci --omit=dev`, official Node 24.22.3 linux-x64 pinned by SHA-256 -> desktop/stage/app.tar + app.build stamp) then `tauri build` -> AppImage.
- Decision: an AppImage is read-only, but the download manager writes tools beside the code (.venv, .venv-python, .tools, node_modules/.remotion). So on the first launch of each build, the shell unpacks app.tar into $XDG_DATA_HOME/rabbithole-app and keeps the tool folders (Rust unit test covers this). Tradeoff: about 1.5 GB extra disk and a one-time unpack on each new build. The data folder is still $XDG_DATA_HOME/rabbithole, shared with npm start.
- The shell spawns `node server/main.mjs --port 0`, reads the "Rabbithole: <url>" line and navigates the webview to it. Host/Origin/CSRF checks are unchanged. If startup fails (for example ELOCKED), the server's message shows in the window. Close or exit sends SIGTERM and waits up to 10 s before SIGKILL. PR_SET_PDEATHSIG stops the server if the shell dies.
- Downloads: on_download opens GTK FileChooserNative on the main thread (rfd's GTK backend starts its own GTK thread; rfd is kept only for non-Linux). New-window links open through xdg-open.
- bundleMediaFramework=true: without it the AppImage's WebKit lacked GStreamer appsink/autoaudiosink and the web process crashed on the Videos page.
- server/media/video-sandbox.mjs binds process.execPath, because the bundled node lives under the home folder that bwrap hides.

Evidence (live, this machine, Xvfb :77 + metacity):
- `npm run desktop:build` -> desktop/target/release/bundle/appimage/Rabbithole_1.0.0_amd64.AppImage (723 MiB).
- Launched with setsid and no terminal: "Node 24.22.3", "Data directory: /home/thomas/.local/share/rabbithole", "Rabbithole: http://127.0.0.1:45959" (free port). The window showed the owner's saved trees. The download manager installed Manim, offline Python and the browser into rabbithole-app.
- Videos > Export MP4: POST export 200, then a native GTK "Save file" dialog prefilled "Artemis I_ Around the Moon and Home.mp4". Saved to /tmp; the file was byte-identical to the library MP4.
- Window close button: the server process exited, rabbithole.lock was released and the shell exited.
- cargo test 1/1, check-size ok, format:check ok, test:affected 801/801 pass, test/media/videos-playback.test.mjs 2/2 including the bwrap probe.

Build-host notes: this machine lacked libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev and patchelf and sudo was unavailable, so the -dev debs and patchelf were extracted into /tmp/rh-devlibs (PKG_CONFIG_PATH/PATH) for the build. The README lists the apt packages. Not checked: other distros, Wayland, GPU WebGL. Export-button icons render as blank squares in WebKitGTK on Xvfb (cosmetic; the spec defers webview fixes).

title: Desktop app for Linux and Windows
description:
Spec: docs/desktop-and-export-spec.md, part C. ADR: docs/adr/0011-tauri-desktop-for-linux-and-windows.md.

A one-click Tauri app for Linux (AppImage) and Windows (NSIS), wrapping the unchanged Node server as a sidecar on loopback.
