title: Many copies of a part, instanced in 3D
description:
## What to build

The video kit gains one helper that places many copies of a set piece or part, such as a crowd of people in a city. Copies vary only through the piece's props (position, scale, palette role, state), seeded so frames stay stable. In 3D the helper draws copies with three.js instancing per mesh of the piece, using the installed three.js only, so hundreds of copies play smoothly live. The piece writer is told about the helper. See spec: Set piece parts.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The helper renders the requested number of copies in 2D and 3D with seeded, stable variation
- [ ] 3D copies use instancing; no new dependency
- [ ] The piece writer prompt mentions the helper
- [ ] Video kit tests cover 2D and 3D copies
notes:
Done: kit `Copies({of, count, seed, vary(i, rand)})` in server/media/video-stock.tsx, re-exported from ./kit (it lives in video-stock because video-kit.tsx would pass the 500-line size check, and video-stock is already staged beside every cut and piece still). rand() is remotion random(`seed:i:n`), so the same seed draws the same copies on every frame. 2D: renders one element per copy. 3D (inside a fiber context): copies are grouped by their props other than position/rotation/scale (state, roles, highlight), one hidden template is rendered per group, and every mesh in it becomes a three.js InstancedMesh with matrix = copy TRS x mesh-local. Uses only the installed three and fiber. Tradeoff: instanced meshes are rebuilt every render (cheap for hundreds; noted as a shortcut in the code), frustumCulled is off, and non-mesh objects (lines, points) are not copied in 3D. The piece writer (PIECES_PARTS_NOTE) is told about <Copies>.
Evidence: test/media/video-copies.test.mjs checks 2D (40 copies, stable per seed, varied) and 3D on a bare fiber root (300 copies, 2 states -> 2 templates, 4 InstancedMeshes of 150, head offset scaled, stable matrices, rerender replaces them). video-piece-library test asserts the prompt mentions the helper. tsc is clean; npm run test:render passes 8/8. npm test: 726/737 pass. Fails: videos-streaming "closed video block..." and branch-tree "sibling branches interleave..." also fail on stashed master (pre-existing, unrelated), plus one concurrency-timing failure ("closed blocks start chat-model workers") that passes when its file runs alone.

title: Set pieces built from parts
description:
## What to build

A set piece may be built from parts: other set pieces in the same module or saved library pieces. The piece writer prefers a flat build and uses a part only when it is reused at least twice or already saved; anything with no fitting part is drawn by the piece itself; no fixed nesting limit. The planner is unchanged; the library lookup also runs for candidate parts with the same reuse, variant or new choice. Parts are saved as library pieces of their own with both forms, and a piece records the parts it uses instead of copying them. A reused piece brings its parts, scoped and role-remapped. Within one video, the video's own set piece wins over a library part of the same name. An improved part reaches every piece using it in future videos; the current and saved videos keep how they looked. Library view unchanged. See spec and ADR 0006.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The piece writer is told about parts and the flat-build preference
- [ ] Parts are saved as their own library entries with 2D and 3D forms, and pieces refer to them
- [ ] Reusing a piece brings its parts; the video's own piece wins a name clash
- [ ] Improving a part changes later assemblies of pieces that use it but not saved videos
- [ ] Pieces saved before this change still load and reuse
- [ ] Video-pieces, piece-library and video-piece-library tests cover the above
notes: Done 2026-11-16. pieces table gains nullable parts JSON [{name,id}] (additive ALTER; NULL reads as []). Piece writer always gets PIECES_PARTS_NOTE (parts = same-module or library pieces, flat build preferred, part only when drawn twice or likely saved, no nesting limit). Decision: the writer asks for candidate parts with a first answer {"parts":[{name,look}]}; the app runs the same library lookup for those looks and calls again with parts + their matches; choices cover names and parts (reuse/variant/new). One lookup round per video (not counted as a failed attempt); a malformed request is retried. libraryPieces records another entry it draws as parts by name instead of copying it (non-entry exports still copied); onPieces saves parts first and stores ids. store.pieceTree resolves parts at their current versions (nearestPieces returns trees), withParts (video-pieces.mjs) scopes parts inside each form via assemblePieces, skipping names the video draws itself (own piece wins), and remaps roles over the union of the tree roles. Stills and GET /api/pieces/:id compile the assembled piece (shown source stays the piece own code; roles = union). improvePiece tells the model the part names; store.improvePiece leaves parts untouched. Saved videos keep their assembled module. Shortcuts: an audit only offers pieces named in the cut code, so a poor part drawn inside another piece is flagged as that piece; parents of an improved part keep stale stills until they are improved. withParts moved into video-pieces.mjs to keep video-plan.mjs under 500 lines. Tests (fixtures, unit/integration): store/pieces (refs, tree current versions, old NULL parts), media/video-piece-library (parts request round, part lookup, own part wins, parts saved as own entries, improvement reaches later assembly not saved video; reuse brings parts in 2D+3D scoped and remapped; bad request retried), video-pieces (split refers instead of copying), video-piece-improve (parts named). npm test 714/725 pass, the same 3 unrelated failures as on clean master (closed video block mid-reply, chat-model workers queue, sibling branches interleave); npm run test:slow 21/21.

title: Fixes, repairs and piece improvements return patches
description:
## What to build

The fix after a cut audit, the repair of a cut that failed to validate or render, and the improvement of a poor library piece return a unified diff against the source they were given instead of the whole source. The app applies it with the diff package (jsdiff), added as a direct dependency. If the diff does not parse or apply, one follow-up call asks for the whole source as today; no patch retry. Patched cuts go through the same validation and rendering, a patch that breaks a cut is discarded, and attempt limits hold with the fallback counted. The source given to the fixer carries line structure to diff against. First-time writing and the cut audit are unchanged. See spec: Cut patches.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A valid diff patches the cut, repair or piece and only the changed lines change
- [ ] An unparseable or non-applying diff triggers exactly one whole-source call
- [ ] A patch that breaks a cut is discarded as today; attempt limits still hold
- [ ] Piece improvement patches both forms together when a 3D form exists
- [ ] The cut audit's input and output are unchanged
- [ ] Video audit, repair and piece-improvement tests with a fake chat model cover the above
notes:
Done 2026-11-17. Fix, repair and piece improvement answer a unified diff; server/media/patches.mjs applies it with jsdiff (diff ^8.0.4, new direct dependency): withSource() sends the JSON task then the source as raw lines after "<field>:" (code / failedCode / source), patched() returns null when the diff does not parse, has no hunks, has several files or does not apply. Fix: FIX_NOTE asks {"patch","emphasis"?}; null => one FIX_WHOLE_NOTE call (old note and input, {"code"}); a patched fix still validates/renders or is discarded as before. Repair: with failed code REPAIR_PATCH_NOTE asks a diff of failedCode; on null one REPAIR_NOTE whole-source call (old note/input). Decision: the patch call and its fallback make up one attempt (CUT_ATTEMPTS=2 stays; counting the fallback as its own attempt would leave no room for it), so a repair costs at most 2 calls and no attempt is added. Repairs without failed code (oversized output) stay whole-source. Piece improve: both forms sent as one module (2D source + 3D source without the shared leading lines), patched together, then validated as before; null => one whole-source call with source/source3d JSON as before. Cut audit input/output unchanged. Usage stage detection covers both notes.
Tests (fixtures, fake chat model, unit/component): video-audit (patch applies, only changed lines; bad/non-applying patch => exactly one whole call; breaking patch discarded; auditFix unit), video-repair (patch repair; non-diff => one whole call in same attempt; still-broken patch hits the limit, no further call), video-piece-improve (2D and both-form patches, fallback with both saved forms, invalid patch rejected), manim-audit, video-models; other fakes updated via test/support/video-kit fixerTask/patchOf/repairAnswer. npm test 724/735 pass, 8 skipped; failures pre-existing at HEAD (videos-streaming "closed video block", branch-tree "sibling branches") plus flaky visuals-queue (passes alone). npm run test:slow 21/21 (server/http changed). No live provider check needed (spec: model calls faked).

title: Classmates talk in their own voices
description:
## What to build

Each classmate gains a private voice beside their hidden level: how they talk and how they think, fitting their level. The server stores voice and level, never sends them to the browser, and passes both to every reply turn so a voice holds for the whole discussion. Validation requires a voice per classmate and distinct voices; discussions saved before this still load. The discussion and reply-turn rules describe casual online chat: everyday words and slang, contractions, the odd swear word or typo, short lines, rarely an emoji, no buzzwords or performed eagerness, in the learner's language. The tutor's lines stay plain and clear; honest misunderstandings stay. The natural-writing skill must not flatten classmate voices. See spec: Classmate voices.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A discussion block without a voice per classmate, or with repeated voices, is rejected with a clear problem
- [ ] Voices and levels never reach the browser
- [ ] Reply turns receive each classmate's voice and level
- [ ] Discussions saved before this change still load and accept replies
- [ ] Discussion rules describe the voice range, learner's language and plain tutor
- [ ] Discussion validation, turn and route tests cover the above
notes: Done 2026-11-16. readDiscussion (server/media/discussions.mjs) requires a non-empty voice (<=500 chars) per classmate and case-insensitive distinct voices, stores {name,level,voice} in the saved source; discussionArtifact already sends names/lines only. Reply turn prompt passes saved classmates (level+voice) unchanged; old voiceless discussions load and reply (new HTTP test). DISCUSSION_RULE and DISCUSSION_TURN_RULE describe casual chat voice range, learner's language, plain tutor, honest misunderstandings; humanizer.md 'When not to act' keeps classmate voices. Decision: voice is free text, distinct by exact text (case-insensitive) — simplest check; semantic sameness not enforced. Tests: test/media/discussions, test/http/discussions, test/http/discussion-replies pass (fixture-only, no live provider). npm test: 722/732 pass in 732; 2 failures (videos-streaming 'closed video block...', store/branch-tree 'sibling branches interleave...') also fail on a clean HEAD copy, unrelated.

title: Discussion lines arrive one at a time
description:
## What to build

Discussion lines appear one at a time, for the opening and for reply turns. Before each line a typing indicator names the speaker for a pause that grows with the line's length (about 1 to 4 seconds, small random jitter, same speed for everyone); then the whole line appears, never token by token. There is no skip. The learner can type while lines arrive; sending is disabled, with a short hint, until every written line has appeared. Seen lines are remembered per discussion: reopening shows them at once and leaving mid-way resumes the pace. When the discussion closes, remaining lines appear at once. The discussion rule asks the tutor to place the discussion last in its reply. Generation is unchanged. See spec: Paced discussions.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Opening and reply-turn lines reveal one at a time behind a speaker typing indicator, whole lines only
- [ ] Pauses grow with line length and vary slightly
- [ ] The reply box accepts typing while lines arrive; send is disabled with a hint until every line has appeared
- [ ] Reopening shows seen lines at once; returning mid-way resumes pacing; closing shows all remaining lines
- [ ] The discussion rule asks for the discussion to come last in the reply
- [ ] Discussion card component tests with fake timers cover the above
notes: Done. DiscussionCard (src/media/DiscussionCard.tsx) reveals lines from a queue: '<speaker> is typing…' status for linePause(text)=min(1000+20ms/char,4000)×(0.9–1.1 jitter), whole lines only; a line still streaming waits in the indicator; Learner lines appear instantly. Seen count stored per discussion in localStorage 'rabbithole.discussion-seen.<artifact id>' (reopen shows seen lines, mid-way resumes pace); closed shows all. Reply box stays typeable (composer still disabled during an in-flight stream, as before); send button and Enter blocked with hint 'You can send once every line has appeared.' DISCUSSION_RULE now asks for the block placed last with no reply text after it. Tradeoff: discussions with no stored count (older ones, other browsers) pace once from the start. Removed orphan data-streaming CSS. Evidence: component tests with mock timers in test/media/discussion-card.test.mjs (pacing, length/jitter, typing-while-waiting, remount resume, close mid-way, streaming line hidden), rule test in tutor-style; chat-page and discussion-branch tests seed seen counts. npm test: 721 pass, 2 fail (videos-streaming.test.mjs:49, branch-tree.test.mjs:55) that also fail on clean HEAD, unrelated. No browser verify (not named in acceptance).

title: Everyday analogy guidance in replies, visuals and videos
description:
## What to build

The fixed teaching skill tells tutor replies, visuals and video narration to open with an everyday analogy when a concept is new or abstract to the learner, map the formal idea onto it, say plainly where it breaks down, and skip it for quick factual answers, casual turns and concepts the learner already knows. Familiarity is used where a prompt already receives it. The video planner decides how an analogy shapes a video and keeps one analogy across its cuts. A learner's own analogy is taken seriously and refined, but never required to be reused; discussion prompts do not push analogies. The learner's tutor style still applies on top. See spec: Everyday analogy.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tutor replies, visual writers and video narration receive the analogy guidance through the teaching skill
- [ ] The video planner is told to keep one analogy across a video's cuts and to decide how it shapes the video
- [ ] The tutor style still follows the skills and overrides them where it differs
- [ ] Discussion prompts gain no analogy rule
- [ ] Prompt assembly tests cover the above; wording checked against the semaphore conversation
notes: Done. New Rabbithole-own skill server/media/prompts/analogy.md (ANALOGY_SKILL) appended to TEACHING_SKILL, so tutor replies (TUTOR_SKILLS, before tutor style which "follow it where it differs") and video planner narration get it; visual worker INSTRUCTIONS append ANALOGY_SKILL (it never had the teaching skill; decision: give only the analogy part to avoid tutoring rules in the drawing prompt). Planner rule: decide how analogy shapes video (open/return/beside formal), one analogy across every cut, named in layout areas/recurring objects. DISCUSSION_RULE and DISCUSSION_TURN_RULE untouched, asserted analogy-free. Familiarity: "from familiarity where you have it, conversation otherwise" (no new plumbing). Wording checked against the local semaphore tree 33fa26be (messages 149-160): first reply already used a printer-room analogy but skipped mapping/breakdown; reply to learner traffic-police analogy refined it and named a breakdown ("does not decide which car goes next"), matching the new guidance; no live model run. Tests: test/media/tutor-style.test.mjs new analogy test, visuals-prompts asserts ANALOGY_SKILL; focused suites 27/27 pass. npm test: 724/727; 3 failures (videos-streaming, visuals-queue, branch-tree streaming-text timing) also fail on pristine HEAD sources, pre-existing flakes unrelated.

title: Learner messages render as markdown
description:
## What to build

The learner's own messages render through the same markdown renderer as tutor replies, so code (coloured), lists, emphasis and maths show as typed. Reply-only features (suggestions, inline media, passage branching) are not applied. The stored message text is unchanged. See spec: Code colours.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A learner message with a fenced code block shows it coloured, and lists and emphasis render
- [ ] Learner messages show no suggestions, inline media or branchable passages
- [ ] Stored text, copying and the first-question display are unchanged
- [ ] Unit or component tests cover learner message rendering
notes: Done. ChatThread learner bubble now renders <Reply text underlines={[]}/> (same renderMarkdown as replies: maths, Prism code colours, lists, emphasis) instead of pre-wrap Text. Reply-only features absent by construction: no Passage (no selection/branching), no inline artifacts, suggestions stay in ReplyFeedback. Stored text, reply copy button indexes, first-question display and map node snippets unchanged (map stays plain 3-line snippet). Decision: workspace.css keeps the bubble's own font for learner prose instead of the Literata reading face; code keeps code face. Tradeoff: single newlines now follow markdown soft-break rules rather than pre-wrap. Evidence: test/shell/chat-page.test.mjs 'learner messages render markdown...' (em, li, coloured java keyword, no .passage/figure, stored text equal). tsc clean. npm test 723/726; 3 failures (video block, chat-model workers queue, sibling branches) are the pre-existing TreeTutor-tow failures seen in hfi.1. No browser check (not named in acceptance).

title: Code in every language is coloured
description:
## What to build

Fenced code in tutor replies is coloured in every common language, including Java, C#, Ruby, Scala and Dart, which show plain today. Prism (already in the dependency tree, added as a direct dependency) replaces Astryx tokenizing; its tokens map onto the theme's existing syntax colour roles, and unmatched tokens stay plain. Prism only tokenizes: the renderer keeps building React elements and Prism's in-page autoloader is never used. Grammars load only for languages in use. Unlabelled, text and plaintext fences stay plain. See spec: Code colours.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Java, C# and Python fences in a reply render coloured tokens using the theme syntax colours in light and dark appearance
- [ ] Unlabelled, text and plaintext fences render plain
- [ ] The copy button copies the exact code and passage branching inside code still works
- [ ] No new theme colours; existing token classes keep working in every theme
- [ ] Markdown renderer unit tests cover the above
notes: Done. Prism 1.30.0 added as exact direct dep (lockfile root entry hand-edited to keep formatting). New src/markdown/codeTokens.ts: lazy-imports Prism core + prismjs/components.js (aliases/requires) on first labelled fence, then grammar chunks via relative dynamic import of node_modules/prismjs/components/prism-<id>.min.js (Vite splits one chunk per grammar; autoloader never imported; Prism.manual set so no page highlighting). Tokens flattened to per-line offsets, Prism type/alias mapped onto the 13 existing astryx-token-* roles; unmapped stay plain. markdown.ts swaps Astryx tokenize for codeTokens; Reply.tsx re-renders via useSyncExternalStore when a grammar finishes loading. Decision: first render of a new language is plain until its grammar loads (tradeoff: brief plain flash vs bundling all grammars). builtin maps to type role. Evidence: test/chat/code-colours.test.mjs (Java/C#/Python coloured roles, ''/text/plaintext plain, exact code text, raw-offset selection inside coloured code) and copy-buttons test now uses a coloured java fence and copies exact source; tsc passes; vite build emits separate prism core/components/per-grammar chunks. npm test: 716/719 pass; 3 failures (branch-tree, videos-streaming, visuals-queue) fail identically with my changes stashed, tracked by TreeTutor-tow. Light/dark: classes use existing light-dark() theme vars; no browser check run (not named in acceptance).

title: Code colours, everyday analogies, paced discussions, cut patches and set piece parts
description:
Spec: docs/analogies-discussions-and-piece-parts-spec.md. Decisions: ADR 0006 (set pieces built from parts), building on ADR 0002, 0004 and 0005. Glossary: everyday analogy, discussion, classmate, part, set piece, piece library.

Code in every language is coloured in tutor replies and learner messages, which render as markdown. Replies, visuals and videos open with an everyday analogy when a concept is new or abstract. Discussion lines arrive one at a time at a typing pace, and each classmate talks and thinks in their own casual voice. Fixes, repairs and piece improvements return patches instead of whole sources. Set pieces can be built from parts saved in the piece library, with many copies instanced in 3D. Saving both piece forms is TreeTutor-t9g.2, which the media tickets wait for.

title: Three streaming tests fail since the 250 ms streaming-save throttle
description: Since commit 77670c3 (streaming saves a reply at most every 250 ms), three tests fail deterministically on clean HEAD: videos-streaming.test.mjs 'a closed video block starts its job mid-reply…' (saved text 'Before.' vs 'Before.\nAfter.'), visuals-queue.test.mjs 'closed blocks start chat-model workers while text streams…', branch-tree.test.mjs 'sibling branches interleave independent saved turns…'. They read the mid-stream saved text before the throttled save lands. Fix: have the tests wait for the throttled save (until()), or flush the pending save when a block closes. Found while verifying TreeTutor-t9g.7.
notes: Duplicate of Rabbithole-x9y, fixed in commit 010672c (send.mjs flushes the pending save; the tests wait for the throttled save). Verified on HEAD 03548bc: node --test test/store/branch-tree.test.mjs test/media/visuals-queue.test.mjs test/media/videos-streaming.test.mjs gives 12/12 pass on 3 runs. check-size passes. test:affected: no tests affected because there's no code change. format:check flags 13 committed files from earlier work (server/http/jobs/media.mjs, server/media/video-cuts.mjs, video-stage.mjs, src/media/player.tsx and 9 tests). That is unrelated to this issue and was left untouched.

title: Clips with their own sound pause the narration
description:
## What to build
The planner decides per clip whether its own sound plays. When it does, the narration track pauses for the clip's length and subtitles show only the narration; muted clips keep playing under the narration. Live playback and the MP4 match. See spec: Exhibits.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Plans mark each clip's sound on or off
- [ ] A clip with sound puts a pause of its length into the narration, and its audio plays there
- [ ] Subtitles show only narration
- [ ] Live playback and the MP4 match
- [ ] Video job integration test with fake narration covers the pause
notes: Done. Plans: clips must carry "sound": false (muted under narration) or true with "sentence" (0-based sentence of the cut narration after which the clip plays); at most one sound clip per cut; CLIPS_NOTE tells the planner when to choose sound. Downloader: sound clips use yt-dlp bv*+ba and ffmpeg -map 0:v:0 -map 0:a:0 AAC (a source without audio fails, so the exhibit is dropped); muted stay -an. fetchExhibit carries sound/sentence. stageNarration(dir, result, signal, pause): Remotion-bundled ffmpeg splices silence of round(seconds*30) frames into narration.mp3 at the end of that sentence (clamped to the last sentence), re-probes duration, shifts later sentences/words, so captions and captions.vtt hold only narration and none falls in the pause; timing.pause={id,startFrame,frames}. CUT_ENTRY and live Narrated play the clip mp4 as <Audio> in a Sequence over the pause (the wrapper owns it, so the sound plays even if the writer hides the exhibit); stock.json and player.tsx give the sound clip from=pause.startFrame, which Exhibit uses over the cut-passed from. Writer EXHIBIT_NOTE explains sound clips. Decisions: pause placed after a planned sentence (tradeoff: planner sentence count can differ from TTS, so clamped); retries reuse the spliced narration. Tests: video-plan (sound required, sentence, one per cut); exhibits (sound download args, sound passed and recorded); video-exhibits job test with fake narration (2 sentences): pause {exhibit1,24,180}, sentence 2 shifted 6 s, track 1.92+6 s, captions/vtt shifted with none in the pause, stock from=24; live-player component: before the pause only narration audio and no footage, during it the clip audio and video, after it video without sound; video-exhibits-render real render: black mat before the pause, red footage at 3 s, MP4 longer than 4.8 s, clip tone louder than -35 dB inside the pause. Results: tsc clean; npm run test:render 8/8 pass; npm test 718 tests, 707 pass, 8 skipped, 3 fail = the known TreeTutor-tow failures. No live provider video and no live sound-clip download run (fixtures only for the sound path).

title: Muted clip exhibits
description:
## What to build
Setup installs yt-dlp into the project-local Python environment the way it installs Manim, and reports when it or ffmpeg is unavailable; videos then have no clips. A plan may name clip exhibits with the wanted moment; the exhibit fetcher downloads and trims the clip to those seconds and hands it to the cut as data. Clips play muted under the narration inside the exhibit frame, live and in the MP4, and are saved as resources. A failed download drops the exhibit. See spec: Exhibits.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Setup installs yt-dlp and reports a clear message when it or ffmpeg is unavailable
- [ ] Plans with clip exhibits validate; no clip option without the downloader
- [ ] The fetcher downloads and trims clips; failures drop the exhibit
- [ ] Clips play muted in the exhibit frame, live and in the MP4, and are saved as resources
- [ ] Fetcher unit test with a fake downloader; setup script test following the Manim setup tests
notes: Done. Setup: new scripts/clips-setup.mjs ensureClips (run from start.mjs after ensureManim) installs unpinned yt-dlp into the Manim .venv with uv pip; it is optional like offline Python: missing ffmpeg (apt/brew command given) or a failed install warns "Clip exhibits unavailable ... videos have no clips" and start-up continues. server/media/clips.mjs: detectClips (fresh probe of .venv/bin/yt-dlp and PATH ffmpeg per plan), downloadClip (yt-dlp --download-sections *start-end, <=720p, then ffmpeg -t length -an, scaled/padded to 1280x720 30fps H.264 yuv420p faststart, 40 MiB cap, temp dir removed). Plans: CLIPS_NOTE appended after EXHIBITS_NOTE only when search is ready AND clips detect ready; videoPlan({clips}) accepts {kind:clip,query,show,start,end} (finite seconds, end>start, at most MAX_CLIP_SECONDS=15) and rejects clip kind otherwise. Fetcher: clip searched with SearXNG videos category (search tool third arg is now a category: images/videos; runner passes images), top 3 results tried, page host must resolve to public addresses, records url/title/site/seconds, type video/mp4; any failure drops the exhibit (existing fetchExhibits, moved into exhibits.mjs for the 500-line limit). Staging copies the clip into the cut public folder as <id>.mp4 (the write-time check runs before public exists and renders nothing); stock.json carries {clip:<id>.mp4}. Kit Exhibit gains from={frame}: 16:9 black-backed mat, Sequence from + Loop(seconds) + muted OffthreadVideo (staticFile in render, blob URL live). Live route flag image renamed media (clip bytes served like images); writer EXHIBIT_NOTE and audit text cover muted clips. Resources saved with kind clip. Decisions: yt-dlp unpinned (sites change; tradeoff: less reproducible); no per-video warning when clips are unavailable (setup reports it); host check only covers the page host, yt-dlp follows its own redirects. Tests: test/scripts/clips.test.mjs (install, later start, ffmpeg missing linux/darwin, failed install, still unusable, detect); exhibits.test.mjs (fake downloader: videos search, fallback, recorded source; failures, private host, no downloader; downloadClip args with fake run: section, -t, -an, nothing saved); video-plan clip validation; video-exhibits job test (CLIPS_NOTE, writer data, drop, staged stock.json clip + public file, clip resource, rejected without downloader); live-player Exhibit clip renders muted video with blob src; video-exhibits-render real render: red clip pixels inside the frame in the MP4. Results: tsc clean; npm run test:render 7/7 pass; npm test 701 tests, 691 pass, 7 skipped, 3 fail = the known TreeTutor-tow failures. Live (not fixture): real ensureClips installed yt-dlp into .venv; real downloadClip of a YouTube video 60-64s gave 4.000s 1280x720 H.264 with no audio stream (this run found and fixed a --ffmpeg-location bug). No live provider video run.

title: Image and quote exhibits in videos
description:
## What to build
A video plan may name image and quote exhibits per cut, found with the web search tutor tool; without search configured the planner gets no exhibit option. A new exhibit fetcher downloads images and records URL, title and site; a failure drops the exhibit and the cut is written without it. The media reaches the cut as data so the sandbox stays offline. A kit exhibit component frames the media as real, takes position, scale and rotation from the cut and draws a short dim source line. Each exhibit is saved as a resource of the video's learning tree, never in the piece library, and the background MP4 render gets the same data. Visuals get no exhibits. See spec: Exhibits; ADR 0005.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Plans with image and quote exhibits validate; no exhibit option without web search
- [ ] The exhibit fetcher downloads images and records source details; failures drop the exhibit
- [ ] Cuts using the exhibit component pass validation; raw image tags and URLs are still rejected
- [ ] The exhibit shows framed with a dim source line, live and in the MP4
- [ ] Exhibits are saved as resources of the learning tree and never enter the piece library
- [ ] Unit test for the fetcher with a fake HTTP server; video job integration test for resources
notes: Done. Plans may name up to two image/quote exhibits per Remotion cut (videoPlan validates kind, query, show or text/by; Manim cuts and plans without search reject them). EXHIBITS_NOTE reaches the planner only when the web_search tutor tool is switched on and SearXNG status is ready (decision: honour the tutor-tool toggle as well as the server; tradeoff: one store read per new plan). New server/media/exhibits.mjs fetchExhibit: image search, download through read_page public-address checks (request/body now exported), up to 3 results, 5 redirects, 3 MiB cap, type from magic bytes (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, no SVG); quotes credit the result whose title/snippet contains the quote, else the top result. fetchExhibits in videos.mjs drops a failed exhibit with a warning; image bytes go to cut-N/exhibits/, staged into stock.json as data URLs (sandbox stays offline); live playback gets metadata from /cuts plus image bytes from /cuts/<i>/exhibit as blobs posted to the frame. Kit <Exhibit id x y width scale rotation opacity> draws a paper mat, shadow and a dim title · site line; a missing exhibit draws nothing. Writers and audits see only the fetched exhibits of their cut plus EXHIBIT_NOTE; audit told exhibits are meant to look real. title: Piece cards show 2D and 3D stills
description:
## What to build
Stills of a piece's 2D and 3D forms are rendered server-side when the piece is saved or improved, using the cut audit's still-rendering path, and stored with the piece. Pieces saved earlier are backfilled like unembedded pieces. Library cards show both stills, or the 2D still with a 2D only note. See spec: Piece library view.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Saving or improving a piece stores its 2D still and, when it has one, its 3D still
- [ ] Pieces without stills are backfilled
- [ ] Cards show both stills, or the 2D still with a 2D only note
- [ ] Cards load without starting a live player per card
- [ ] Store and route tests for stills; component test for the cards
notes: Done 2026-11-16. Stills: new server/media/piece-stills.mjs stages a piece workspace with stageCut (kit, colors, host data) plus its own entry (frame 0 = 2D form on the ground, frame 1 = 3D form in a ThreeCanvas at the turntable camera, 3/4 turn) and renders through sandboxSnapshot, the cut audit's still path (960x540 JPEG). pieces table gains still/still3d BLOBs (migration); improvePiece clears them; stillPiece(id, improved, ...) ignores stills of an older improvement. A background queue (ctx.pieceStills) renders unstilled pieces one at a time; triggered after onPieces saves and after an improvement in generateVideo (stills param), and by GET /api/pieces for backfill (like the embedding backfill). Failed pieces are skipped until improved or restart (logged WARN media piece stills failed). Off unless createApp gets pieceSnapshot; main.mjs passes sandboxSnapshot. GET /api/pieces/:id/still[3d] serves image/jpeg (immutable; client adds ?v=improved). List rows gain solid/still/still3d flags. Cards: two 16:9 img stills, or 2D still + '2D only', or 'still pending' placeholder; no iframe per card. FONTS extracted from CUT_ENTRY for reuse. Decision/tradeoff: one sandbox render for both forms (one bundle, ~12s) - a crashing 3D form loses the 2D still too until improved. Evidence: live sandbox render of a 2D+3D fixture piece produced both JPEGs (viewed, correct). Tests: store/pieces (stills, stale guard, flags), http/pieces (backfill via fake snapshot, staged entry, JPEG route, 404, failure not retried), media/piece-library (cards), media/video-piece-improve (improved piece re-stilled from new source); 18/18. tsc clean. npm test 704 pass / 3 fail = same pre-existing failures as t9g.1 (videos-streaming, visuals-queue, branch-tree). test:slow 21/21. test:render 7/7 (CUT_ENTRY touched).

description:

notes: Done 2026-11-16. GET /api/pieces/:id adds code3d (source3d compiled like cut code, null when 2D-only). PieceLibrary detail posts {type:'piece', code, code3d, name, paletteRoles} to the same sandbox=allow-scripts /player.html frame; with a 3D form the frame gets class piece-forms (aspect 32:9, 2D stage and 3D turntable side by side) and a read-only '3D source' code block; a 2D-only piece shows '2D only: this piece has no 3D form.' title: Set pieces keep their 3D form
description:
## What to build
A set piece stores its 2D form and an optional 3D form in one library entry. The set-piece step saves each recurring object's 3D export with its 2D piece instead of discarding it, reuse brings both forms, a variant derives both, and an improvement replaces both together after validating each. title: Pieces view in the sidebar with paging and search
description:
## What to build
A Pieces button in the sidebar opens the piece library as its own view; the Videos view drops its Pieces tab. The list is paged and has a search bar that ranks pieces by meaning using their embeddings, falling back to a text match on name and look when no embedder is usable. - [ ] A Pieces view tab in the sidebar opens the piece library; the Videos view has no Pieces tab

title: Visuals render 2D stock pieces
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, sections "Visual frame runtime", "Visual request contract" and "Stock catalog module (new)".

## What to build

Second half of the 2D tracer bullet: a visual that names an offered Fluent Emoji piece shows it.

- A piece is fetched the first time a finished visual uses it, written atomically to a cache folder in the data directory and read from there afterwards; no eviction (mark it as a shortcut).
- A piece that cannot be fetched becomes a validationError, through the existing single retry.
- The host gets the used pieces' data from a local app route and delivers it with the render message.
- The frame's stockPiece(id) global returns a ready SVG element; a missing ID is reported in words. The frame still makes no network request.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-diw.1
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] A piece is fetched once and served from the cache afterwards (unit test with a fake download).
[ ] A failed piece fetch produces a validationError retry (visuals failures test).
[ ] The local app route returns cached piece data for an ID and refuses an unknown ID (in-process app test).
[ ] stockPiece(id) in the frame returns an SVG element from delivered data and reports a missing ID in words (jsdom unit test).
[ ] The frame makes no network request; the existing sandbox restrictions still pass.
notes: Done (2026-11-16). stock.mjs stockCatalog gains piece(id): unknown ID -> null; else reads <data>/stock/pieces/<encoded id>.svg, or fetches raw.githubusercontent.com at the pinned revision, checks it is SVG and writes atomically (shared writeAtomic with the index). Shortcut comment: no eviction. Validation (visuals.mjs) fetches each named piece after the offered check; a failed/null fetch -> validationError "could not be fetched", existing single retry. Route GET /api/stock/:id returns JSON {svg} (decision: JSON not image/svg+xml so the app origin never serves SVG as a document), 404 for unknown. VisualFrame host, on the finished render only, fetches /api/stock/<id> for each stockPiece literal in the source and posts pieces with the render message (failed fetch -> null). sandbox.ts stockPiece(id) global uses visualMarkup.ts stockPiece: DOMParser + importNode, fresh SVG element per call. Decision: a missing/invalid piece returns a visible SVG reading "Stock piece <id> is missing" instead of throwing, so the visual keeps running and the learner sees the gap in words. Frame makes no request (data arrives by postMessage). Evidence: stock.test (fake download: fetched once, cached across catalogs, unknown null, failure/non-SVG rejected), visuals-failures (failed fetch -> validationError retry), visuals-stock (in-process route 200/404), visual-markup (jsdom stockPiece), inline-media (host fetches and delivers pieces; partial renders unchanged). Live: real fluent-emoji:horse fetched from GitHub and served from cache second call. npm test 658 pass/0 fail/5 skipped; test:slow 21/21.

title: Callout, timeline and wide layouts
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, section "Reply layouts".

## What to build

Three new reply layouts: callout (a highlighted block for a key idea, warning or takeaway, exposed as a labelled region), timeline (ordered or dated entries with one heading per entry, exposed as a list) and wide (one visual or image spanning the full reply width). Each keeps the no-nesting rule and falls back to plain flow at narrow width or on a bad shape. The tutor rules describe each by shape only.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-z8g.1
design: UI change: use the Impeccable skill, with Astryx components.
acceptance_criteria:
[x] Callout renders as a labelled region holding its content (component test).
[x] Timeline renders as an ordered list with one entry per heading.
[x] Wide renders one visual or image at full reply width.
[x] A bad shape or narrow width falls back to plain flow.
[x] The tutor rules describe the three layouts by shape, with no example reply.
notes:
Implementation plan and defaults: extend the shared Markdown layout renderer, its styles and tutor shape rules; extend the existing reply-layout component suites and prompt unit test. Callout uses a nonempty Astryx Section with the generic accessible name Callout, so a title is optional and no new directive option is needed. Timeline reuses heading grouping as an ordered list, requires at least two entries with one same-level heading each, and uses a quiet continuous rule rather than cards. Wide accepts exactly one image or visual, without prose; artifact kind metadata keeps videos and discussions in plain flow. Reuse the existing 480px Reply fallback and source-offset leaves. Suppress layout styling throughout nested directive trees, preserving all text/media. Scope includes Reply slot metadata, shared renderer/layout styles, tutor rules and focused tests; no provider, persistence or transport changes. Verify focused component/prompt tests, Impeccable source review/detector, build, formatting and one final npm test. No browser/native provider checks are required by the acceptance/spec. Leave Git unstaged and uncommitted for Ralph.

Callout uses a nonempty Astryx Section with role=region and accessible name Callout, keeping a heading optional; definition-only callouts stay plain. Timeline uses a native ordered list, at least two same-level titled entries, a continuous quiet rule and one heading per entry. Wide uses exactly one linked/reference image or one visual across the reply width; images retain sources and lose the ordinary height cap. Reply supplies artifact-kind metadata so a video or discussion is not claimed as a wide visual. Nested directive trees, malformed shapes and widths below 480px render in plain flow; returning to 480px restores layouts and media exactly once. Canonical reply text, raw passage offsets, reveal marks and previews stay intact. Shared tutor rules describe all three shapes without worked reply examples and retain neutral section choice/no nesting.

Evidence: added regressions first; focused suite initially had six failures for missing structures, nesting fallback, resize restoration and tutor wording. title: Videos use stock pieces
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, section "Videos".

## What to build

The set-piece writer is offered stock matches beside the piece library's closest pieces for each planned object. The choice per object becomes stock, reuse, variant or new; stock must name an offered stock ID and writes no code, a variant of a stock piece is rejected, and the prompt says to prefer stock when a piece fits. Cut code places stock pieces through a host-provided call, so the existing ban on loaders and static files stays. Manim cuts get 2D pieces only, as SVG; other cuts get 2D and 3D. A failed fetch is retried once; if it still fails, the writer is asked again without that piece and chooses reuse or new. The background MP4 render reads pieces from the same local cache as live playback. Stock pieces are never saved to the piece library and a cut audit never replaces one.

## Blocked by

[x] A failed stock fetch retries once, then the writer is asked again without that piece.
[x] A Manim cut is offered 2D pieces only.

- Writer input carries catalog matches next to per-object library matches. Stock is preferred when it fits; choices validate offered IDs, forbid stock variants and model-written stock code, and retain reuse/variant/new.

A second failure withdraws that object's stock offers and removes the failed ID from the remaining offers; the writer is asked again for reuse/new. Normal validation attempts remain bounded. title: Embedding matching for stock pieces
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, section "Stock catalog module (new)".

## What to build

Stock piece matching uses the local embedder already used by the piece library. Each catalog entry's title and type is embedded once and stored apart from the piece library's pieces. Each object name the tutor lists is embedded and matched by cosine to the top 3 entries. Keyword matching stays as the fallback while the embedder is unavailable.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-diw.1
acceptance_criteria:
[x] With a fake embedder, match returns the 3 closest entries by cosine for each object name (unit test).
[x] Without an embedder, match falls back to keyword matching and still returns results.
[x] Entries are embedded once; a second preparation does not embed them again.
[x] Stock entries never appear among the piece library pieces.
notes:
Implementation decision (2026-11-16): reuse one localEmbedder instance for video/library and stock matching at startup. Add optional embed injection to the existing stockCatalog factory; keep current match response and dimension filtering. Prepare title + type vectors lazily per pinned catalog, in bounded batches; persist atomically under data/stock with catalog hash and embedding model revision, separate from pieces/SQLite. Share in-flight preparation and reuse it across matches/restarts. On preparation or query failure use existing keywords and retry on later requests. Tradeoff: first semantic match waits for catalog preparation; completed catalogs cache independently. Checks: fake-embedder cosine ranking/cache/recovery unit tests and a storage-boundary isolation check; no UI, render or provider-specific behavior changes.
Verified (2026-11-16). server/media/stock.mjs now embeds each catalog title + type in batches of 32, stores vectors atomically in data/stock/<catalog>-<revision>-embeddings.json keyed by catalog hash and MODEL/REVISION, shares in-flight preparation, and reuses vectors across matches and factory restarts. Matches embed object names and scan cosine via the existing helper for the top 3, preserving current response metadata and pre-ranking 2D/3D filtering. Empty requests do not load or embed. Missing/rejecting embedder or query failure uses keyword matching; later requests recover without re-embedding prepared catalogs. Invalid JSON, malformed vectors and stale model/catalog keys are regenerated. Startup shares one localEmbedder instance with video/library/retrieval. No new dependency, schema or piece-library writes.
Acceptance evidence: test/media/stock.test.mjs fake catalog downloads and fake embeddings prove distinct object rankings with unnormalized vectors, per-name top 3 across catalogs, dimension filtering, concurrent and repeated preparation, restart reuse, absent/failed embedder fallback, recovery, and stale/corrupt cache regeneration. test/store/pieces.test.mjs uses a real temporary SQLite Store plus fake stock/embedder to prove its saved list, unembedded list and nearest-piece results stay unchanged. Targeted embedder, visual-stock, video-stock, video-stock-pipeline and video-piece-library checks passed.
Final npm test ran once: 680 tests, 675 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed (32.5 s). Changed-file Prettier, node --check for both server files and git diff --check passed. title: Stock shortlist in visual requests (2D)
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, sections "Visual request contract", "Stock catalog module (new)" and "Visual prompt".

## What to build

First half of the 2D tracer bullet, with Fluent Emoji flat as the 2D catalog. The visual model is offered fitting stock pieces and may only name offered ones:

- The catalog index downloads on first use at a pinned revision, checked against a recorded hash like the embedding model files; a mismatch is refused. The index is not committed to the repository.
- The tutor's visual request gets an optional objects list (concrete object names, with length and count limits beside the existing field limits), described in one sentence of the tutor rules.
- The visual worker matches each object to the top 3 stock pieces by keyword and lists them (ID, title, type) in the visual model's request; with no objects, no shortlist.
- The visual prompt says to place a piece with stockPiece(id), to use only offered IDs or none, and to keep a stock piece's own colours unless its real colour carries no meaning, when it may be tinted to theme colours.
- Validation rejects a stockPiece ID that was not offered with a validationError, through the existing single retry.
- IDs are the catalog's own, prefixed so they cannot collide with the 3D catalog.

Rendering the pieces in the frame is TreeTutor-diw.5.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
design: Fluent Emoji has no single catalog JSON: each emoji folder carries its own metadata file. Build the index from the repository at a pinned commit (for example its tree listing plus metadata) and record that choice. Only the flat style is used; it uses solid fills.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] A hash mismatch on the index is refused; a matching index is reused without a download (unit test with a fake download).
[ ] A visual request with objects puts the top 3 matches per object in the model input; one without objects gets no shortlist (visuals prompt test, fake provider).
[ ] An unoffered stockPiece ID produces a validationError retry (visuals failures test).
[ ] The tutor rules describe the optional objects field and its limits are enforced.
[ ] 2D IDs carry a catalog prefix.
notes: Done (2026-11-16). New server/media/stock.mjs: Fluent Emoji flat index built from the GitHub git tree listing of microsoft/fluentui-emoji at pinned commit 1ffb34c7; the recorded SHA-256 covers the built canonical index (1595 entries, ~213 KB, cached in <data>/stock/), because GitHub API JSON formatting is not pinned while the commit paths are. Mismatch, truncated listing or failed download refuses; matching cache reused. IDs fluent-emoji:<asset stem>; tone emojis use the Default tone. Decision: type is "emoji" for every entry, since group/keywords need ~1600 metadata.json fetches; tradeoff: keyword match uses titles only (diw.2 adds embeddings). Visual request gets optional objects (OBJECT_LIMITS count 6, length 60; trimmed/deduped tolerantly like other fields), one tutor-rules sentence. runVisual matches objects via ctx.stock (createApp option stock, main passes stockCatalog(dir)); an unavailable catalog logs a warning and the visual proceeds without shortlist. Model input carries stockPieces [{object,pieces:[{id,title,type}]}] only when non-empty. visual.md has the stockPiece(id)/only-offered/colour rules. validate rejects unoffered or non-literal stockPiece IDs -> validationError single retry. Caveat: frame stockPiece global lands in diw.5; until then a visual that uses a piece fails at render. Evidence: test/media/stock.test.mjs (fake download), visuals-stock.test.mjs + visuals-failures.test.mjs (fake provider), tutor-style rule assertion; live: real index downloaded from GitHub and hash matched. npm test 654 pass/0 fail/5 skipped; test:slow 21/21.

title: Scene-change steps and stepping rules
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, sections "Visual frame runtime" and "Visual prompt".

## What to build

The step helper accepts a scene step (an object marked as a scene change with its own show function) beside the plain step function. A scene step fades the visual's root out, runs its show function and fades it back in over the step duration; under reduced motion and on first render the switch is instant. Controls, indicator, keyboard and focus behave as today.

The visual prompt states, without worked examples: show every stage at once when stages belong side by side; step when later stages replace earlier ones in the same place; within stepping, continue (keep the same elements and animate their attributes with d3 transitions using the step duration, never rebuild or toggle near-copies) or change scene only when the layout really changes; mixing both is allowed. The prompt also says the frame holds only this visual, so CSS selectors need no id scoping.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] A scene step fades out, runs its show function and fades in using the step duration; a plain step still runs directly (jsdom unit test).
[ ] Under reduced motion and on first render both kinds of step switch with 0 duration.
[ ] Previous, Next, the Step n of m indicator, keyboard handling and focus are unchanged across scene steps.
[ ] The visual prompt carries the single view, continue and change-scene rules with no worked examples, and the no-id-scoping line (visuals prompt test).
notes: Done. stepThrough accepts {scene:true, show}: fades root opacity out over duration/2 (setTimeout), runs show with {index,duration}, fades back in; duration 0 (reduced motion/first render) runs show instantly. A step during a fade first runs the pending scene so later continuing steps start from it. Controls/indicator/keys/focus unchanged (updated synchronously). Prompt: side-by-side vs step, continue (d3 transitions on same elements, never rebuild/toggle near-copies) vs scene change only on real layout change, mixing allowed, no id scoping; no worked examples. Tests: test/media/step-through.test.mjs (scene fade, interrupt, reduced motion), visuals-prompts.test.mjs (rules present). npm test: 650 pass, 0 fail. Decision: fade-out and fade-in each take half the step duration so the whole switch fits the step duration; root keeps inline opacity transition afterwards (harmless).

title: SVG parts hide in stepped visuals
description:
Spec: docs/steps-stock-pieces-and-layouts-spec.md, section "Visual frame runtime".

## What to build

In the visual frame, setting the hidden property on an SVG element hides it, as it already does for HTML elements. Today the property does nothing on SVG, so every step of the latest stepped visual ("Loading a satellite onto Falcon 9") looks the same. The fix lives in the frame, so stored visuals start stepping when they re-render, without regeneration.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Setting hidden to true on an SVG group inside the frame sets the hidden attribute and the group is not displayed; setting it to false shows it again (jsdom unit test extending the step-through tests).
[ ] HTML elements keep their native hidden behaviour.
[ ] No prompt change is needed for the fix.
notes: SVG hidden fix: reflectSvgHidden(view) in src/media/stepThrough.ts defines an SVGElement.prototype hidden accessor reflecting to the hidden attribute; sandbox.ts installs it at frame start (applies to stored visuals on re-render, no prompt change). sandbox.html base style adds 'svg[hidden], svg [hidden] { display: none !important; }' — scoped to SVG so HTML keeps native UA hidden behaviour; !important so visual CSS display rules cannot unhide a hidden part (tradeoff: visuals cannot override it). Evidence: jsdom unit test in test/media/step-through.test.mjs (attribute + computed display none/visible, HTML property untouched); npm test 648 pass/0 fail (5 skipped); tsc --noEmit clean. No live/browser check run (not required by acceptance).

title: Branching from discussion lines
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions"., section "Discussion".

## What to build

The learner can select contiguous text in any discussion line, including a classmate's, and branch from it like any passage. The passage records the discussion and line it came from and is underlined there in its branch family's ink. The child's inherited context includes the passage and the discussion's compacted paragraph, or its lines while it is still open.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-ywy.7
design: UI change: use the Impeccable skill, with Astryx components. Detailed before/after mockup: docs/mockups/discussions.html, section D, fixes 19-21 (red numbered markers; quoted copy is exact). Section 0 lists the shared rules and the mockup-to-app token map. The spec wins on any difference.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Selecting text in a classmate's line offers branching and creates a child conversation with that passage (component and in-process app tests).
- [ ] The passage is underlined in the discussion line after reload.
- [ ] The child's inherited context includes the discussion's paragraph when closed, or its lines when open.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes:

Implementation: Passage selection capture first checks for a selection inside one discussion line ([data-line] inside the card's [data-artifact]); offsets are line-relative and ignore address chips. title: Discussion replies and closing
description:

## What to build

The learner replies inside an open discussion card. title: Lookup and recall tutor tools
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions".

## What to build

The tutor gets three tools it calls when it decides to: look_up_concept returns the nearest concepts to a description with familiarity (or guess, or unknown), topics and links; search_conversations mixes embedding and keyword matches over messages, titles and inherited context across all learning trees and returns about five candidates (conversation id, learning tree title, address, conversation title, one matching line); read_conversation returns a conversation's inherited context and messages within a fixed budget, otherwise one compact paragraph from the existing compaction job, cached until the conversation changes. Results are context only: no resource, citation or link. Saved messages get embeddings, backfilled like concepts. Each tool has its own Settings switch, on by default.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-ywy.3
design: UI change: use the Impeccable skill, with Astryx components. Detailed before/after mockup: docs/mockups/discussions.html, section F, fix 27 (red numbered markers; quoted copy is exact). Section 0 lists the shared rules and the mockup-to-app token map. The spec wins on any difference.

title: Concept neighbourhood in the chat prompt
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions".

## What to build

Before each reply the chat model receives the familiarity of concepts around the learner's message from the whole knowledge graph, across learning trees: concepts in the message (embedding match plus whole-name match), their linked concepts one hop out, a second hop when fewer than about 15 are found, cut to the budget nearest first. Each concept comes with its familiarity, a guess from linked concepts (marked as a guess), or unknown, plus its builds-on links within the set. Instructions tell the tutor to lean on familiar concepts, take care with shaky ones, correct recent misconceptions and explain unknown ones normally. This replaces the tree-only strong-concepts list. Concept names get embeddings from the existing local embedder, backfilled when it becomes usable; without it matching falls back to whole names.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-ywy.1
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The prompt the fake provider receives lists the message's concepts and their one-hop neighbours with familiarity, guess or unknown, and builds-on links.
- [ ] Fewer than the budget at one hop triggers the second hop; the set never exceeds the budget.
- [ ] Concepts from other learning trees are included.
- [ ] A reworded concept name matches through the fake embedder; with the embedder unavailable, whole-name matching still works and concepts are embedded once it is usable.
- [ ] The old strong-concepts list and its instructions are gone from the prompt.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes: Implementation plan: replace the tree-only strong-concepts prompt with one shared whole-graph neighbourhood for chat and discussion replies; reuse the local piece-library embedder and Float32 storage, retry missing concept embeddings on later retrieval. Verify graph traversal and estimate/guess/unknown semantics with unit tests, then prompt delivery with an in-process fake provider/embedder; finish with npm test and required slow/format checks. Routine defaults: 15 concept budget, semantic candidates above a cosine threshold with whole-name/alias matches first, one hop always then hop two only below budget. No frontend changes, remote operations or agent-side commits.

title: Verdict fallback by the quick thinking model
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions".

## What to build

When a completed reply to a learner message has no readable verdict block, a background job gives the quick thinking model the learner's message and the reply, and it returns verdicts in the same shape as the tutor's block, recorded as observations. Familiarity no longer depends on the chat model always remembering its block.

## Blocked by

- TreeTutor-ywy.1
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A reply with a missing or malformed verdict block starts one fallback call to the quick thinking model; a reply with a readable block starts none (in-process app test with the fake provider).
- [ ] Fallback verdicts are saved as observations against the learner message, like tag verdicts.
- [ ] A failed fallback call records nothing and does not affect the reply.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes:
Implemented and verified TreeTutor-ywy.2.

What: server/http/jobs/verdicts.mjs adds a detached verdict fallback job (ctx.verdicting map, included in app.settled()/stop()). In send.mjs finish(), a completed, non-empty reply whose diagramReply() found no readable verdict block (missing or malformed) calls ctx.startVerdicts(conversation, learnerMessage, body.text, replyText). The quick thinking model (ctx.quickFor: saved quick model, else the chat provider's cheap default) gets a thread-less prompt with {message, reply} and the same level/confidence scale (VERDICT_SHAPE, now shared with VERDICT_RULE; the rule text is byte-identical). Output is parsed by the existing readVerdicts (now exported; surrounding ``` fences tolerated) and saved with store.observe(learnerMessage, verdicts), the same path as tag verdicts.

Decisions/tradeoffs: an empty [] block counts as readable (tutor judged "nothing"), so no fallback. Failure, unset quick model, or unreadable output records nothing and only logs a WARN with private text redacted; the reply is untouched. A newer reply for the same learner message (Retry) aborts a running fallback before observing, so a stale result never overwrites. Usage is recorded under a new usage task 'verdict' (schema CHECK widened via the existing rebuild migration, now keyed on 'verdict'; dashboard label "Familiarity verdicts"). Like suggestions, the job is opt-in per createApp (verdicts=false default, main.mjs passes true), so existing fake-provider tests without blocks make no extra calls. Scope: main-thread send/retry replies only; discussion-card replies keep tag-only verdicts (not named by acceptance).

Evidence (in-process fake providers, not live models): test/http/verdicts.test.mjs — readable block -> 0 fallback calls; missing block -> exactly 1 quick call with quick-model, no thread, prompt {message, reply}; valid entries saved as one observation against the learner message (invalid entry dropped); malformed block -> 1 call; throwing fallback -> 0 observations, reply text/status unchanged; usage rows task='verdict'. title: Familiarity from the tutor's verdict tag
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions".

## What to build

The tutor judges, in every reply, what the learner's latest message showed about each concept it touched, and reports it in a hidden verdict block early in the reply: concept, level 0-5 (misconception, heard of it, partial, explains, applies, teaches) and confidence low/high. The learner never sees the block. Each entry becomes an observation, and familiarity is derived from observations by a pure function: a running average from a 0.3 prior, stepped further by high confidence, fading toward 0.2 at a rate set by a stability that grows only when the concept is shown again after a gap and resets on a misconception. Meeting a concept in a reply, ignoring a suggestion and creating a branch no longer move familiarity. The learner can no longer correct familiarity: the correction route and controls go, and the knowledge map is read-only and shows the new estimate.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
design: UI change: use the Impeccable skill, with Astryx components. Detailed before/after mockup: docs/mockups/discussions.html, section E, fixes 22-26 (red numbered markers; quoted copy is exact). Section 0 lists the shared rules and the mockup-to-app token map. The spec wins on any difference.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] The verdict block never appears in streamed or saved reply text, including when split across stream chunks; a reply whose learner message shows nothing has no block.
- [x] Each verdict entry is saved as one observation per concept per learner message; a retried reply replaces that message's observations.
- [x] A verdict naming a concept not in the graph creates it.
- [x] Unit tests of the familiarity function pin: the prior, high vs low confidence, a misconception pulling a known concept down, fading toward 0.2 and never below it by fading, stability growing only across gaps, a misconception resetting stability, and met evidence having no effect.
- [x] Branch creation no longer records asked evidence; ignored evidence is no longer recorded.
- [x] The schema upgrade deletes asked, used, ignored, known and unknown evidence rows and keeps met rows.
- [x] The correction route returns not found; the knowledge map has no correction controls and lists observation counts by level (component test).
- [x] npm test passes.
notes:
Implemented and verified TreeTutor-ywy.1.

Decisions and tradeoffs: prior 0.3 with weight 1; low/high observation weights 1/2; accumulated weight capped at 6 so fresh misconceptions remain responsive. Decay tends toward 0.2 with starting stability 2 days; level >=2 after a gap >=1 day triples stability; level 0 resets stability. These are named constants in server/familiarity.mjs. Store the anchored level (value = level/5), confidence, learner message id and time. Last valid verdict per canonical concept/message wins, including aliases. A closed readable tag from a failed/interrupted reply still judges the learner and is retained; Retry replaces that learner message's observation set, including clearing stale concepts. Invalid/unclosed blocks create no observations. Merge keeps the target verdict on a same-message collision. Keep Merge per mockup E; remove all familiarity correction controls/routes. An unobserved map concept uses the 0.3 prior. No extra model calls added. Fallback is TreeTutor-ywy.2; embeddings, linked guesses and neighbourhood retrieval are TreeTutor-ywy.3 and remain outside this issue.

Acceptance evidence: test/chat/verdicts.test.mjs checks every character boundary of backtick/tilde/tag blocks, split CRLF, truncated and malformed blocks, validation/deduplication, video co-existence and fixed early-verdict instructions. test/http/verdicts.test.mjs uses an in-process fake provider to check live SSE and saved text are stripped on every write; per-learner-message deduplication, aliases, new topicless concepts, failed-reply observations and Retry replacement, and a no-block greeting with no extra calls. test/store/familiarity.test.mjs pins prior, confidence, misconceptions, fading/floor, spaced stability and reset; Store checks show met-only evidence has no effect and the schema upgrade deletes asked/used/ignored/known/unknown while retaining met. test/chat/suggestions-knowledge.test.mjs proves branches, mentions and ignored suggestions add no old evidence, correction POST returns 404, and merge/persistence/aliases/rollback preserve observations. test/map/knowledge-page.test.mjs checks six ordered counts including zeros, the estimate and absence of correction controls; passage form tests cover removed menu and retained accessibility. Updated the schema inventory in test/store/preview.test.mjs.

Checks: final npm test PASS (605 total: 600 passed, 5 existing opt-in skips, 0 failed); npm run test:slow PASS; npm run build PASS (existing large-chunk advisory only); all changed code passes Prettier; git diff --check PASS. The first full run caught and fixed the schema inventory expectation. A concurrent-build rerun hung in the existing video-audit fixture; stopped its worker, verified that file standalone, then reran npm test alone successfully without video changes. Repository-wide npm run format:check reports 8 untouched HEAD files: scripts/verify/verify-settings-window.mjs, src/chat/useTreeActions.ts, test/chat/suggestions-models.test.mjs, test/media/artifact-render.test.mjs, test/media/video-plan.test.mjs, test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs, test/providers/tool-loop.test.mjs, test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs. Left that unrelated formatting outside scope. No browser/live-provider or video-render verification required by this acceptance; fixture checks do not claim model judgement quality or native provider-release evidence. No docs/verification files regenerated. Existing worktree preserved, including existing log-route allowlist cleanup; branch remains master. No staging, commit, push, pull or sync. title: Familiarity, recall and discussions
description:
Spec: docs/familiarity-and-discussion-spec.md. From the 2026-11-15 grilling session. Terms follow GLOSSARY.md.

The tutor's hidden verdict on each learner message (six anchored levels plus confidence) drives a fading running-average familiarity, with no learner corrections and a read-only knowledge map. title: Left-edge peek and Ctrl+Shift+O for New chat
description:
Spec: docs/sidebar-spec.md, section "Implementation Decisions".

## What to build

While Focus mode is on, a strip a few pixels wide along the full left edge of the window reveals the sidebar as an overlay when hovered and hides it when the pointer leaves; it renders nothing visible and covers no page controls. Keyboard focus reaching the strip reveals the sidebar with focus moved into it, and focus leaving hides it and returns focus. No sliding under prefers-reduced-motion. Ctrl+Shift+O runs New chat from any page, including while typing in the composer, prevents the browser default, ignores repeats and IME composition, and does nothing while a tree is already opening. Check by hand once whether Chrome and Firefox give up Ctrl+Shift+O and record the result here.

notes: Done 2026-11-16. Desktop Focus mode now keeps nav.sidebar mounted with data-peek; .sidebar-peek wrapper holds an invisible 6px fixed left-edge button.peek-target (aria-label "Show sidebar overlay", draws nothing) plus the sidebar as a fixed overlay (data-revealed, slides via transform; visibility hidden when closed so it is out of the tab order). Hover on strip reveals; pointer leaving the wrapper hides. Focus on strip reveals and moves focus to the first sidebar button; Shift+Tab back onto the strip or focus to nowhere hides and returns focus to the element focused before; Tab forward into the page hides and leaves focus there (decision: yanking focus back after a forward Tab would fight the user). description:
Spec: docs/media-cost-and-skills-spec.md, section "Piece library".

## What to build

A cut audit may also flag a saved piece the cut uses as poor. The smart model then rewrites that piece, and once it validates the rewrite replaces the library entry and its last-improved time for future videos. The current video keeps the piece it started with; saved videos never change.

- [ ] Invalid rewrite leaves the library entry unchanged

notes: Done 2026-11-15. Remotion cut audits now get libraryPieces (set-piece names the cut code mentions that map to a library id; onPieces returns {name: id} for saved and reused pieces) and may add "pieces":[{name,why}] to either answer (AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS rule; parsed by poorPieces, unknown names/no reason ignored). Each flagged piece (deduped per video) goes to onPoorPiece: the smart model (call) gets PIECE_IMPROVE_INSTRUCTIONS with {name,look,props,roles,source,why} (improvePiece in video-pieces.mjs); the answer must pass cutSource in set-piece mode against the piece own saved roles, then libraryPieces normalises it; store.improvePiece replaces source/props/roles and improved time. Invalid or failed rewrite logs a warning and leaves the entry. data.pieces (current video) never changes. Improvements run alongside rendering; the job awaits them before publishing; they never fail the video. Usage stage "improve". Decisions/tradeoffs: one rewrite attempt, no retry; Retry attempts reusing earlier pieces (prior.pieces) offer no library pieces to the audit since the name->id map is not persisted; "uses" is a word match on the cut code. title: Set-piece step reuses, varies or draws pieces from the library
description:
Spec: docs/media-cost-and-skills-spec.md, section "Piece library".

## What to build

After the plan is saved, each recurring object's look is embedded and its top 5 library matches go to the set-piece step (chat model) with their source. For each object it chooses reuse (as is), variant (derived from one) or new, and writes code only for variants and new pieces. Variants and new pieces are saved when the set pieces are accepted; reused pieces record the new video. A reused piece takes the new video's palette roles. Without an embedder the step gets no matches and draws every piece new; pieces saved without an embedding are embedded when the embedder is next available.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Fake-provider video tests cover reuse, variant and new with the right library entries
- [ ] Reused pieces render with the new video's palette roles
- [ ] No-embedder path draws new pieces and backfills embeddings later
- [ ] npm test passes
notes: Done 2026-11-15. Flow: after the plan is saved, writeCuts calls matches(looks) (videos.mjs) before the set-piece step; with an embedder one embed call covers the looks plus every piece saved without an embedding (store.unembeddedPieces/embedPiece backfill), then store.nearestPieces gives each look its top 5. The set-piece step (server/media/video-pieces.mjs writeSetPieces, chat model) gets library [{name, matches:[{id,name,look,props,roles,source}]}] and PIECES_LIBRARY_NOTE; it answers JSON {pieces:[{name,use:reuse|variant|new,id?,roles?}],code}. pieceChoices validates (every name once, reuse/variant id must be an offered match, roles map into brief roles, reused names not redefined in code). Reused pieces are assembled server-side (assemblePieces): imports merged, each reused piece wrapped as export const <Name> = (() => {...; return <Inner>})() so helpers cannot clash; remapRoles rewrites colors.<savedRole> to the brief role (kept if the brief has it, else the object colorRole, overridable by roles). The assembled module then passes cutSource as before. On acceptance onPieces saves only variant/new entries (with the look vectors from the match step) and usePiece records the new video on reused pieces. No embedder, failed embedder or empty library: no library field, plain module answer, every piece new (old path), saved without embedding, backfilled on the next embedder run. Fix: media.mjs labels stage pieces by startsWith(PIECES_INSTRUCTIONS) since the note is appended. Decisions/tradeoffs: model writes no code for reuse (cost goal) so assembly is server-side; variants are saved as plain new entries (no lineage stored); a second distinct default import from one module in reused sources would be dropped (rare). Evidence (fake providers, fixtures): test/media/video-piece-library.test.mjs (reuse Winner as Champ renders with colors.champ -> kit "champ": palette.leaf, Winner records new video, variant Loser and new Note saved with embeddings, Box not re-used, unembedded Ghost backfilled and offered, stage label pieces; choice validation and import merge unit test); test/media/video-pieces.test.mjs (no-embedder step gets no library). Full suite: npm test stalls at default concurrency (pre-existing, recorded in l0p.6, killed at 900s); node --test --test-concurrency=8 over test/**: 612 tests, 607 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped; check-size passes. Note: I briefly overwrote test/media/video-library.test.mjs and restored it from HEAD.

title: New videos save their set pieces to the piece library
description:
Spec: docs/media-cost-and-skills-spec.md, section "Piece library".

## What to build

Accepted set pieces of a new video are saved to the piece library in SQLite, one entry per exported piece: name, look, props, source, palette roles, look embedding, videos using it, created and last-improved times. Pieces colour only through palette roles. Embeddings come from Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via @huggingface/transformers, downloaded on first use, pinned to one commit and checked against SHA-256 hashes recorded in the repo; a mismatch or failed download refuses the model. The embedder is one injected function from texts to vectors. Vectors are blobs searched with a plain cosine scan returning the top 5. The library starts empty; Remotion pieces only. Without an embedder, pieces are saved without an embedding.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Store tests with a temp database: save pieces, read embeddings, top-5 cosine ranking, videos using a piece
- [ ] Loader unit tests with a fake download: hash mismatch refuses, matching download accepted
- [ ] A video with a fake embedder saves its pieces; without an embedder it still completes
- [ ] npm test passes
notes: Done 2026-11-15. Piece library in SQLite: tables pieces (name, look, props JSON, source, roles JSON, embedding Float32 BLOB, created, improved) and piece_videos (piece, video); store methods savePiece, usePiece, piece, nearestPieces (plain cosine scan, top 5, unembedded pieces skipped). When a new video accepts its set pieces, writeCuts calls onPieces; generateVideo splits the module with libraryPieces (video-plan.mjs) into one self-contained entry per export (imports + private helpers + the export + any other export it draws), props = contract x/y/scale/highlight/state plus destructured names, roles = brief roles used via colors.<role>, embeds the looks with the injected embed function and saves each entry with the video id. Retry with kept set pieces does not save again. Library failures and embedder failures only warn; the video still completes and pieces save without an embedding. Set pieces now colour only through roles: cutSource with names rejects palette hues (palette.amber), kit hex literals and series; cuts are unchanged. Embedder: server/media/embedder.mjs, @huggingface/transformers 4.3.2 (exact), Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 pinned at 751bff37182d3f1213fa05d7196b954e230abad9, q8 files (config, tokenizer, tokenizer_config, onnx/model_quantized) checked against SHA-256 hashes recorded in the module; a failed download or mismatch refuses the model, and a cache with the wrong hash is downloaded again and checked. Downloaded into <data dir>/models on first use; transformers then runs with remote models off. Embedding is awaited before cuts, so the first video waits for the ~23 MB download. Left for l0p.7: backfilling embeddings of pieces saved without one, and the reuse/variant flow.
