title: Manim cut audit
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. A Manim cut renders first; snapshots come from frames of its rendered clip; the audit runs as for Remotion cuts; a changed cut is validated and re-rendered, otherwise the clip is kept; a failed fix falls back.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: Manim cut audited from clip frames; unchanged audit causes no re-render; changed audit re-renders; broken fix falls back.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Manim cuts now render their clip inside writeCuts once written+narrated (clip callback from videos.mjs: manim.render, validateOutput, fps/duration check, copy to public/manim.mp4; manimUnavailable warning moved into the callback). A failed first clip render spends the repair (rewrite with the path-stripped diagnostic, then cutError "Cut N of M") exactly as the render loop did. Then the existing audit runs: snapshots via videoSnapshot of the staged MANIM_COMPONENT wrapper (frames of the rendered clip), MANIM_AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS (new, Python rules), no setPieces, same previous-last-frame sharing. auditFix(raw, brief, sentences, engine): Manim code is trimmed, not cutSource. A fix is checked (write-time check) and rendered to a new clip; public/manim.mp4 is replaced only on success; any failure restores pre-audit code/marks and keeps the old clip. Unchanged audit -> no re-render. playable() now needs audited for both engines (+clip for Manim); phase for a Manim cut 1 after narration is auditing. rewrite() clears cut.clip, and the render loop renders a clip only when missing (after a render-time repair). Decisions: separate Manim audit instructions since the code language differs; clip renders now run concurrently per cut writer instead of in the sequential render loop; repaired Manim cuts are still audited (03j.9 owns merged repair). Evidence (fixture job tests, test/media/manim-audit.test.mjs, 4 pass, real check-only validator): audited from clip-wrapper stills holding the original clip; unchanged -> check,render only; changed -> re-checked, re-rendered, fix saved and its clip used in the MP4; RED fix rejected by validator -> no re-render, original kept; fix render failure -> original code and clip kept. Mutation (skip Manim audit) fails all 4. npm test 475 pass 0 fail; tsc ok; prettier ok; npm run test:render 5 pass.

title: Merged repair counts as the audit
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. A failed cut's repair input holds the error, failed code, set pieces, style brief and the previous cut's last frame when it exists, asking to fix the error and check continuity. A repaired cut skips the cut audit. Metered as video stage 'repair'.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: a failed cut gets one repair call with the previous frame and set pieces, then no audit call; usage stage repair.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. Completed the existing partial implementation in server/media/video-cut.mjs, server/media/video-cuts.mjs and server/http/jobs/media.mjs; added test/media/video-repair.test.mjs.

Repairs append REPAIR_NOTE to the existing Remotion/Manim instructions. Input contains validationError, failedCode (raw failed write or current code for a render failure), styleBrief, cut, previousEndState, Remotion setPieces when present and previousLastFrame. The preceding cut's validated private JPEG is attached when available. Instructions fix the actual error and check continuity against the plan, using the preceding frame as context rather than copying its deviations. A successful validated repair marks the cut audited and makes no further audit model call. Metering remains task video with stage repair.

Decision/tradeoff: repaired and kept cuts still take snapshots to supply continuity frames to following cuts, but skip the audit model call. Repairs wait for the preceding snapshot, never its audit answer; first cuts and missing frames use previousLastFrame=false with no attachment. The existing two-attempt limit, provider/auth failure handling and diagnostic path stripping remain. Overflow output is already discarded by the bounded provider reader, so failedCode is omitted in that case. Manim keeps the existing written-look contract rather than receiving React set-piece source. A render failure can occur after the original audit; its repair receives no second audit.

Acceptance evidence (fixture job tests): a write-validation failure gets exactly one repair carrying the failed code, error, style brief, set pieces and previous frame; repaired code is stored, no separate audit follows, log stage=repair once. Adjacent repaired cuts share a frame of repaired code, and cut 1 works without a predecessor. Render-failure repair sees TypeError with [path]:3:4, failed source and preceding frame, succeeds on its second render and receives no further audit. Focused repair/cuts/audit/Manim tests: 26 pass. npm test run once: 481 pass, 5 skipped, 0 fail. npm run test:render: 5 pass with real sandboxed Remotion, multi-cut, Three.js, overlay and mixed Manim renders. These real renders use fixture model output; no live provider inference or visual-quality judgment was performed. npx tsc --noEmit and scoped Prettier checks pass; git diff --check passes. Full npm run format:check fails only on unchanged src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs; confirmed both fail formatting in HEAD too and preserved them. No browser/E2E check required or run. No docs/verification files regenerated. Git remains unstaged/uncommitted for Ralph.

title: Cut audit for Remotion cuts
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md, ADR 0002. Injectable videoSnapshot renders stills of a staged cut in the render sandbox: end of each narration sentence plus last frame, 960x540, private workspace files cleaned up. Once written and narrated, each cut is snapshotted and audited; all audits run at the same time. One Smart call with images gets code, snapshots, set pieces, style brief, cut plan entry, previous cut's planned end state and pre-audit last frame. It aligns to the plan, may replace emphasis marks, returns no change or full replacement code. Replacement is validated and rendered; on failure the pre-audit cut is used; an audit never fails a video. A cut is playable only after its audit settles. Auditing phase with counts; metered as video stage 'audit'. Cancel stops snapshots and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: audit fix replaces a cut before it is playable; broken fix falls back; audits start together; marks can move; cancel during audit; usage stage audit; phases advance only.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Snapshots: injectable videoSnapshot(cutDir, [{frame,file}], signal) beside videoRender; default sandboxSnapshot runs video-render.mjs stills mode (renderStill JPEG, scale 0.5 = 960x540) in the same bwrap sandbox; frames = each sentence endFrame (clamped to audioFrames) and audioFrames (narration last frame, before the pause fade), minus 1, deduped; server-chosen files in cut-N/out, checked regular/<=2MB/inside out; existing out cleanup removes them. Audit: in writeCuts, each Remotion cut once written+narrated is staged, snapshotted and audited inside its own writer, so audits run concurrently; audit i waits only for cut i-1 pre-audit last frame (shared via per-cut resolvers, resolved null on failure/Manim/kept). One Smart call AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS with images (own stills + previous last frame) and JSON input styleBrief, cut plan entry, previousEndState, setPieces, code, emphasis, snapshots count, previousLastFrame. Answer JSON {"change":false} or {"code","emphasis"?} (auditFix: cutSource validation, marks via exported emphasisMark and sentence < count). Fix accepted only if its snapshot render succeeds; otherwise pre-audit code/marks restored. Any non-abort error (snapshot, provider, parse) settles the audit unchanged; audit never fails a video. cut.audited=true; playable() for Remotion now needs audited; cut.emphasis overrides plan marks in stage (MP4) and live /cuts route. Retry keeps audited flag/marks of kept cuts. Phase auditing (server PHASES, client STEPS/SPAN/label "Auditing cuts", detail "n of N cuts audited"); metered stage audit. Cancel aborts snapshot sandbox and audit call through the job signal. Decisions/tradeoffs: snapshot failure of the original cut skips the audit instead of spending the repair (03j.9 owns merged repair); the fix is checked by its snapshot render, a later full-render failure goes to the existing render repair path, not back to the pre-audit code; Manim cuts skip the audit (03j.10); repaired cuts are still audited until 03j.9; test kits default to a no-still snapshot fake so existing call counts are unchanged. Evidence (fixture job tests, test/media/video-audit.test.mjs, 5 pass): audits in flight together; phase auditing and no cut playable during audit; fix + moved marks saved, staged into the MP4 render and served live; inputs/images (2 stills, cut 2 also gets cut 1 last frame); stage=audit logged twice; snapshots removed; validation-failing and render-failing fixes fall back; cancel during snapshot and during audit -> canceled, no media; phase order via job(); auditFix parsing. Mutation: dropping the audited gate fails 2 tests. npm test 468 pass; tsc ok; prettier ok; npm run test:render 5 pass with real sandbox stills reaching the audit (2 JPEGs).

title: Set pieces
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Each recurring object in the plan gains a look (shape, parts, proportions, size in frame pixels). A new stage between plan and cut writing: one Smart call writes one shared module exporting a component per set piece (position, scale, highlight/state props), validated like cuts, staged into every Remotion cut workspace; cut instructions require using it for recurring objects. Manim cuts receive look descriptions. Two tries; failure reads 'Set pieces: <reason>. Retry keeps the plan.' Retry keeps set pieces that succeeded. New live phase; metered as video stage 'pieces'.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: one pieces call per video before any cut call; module staged into every Remotion cut; Manim cut input carries looks; failure message; Retry reuses pieces; phase order; usage stage pieces.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Plan: recurringObjects[].look optional text (validator rejects blank; PLAN_INSTRUCTIONS asks for shape, parts, proportions, size in frame px). pieceNames(plan): PascalCase component per object with a look, only when the video has a Remotion cut. writeCuts: after the initial persist (plan saved first so Retry keeps it), one Smart call (PIECES_INSTRUCTIONS) writes one module, validated by cutSource(raw, brief, names) (same style/import rules; must export each name; cannot import ./pieces); two tries, repair sees validationError; failure "Set pieces: <reason>. Retry keeps the plan."; provider errors keep their wording. data.pieces saved in video source; Retry passes prior.pieces so succeeded pieces are reused. Remotion cut input gets setPieces source; stage() writes pieces.tsx into every Remotion cut dir; cutSource allows ./pieces for cuts. CUT_INSTRUCTIONS require ./pieces for recurring objects; MANIM_INSTRUCTIONS draw from looks (Manim input carries styleBrief looks, no setPieces). Live phase "pieces" (PHASES, STEPS, label Writing set pieces); live /cuts route returns compiled pieces and the player sandbox resolves ./pieces. Metered stage "pieces" (instructions === PIECES_INSTRUCTIONS). Decisions/tradeoffs: look optional so older saved plans and look-less plans skip the stage (no extra call); pieces run before narration, not in parallel (simpler; cut writers wait for pieces anyway); name collisions after PascalCase not handled. Evidence (fixture job tests, test/media/video-pieces.test.mjs, 4 pass): validator/pieceNames; one pieces call after plan and before any cut, phase=pieces during it, pieces.tsx staged in cut-0/cut-1 not Manim cut-2, setPieces in Remotion inputs, Manim input carries look, live route serves pieces, log stage="pieces" once; pieces fail twice -> named error, 0 cut calls, Retry no plan call, then Retry after a cut failure makes no pieces call; instruction text. Mutation check: removing staging fails test. npm test 463 pass; tsc ok; prettier ok. test:render not run (fixture render plans have no looks; real bundling of ./pieces unverified). Not done: VideoCard FAILURE_REASON does not show Cut/Set pieces errors to the learner (pre-existing, outside this ticket).

title: Continuing cuts and scene-change transitions
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Plan gains per-cut join (continue|scene) and, for scene, transition (fade, slide, wipe, flip, clockWipe, iris, plus direction where it applies); cut 1 is scene; unknown values rejected; old plans read as scene with today's fade. Continuing cut: no exit/entry fade, hard cut. Scene change: @remotion/transitions effect one side at a time (exit over the pause, then entry), never overlapping, same in live player and final MP4 join. Reduced motion uses the short fade. Add @remotion/transitions pinned to the installed Remotion version.
acceptance_criteria: Plan tests accept and reject join/transition values and read old plans as scene; live-player tests cover exit/entry progress per join type and reduced motion; live cut data carries joins.
notes: Implemented 2026-11-15. Plan: cuts take join (continue|scene), transition (fade|slide|wipe|flip|clockWipe|iris), direction (slide/flip: 4 sides; wipe: also diagonals). Validator rejects unknown join/transition/direction, a direction on a non-directional effect, transition on a continue cut, and cut 1 = continue (decision: reject rather than coerce, consistent with 'unknown values rejected'). Missing join/transition reads as scene+fade (old plans). cutJoin() in video-plan.mjs normalises. Timing: cut.timing gains entry (join into the cut; null for cut 1) and exit (join into next cut; last cut fades out as before), replacing transitionIn; kit joinAt() still reads old transitionIn timings. Playback: kit Joined/joinAt used by both CUT_ENTRY (per-cut MP4 render, concat join unchanged) and liveVideo, so live and MP4 match. Exit side plays over the 15-frame pause, entry side over first 15 frames (fade: 8, as before); never overlapping. Decisions: clockWipe/iris have no-op exiting sides in @remotion/transitions, so the outgoing cut plays the entering side reversed; presentation wrapper is constant per cut so the cut never remounts mid-play (idle slide sits 0.01% off by library epsilon). Reduced motion (matchMedia in the player frame) turns every transition into the short fade; continue stays a hard cut. @remotion/transitions pinned 4.0.542. Evidence: node --test video-plan, video-cuts, videos-live, live-player pass (join accept/reject + old plans; joinAt per join type and reduced motion; live slide-out in Thumbnail; every transition renders; live cut data carries entry/exit). npm run test:render 5/5 pass (real sandbox bundles transitions). tsc + vite build OK.

title: Pen for emphasis, with a live pen tip
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Plan and cut instructions say the pen emphasises what the narration is currently about, like a presenter marking a slide, and never draws content. Tools stay circle, underline, arrow, freehand. The overlay draws a pen tip riding the stroke end while a mark draws, then lifting away; hidden under reduced motion. Same in live player and MP4.
acceptance_criteria: Emphasis tests cover tip position along the stroke and its lift, and no tip under reduced motion; prompt tests assert the pen purpose wording.
notes:
Implementation scope: use the existing shared Sketch overlay for live playback and MP4, preserve circle/underline/arrow/freehand and mark timing. Default: a small paper pen with amber nib follows the exact stroke by arc length, then lifts diagonally and fades over 8 frames; reduced motion hides the tip. Arrowheads will draw sequentially with their shaft so one tip can follow the actual revealed stroke (existing independent subpaths reveal simultaneously). Update plan and both Remotion/Manim cut purpose wording. Verify geometry and reduced-motion component behavior, prompt assertions, real sandbox render, final npm test/build/format. Preserve pre-existing media job/repair edits; no staging or commits.
Implementation and focused verification: shared video-kit Sketch now draws a paper pen with amber nib at the exact stroke end, then lifts/fades over 8 frames; all four tools remain. Continuous arrowhead geometry prevents simultaneous subpath reveal. Plan, Remotion cut and Manim cut prompts require emphasis of the current narration like a presenter marking a slide, never content drawing. Focused tests: 7 emphasis tests plus 5 live-player tests passed; 17 plan/cut/Manim regression tests passed. Final npm test: 489 total, 484 passed, 5 opt-in render tests skipped, 0 failures. npm run build passed. Changed-source Prettier and git diff --check passed. Repository format:check reports only existing, unchanged src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs formatting; left untouched. Impeccable detector returned []; existing design sidecar drift left untouched. Native MP4 emphasis test passed pixel checks for tip while drawing and disappearance after lift, with real sandboxed Remotion and fixture-generated code/narration; extracted frames at 6/23/30 visually confirm drawing/lift/absence. Full test:render still finishing mixed Manim case; final evidence follows. No live model generation or browser E2E required/run, no docs/verification artifacts regenerated, no staging/commit.
Final result: all issue acceptance checks passed. npm run test:render passed 5/5 native sandboxed render checks with no skips (146.4 s), including real MP4 pen drawing/lift pixels, Three.js, multi-cut joins and mixed Manim/Remotion. This is actual renderer evidence using fixture generation/narration, not live Claude/Codex generation. Shared overlay component and geometry tests prove current live-player rendering, tip position/lift and reduced-motion hiding; both engine prompts and the plan assert pen purpose. Full npm test/build passed; unchanged unrelated formatting failures documented above. No remaining issue acceptance; no external blocker. Scoped implementation files: server/media/video-kit.tsx, video-plan.mjs, video-cut.mjs (purpose wording only, preserving inherited repair edits), manim-cut.mjs, test/media/video-emphasis.test.mjs and videos-playback.test.mjs. Logs: /tmp/treetutor-03j5-{test,build,render,format}.log; visual frame strip: /tmp/treetutor-03j5-pen-frames.png. Ralph stages/commits after this response.

title: Retry rewrites only failed cuts
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Retry without differentVersion reuses the attempt's saved plan, narration, timing and non-failed cuts, copied into the new attempt workspace (never shared). No plan call; only failed cuts are written again. New attempt keeps ownership, cancel and late-output rules. Cut failure error gains 'Retry keeps the other cuts.' Make a different version still plans fresh.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: after one cut fails, Retry makes no plan call and exactly one cut call, keeps other cuts' code and narration, and publishes; different version plans fresh; cancel and late output still rejected.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Retry (route action retry) on a FAILED video passes the pre-retry row to startVideo -> generateVideo({previous}). If its saved source has a plan, generateVideo copies (fs.cp, never shares) video-work/<id>/<oldAttempt>/cut-i into the new attempt workspace for every cut with timing, keeping timing only if public/narration.mp3 came along (else the copy is removed and the cut is narrated again). No plan call; writeCuts takes kept cuts: code kept for cuts not marked failed, timing kept where copied; only missing/failed code is written and only missing timing narrated. New attempt id unchanged, so ownership, cancel and late-output rules hold. A failed attempt now keeps cut public/ and narration.json (canceled/stopped attempts still discard audio) so Retry can reuse narration. cutError appends "Retry keeps the other cuts.". Make a different version (regenerate, new id) still plans fresh. Decisions: reuse only from status failed (a canceled/interrupted attempt may not have settled its workspace, so it plans fresh); differentVersion in a frozen input does not block reuse (the saved plan is already that version); Manim clips are re-rendered (clip not reused); a failed cut first write gets no error text (merged repair is a later ticket); set pieces not applicable yet. Tests (fixture-level job tests): video-cuts "Retry after a failed cut ..." -> after cut 2 of 3 fails, retry makes 0 plan calls and exactly 1 cut call, keeps cut 1/3 code and timing, 0 new narration, publishes; canceled retry with held late cut output stays canceled, no media; retry after cancel plans fresh; regenerate plans fresh. Updated expectations: videos-narration (calls 8->6), videos-recovery (reordered: malformed plan first, later retries reuse plan, compose==2), media-replies (unmeasured failure moved to cover cut call), error strings. Evidence: node --test test/media/video-cuts.test.mjs 7 pass; npm test 459 pass x4 (one earlier run had an unrelated flake in artifacts-stop diagram 30ms timeout). test:render not run (no render pipeline change).

title: Repair sees the real error; failures name the cut
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Render-failure repair input carries the first diagnostic line with absolute paths removed, instead of the fixed hint. A failed video stores 'Cut N of M: <reason>.' with private paths removed; provider and sign-in failures keep their next-step wording. Two tries per cut unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Job tests: repair input holds the stripped render error and no absolute path; a failed video error reads 'Cut N of M: ...'; provider failures keep existing wording.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. sandboxProcess keeps a bounded copy of stderr (first 64 KiB); firstDiagnostic picks the first line containing "...Error:"/"...Exception:" (or else the first non-empty line), and withoutPaths swaps absolute paths and file:// URLs for [path]. On a render failure the repair input validationError is now withoutPaths(diagnostic ?? message) instead of the fixed hint. When a cut runs out of tries (validation in rewrite, or render), it fails with "Cut N of M: <reason>." (cutError in video-cuts.mjs). Provider, narration, sign-in and Manim-unavailable errors keep their wording. Fix: writeCuts now rethrows signal.reason, because siblings were failing with AbortError (code) and that mapped the error to "Video could not be generated.". Decisions: paths become [path] and are not cut down to the basename (a basename such as /home/<user> would reveal the user); a timeout attaches no diagnostic; "Retry keeps the other cuts." is left for 03j.4. Evidence: node --test test/media (117 pass), npm test 458 pass, npm run test:render 5 pass (real sandbox). Job tests are fixture-level: injected render diagnostic with workspace path -> repair "TypeError: ... at [path]:3:4"; exhausted -> "Cut 2 of 3: ..."; provider failure -> "Video provider failed to generate a composition."

title: Manim cuts checked when written
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Check-only mode of the Manim entry point runs the validator in the render sandbox without rendering. The cut writer calls it straight after a Manim cut is written, using the same write-time repair path as Remotion cuts. Render-time check stays.
acceptance_criteria: Job test: an invalid Manim cut is rejected and repaired before any render call; a valid one renders unchanged; the repair input carries the validator error.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. manim-render.py --check validates staged Cut.py/brief.json only (no Manim import, no render) and prints {"ok":true} or {"error":<real validator/syntax message>}. checkManim (manim-cut.mjs) runs it in the same bwrap sandbox/bindings as renders, 30s budget. writeCuts takes optional check; rewrite() stages a Manim cut and checks it straight after writing; failure spends the repair and validationError carries the message (paths stripped; generic sandbox failure falls back to diagnostic); manimUnavailable and abort stay final. videos.mjs default manim adds check; injected test runtimes without check skip it. Render-time check unchanged. Decisions: check reuses stage() so the sandbox sees the same files as a render; kept Retry cuts are not re-checked (render-time check covers them). Evidence: job tests in test/media/manim-cuts.test.mjs use the real --check script unsandboxed: invalid (RED) runs check,check,render and the repair input matches /RED/; valid runs check,render with Cut.py unchanged; file 7/7 pass. Live sandbox (real bwrap + .venv): valid ok; RED -> named validator error; syntax error -> line number. npm test 476 tests: 471 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

title: Manim validator accepts kit expressions, and both instructions state the rules
description: Spec: docs/video-consistency-spec.md. Manim validator rejects only literal colour/font text (hex, rgb/hsl, common CSS names, non-kit Manim colour constants, non-house fonts), like the fixed Remotion validator; any expression built from kit values passes. Errors name the offending argument. Remotion cut and Manim instructions each gain one rule block mirroring the validator: colour/font literals checked; colours only colors.<role>, palette.<neutral> or series; fonts only fonts.heading/fonts.reading; allowed imports.
acceptance_criteria: Manim validation tests pass loop variables, parameters, t2c, lookups by variable key; foreign hex, RED and non-house fonts still fail with named errors; prompt tests assert the rule block in both instructions.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. manim-render.py validate(): rejects only literal colour/font text in style positions (hex/rgb()/hsl() anywhere; CSS colour names, non-house font strings and f-string parts in color/fill/stroke/font/t2c/t2f/t2g args, set_color*/set_fill/set_stroke args, style dict keys, attribute assignments; Manim colour constants like RED/BLUE_E unless locally bound; colors/palette/fonts constant keys outside the brief). Any other expression passes: loop vars, params, t2c dicts, variable-key lookups, calls. Errors name the argument, e.g. 'font="Arial"', 'RED', "colors['missing']". Import/scene/config/camera/disallowed-call rules unchanged. CUT_INSTRUCTIONS and MANIM_INSTRUCTIONS each gained one 'Validator rules' block. Decisions: Manim block omits series because the Manim kit exports none (adding it was out of scope); all hex literals stay rejected in Manim (stricter than Remotion, matches 'colours only from kit'). Evidence (fixtures, no live render): python3 -I test/media/manim-validation.py 4 tests OK (kit expressions pass, named errors, invalid list incl BLUE_E/rgb/f-string font); node --test test/media/video-pieces.test.mjs test/media/manim-cuts.test.mjs 10/10; npm test 469 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

title: PDFs read by structure
description: PDF attachments are read with pdfjs-dist page by page: visible text becomes text parts; each embedded image covering at least 10% of the page becomes an image part; a page that is one image covering most of the page plus only invisible text is a scan, sent as that image with its hidden OCR text ignored; vector drawings are not rasterised. Image parts then follow D3 (native) or D4 (OCR). Chips summarise delivery (read as text, sent as image, OCR).
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation unit tests with small fixture PDFs: typed text; large figure plus small logo; scanned page with invisible OCR layer; vector-only page; non-vision model path uses OCR.
- Integration: PDF send reaches a fake provider with ordered text and image parts.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Completed 2026-11-14. PDFs are now prepared page by page with pdfjs-dist ^6.5.438 in server/pdf.mjs. Visible operator glyphs become named page text parts, with PDF TextContent restoring whitespace where it matches; invisible and clip-only render modes (3 and 7) are omitted, including saved/restored graphics state. Embedded images drawn over at least 10% of the CropBox become PNG image parts using the decoded original pixels. Transforms, Form XObjects, inline/repeated images, packed grayscale and coloured bitmap stencils are supported. Small/off-page images are skipped. Vector paths are never rasterised; their labels survive, and a page without readable text or qualifying images has an explicit placeholder. Scans naturally yield only their page image with hidden OCR omitted; no separate scan-area heuristic is needed. Malformed/password-protected PDFs refuse preparation with an actionable reason. Original bytes are copied into pdfjs so its worker cannot take away the bytes saved for reopening.

Delivery/storage: server/attachments.mjs sends extracted image parts through the existing native/OCR capability path; non-vision models get OCR text and the existing exact OCR-unavailable refusal. server/http/attachments.mjs retains prepared parts through send/retry and writes derived PNGs beside the original attachment under the conversation folder (owner-only files). Retry reparses the original for the current capability before changing the failed reply; a preparation refusal preserves the saved question/reply and delivery. The existing attachment text column remains the history/compaction source, so no schema change was needed. SSE/GET chip metadata excludes prepared text, parts and image bytes. Original PDFs download unchanged with an inert binary type even for text-only delivery. Deleting the conversation removes originals and derived images through the existing folder lifecycle.

Provider/UI: PDF turns pass ordered text/image parts to all three adapters. Claude stream-json, Codex localImage inputs and OpenAI-compatible content arrays preserve captions/page order; later turns and inherited-context preparation receive text/image names only. Existing text-plus-images callers remain supported. PDF chips identify the PDF and show all applicable read as text / sent as image / OCR labels; mixed OCR still opens the existing accessible explanation popover. Impeccable context and craft guidance applied; detector returned no findings. Existing Astryx components/styles retained.

Routine decisions/tradeoffs: use content-stream order within each page, without geometric column rearrangement. Mixed summaries use comma-separated delivery kinds in the existing field. Reparse on Retry instead of storing another structured representation in SQLite. PNG encoding uses pdfjs's bundled Node canvas factory for embedded pixels only. CMaps, standard fonts, WASM and ICC data resolve from the installed package; worker network fetching and eval are disabled. No application file/page/count limits, smart-model calls, new settings or page rasterisation were added.

Evidence: 25 focused checks passed across PDF preparation, PDF send, existing attachments/OCR, chip components and provider adapters. test/fixtures/pdf holds small deterministic actual PDFs plus a reproducible generator/README: typed text/TJ spacing, large figure plus small logo, full-page scan with deliberately wrong invisible OCR, vectors with/without labels, a four-page ordered document, render-mode restoration, exact 10% and 9.75% boundaries, transformed/off-page images, inline/monochrome/stencil/repeated bitmaps. Tests check actual extracted PNG dimensions and RGB/grayscale/stencil pixels, OCR replacement/refusal with injected recognisers, ordered multipart delivery to a fake provider, all three adapter wire shapes, original downloads, owner-only derived files, hidden-text omission, history/compaction, retry in both capability directions, atomic refusal and conversation cleanup. These are fixtures, not live Claude/Codex or real OCR evidence; this issue requires no new native/browser/render run.

title: OCR fallback for models that cannot read images
description: When the chat model cannot read images, image parts go through tesseract.js OCR on the server and are sent as text. English language data downloads on first use and is cached in the app data directory. The chip shows OCR with an icon whose popover explains OCR can miss handwriting and diagrams and suggests a model that reads images. If OCR cannot start (for example the download fails), the send is refused with: This model can't read images and OCR language data couldn't be downloaded. Retry is possible on the next send.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation unit tests with an injected recogniser: OCR text replaces image parts for non-vision models; vision models skip OCR; OCR-unavailable refusal.
- Component test for the OCR chip popover.
- Manual opt-in real OCR test script documented, not part of npm test.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Completed 2026-11-14. Implemented OCR fallback for PNG/JPEG/WebP attachments when the selected provider does not read images. server/attachments.mjs now accepts readsImages and an injected recogniser, returns only OCR text parts with delivery ocr for non-vision models, and leaves native images/text files alone. OCR startup failures refuse the entire send before messages/files are saved with the required exact error: This model can't read images and OCR language data couldn't be downloaded. Empty OCR has an explicit no-text placeholder; malformed image recognition gives an actionable image-specific refusal.

Runtime: server/ocr.mjs uses tesseract.js ^7.0.0, lazy English data under <app data directory>/ocr, one worker per app, serial recognition jobs to protect the worker image buffer, failed-start reset and termination so the next send retries, and app shutdown cleanup. Starts the worker with no language then reinitializes English so a failed language download leaves a worker that can be terminated; errorHandler prevents the library throwing an uncaught failure. No OCR/download on native image or text-only turns. server/http/attachments.mjs holds upload/retry preparation to keep send.mjs below the existing 500-line ceiling. Retry prepares original images for the current capability and saves the new delivery/text only after preparation succeeds; refused retries preserve the failed reply. The conversation is active throughout OCR; a second send is refused and Stop prevents later persistence. Original OCR images still open inline through the existing sandboxed asset route. History and compaction receive recognized text, never an image payload for a non-vision model.

UI: src/chat/Attachments.tsx shows Image · OCR and a DocumentMagnifyingGlass icon opening the existing Astryx Popover. Copy explains recognized text can miss handwriting and diagrams and recommends an image-reading model such as Claude or Codex. Help is a separate named button beside the attachment link, avoiding nested interactive controls. Existing Paperback styling/components retained; no extra CSS or UI dependency.

Decisions/tradeoffs: reuse the provider readsImages capability from D3 (including the existing per-endpoint Accepts images setting); English only, no smart model or added provider calls. Reprepare original images on Retry to follow the current capability rather than resend stale image parts; this can repeat OCR work on a retry. One queued worker saves memory at the cost of serial OCR across simultaneous image sends; text/native image calls remain independent. Opt-in real OCR uses a fresh temporary data directory so it proves a first download without modifying the user's app data.

Evidence: test/http/ocr-preparation.test.mjs unit tests inject recognisers for all three image types, native/text bypass, empty OCR, exact unavailable refusal and malformed-image refusal. test/chat/attachments.test.mjs component checks OCR label/icon, separate link/button, popup copy, expanded state and Escape dismissal. test/http/attachments.test.mjs retains native image, storage/history/compaction, atomic refusal and asset coverage with injected OCR unavailable. test/http/ocr-send.test.mjs uses a fake provider/recogniser for atomic multi-file refusal, next-send recovery, OCR text-only payload, history/compaction, original image asset, failed-reply preservation on refused Retry, capability changes in both directions on Retry, shutdown cleanup and Stop/duplicate-send handling while OCR waits. These HTTP/component checks are fixtures, not live model evidence.

Real native OCR: npm run test:ocr passed against tesseract.js 7.0.0. scripts/test-ocr.mjs first received a forced HTTP 503 language download refusal, then the same recogniser retried via the default CDN and recognized Binary heaps from test/fixtures/ocr.png. English eng.traineddata was cached under /tmp/treetutor-real-ocr-brLJK4/ocr. A fresh worker with language downloads unavailable recognized the fixture twice from that cache with zero language requests. This script is documented in docs/agents/testing.md, requires explicit opt-in, and is excluded from npm test; direct execution without the opt-in flag confirms it skips.

Final gates: npm test ran once: 450 tests, 445 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped. npm run build passed (includes tsc --noEmit); check-size and git diff --check passed. Prettier passes on all changed code; Impeccable detector returned no issues for Attachments.tsx. Global npm run format:check reports two pre-existing unchanged files (src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs); both also fail formatting when read from HEAD, left untouched to preserve scope. Build retains the existing large-chunk warnings. No browser verify, live Claude/Codex calls or video-render tests were required or run; no docs/verification files regenerated. Git staging/commit/push left to Ralph as requested.

title: Images to models that read them
description: Image attachments (PNG, JPEG, WebP) are sent natively: Codex and Claude using the shapes from D1, custom endpoints as image_url data URLs when the model's new Accepts images switch (endpoint settings, default off) is on. Custom endpoints send an image only on the turn it was attached; history turns replace it with [image: name]. Chips show sent as image. Until D4, an image for a model that cannot read images is refused with the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provider adapter tests with existing fakes: image parts shaped per provider; custom endpoint history placeholder.
- Store and settings tests for the Accepts images flag.
- Integration: refusal when the model cannot read images.
- Component test for the Accepts images switch and chip label.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Done 2026-11-14. Server: server/attachments.mjs prepares PNG/JPEG/WebP (IMAGE_TYPES, by media type) as delivery 'image' with stored text "[image: name]", so history (tutorContext) and compaction see only the placeholder; other image types (e.g. GIF) are still refused as unsupported. send.mjs: imageRefusal() refuses before anything is saved (new send: after preparation, before files are written; retry: before the failed reply is discarded) with "<name>: this chat model can't read images. Choose Claude, Codex or a custom endpoint with Accepts images on, then send again." (until D4/OCR). This turn's images go to the adapter as tree.images [{name,type,path}] (stored file path); prompt text still includes the [image: name] line. Adapters: Claude/Codex readsImages = true; Claude adds --input-format stream-json on image turns and writes one {type:'user',message:{role:'user',content:[text, image base64 blocks]}} line, text turns unchanged; Codex appends { type:'localImage', path } after the text item; custom endpoints send the last user message as [{type:'text'}, {type:'image_url', image_url:{url:'data:<type>;base64,...'}}] only on the attaching turn, history turns are plain text with [image: name]. Endpoint adapter readsImages = saved acceptsImages. Endpoint file entries gain optional acceptsImages (default false; add/edit take a boolean, edit without the field keeps it, legacy save keeps it; list() always reports it; toggling replaces the adapter like other setting changes). Asset route serves image deliveries inline with their image type (still CSP sandbox + nosniff). Client: Accepts images Switch in the endpoint add/edit form; chips show "Image · sent as image" with a photo icon (pending and message chips). check-size forced a move: endpoint settings validators (settings, readOwned, lastTest, endpointName, EndpointError) moved verbatim to server/providers/endpointSettings.mjs; openai.mjs re-exports EndpointError.
Decision/tradeoff: Accepts images is per endpoint (applies to every model on it), not per model, because endpoint settings list no models and the model is resolved lazily after preparation; per-model would need a model list in settings. Upgrade path: store a model id list instead of a boolean if mixed vision/non-vision endpoints become common.
Evidence (fixtures/fakes, no live provider this ticket; D1 shapes were verified live on TreeTutor-9lj.1): test/providers/images.test.mjs (Claude launcher fake: stream-json args + base64 block, text turn plain; Codex protocol fixture: localImage after text; fake OpenAI server: image_url data URL on this turn, history placeholder, acceptsImages default off/persist/edit keep/off). test/providers/endpoints.test.mjs (settings route saves and clears acceptsImages; list fixtures updated). test/http/attachments.test.mjs (prep unit for png/jpeg/webp; integration: refusal for non-reading model with nothing saved, image path passed to a reading model, later turn has no images and [image: red.png] in history, asset served inline image/png sandboxed). test/shell/endpoint-settings.test.mjs (switch default off, sent on add, shown and sent on edit). test/chat/attachments.test.mjs (image chip "Image · sent as image"). npm test: 444 tests, 439 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped. tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build passes; prettier clean on changed files.

title: Text-file attachments end to end
description: Tracer bullet for attachments. The question box accepts files by paperclip, paste and drop, showing pending chips with remove buttons. Send accepts multipart form data (JSON body still works); files are saved under the app data directory with an additive attachments table and served back through a conversation-scoped asset route with a safe content type and Content-Disposition. Text files are prepared as text with a file-name header and sent to every provider. Message chips show name, type and read as text. Attachments delete with their conversation. Compaction receives attachment text. Unsupported types are refused before sending. An attachment-only first question titles from the attachment text, or the file name.
acceptance_criteria:
- Preparation module unit tests for text files.
- Integration: multipart send stores and delivers text to a fake provider; JSON send unchanged; asset route headers; delete with conversation removes rows and files; unsupported type refused; compaction prompt includes attachment text; attachment-only title.
- Component tests: composer paperclip, paste and drop feed one handler; pending chips removable; message chip label.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes:
Done 2026-11-14. Server: server/attachments.mjs prepareAttachment({name,type,bytes}) -> {delivery:'text', parts:[{text:'[Attached file: name]\n...'}]}, refuses images/PDF (until their tickets) and non-UTF-8 or NUL content with "<name>: this file type can't be attached. Attach a plain-text file."; withAttachments(text, attachments) joins question + prepared text. app.mjs parses multipart/form-data (Request.formData, no new dependency) only for POST /api/trees/:id/messages (fields text, theme JSON, files); JSON body unchanged, CSRF still required. send.mjs prepares every file before saving anything (one bad file refuses the send, nothing stored), writes files to <data dir>/attachments/<conversation>/<attachment id> (0600), saves the message then rows in the additive attachments table (id, conversation, message, name, type, size, delivery, text, created; FK to messages). Provider prompt = withAttachments(question, attachments) for every provider (no adapter change needed for text); history (tutorContext) and compaction (compactionMessages) fold attachment text into the learner message; retry resends the saved attachments. Asset route GET /api/trees/:conv/attachments/:id: looked up by conversation+id, text/plain; charset=utf-8, Content-Disposition inline with ASCII filename + filename*, CSP "sandbox; default-src 'none'", nosniff. GET tree and the saved SSE event omit prepared text. Delete removes rows in the transaction and the conversation folder after commit. Attachment-only first question: placeholder title = file names, title job reads the attachment text (capped 4000 chars, starts with the file name header). Client: src/chat/Attachments.tsx (AttachButton paperclip + hidden file input, PendingAttachments drawer chips with remove, MessageAttachments chips linking to the asset route with "Text file · read as text"); paste and drop use the Astryx ChatComposerInput onFiles prop, so all three feed one add(); both the first-question and focused composers; pending files kept per conversation in useChatState like drafts and moved with the first question; a Send button appears for files with an empty draft; useReplyStream sends FormData when files are pending.
Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) Prepared text stored in the attachments.text column so history/compaction never re-read or re-extract files (later PDF/OCR); deviation from the spec's column list, additive. (2) Text detection by content (valid UTF-8, no NUL) rather than media type, since code files arrive with empty or wrong types (.ts = video/mp2t). (3) Client relies on the server refusal for unsupported types (shown as the send error, before any provider call or save) instead of duplicating the rule in the browser. (4) shortcut: attachment folders removed after commit (crash in between leaves files); files buffered in memory during upload.
Evidence (fixtures, fake providers, no live provider): test/http/attachments.test.mjs (preparation unit tests; integration: JSON send unchanged, unsupported refused with nothing saved, multipart stores row+file and delivers text to fake provider, client JSON omits text, history carries text, compaction prompt includes text, asset headers + cross-conversation 404, attachment-only title placeholder and quick title, delete removes rows+folder). test/chat/attachments.test.mjs (paperclip/paste/drop feed one handler, chips removable, files-only Send, message chip label/link). Updated test/store/preview.test.mjs table list and chat-states fixtures. npm test: 440 tests, 435 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped (an earlier full run had one timing flake in visual-detach that passed alone twice and on the rerun). tsc --noEmit clean; npm run build passes; prettier clean on changed files (format:check flags pre-existing src/media/VisualFrame.tsx and test/media/visual-ask.test.mjs, untouched).

Record the shapes, versions and any limits as a comment and in the epic's Decisions so far. No product code.

comments.author: Thomastienn
comments.text:
D1 image input shapes — verified LIVE 2026-11-14 (red 64x64 PNG, both models answered "Red").

Versions: codex-cli 0.167.2 (app-server), Claude Code 2.1.325.

Codex app-server (schema from `codex app-server generate-ts`, v2/UserInput.ts):
- turn/start input: [{ type: 'text', text, text_elements: [] }, { type: 'localImage', path: '/abs/file.png' }]
- optional `detail`: 'auto' | 'low' | 'high' | 'original'.
- Alternative { type: 'image', url: 'data:image/png;base64,...' } also works (or fileId).
- Live: localImage with path outside thread cwd works under sandbox 'read-only', approvalPolicy 'never', shell tool disabled (app-server reads the file itself, not the model's tools).

Claude CLI (current -p invocation + `--input-format stream-json`):
- stdin one JSON line: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"..."},{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":"image/png","data":"<b64>"}}]}}
- Live with -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --max-turns 1 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands --system-prompt ... --session-id ...: success, partial stream events still emitted.
- A later plain-text `--resume <session>` turn (no --input-format) still sees the image ("Red"), so only image turns need stream-json input.

Limits: not probed; provider-side limits apply (Anthropic API documents ~5 MB per base64 image, 8000 px max side). Per spec, no app caps; surface provider errors.
Decision: Codex uses localImage with the stored attachment path (no base64 copy); Claude sends base64 image blocks via --input-format stream-json on turns with images, plain text stdin otherwise.

title: Step-through helper and visual text rules
description: The sandbox injects a small shared step-through helper before the fragment: the fragment declares steps, the helper renders previous, next and Step n of m in house style, wires Enter, Space and arrow keys, and animates between states with d3 or CSS transitions, skipping animation under prefers-reduced-motion. No network or app messaging. The visual prompt asks for the helper when an idea has stages, forbids explanatory paragraphs inside the fragment, and requires result lines in primary text at reading size; predict-then-reveal contract kept.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests in jsdom: steps run in order; controls and indicator update; keys work; reduced motion skips transitions; first and last step bounds.
- Visual prompt unit tests: step helper and text rules present; predict-then-reveal kept.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. src/media/stepThrough.ts: stepThrough(root, steps, duration=300) installed as frame global in sandbox.ts (before any fragment render). Renders Previous / Step n of m (aria-live) / Next after root in .tt-steps group, styled in sandbox.html like summary chips (zero-specificity :where). Each step fn gets {index,duration}; sets --step-duration on root; duration 0 on first render and under prefers-reduced-motion. Enter/Space handled on keydown with preventDefault (plus Space keyup preventDefault) so one step per press; arrows on the group; focus moves off a disabled bound button. No messaging/network. Prompt visual.md: prefer helper for staged ideas, no own step controls, no explanatory paragraphs (predict-then-reveal answer excepted), labels inside graphic, result lines primary text at reading size; predict-then-reveal paragraph unchanged. Decision: helper places controls after root rather than inside, so fragments own root content; tradeoff: root must be an HTML element (not inside SVG). Tests: test/media/step-through.test.mjs (jsdom unit, 4) + prompt test in visuals-prompts.test.mjs. npm test 431 pass/0 fail/5 skipped (one visual-detach timing flake on first run, passed 3/3 alone and on full rerun); npm run build ok. title: Origin strip in child conversations
description: Every child focused chat shows an origin strip above the thread: the parent's address chip in branch family ink, the source (passage text, suggested term or visual title) and the learner's first question in full. notes: Done: src/chat/OriginStrip.tsx above the thread in every child FocusedChat (section aria-label 'Conversation origin', family ink via inkStyle(child ink)). title: Model-written conversation titles
description: When a conversation's first learner message is saved and its title is unrenamed, a quick thinking title job runs: a root reads the question, a child reads its inherited context and question. Output is a plain title of about 60 characters at most, in the question's language. The placeholder (question cut at 200 characters) shows at once for roots and children; the job replaces it only if still unrenamed. Unset model or failure keeps the placeholder and logs a warning. Metered as quick thinking usage. Delivered through the existing tree state refresh.
acceptance_criteria:
- Title prompt builder unit tests: root and child inputs.
- Integration with a fake quick thinking provider: placeholder saved, then replaced; rename during the job wins; unset model and failed or empty result keep the placeholder with no learner-facing error; usage recorded as a quick thinking task.
- npm test passes.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. server/http/jobs/title.mjs: titlePrompt (root {question}; child {inheritedContext:{snapshot,selectedPassage},question}), cleanTitle (one plain line, quotes/markdown stripped, <=60 chars at word boundary), titleJobs.startTitle: detached quick thinking call (no thread), waits for a child compaction, metered as usage task "title", store.retitle only WHERE title_renamed=0. send.mjs starts it on the first non-retry learner message of an unrenamed conversation; placeholder (question cut at 200; child = branch question) is saved at once by existing code. /api/state exposes titling ids; useLearningTrees adds them to activeKey so the existing state refresh polls until the title lands. app.stop aborts and settled() awaits title jobs. Schema: usage_events rebuilt once to allow task title (rows/indexes kept); Usage dashboard label "Conversation titles". Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) "unset model" = no quick thinking model pinned in the active profile; then no call, one WARN title log (no fallback to the chat provider, unlike compaction) so titles never silently spend chat-model tokens. (2) Failures, invalid selection, non-completed or empty output keep the placeholder, WARN log with redacted cause, nothing learner-facing. (3) New usage task "title" rather than reusing suggestions/compaction so the dashboard stays truthful; costs a one-time table rebuild. Evidence (fixtures, no live provider): test/http/titles.test.mjs (prompt unit tests root/child, cleanTitle, integration with fake quick provider: unset keeps placeholder + warning, replaced title, usage task title claude/quick-model 7/3, only first message titles, rename during job wins, failed and empty keep placeholder, child prompt carries inherited context; upgrade test for old usage table). Updated tests for the new extra call/warning: logging, suggestions-models daily usage, typed-effort, manim-cuts (media-only warnings). npm test: 425 tests, 420 pass, 0 fail; tsc --noEmit clean; prettier clean.

title: Empty first run
description: A fresh database creates the profiles tables empty with no active profile, and new learning trees get no default provider (not codex). The learner can open the app and create learning trees; Send is refused with a stable error the client shows as Choose a chat model in Settings with an Open Settings action. Settings shows Not set for every role without a model. Creating the first profile makes it active. Existing databases keep their Default profile and choices.
acceptance_criteria:
- Store tests: fresh database has no profiles and no active profile; old role rows still seed Default once; first created profile becomes active; tree creation with no default has null provider and model.
- Integration: send with no chat model returns the stable error; quick thinking and smart jobs skip without errors when unset.
- Component tests: Send gate message with Open Settings; Not set labels in Settings.
- Upgrade test with an existing database shows no change.
- npm test and npm run build pass.
notes: Done 2026-11-14. Fresh DB: profiles tables empty, profileRow() null, profiles() {active:null}; trees.provider nullable, store.create() default null provider/model; first createProfile becomes active (starts empty when no source). main.mjs passes defaultProvider null on a fresh DB (store.assumesProvider = trees.provider NOT NULL), so the unset chat role has no provider; POST /api/trees with no default makes a null-provider tree; send/retry refuse with 409 {error:"Choose a chat model in Settings.", code:"chat_model_unset"}. Smart resolving to no provider skips visual/video requests (reply completes, no artifact). Client: FirstQuestion shows "Choose a chat model in Settings" + Open Settings; Chat/Smart settings show Not set; composer model label Not set; profile actions hidden with no active profile. Decisions/tradeoffs: (1) every pre-existing database seeds Default (not only those with saved role rows) because its trees.provider is NOT NULL and its learners relied on the assumed provider: existing installs unchanged. (2) Saving a role before any profile exists creates and activates "Default" so the learner can pick a chat model straight from Settings. (3) Quick thinking unset keeps falling back to the conversation provider default (existing behaviour); Not set labels only on chat and smart. title: Manim cuts
description:
## What to build
The plan may mark a math cut (equations, transforms, graphs) for Manim. The smart model writes Python scene code using a Manim house kit (dark-paper ground, palette, Archivo and Literata, margins, subtitle space). Manim renders it inside the bubblewrap sandbox to a 1080p30 clip placed on the cut timeline. If Manim is unusable, the video fails with a clear message and a log warning; chat and visuals keep working. See the spec's Manim cuts section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [x] Integration test with a fake Manim engine: a plan with a math cut routes it to Manim and places its clip in order.
- [x] Integration test: an unusable Manim fails the video with a clear message.
- [x] npm run test:render passes with a real Manim cut.
- [x] npm test passes.
notes:
Verified 2026-11-14. All four acceptance criteria pass.

Implementation and decisions: the smart plan can choose manim for equations/transforms/graphs alongside Remotion. Manim cuts receive an isolated Python writing prompt with only their style brief, own cut and previous planned end state. The Python house kit supplies dark-paper ground, assigned palette roles, Archivo/Literata, shared pixel coordinates/margins and measured narration timing. MathTex remains LaTeX glyphs. Existing Fontsource WOFF assets are decompressed to TTF with the Python standard library inside the sandbox because Pango silently substituted fonts when given WOFF on this machine; no package or font download was added. The house kit pads the end state through the fixed pause, using cut_duration because Manim owns Scene.duration for each animation.

AST validation runs inside bubblewrap before generated Python executes. It checks named kit imports, the Cut(HouseScene) contract, palette/font references and common style setters/dictionaries, and rejects external imports/resources and house-config changes. Bubblewrap remains the security boundary: shared rendering isolation masks home and the app data root, clears environment and disables network, while unmasking only the read-only project Python environment, its exact uv interpreter installation and trusted runner. Python runs with -I -B. Child termination, cancellation and finite render budgets reuse the existing sandbox process handling. Private renderer diagnostics are drained rather than sent to chat or the terminal.

A raw Manim 1080p30 clip is validated and saved privately as cut-N/public/manim.mp4. A server-owned OffthreadVideo component places it inside the existing Remotion wrapper, which clips content to the margins and reserves the 120px subtitle band, then applies the same narration, subtitles and eased transitions. The existing sandboxed join preserves mixed-engine plan order. Ordered private cut metadata retains engine, code, timing, status and clip; public API/tutor history still receive metadata only. Existing videos are untouched. Bad scene code/rendering uses the existing two writing attempts for that cut only, reusing narration. An unavailable runtime fails without retry, with npm start repair guidance and one WARN video terminal entry through the new injected log seam. No shared logger existed yet; this issue adds only the required warning seam, leaving broader logging to its own issue. Chat and inline visuals never probe/import Python.

Evidence:
- test/media/manim-cuts.test.mjs: five passing checks. Cheap Python AST unit checks accept kit math and reject external imports, malformed classes, off-brief colors/fonts, style dictionaries, aliases and house mutations without importing Manim. In-process createApp tests with fake providers/TTS/Manim render engine place math between two Remotion cuts, preserve measured 75-frame timing and ordered clip metadata, record plan/cut/retry usage, and rewrite only the failed math cut. Detection/runtime unavailability gives one clear failure/warning, no playable media or automatic retry, then normal chat and a newly generated inline visual both complete. These are explicitly fixtures, not native inference evidence.
- npm run test:render: PASS, 4 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped (80.33s). Real bubblewrap Remotion, three-cut join and Three.js checks remain passing. New mixed Remotion/Manim check renders actual LaTeX transforms plus Archivo and Literata from bundled fonts, saves the raw math clip at 1920x1080/30fps for 2.5 seconds and joined narrated MP4 at 1920x1080/30fps for 5 seconds with AAC. Pixel probes prove math appears in the second timeline position, raw math leaves the subtitle band empty, wrapper subtitles appear and the final pause fades to dark paper. The native Python sandbox probe denies home/app-data/repository reads, runtime/outside/narration writes and outbound network; only its workspace is writable and no host environment variables pass through. Fixed source and prerecorded tone narration are fixtures, while both renderers, fonts, LaTeX and sandbox evidence are native.
- Final focused native Manim rerun after disabling Python bytecode: PASS (25.58s). One extracted fixture frame was inspected; house text, equation, spacing and subtitles fit. No browser check claimed.
- Full-suite regression found and fixed: legacy fixtures recognize private video generation by the Remotion wording. The plan now accurately says narrated Remotion video with optional Manim math cuts, preserving that existing contract. All 24 checks in affected playback/jobs/requests/tag/deletion/usage files pass (20 passed, 4 opt-in native skips). Initial full run was stopped after diagnosing its hung playback fixture; this was repaired, not waived.
- Final npm test: PASS, 367 total, 363 passed, 4 opt-in native renders skipped (all passed separately), 0 failed (12.66s).
- npm run format:check, ruff format --check for the new Python files, 500-line JS/TS/CSS gate and git diff --check: PASS. Impeccable detector: [].

Limits: no live model or Edge TTS service requests, browser/E2E run, new live player or cursor/sketch work. Live playback remains its separate dependent feature; this issue provides the ordered clip and the MP4 timeline. No build required by testing.md: no TSX/build files changed; actual generated TSX wrappers compiled during native renders. No docs/verification files regenerated. Current master branch preserved; existing .beads/issues.jsonl changes retained. Files: server/app.mjs; server/http/jobs/media.mjs; server/media/{video-plan,video-cuts,videos,video-sandbox,manim-cut}.mjs; server/media/{manim-kit,manim-render}.py; test/media/{video-plan,videos-playback,manim-cuts}.test.mjs; test/media/manim-validation.py; test/support/video-kit.mjs; required local Beads export/progress. Nothing staged, committed, pushed, pulled or remotely synced. Ralph owns the pending implementation commit.

title: Manim install on first run
description:
## What to build
npm start creates a project-local Python environment with uv on first run and installs a pinned Manim, beside the npm install step. If Cairo/Pango headers or LaTeX are missing, startup stops with the exact apt or brew command. A usable Manim is detected for later video jobs. Chat and visuals do not depend on it. See the spec's Manim cuts section.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Unit test: the dependency check reports the exact install command for missing Cairo/Pango or LaTeX, and passes when present (injected probes).
- [ ] Running npm start on this machine creates the environment and reports Manim ready.
- [ ] .venv/ is git-ignored.
- [ ] npm test passes.
notes: Implementation decisions: pin Manim 0.22.1 (verified against PyPI/current official install guide); uv provisions Python 3.12 into git-ignored project .venv, avoiding the system Python 3.14 dependency surface. Existing environments are repaired in place, never removed. Missing Cairo/Pango/pkg-config or latex/dvisvgm stops launcher with exact apt/Homebrew commands; system packages are never auto-installed. Missing uv gives official install command. Exported detectManim returns availability, pinned version and absolute Python path without throwing; no Python dependency added to chat/visual imports. Existing built app remains accessible via node server/main.mjs during setup repair. Scope includes launcher, setup/detection modules, README, ignore rule, cheapest unit tests and existing launcher fixtures; no cut rendering implementation in this issue. Initial native npm start created .venv with CPython 3.12.12, built pycairo/ManimPango, installed Manim 0.22.1 and printed Manim ready. App responded HTTP 200 on 127.0.0.1:40725 using isolated temporary data; native Text and MathTex creation passed (Cairo/Pango plus LaTeX/dvisvgm). Final verification: focused node --test test/scripts/manim.test.mjs test/http/launcher.test.mjs passed 8/8. npm test ran once at the end: 361 total, 358 passed, 3 opt-in render tests skipped, 0 failed (12.75s). npm run format:check and git diff --check passed. A second native npm start reused Manim without installation and returned HTTP 200; both native app processes stopped afterward. git check-ignore .venv/bin/python confirmed exclusion. No docs/verification files regenerated. Linux native provisioning/text/math and restart evidence is real, while missing-dependency/macOS checks and launcher build use explicitly labelled fixtures. No browser or video render tests: this task changes installation/detection, not rendering. Existing node_modules were present during native npm start, so this is a fresh Python environment check, not a clean npm dependency installation claim. Files: .gitignore, README.md, scripts/start.mjs, scripts/manim-setup.mjs, server/media/manim.mjs, test/scripts/manim.test.mjs, test/http/launcher.test.mjs, and required local Beads export/progress.
