title: Extract concepts, topics and links from the suggestion call
description:
## What to build

Extend the same suggestion call to return the reply's concepts, their topics (a concept can belong to several) and concept links ("related" or "builds on"). Store them in one knowledge graph across all learning trees, kept locally. Send the existing concept names of the reply's topics and reuse a matching concept rather than creating a duplicate. No embedding model. Settings warns when a call's concept-name list exceeds about 2k tokens. Spec stories 7, 43–46, 53, 55–56.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- One suggestion call per reply returns suggestions and graph data together; no extra model call.
- Concepts, topics, memberships and links are stored globally and survive restart.
- A concept met under a matching name in another learning tree is reused, not duplicated.
- The Settings warning appears when the name list passes the threshold.
- Integration tests over the fake provider CLIs cover extraction, reuse across trees and the warning.
notes: Implemented 2026-11-10. Suggestion call prompt now also returns concepts (name, topics[]) and links (from,to,kind related|builds on); one call, no extra model call. Global SQLite tables concepts/topics (UNIQUE NOCASE names), concept_topics, concept_links (additive, survive restart). GET /api/graph exposes {topics,concepts,links}. Decision: the reply topics are unknown before the call, so v1 sends every topic with its concept names (knownConcepts) and tells the model to reuse known names; server also reuses case-insensitive name matches. Tradeoff: list grows with the whole graph, which the warning flags (embedding pre-filter is 5ut.11). Each call records nameTokens (~chars/4 shortcut); /api/state.conceptNameTokens = latest; Settings shows a warning Banner above 2000. Invalid concepts (no topic/empty name) and links (unknown kind, missing end, self) are dropped without failing suggestions. Evidence: npm test 139/139 pass (fixture-backed: test/suggestions.test.mjs graph extraction, restart, cross-tree reuse on Claude then Codex, isolation, warning); npm run build + astryx doctor --built dist pass (0 fail); live check: app on seeded temp data dir with nameTokens 2600 rendered the Settings warning in the browser. Evidence/familiarity left to 5ut.7.

title: Choose the suggestion model and switch suggestions off
description:
## What to build

Settings lets the learner pin one suggestion model instead of the per-provider default, and switch automatic suggestions off. Only signed-in subscription providers are offered; never substitute API-key access. Spec stories 22, 25.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pinned model is used for new suggestion calls across conversations; unpinning restores the per-provider default.
- With suggestions off, saved replies start no suggestion call; existing saved suggestions stay visible.
- A signed-out provider is not offered as a working choice.
- Integration tests cover pinned, default and off.
notes:
Implemented and verified 2026-11-10.

Decisions/tradeoffs:
- Persist one global {enabled, model: {provider, model}|null} in an additive SQLite suggestion_settings table. Defaults: enabled, unpinned. Server-side storage makes the setting apply to new suggestion calls across conversations and survive app/browser restart, without changing tutor model choices.
- Read settings when a completed reply is saved. Off prevents new suggestion records/calls; existing saved suggestions stay visible. Calls already started finish and save their usage/results. Re-enabling never backfills. This avoids discarding paid in-flight results.
- Unset model follows the conversation's existing subscription default (Claude Haiku; catalog Luna for Codex). A pin captures one subscription provider/model across conversations, including conversations whose tutor uses another provider. Unpin restores the per-provider default.
- Settings offers only signed-in Claude/Codex catalog entries. Save and inference both validate subscription access; unavailable/stale pins remain saved, show disabled in Settings with sign-in/unpin guidance, and fail visibly through the existing Suggestions unavailable state. No provider substitution and no custom/API-key fallback. A custom-endpoint conversation must explicitly pin a subscription model to get suggestions.
- Settings uses existing Astryx Switch/Selector primitives with loading, saving, error, refresh and unavailable states. Existing saved suggestions/rendering and manual passage selection remain unchanged. Partial setting updates preserve the other value, including while model validation awaits.

Evidence:
- test/suggestions.test.mjs: 15/15 passed. Three added HTTP integration checks use real Store, app server and Claude/Codex adapters over fake provider CLIs (plus real OpenAI adapter over fake HTTP endpoint): both provider pins, cross-conversation use, persistence/restart, unpin to Haiku/Luna, tutor choice unchanged, off with in-flight calls, saved suggestions preserved, no backfill, signed-out provider omitted, invalid/missing/custom model rejection, CSRF, stale pin with no provider/API fallback, off/unpin while signed out, and custom endpoint used only for its explicit tutor request.
- Extended protocol fixture accepts explicitly requested pin models while retaining cheap-model verification by default. Updated the existing preview schema assertion for the additive settings table; preview checks pass.
- npm test: 148/148 passed, 0 failed (38.6s; /tmp/treetutor-5ut5-tests.log). npm run build: TypeScript and Vite production build passed.
- npx astryx doctor --built dist: 20 pass, 0 fail; 2 existing theme/font warnings. Impeccable detector: [] for changed UI sources. git diff --check passed.
- Vite-loaded Settings component in jsdom: enabled state loaded, real switch click issued {enabled:false} and displayed off. This was a component smoke check with fixture API data, not browser/E2E or native provider inference. Required provider behavior above is fixture integration evidence; no new live Claude/Codex inference was claimed.
- Kept current branch and unrelated work. No staging, commit, push or remote sync. Ralph's implementation commit remains pending.

title: Branch from an underline or highlight through the passage textbox
description:
## What to build

Clicking or pressing Enter on an underline, or highlighting any reply text, opens a small empty textbox above that passage. An empty box cannot be sent; Enter sends, Escape closes. Sending uses the existing branch-creation flow with the passage and the learner's prompt, so a short prompt such as "explain" works. The suggestion becomes explored once the child is saved: its underline turns solid and activating it opens the existing child. A highlight overlapping an underline wins. A failed branch keeps the typed prompt. Works at every nesting depth. Spec stories 28–42.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Underline and highlight both open the same empty textbox above the passage; empty input cannot be sent.
- Sending creates one child with the exact passage and inherited context; it opens in the chat panel as any branch does.
- The explored underline is solid; activating it opens that child, with no duplicate created.
- Manually highlighting the same text can still create a second branch.
- Escape closes the box and returns focus; a failed branch keeps the prompt for retry.
- The whole flow works from the keyboard, including in a grandchild.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. Server: branching with suggestion:true stores child id on the matching ready passage (same transaction as the child; Store.branch); a live child is never overwritten; tree() drops refs to deleted children so the underline reads unexplored again. Manual branches never mark. Client: underlineRanges keeps child; explored underlines render u.suggestion.explored (solid) named "Explored passage: X. Opens its chat". Passage: click/Enter/Space on an underline opens the passage textbox (unexplored) or openConversation(child) (explored). Pointer highlight (mouseup with a selection) opens the textbox directly and sets a flag so the following click never activates an underline: highlight wins. Box floats above the passage (.passage-box, absolute, translateY(-100%)); keyboard selection-mode path keeps Ask about selection and an inline box. Box is a small TextInput "Question about this passage" with the passage as description + Create focused chat/Cancel branch; Enter submits natively, and the disabled submit blocks empty prompts. Escape refocuses the underline (or the reply section for highlights). A failed branch keeps the prompt (existing flow). Decisions/tradeoffs: dropped the Follow this passage heading, quote block and footnote for a small box; the box can cover the line above the passage; a stale duplicate suggestion:true request still creates a branch but does not steal the reference. Evidence: test/suggestions.test.mjs new integration test (explore, no overwrite, manual not marking, grandchild, delete resets); test/turn + test/markdown explored cases; npm test 141/141; build OK; astryx doctor 0 fail. Browser (agent-browser, built app, in-process fake provider fixture, not a live provider): new scripts/verify-suggestion-branching.mjs passes 3/3 after fixing a script race. It covers: click opens an empty box above the underline; empty Enter sends nothing; Escape refocuses the underline; Enter on the underline opens the box; failed branch keeps "fail me"; "explain" creates one child "mutex" and marks it explored; solid vs dotted computed style; Enter on the explored underline opens the child with no duplicate; grandchild by keyboard; highlight inside an explored underline creates a second branch "ute". Updated verify-passage-selection.mjs (highlight opens box directly) and verify-keyboard-journey.mjs (INPUT); both PASS.

title: Save suggestions for new replies
acceptance_criteria:
- A completed saved reply triggers exactly one suggestion call; failed, partial and canceled replies trigger none.
- Saved suggestions are exact slices of the saved raw reply; invalid, mismatched and overlapping candidates are discarded.
- Reopening the tree or switching provider/model starts no new suggestion call; replies saved before this feature get none.
- Suggestion instructions and results never appear in tutor history or inherited context.
- Two conversations can run suggestions concurrently while chat stays usable.
- A failed call shows "Suggestions unavailable" and manual highlighting still works.
- Integration tests over the fake provider CLIs, extended to answer suggestion calls, cover the cases above.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. server/suggestions.mjs (reused stash anchored/suggest; dropped stash's 3-cap and proposed questions): after a completed non-empty reply, app starts one detached thread-less call (instructions separate from TUTOR_INSTRUCTIONS) with {inheritedContext, question, answer}. Model: Claude 'haiku'; Codex = first catalog model matching /luna/ (live catalog via ~/.codex/models_cache.json: gpt-6-luna, also gpt-5.6-luna; falls back to conversation model); custom endpoint keeps conversation model. Passages validated as exact UTF-16 slices (no surrogate split), overlapping/duplicate/mismatched dropped, no cap; unparseable output = failed. Store: additive table suggestions(message PK, conversation, status pending|ready|failed, passages, usage) created outside migrate so older builds still open DB; INSERT OR IGNORE = once per reply, so reopen/provider switch never rerun; no backfill; pending -> failed on restart; deleted with conversation. Usage of the call (also on failure) saved with the row; reply token line sums it ('…, including suggestions'); today's total includes it, reply count does not. tutorContext strips suggestions. UI: state.suggesting polls like videos; failed shows 'Suggestions unavailable' under the token line; manual highlighting unchanged. createApp suggestions flag defaults false (tests), main.mjs true; 5ut.5 adds Settings switch. Evidence: test/suggestions.test.mjs (5 tests over fake Claude/Codex CLIs: once-only + haiku, exact passages, usage, isolation of tutor/compaction prompts, reopen/switch/pre-feature none, failed/interrupted none, Codex luna, failure + manual branch, concurrency of two conversations with chat usable, stop mid-call -> failed no rerun); npm test 135/135; tsc + vite build OK; astryx doctor 0 fail. Live Claude Haiku suggest() on a website answer: 6 valid passages, usage 915/1802/0. Live Codex suggestion not run (plan usage limit noted in 5ut.1).

title: Draw suggestions as dotted underlines in replies
description:
## What to build

Render saved suggestions as subtle dotted underlines in the formatted reply, using a pure mapping from the reply's canonical text and its suggestions to underline ranges that matches the offsets manual selection uses. Underlines are reachable with Tab, have descriptive accessible names, and their arrival is announced once, politely. They never move focus, scroll or open anything. Spec stories 8–10, 12, 14–16, 39–40.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Underlines appear only after the reply is saved and cover exactly the saved passages, including in Markdown, code, emoji and repeated phrases.
- Tab reaches each underline; screen readers hear one polite availability announcement.
- Arrival of underlines does not change focus or scroll position.
- The pure mapping has its own tests, following the existing client helper tests.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. Pure mapping underlineRanges(text, suggestions) in src/turn.ts: only status ready; keeps passages that are exact raw UTF-16 slices (same offsets as rawOffsets/manual selection), in bounds, non-overlapping, sorted. renderMarkdown(raw, reveal, underlines) splits text leaves at underline bounds into <u class="suggestion"> pieces keeping data-o/data-e, so manual selection offsets are unchanged; source-passage reveal wins over underline. First piece of each underline is its one Tab stop (tabIndex 0, role=button, aria-label "Suggested passage: <plain text>"); role=button chosen because 5ut.4 wires Enter/click to the passage textbox (no action yet). Dotted, secondary-color underline; focus-visible outline. Each reply has an sr-only role=status region mounted while empty, filled with "N suggested passages in tutor reply K" when suggestions become ready: announced once politely; reopened replies render it at mount (not re-announced). No focus/scroll code; underlines only for completed replies with ready suggestions. Decisions/tradeoffs: overlap with learner selection is NOT resolved here (dropping underlines on selection would re-render and destroy the browser selection); selection-wins belongs to 5ut.4 click handling. shortcut: passages covering only hidden syntax or math draw nothing. Evidence: test/turn.test.mjs (mapping: ready-only, mismatch/overlap/out-of-bounds dropped, repeated phrase, emoji, code), test/markdown.test.mjs (rendered pieces cover exact raw spans across emphasis/list items/code lines, one Tab stop and name per underline, second repeated "same" only, selection offsets over underlines unchanged). npm test 137/137; tsc+vite build OK; astryx doctor 0 fail. Browser check (agent-browser, local app over an in-process fake provider with 6s suggestion delay, fixture not live provider): underlines appeared after save (4->8->12), composer focus kept, chat scrollTop 600 unchanged, status region empty then "4 suggested passages in tutor reply 2", Tab from reply walks mutex, 😀, x = 1, Frontend then the Select passage button; computed text-decoration-style dotted; screenshot shows subtle dotted underlines.

title: Show token usage under each final response
description:
## What to build

Each provider adapter reads the usage its provider reports for a turn (input, output and cache-read tokens) and the server saves it with the resulting message. Every final tutor response shows a small line of token usage under it; Settings shows today's total. Usage the provider does not report is stored and shown as "usage unavailable", never estimated. Confirm what the Codex app-server reports per turn and record the finding. Spec stories 1–6.

Spec: docs/break-down-spec.md (agreed 2026-11-09). Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md. Size: one fresh context of 100k–150k tokens and under one hour of implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Claude reply shows input, output and cache-read tokens under the final response, and the numbers survive reopening the tree.
- A Codex reply shows its reported usage, or "usage unavailable" if none is reported; the Codex finding is recorded.
- Settings shows today's total across conversations.
- Failed, partial and canceled replies do not invent usage.
- Integration tests through the app server over the fake provider CLIs cover reported and missing usage.
notes: Done 2026-11-10. Adapters emit {type:'usage'} (Claude result.usage; Codex thread/tokenUsage/updated .last), app saves only on completed replies after integer validation into nullable messages.usage JSON {input,output,cacheRead,at} (additive column, no schema version bump so older builds still open DB). /api/state.usage = today's (server-local midnight) total. UI: line under each completed assistant reply ('Token usage unavailable' when null); Settings shows today's usage. Decisions: Claude input includes cache_creation tokens (live input_tokens is ~2); Codex input excludes cachedInputTokens. Codex finding: codex-cli 0.167 app-server emits thread/tokenUsage/updated per turn; native rollouts show one token_count per turn. Live Claude PASS; live Codex turn blocked by ChatGPT plan usage limit (failed reply stored no usage). Custom endpoint shows unavailable (no stream_options). Evidence: docs/verification/token-usage-results.json; test/usage.test.mjs; npm test 129/129, build pass.

title: Verify the finished product and record release evidence
description:
## What to build

The final acceptance pass for the finished product: every PRD criterion plus the media and suggestion checks, run on the shipped build with live providers, and a release record.

## Work order

1. Regression: `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and every fixture script.
2. Live journey on Claude and on Codex: New chat, first question, branch, nested branch, concurrent replies, provider switch in both directions, restart, and resume. Compare saved messages, anchors, snapshots, positions, viewport, folds, selection and panel mode before and after the restart.
3. Later increments: a tutor-chosen diagram, a requested video and suggestions each work in a nested child; their generation context stays out of tutor history, verified by inspecting submitted histories and branch snapshots before and after generation, a provider switch and a restart.
4. Optional additions that shipped (rich replies, rename and delete, custom endpoint, Vim bindings): run their acceptance once more inside the full journey. State plainly which optional items did not ship.
5. Local delivery: loopback-only listener, local save location, no credentials in responses, first-run command from a clean checkout.
6. Write docs/verification/product-release.md: a pass or fail row per PRD criterion with links, the providers and models actually used, known limitations and anything unverified. Set the version in package.json to 1.0.0 and add a short changelog.
7. Close the epics whose children are all closed. Leave open, with the reason, anything that did not pass.

## Start here

PRD.md acceptance criteria and its media paragraph, docs/verification/text-release.md, docs/verification/later-increments.md, scripts/verify-release-journey-live.mjs.

## Out of scope

New features and fixes larger than a release defect; file those as separate issues. Pushing, publishing or tagging on a remote.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every PRD acceptance criterion and the media and suggestion checks have a recorded pass or fail with linked evidence from the shipped build; fixtures are not presented as live evidence.
- The live journey passes on both Claude and Codex, including both-direction switching and an actual restart with identical saved fields.
- Generation transcripts for diagrams, videos and suggestions are shown to be absent from tutor histories and branch snapshots.
- docs/verification/product-release.md exists with the matrix, the limitations and the list of optional items that did or did not ship; the version is 1.0.0 with a changelog.
- Unresolved failures stay open as issues rather than being waived.

title: Package first run: one start command, preflight checks and a user guide
description:
## What to build

Make TreeTutor something a learner can start and trust on their own machine without reading the source: one command, clear preflight messages, safe upgrades of saved data and a user guide.

## Work order

1. Start: a single documented command builds when the built assets are missing or stale, starts the loopback server and prints the address. A busy port gives a clear message and an option to choose another. Binding stays loopback-only.
2. Preflight: on start, report the Node version requirement, whether the Claude Code CLI is installed and signed in, and whether Codex is connected, each with the exact next step. A missing provider never blocks opening saved trees.
3. Saved data: record a schema version, and copy the database to a dated backup before any migration that rewrites data. A database from each earlier commit's schema still opens. Print the data directory location, and document backup and restore.
4. Shutdown: stopping the server ends active replies cleanly and marks them interrupted, as the store already does on start.
5. User guide in README.md: install, start, providers and sign-in, the learning journey, keyboard controls, where data lives, privacy (what leaves the machine) and troubleshooting. Remove stale development-only instructions from the user path.
6. Tests: an integration test for start-up on an old-schema database, the backup, and the busy-port message.

## Start here

server/main.mjs, server/store.mjs (constructor migrations), package.json scripts, README.md, scripts/verify-local-delivery.mjs.

## Out of scope

Hosted deployment, a desktop installer, auto-update and telemetry: the PRD keeps TreeTutor a local web app.

title: Rename and delete chats and branches
description:
## What to build

Let the learner rename any conversation, delete a whole chat, and delete a branch together with its descendants.

## Work order

1. Rename: an inline rename for the chat header title and the sidebar entry, saved through a new endpoint with the existing 200-character bound. A renamed root is never retitled by a later first question.
2. Delete a chat: removes the root, every descendant, their messages, branches, artifacts and layout in one transaction, after a confirmation that names the chat and its number of conversations. Deleting the open chat moves to the next saved chat or the New chat state.
3. Delete a branch: removes that conversation and its descendants only; the parent conversation and its messages are untouched. Selection moves to the parent.
4. Stop any active reply in a conversation being deleted and ignore its late events. Remove artifact files that belong to deleted conversations.
5. Confirmation is keyboard accessible, focuses the safe choice first and returns focus sensibly afterwards. There is no undo, so the confirmation says so.
6. Integration tests for cascade, transaction rollback on failure, active-reply handling, ownership and CSRF.

title: Render Markdown, code and math in replies with exact passage anchors
description:
## What to build

Show tutor replies as formatted text: headings, lists, emphasis, tables, code blocks with highlighting and math. Passage selection, branch anchors and source reveal must stay exact against the saved raw message text, which remains the canonical source.

## Work order

1. Renderer: choose a Markdown renderer that exposes source positions and add it with the smallest dependency set; record the choice. Raw HTML in replies is not rendered. Links open safely in a new tab and never navigate the app. The Content-Security-Policy stays free of unsafe script sources.
2. Offsets: every rendered text node carries the start offset of its source text. Map a DOM selection back to raw UTF-16 start and end offsets through those markers, so the anchor's text is still an exact slice of the saved message and the branches endpoint's validation is unchanged. A selection that crosses hidden syntax resolves to the raw span that covers it.
3. Reveal: highlight a saved anchor inside the rendered reply, including anchors that start or end inside formatting or code, and anchors saved before this change.
4. Keyboard selection: keep the read-only raw-text selector as the keyboard path, with its offsets unchanged.
5. Streaming: render partial Markdown without flicker or layout jumps; an unfinished code fence displays as code.
6. Map node previews stay plain text; strip syntax for readability without persisting anything.
7. Tests: offset mapping across emphasis, lists, code, tables, math, emoji and repeated phrases; old anchors still reveal. Update scripts/verify-passage-selection.mjs.

## Start here

docs/architecture-proposal.md (canonical-text indexing), src/ChatPage.tsx (`Passage`, `captureSelection`, reveal), server/app.mjs (branches endpoint validation).

title: Generate Mermaid diagrams in an isolated worker and save finished artifacts
description:
## What to build

The server half of Mermaid diagrams. When the tutor decides a diagram would help, it asks for one; a separate worker with its own provider session produces Mermaid source from a minimal frozen task; the server validates the result and saves it as an artifact owned by the originating conversation and message. Only the artifact id, title and a concise description ever enter tutor context.

## Work order

1. Contract: decide and record how the tutor signals a request (for example a fenced directive in its reply that the server removes from the visible reply) and the frozen task handed to the worker: the diagram intent and the minimal relevant excerpt. Never pass the full transcript, the tutor thread id or credentials.
2. Worker: run through the conversation's provider with `thread: null`, as branch compaction does, separate from the tutor session, abortable, and bounded in time and output size. It must work through both server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs.
3. Validation: accept only Mermaid source that parses. Reject click, href and script directives, HTML labels and oversized output. Store nothing executable.
4. Storage: add an artifacts table in server/store.mjs (id, conversation, message, kind, status, title, description, source, created) with at least pending, ready and failed. Return a conversation's artifacts with its messages. Check ownership so one tree cannot read or attach another tree's artifact by id.
5. Tutor context: later tutor turns, provider switches and branch compaction see only a short marker with the title and description of a ready artifact; never the worker prompt, the source or the worker transcript.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for request, context isolation, validation rejects, ownership and both provider adapters.

## Start here

PRD.md "Isolated media generation". server/app.mjs (message handler, branch compaction as the model for a separate `generate` call), server/store.mjs, server/claude.mjs, server/codex.mjs.

## Out of scope

Rendering in the chat (next task). Restart and failure recovery hardening and live evidence (TreeTutor-vm4.1). Video. A diagram editor.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tutor reply that asks for a diagram produces one saved ready artifact linked to that conversation and message, and the visible reply contains no directive text.
- The worker receives only the frozen minimal task: a test asserts the tutor thread id and unrelated messages are absent, and that worker output does not appear in tutor history or the next tutor prompt.

- An artifact of another tree cannot be fetched or attached.

title: Render saved Mermaid diagrams inline in the originating chat
description:
## What to build

The client half of Mermaid diagrams: show each saved artifact inline at its message, rendered safely, with a text alternative and keyboard access, and restore it on reload with no new inference.

## Work order

1. Add the `mermaid` package, loaded lazily so the map and chat bundle stay small. Render with the strict security level, no HTML labels and no links. Keep the Content-Security-Policy in server/app.mjs free of unsafe script sources; adjust only what rendering provably needs and record why.
2. Inline card at the originating message: title, diagram, the description as the text alternative, and a disclosure for the Mermaid source. Pending and failed states. The card is focusable; a large diagram scrolls or zooms inside the card. Use theme tokens so both colour schemes work.
3. In the map node transcript, show a compact "Diagram: title" row instead of the drawing.
4. Reload and reopen restore the same artifact without calling a provider. A render error falls back to the description and the source.
5. Passage selection and branching on the reply text keep working around the card, with unchanged offsets.
6. Tests: integration coverage for the artifact payload and render-state logic, plus one browser fixture for render, keyboard focus and reload.

## Start here

PRD.md "Content rollout" and "Isolated media generation". src/ChatPage.tsx (message list, `Passage`), src/TreeOverview.tsx (transcript rows), the artifact payload from the previous task.

## Out of scope

Failure, interruption, late-event and restart recovery and the live isolation evidence (TreeTutor-vm4.1). Editing diagrams. Export.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- A ready artifact renders inline at its originating message in the chat it came from, and nowhere else.
- The description is exposed as the text alternative; the card and its source disclosure are reachable and operable by keyboard with visible focus.
- Source containing links, scripts or HTML labels does not execute or navigate; the page's CSP has no unsafe script source.
- Reload and server restart show the same diagram with no provider request. A render failure shows the description and source instead of a blank card.
- Selecting a passage and branching from the same reply still produces exact anchors.
- The map node shows the compact diagram row.
- `npm test`, `npm run build`, the Astryx built-output doctor and the fixture pass.
notes:
Verified result: TreeTutor-vm4.8 acceptance PASS. Saved Mermaid artifacts render only after their owning assistant reply and in their originating conversation. Cards sit outside Passage, keep the description visible and as the image alternative, provide keyboard focus, native scrolling for large drawings and an Enter/Space source disclosure. Pending generation/rendering, generation failure, renderer failure and invalid/unsafe saved sources remain honest; renderer failure opens the saved source. Failed generation has no source under the existing contract. Map messages carry only id/title/status and show compact Diagram: title rows. SSE pending/final records reconcile by id; conversation/message guards reject foreign attachments and reopen overlays retain in-flight artifact state without changing canonical reply text.

Decision/tradeoff: Mermaid 12.3.0 was already pinned by vm4.7; no package/lockfile changes. Dynamic import runs only for a ready artifact in an open chat; initial map requests no Mermaid renderer. Shared 16-KiB/plain-label source guard keeps browser and server rules identical. Strict Mermaid security, HTML labels disabled globally/flowchart, no callback binding, no error SVG; reject HTML/link/script/image output and display SVG through a data image rather than inserting HTML. Existing CSP is byte-identical: script-src self and existing img-src self data suffice, with no new script/style permission. Classic/base appearance uses computed Astryx color/font tokens; serialized renders keep theme config with each diagram and system color changes rerender it. Plain labels and noninteractive images intentionally retain the conservative vm4.7 contract. Explicit .ts imports are enabled in the existing no-emit TypeScript configuration so Node and browser share checks/state logic.

Evidence: docs/diagram-artifacts.md; docs/verification/diagram-rendering.md, diagram-rendering-results.json and diagram-rendering-checks.json. Final npm test 76/76 PASS, no failures/skips/cancellations (38.3s); npm run build PASS; Astryx built-output doctor 20 pass/2 existing font warnings/0 fail; Impeccable detector []; git diff --check PASS; source/evidence hashes and local links PASS. Browser fixture 10/10 PASS: real flowchart/sequence/class/state/ER/pie rendering, focus and both scroll axes, keyboard disclosure, light/dark/narrow containment, actual repeated-emoji mouse branch at UTF-16 [10,19), canonical keyboard selection, live pending-to-ready events, descriptions/source fallbacks, four unsafe persisted-source probes with no executable DOM/navigation/probe request/CSP violation, exact saved artifacts after reopen/reload and separate server-process restart. PIDs 3217755 -> 3219388 reopened the same SQLite file; all 3 root artifacts/messages identical and synthetic generate-call count stays 4 across reload/restart (prior compaction, child reply, tutor reply, worker). Existing passage-selection browser regression separately PASS, including keyboard branch/cancel/focus. Desktop/dark/narrow captures inspected.

Evidence boundary: fixture providers and seeded unsafe records; actual Chromium, production assets, HTTP/SSE, SQLite, Mermaid parse/render and process restart. Integration render-state callback is substituted; browser rendering is real. No live native inference/semantic diagram quality, media context-isolation evidence or pending-worker restart/failure/late-event recovery claim; vm4.1 retains those gates. Existing Vite large-chunk advisory and Astryx font warnings remain. Ponytail and Matt Pocock skills unavailable in checked paths/catalog; Caveman, RTK, codebase-memory, Beads, Impeccable, Astryx and agent-browser used. Beads/Ralph already initialized.

Preserved all 40 protected startup files byte-for-byte, including the original server/app viewport/CSP and package/workflow edits. Existing changes in shared files remain; master/HEAD unchanged. title: Check-yourself predict-then-reveal visuals
description: Deferred from the inline visuals epic TreeTutor-zhf (grilling 2026-11-11). Small predict-then-reveal questions embedded in replies on the visual engine. Needs tutor guidance on when to quiz before implementation. Do not start until the visual worker ships and the owner revisits.
design: This invocation revisits the deferred issue after TreeTutor-zhf.5 shipped. Smallest implementation: reuse ordinary treetutor-visual requests and the existing isolated smart worker/sandbox, with tutor and worker guidance for an optional predict-then-reveal interaction. Offer at most one brief check per reply only for a useful next-step/cause-and-effect prediction after enough context; honor explicit requests and opt-outs, skip short factual/casual turns, and never gate continuing the conversation. Put the prediction and correct result plus a concise why into intent/excerpt; keep surrounding prose and metadata spoiler-free. Render an initially closed native details/summary labelled Reveal answer, with the question visible, answer/visual outcome/explanation inside. Reveal/close is local, ungraded and unsaved; reload resets it without inference. No new schema, endpoint, score, model call type, or app controls. Tradeoff: generative tutoring policy is prompt-guided rather than a deterministic quiz scheduler; reveal state does not persist.
acceptance_criteria: Tutor guidance defines when to offer/skip a prediction and respects learner requests/opt-outs. Worker guidance provides a visible question and initially hidden correct outcome plus explanation, keyboard-accessible reveal without grading or app/network access. Existing four-field requests stream inline, persist and reopen through the visual engine without duplicate messages or inference. HTTP integration verifies actual request/worker/persistence/history boundaries. Focused built-UI checks verify hidden/revealed states, Enter/Space, no reveal provider calls or branching, light/dark, narrow/desktop and reload reset; native smoke verifies real tutor and worker output, distinct from fixtures. Relevant tests/build and diff checks pass; evidence recorded before closure.
notes:
Verified TreeTutor-zjq against AGENTS.md, PRD.md, the full TreeTutor-zhf epic/comments, closed prerequisite TreeTutor-zhf.5 and docs/inline-visuals-spec.md. This invocation revisits the deferred issue under current implementation authorization; removed stale deferred title/needs-design label. No other issue started.

Result and scope:
- Added tutor guidance for at most one brief optional prediction when a next step or cause/effect outcome helps test an idea, after enough context. Explicit requests and quiz opt-outs take precedence; short factual/casual turns and direct explanations stay unquizzed. No answering/reveal gate, grading or familiarity inference.
- Reused the ordinary four-field treetutor-visual request, isolated smart worker, persisted source and sandbox. Intent/excerpt carry question, correct result and reason; title/description/surrounding prose remain spoiler-free. Worker guidance uses a visible initial state/question and initially closed native details/summary labelled Reveal answer, with answer/result/reason inside. Native Enter/Space, visible focus and automatic frame height; no submitted answer, timer, storage, network or app messages from reveal. Ordinary visuals do not add quizzes.
- Found and reproduced a real interaction regression: explicit source reveal of a saved branch from an answer focused a part inside a still-closed disclosure (assertion false !== true). Three added lines in src/sandbox.ts open containing native disclosures only during explicit source reveal, before focusing the part. Final built regression passes. Ordinary reload remains closed.
- Updated only server/diagrams.mjs, the check guidance section of already-dirty server/prompts/visual.md, three added lines in already-dirty src/sandbox.ts, docs/inline-visuals-spec.md, test/visuals.test.mjs, scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs, the two new check-yourself evidence reports and progress handoff. Existing unrelated dirty edits preserved. No dependencies, migrations, routes, React components, design tokens, scores or saved progress added.

Decisions/tradeoffs:
- The selected work request revisits the old deferral after its technical prerequisite shipped. Tutor timing is prompt-guided, not a new deterministic quiz scheduler. Existing model/effort, cancellation, retry, worker isolation and permissions remain the engine contract.
- Native disclosure provides keyboard/accessibility semantics without another library or host protocol. Disclosure state is deliberately local and unsaved; reloading resets to closed without inference. Explicit saved-source reveal opens the answer because the learner requested that exact source.
- Hidden answers are educational disclosure, not a secret from the owner inspecting generated source. No quizzes are graded or reported to the knowledge graph.

Acceptance evidence:
- npm test passed, including final full suite after the sandbox fix (0 failures). node --test test/visuals.test.mjs: 12/12 passed before the sandbox-only fix. Added HTTP integration checks real request -> smart-worker input, inline position, answer-free metadata/history, source persistence and reopen without worker replay. Existing Claude/Codex native-protocol fixtures retain no-tool/fresh-session/effort checks.
- npm run build passed after final sandbox fix (TypeScript plus production Vite; existing large-chunk advisory only). git diff --check passed; no staged changes.
- node scripts/verify-visual-workers.mjs --check-yourself: final PASS, eight focused built-UI groups with synthetic providers and isolated SQLite. Covers visible question, answer/explanation hidden in visual and accessibility tree; Enter opens and Space closes without branching; automatic height; desktop/narrow (1280/390) light/dark; reload resets without inference; no duplicate learner messages/source changes; worker retry/Stop regressions; explicit saved-branch source opens its answer and focuses the exact part without inference. title: Add an OpenAI-compatible provider adapter with locally stored endpoint settings
description:
## What to build

The server half of the custom endpoint from IDEA.md: a third provider that talks to any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API, configured with a base URL and API key kept on this machine. It is an explicit learner choice and never a silent fallback for Claude or Codex.

## Work order

1. Design note: record in docs/ the API surface used (chat completions with streaming, model listing), how history is replayed, and where the key is stored. Keep the key in a file in the local app-data directory with owner-only permissions; it is written through the server and never returned to the browser, logged or placed in SQLite.
2. Adapter: server/openai.mjs with the same `models()` and `generate()` shape as server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs. The API is stateless, so each turn sends the saved discussion plus the fixed inherited branch context; honour the abort signal; map stream chunks to the existing delta and status events.
3. Settings endpoints: save, test and clear the endpoint with CSRF and the existing loopback checks. Report only whether an endpoint is configured and its base URL.
4. Wiring: register the provider in server/main.mjs only when configured. Branch compaction and provider switching work through it with no special cases.
5. Integration tests against a local fake OpenAI-compatible server: streaming, history replay including inherited context, abort, model catalogue, error mapping, compaction, and that no response body or log contains the key. Extend test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

server/claude.mjs and server/codex.mjs (adapter shape), server/app.mjs (`providers`, `/api/models`), test/provider.test.mjs, test/credential-boundary.test.mjs.

title: Show video status and a paused native player inline
description:
## What to build

The learner-facing half of requested videos: an artifact entry at the request's position in the chat with honest status, and a paused native player once the file is ready, without interrupting chat.

## Work order

1. Insert the artifact entry at its original position with a descriptive title and the states from the proposal's table that generation can reach today: Preparing, Rendering, Ready and Failed. Show render progress only when the renderer reports it.
2. Ready state: title, concise text explanation and an inline native `<video>` player, initially paused, kept within the chat width with its aspect ratio. No autoplay.
3. Completion must not move keyboard focus, scroll the conversation or inject generation messages. The learner can keep chatting and navigate elsewhere while a job runs; the result appears only in the originating conversation.
4. Accessibility: one labelled status announcement per state change, not per progress tick. Tab reaches the player. The player owns its keys while focused, so map and chat handlers must not intercept them.
5. Map node transcript shows a compact "Video: title" row with its status.
6. Reload restores a ready video from the local file with no provider request.
7. Browser fixture for the status sequence, keyboard playback, no stolen focus or scroll, and reload.

docs/video-flow-proposal.md "Learner flow" and its acceptance checks 1 and 6. src/ChatPage.tsx and the Mermaid artifact card.

title: Offer grounded branch suggestions after saved replies
description:
## What to build

The first half of automatic suggestions, following docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md: after a reply completes and is saved, evaluate it once for zero to three grounded passages, show them in a compact "Explore further" group under that reply, and let the learner turn one into a branch through the existing editable branch form. This is the original idea's one-click break-down of a subproblem.

## Work order

1. Trigger: evaluate once per successfully saved completed reply, using the provider and model captured at completion and only the completed answer, its question and the fixed inherited context. Run it as a separate `generate` call with `thread: null` so nothing enters tutor history. Never evaluate partial, failed, cancelled or interrupted replies, and never rerun on focus, reopen or provider change.
2. Validation: each candidate is one contiguous passage with message id, exact text and UTF-16 start and end offsets into the saved reply. Reuse the boundary and exact-slice checks from the branches endpoint in server/app.mjs. Discard mismatches, duplicates, overlaps and ungrounded candidates rather than guess. Cover repeated phrases and emoji.
3. Storage: save completed candidates with their source message, separate from tutor messages.
4. UI: the group appears after its source reply without popups, focus moves or scrolling, with one polite availability announcement. Choosing a suggestion opens the existing branch form with the exact passage and an editable question; only submitting creates and focuses a child through the normal compaction flow; cancelling creates nothing and returns focus to the suggestion. Manual selection keeps working throughout.
5. Failure: show a brief non-blocking "Suggestions unavailable" status; no automatic retry.
6. Integration tests with the fixture provider for trigger rules, validation, isolation and the submit boundary; a browser fixture for keyboard choose, edit, cancel and submit.

## Start here

docs/branch-suggestions-proposal.md (selected design) and its acceptance checks 1, 2, 3 and 5. server/app.mjs (reply completion in the message handler, the branches endpoint), src/ChatPage.tsx (`Passage`, branch form).

## Out of scope

Dismissals, accepted-child reuse, restart and late-event handling, and the learning-example quality review (TreeTutor-vm4.5). Learner profiles, ranking, preferences, automatic child creation.

title: Generate a requested video in a bounded isolated worker
description:
## What to build

The generation half of requested videos, following docs/video-flow-proposal.md: an explicit learner request creates a job; an isolated worker writes a Remotion composition and renders a finished local file; the server validates and publishes it as an artifact. No player UI yet beyond what tests need.

## Work order

1. Request: detect an explicit video request in the conversation and save a job with the frozen input from the proposal's contract (exact request, relevant saved excerpt, fixed inherited context, source ids). An ordinary explanation never starts a video. When intent is unclear the tutor asks first.
2. Worker: a dedicated workspace per attempt under the local app-data directory, outside the repository, with no tutor credentials, no access to unrelated learning files, bounded run time and controlled network access. Record the actual sandbox and provider permission settings used; context isolation and execution isolation are checked separately.
3. Render: add Remotion and render programmatically to a private temporary output. Validate that the output path stays inside the workspace, the media is readable and the job owns it, then move it to its final location before marking the artifact ready. A failed save never shows a playable success.
4. Storage and serving: reuse the Mermaid artifacts table for job, attempt, status and result description. Serve finished media only through a same-origin artifact endpoint with ownership checks; never accept a generated absolute path or URL as a media source.
5. Tutor context: only artifact id, title and the concise finished-content description. No source code, logs, transcript or filesystem paths.
6. Integration tests for the job lifecycle to ready, path and ownership validation, and context isolation. One real render, kept short, as recorded evidence.

## Start here

docs/video-flow-proposal.md (selected design), PRD.md "Isolated media generation", and the artifact pipeline delivered for Mermaid.

## Out of scope

The inline player and status UI (next task). Retry, cancel and restart recovery (TreeTutor-vm4.3). Narration, captions, editing, gallery.

## Context and execution

Sized for one agent invocation in a 100k–150k context window: plan about 100k of working context and keep the rest for startup, tools, verification and repair. These are planning targets, not limits. Read code and evidence on demand. Fix recoverable failures inside this task and record a precise checkpoint in the notes instead of creating microtasks. AGENTS.md standing authorization applies; keep Git local. Prefer integration tests (`npm test`); use a browser fixture only where acceptance needs real layout or focus. UI work uses Impeccable and Astryx inside the existing page. Run `npm test`, `npm run build` and the Astryx built-output doctor before closing, and state which evidence is fixture and which is live.
acceptance_criteria:
- An explicit request in a conversation creates exactly one job with the frozen input; an ordinary explanation creates none.
- The worker runs in its own workspace without tutor credentials or unrelated learning files; the evidence note records the real permission and network settings and how each was checked.
- A finished render is validated and published as a ready artifact served only through the same-origin endpoint; an out-of-workspace path, unreadable media or a failed save publishes nothing.
- Tutor history, provider-switch history and branch snapshots contain only id, title and description.
- One real short render completes and its evidence is recorded. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.
notes:
Implemented 2026-11-09 (TreeTutor-vm4.9).

What: tutor requests a video via a hidden fenced `treetutor-video` block (same JSON shape as diagrams); the server starts a job only when the learner's own message names a video/animation/clip/movie (asksForVideo), so an ordinary explanation never starts one even if the model emits the block. Tutor instructions tell it to ask first when intent is unclear. Job = artifacts row (kind 'video', attempt, frozen `input` JSON: request, intent, excerpt, inheritedContext {snapshot, selectedPassage, question}, sources {conversation, requestMessage, replyMessage, parentConversation, parentMessage}). The job runs detached from the reply stream (learner can keep chatting); app.stop aborts it. Files: server/videos.mjs, server/video-render.mjs, store migration (CHECK kind IN mermaid/video; old Mermaid DBs rebuilt in place, verified with a HEAD-schema DB), app media endpoint GET /api/trees/:tree/artifacts/:id/media.

Isolation settings actually used:
- Composing agent (context isolation): existing provider adapters with a fresh session (thread null), separate WORKER instructions, input = frozen JSON only. Claude: `-p --max-turns 1 --tools '' --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config {} --setting-sources '' --disable-slash-commands`, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/AUTH_TOKEN stripped, cwd <appdata>/claude-workspace. Codex: shell/apply_patch/js_repl/code_mode/apps/skills off, web_search disabled, every tool request rejected. The agent has no file, shell or network tools; it returns source text, which the server validates (imports only react/remotion, no dynamic import/require/fetch/network APIs/URLs/media elements, ≤64 KiB, required `// Description:` line) and writes into the attempt workspace.
- Render (execution isolation): `bwrap --ro-bind / / --tmpfs $HOME --tmpfs <appdata> --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /run/user --ro-bind <repo>/node_modules --ro-bind server/video-render.mjs --bind <workspace> --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session --clearenv` (env HOME/PATH/TMPDIR only + PWD), SIGKILL after 180 s; composition step bounded at 120 s. Chromium = pre-installed node_modules/.remotion chrome-headless-shell (no download in sandbox). Checked by test "render sandbox hides home and app data…": app-data DB, ~/.claude and repo files denied, writes outside workspace denied, TCP to 1.1.1.1:443 denied, env = HOME,PATH,PWD,TMPDIR.
- Workspace: <appdata>/video-work/<attempt> (outside repo; default ~/.local/share/treetutor). After each attempt bundle/tmp/out are removed (41 MB bundle); Video.tsx/index.tsx kept as private work.
- Publish: server-chosen out/<uuid>.mp4; realpath must equal <realpath workspace>/out/<name>, regular non-symlink file, 1 KiB–200 MiB, `ftyp` header, duration 0–60 s, row still pending with same attempt → rename to <appdata>/videos/<artifact id>.mp4 → finishVideo; DB failure unlinks the file. Media path is derived from artifact id only; endpoint requires conversation ownership + kind video + ready. fs errors are replaced with generic messages (no paths).

title: Deliver requested videos with isolated generation and recovery
description:
## What to build
After Mermaid, deliver the selected requested-video flow end to end: bounded isolated generation, validated local artifacts, inline native playback, durable status, explicit retry/cancel and restart recovery. Follow docs/video-flow-proposal.md and reuse existing artifact/storage paths.

## Work order
1. Freeze the explicit request and minimal relevant context. Verify dedicated worker workspace/credentials/network/runtime boundaries and output containment/ownership/readability; publish valid local media before ready and serve only same-origin artifact references.
2. Clarify ambiguous intent; show honest preparing/rendering/ready states and a paused native player with text explanation. Keep other chats usable, preserve focus/scroll and native playback keys, and restore finished media locally without inference replay.
3. Retry with the same frozen input without duplicate messages; new requests create new jobs. Cancel only the owning job and ignore stale attempts. On restart mark unfinished jobs interrupted; missing media offers explicit regeneration. Exercise render/save/invalid-output failures and keep all generation work out of tutor context.
4. Run focused integration/permission checks and required UI/build gates; record finished playback and isolation evidence. No autoplay, editing, narration, gallery or general-purpose rendering platform.

## Start here
docs/video-flow-proposal.md, PRD.md and the Mermaid artifact boundary delivered by TreeTutor-vm4.1. The selected design is already agreed in TreeTutor-vm4.2.

## Context and execution
One agent invocation owns this complete task in a 200k context window. Aim for about 140k working context and reserve about 60k for startup, tools, verification and repair; this is a planning estimate, not a measured token guarantee. Read relevant code/evidence on demand, work through internal steps in the same run, and fix recoverable failures here. Create another issue only for a genuinely separate deliverable, external/user gate or evidence that the remaining work cannot fit. Existing implementation authorization and local-only commit rules apply. Prefer integration checks; use browser/E2E checks only where the inherited acceptance requires them. Use Impeccable and Astryx for UI changes.

## Consolidated history

acceptance_criteria:
### TreeTutor-vm4.3.1: Generate a finished video in a bounded isolated worker
Freeze request, relevant conversation excerpt and inherited context; exclude unrelated branches and later messages.
Dedicated workspace has no tutor credentials or unrelated learning files, bounded execution and controlled network access; record actual permission checks.
Validate output containment, ownership and readable media; place final output before marking ready; serve only through a same-origin artifact reference.
Tutor sees only artifact ID, title and concise finished-content description; no source, private transcript, logs or absolute paths.

### TreeTutor-vm4.3.2: Play requested videos inline without interrupting chat
Only explicit video requests start generation; ambiguous intent asks for clarification.
Show preparing/rendering/ready status on the originating saved entry, real progress only when supplied, and a paused native player with text explanation.
Tab reaches player and controls; canvas handlers do not capture playback keys; completion steals neither focus nor scroll.
Continue chatting/navigate during generation; reopen a finished video locally with no inference replay.

### TreeTutor-vm4.3.3: Retry and cancel video jobs without losing saved requests
Retry creates a new attempt using the same frozen input, without duplicating the learner message; changed requests create new jobs.
Cancel affects only that job; late events from canceled or superseded attempts cannot publish ready.
Restart marks unfinished work interrupted without automatic inference; ready media persists and missing files show unavailable with explicit regeneration.
Simulate rendering, persistence and invalid-output failures; status stays honest, other chats work, and generation work stays outside model history.

### TreeTutor-vm4.3: Generate isolated Remotion videos on learner request
Learner requests video and plays finished artifact inline; generation working messages, code, tool output and revisions stay outside tutor context; task/result follows agreed design; failure leaves chat usable.

2026-11-10 implemented and verified. Evidence: docs/verification/video-recovery.md, docs/verification/video-recovery-results.json (and vm4.9/vm4.10 evidence for generation, isolation and playback).
What: statuses canceled/interrupted (+ in-place table rebuild for older DBs); restart marks pending videos interrupted, app.stop leaves them pending so they also become interrupted; POST .../artifacts/:id/cancel (owning conversation, pending only) and .../retry (failed/canceled/interrupted/unavailable; same row and frozen input, new attempt, no message); ready-but-missing/unreadable media reported available:false → Regenerate. VideoCard single action button (Cancel/Retry/Regenerate) keeps focus across state changes.
Decisions: retry reuses the artifact row (replaces the status entry, per proposal) instead of a new row; availability checked with accessSync on read (local, cheap); corrupt-but-readable media still shows ready (shortcut).
Evidence: fixture npm test 89/89 (cancel scoping, late output of canceled attempt ignored, retry same input/no message, render/composition/save failures then success, restart from pre-vm4.3 schema, stop→interrupted, zero provider calls on reopen, isolation tests from vm4.9 still pass incl. live sandboxed render); browser fixture verify-video-recovery 5/5 (synthetic providers, real sandboxed renders, prod build, headless Chrome); verify-video-player 9/9 re-run; npm run build PASS; astryx doctor --built dist 0 fail.
Limits: Chrome only; no native provider inference in this task (live Claude render evidence in vm4.9; Codex not exercised live for video); focused Cancel loses focus to body if the job completes in background.
